headline: Kishor fumes at Bihar CM's 'bechara' remark, calls him 'uneducated criminal'
text: Kishor fumes at Bihar CM's 'bechara' remark, calls him 'uneducated criminal' Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor launched a fresh attack on Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, calling him an "uneducated criminal" who could not be entrusted with governing the state. Kishor made the remark on Thursday in the north Bihar district of Saharsa, where journalists drew his attention to Choudhary's recent interview in which the CM had used the word "bechara" (poor guy) for the Bankipur MLA. The former poll strategist mockingly said, "Samrat Choudhary is right in calling me a 'bechara' because I am left with no other option but to fight to rid Bihar of an uneducated criminal like him". Notably, Kishor has been using adjectives like "anpadh" (uneducated) and "apradhi" (criminal) for Choudhary for a long time before the latter was handpicked by the BJP's top leadership as the party's first chief minister of Bihar. In the run-up to the bypoll to Bankipur, which took place after BJP national president Nitin Nabin gave up the seat, Kishor had urged people to vote for him since his victory "would make Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah take note of the popular discontent with Samrat Choudhary". Replying to another query, Kishor said that floods have been a recurring problem in Bihar for 80 years. "This Kosi region is the worst hit. During my extensive tour of the area, I have come across families which get displaced two to three times in a year because of floods," he said. Kishore alleged that the political establishment does "not work towards finding a solution because floods bring the opportunity for massive corruption". "This is a reason why the Water Resources Department has been a coveted portfolio. Unlike a PWD minister, who may face flak for a poor-quality road, the minister for water resources can easily escape scrutiny for commissioning an embankment that gets swept away in a year," Kishor claimed. The Jan Suraaj Party founder also reiterated his opposition to the state's prohibition law, calling it bogus (farzi), and warned, "We have heard about 'Udta Punjab' because of the drug abuse there. Unless this useless law is done away with, we may witness Udta Bihar as well."

headline: Hours after CJP's school inspection call, Rajasthan bars outsiders from campuses
text: JAIPUR: The Rajasthan education department Sunday evening barred outsiders from entering school premises without prior permission from the principal or head of the institution, hours after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced a statewide campaign to inspect dilapidated govt schools. The order states that only govt officials discharging official duties will be exempt from the permission requirement. Photography, videography, interviews, audio recording or live streaming involving students, teachers or school activities will also need prior clearance from the principal. Every visitor must sign the visitor's register before entering school premises, the order added. The directive comes as CJP prepares to launch its "School Thik Karo" campaign, seeking accountability and repairs at govt schools across the state. National spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka said the organisation has received requests from nine districts — Jaipur, Ajmer, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Dholpur, Bharatpur, Kota, Barmer and Hanumangarh — to inspect unsafe or poorly maintained schools, with volunteers set to visit all districts over the next two weeks. "We have received requests to inspect certain schools in these locations and raise the students' issues as the administration is refusing to heed demands to fix the schools. Providing good education and health facilities are the basics for any state govt. If the govt is not able to provide these, then why hold the positions?" Ranka told TOI. CJP's protest at a govt school in Thanagazi, Alwar, on Friday marked the start of the campaign, Ranka said. He noted that it has been over a year since the school collapse tragedy in Jhalawar, and the education minister has yet to share a concrete plan to fix over 80,000 classrooms in dilapidated condition across the state. The group has warned of a mass movement demanding education minister Madan Dilawar's resignation if a plan isn't presented in the Assembly. headline: Monsoon session of Telangana Assembly commences on September 7; prohibited properties issue rocks House
text: As expected, inclusion of vast stretches of lands in the prohibited properties list under Section 22A of the Registration Act rocked the Telangana Legislative Assembly on Monday, the first day of the monsoon session. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders raised the issue immediately as the House assembled for the day, demanding an inquiry by a sitting judge into the issue. The BJP members trooped into the Well of the House raising slogans demanding judicial inquiry into land deals. Legislative Affairs Minister D. Sridhar Babu assured the members that the government was prepared for a short discussion on the 22A lands. It had resolved to raise the issue in the Business Advisory Committee meeting slated later in the day and had no objection for taking up the issue as the first item as part of the proceedings. The BJP members led by A. Maheshwar Reddy however remained unrelenting and continued their slogans displaying placards seeking a debate on the land deals. Mr. Sridhar Babu alleged that the BJP members were trying to politicise the issue as could be seen from their protest in spite of the assurance from the Treasury Benches. Speaker G. Prasad Kumar too tried to convince the members asserting that the issue would be taken up by the BAC and a discussion would be allowed. Roads and Buildings Minister Komatlreddy Venkat Reddy, who intervened, lamented that the BJP members were not relenting in spite of the assurance given by the Legislative Affairs Minister. He charged the BJP with colluding with the main opposition Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and stalling CBI probe into the irregularities of the Kaleshwaram project. “The BJP needs to answer why the probe by CBI is not ordered?” he said. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, who was watching the proceedings, left the House amid din created by the sloganeering members. With the slogan shouting continuing, the Speaker adjourned the House for 14 minutes. Published - September 07, 2026 11:27 am IST

headline: Nagaland Congress demands probe into liquor deaths, seeks government accountability
text: Nagaland Congress seeks probe into suspected illicit liquor circulation, enforcement lapses and government accountability following deaths reported in Tuensang DIMAPUR — The Nagaland Pradesh Congress Committee (NPCC) has demanded a thorough and impartial investigation into the deaths in Tuensang reportedly linked to the consumption of suspected spurious liquor, questioning how prohibited liquor was able to reach consumers in a state that bans its sale and possession. In a statement on Sunday, the party expressed grief over the deaths and sought stringent action against those involved in the alleged manufacture, supply, transportation and sale of the liquor. The NPCC also called for an inquiry into possible negligence, failure or complicity by the Excise & Prohibition department, police and other enforcement agencies. “If Nagaland is a dry state, how did suspected spurious liquor enter the market, move through the supply chain and reach consumers with such devastating consequences?” the party asked. Related: Tuensang: 10 dead in three days, cause yet to be ascertained The Congress demanded that the state government provide immediate ex-gratia compensation to the bereaved families and appropriate assistance to those undergoing treatment. It also sought public disclosure of forensic and laboratory findings, along with the outcome of the investigation into the deaths. The party called for a comprehensive review of the implementation and enforcement of the Nagaland Liquor Total Prohibition Act, 1989, which prohibits the possession, sale, consumption, manufacture, import and export of liquor in the state. The NPCC maintained that the government could not place the entire responsibility on the victims when prohibited and potentially poisonous liquor was allegedly circulating despite the prohibition law. “When prohibited and potentially poisonous liquor is able to circulate within a prohibition state and results in loss of lives, the government owes the people an explanation,” it stated. headline: AP Government Raises Age Limits For Its 892 Job Vacancies
text: The relaxation does not apply to uniformed posts in the Police, Excise, Fire, Prisons, Forest and Transport departments VIJAYAWADA: In a major relief to aspirants for government jobs, Andhra Pradesh government has enhanced the upper age limits for recruitment to various government posts, 892 of which are vacant across 20 departments. The revised age limits will remain in force until September 30, 2027, benefiting unemployed youth who have been preparing for competitive examinations. The age-limit enhancement will be applicable to recruitments conducted by the APPSC and other recruiting agencies. The general upper age limit for government recruitments has been enhanced from 34 years to 44 years. For non-uniformed government services, the maximum age limit has been raised from 42 years to 44 years. For uniformed services too, the upper age limit for candidates in general category has been increased by two years. AP government has issued two separate government orders (GOs) in this regard. It clarified that the existing age relaxations applicable to candidates belonging to reserved categories would continue unchanged. The age-limit relaxation comes at a time when the AP Public Service Commission (APPSC) has announced a large number of vacancies. The commission has uploaded notifications, eligibility criteria, and application details on its official website. The biggest recruitment drive is for 163 Group-I posts, with applications scheduled to be accepted from October 6 to October 27. The Group-I vacancies include those of 11 deputy collectors, 14 assistant commissioners in tax services, 36 DSPs (Civil), three DSPs (Communications), 14 district educational officers, one tribal welfare officer, three regional transport officers, 15 deputy registrars of cooperative societies, and 12 municipal commissioners (Grade-II). The notification also includes two vacancies of assistant treasury officers, three district employment officers, 14 assistant audit officers, and 35 divisional development officers. Among other vacancies are 18 analyst Grade-II posts in the Pollution Control Board, one assistant director in Tribal Welfare, 12 inspectors of Factories, 17 assistant directors in AP Economics and Statistical Service, 73 hostel welfare officers Grade-II, and 196 assistant statistical officers. The APPSC has further notified posts of 11 English and Telugu reporters in the AP Legislative Assembly, 17 assistant social welfare/tribal welfare officers, eight assistant directors in Forensic Science Laboratory Services and 37 horticulture officer posts. The commission advised eligible candidates to check the prescribed educational qualifications, age criteria, application procedures, and other conditions before applying for the various posts.

headline: West Bengal by-elections to test Trinamool rival groups’ claim over party symbol
text: With by-elections for two Assembly constituencies in West Bengal -Nandigram and Rejinagar- scheduled on October 6, both factions of Trinamool Congress -one led by Mamata Banerjee and the other by Ritabrata Banerjee- have decided to field candidates on both the seats. However, the question is making rounds in the political circles: who will get the “ grass and twin-flowers’ symbol of Trinamool Congress in the upcoming by-elections. “We will contest the by-polls. At the time of filing nominations, we will state that our candidates are from the Trinamool Congress and claim the twin-flower symbol. If the Election Commission does not allot the symbol to us by the deadline, our candidates will contest as independents,” Opposition Chief Whip in the West Bengal Assembly Akhruzzaman said on Wednesday (September 9, 2026). Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman and the majority of the MLAs of the Trinamool Congress had moved away from Mamata Banerjee weeks after the 2026 Assembly poll debacle. 80 MLAs of the Trinamool Congress were elected to the 18th West Bengal Assembly on May 4, 2026, and more than 65 of them have turned rebels and have cut ties with Mamata Banerjee. Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman and other leaders of the rebel faction have made representation to the ECI seeking a claim over the party symbol. The Mamata Banerjee faction will not let the opportunity to field candidates in the by-elections go, particularly when it has only a handful of MLAs in the State Assembly. Sources in the Mamata Banerjee group say that the party will field candidates. Mamata Banerjee loyalists say that the party symbol of grass with twin flowers remains with them till the ECI decides otherwise. There are some speculations that the party chairperson may contest from either of the two seats, though there is no official word on it. Ms. Banerjee lost to Suvendu Adhikari by a narrow margin of 1526 votes in 2021 from the Nandigram Assembly seat. Rejinagar in Murshidabad has a majority of the electorate from the Muslim community, and if all opposition parties support the Trinamool Congress chairperson, she might find her way back into the State assembly. headline: Manipur: Chief of banned outfit, 46 cadres surrender with arms before CM
text: Manipur: Chief of banned outfit, 46 cadres surrender with arms before CM The surrender is seen as a major step towards strengthening the state government’s efforts towards peace and normalcy in Manipur Chief of Kangleipak Communist Party Taibangnganba (KCP-Taibangnganba), a banned underground outfit in Manipur, along with its 46 cadres surrendered 20 arms, 216 rounds of ammunition, and three explosives to Manipur government on Tuesday at the Home Coming ceremony held at 1st Manipur Rifles parade ground in Imphal. The surrender is seen as a major step towards bringing armed cadres into the mainstream and strengthening the state government’s efforts towards peace and normalcy in Manipur. The cadres were led by their self-styled chairman Haobijam Dilip alias Taibanganba who was arrested in New Delhi on May 28 by a joint team of Delhi police special cell, Manipur police and Central Intelligence agencies. Later, Manipur police arrested him again from Tihar jail on June 1 under the charges of illegal extortion and criminal activities and shifted him under transit remand. Dilip alias Taibanganba was previously arrested on May 20, 2022 in Bishnupur district and was later released on medical bail. Chief minister Yumnam Khemchand said many youths took up arms after the May 3, 2023 ethnic clash between Kuki-Zo and Meitei, causing instability. “I also appeal that the remaining cadres’ arms will not bring peace in Manipur and they should join the mainstream,” Khemchand said while welcoming the surrendered cadres. He appealed to people to refrain from any sort of violent protest including the ongoing 48-hour total shutdown imposed by the Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation (JFD), a civil body demanding to postpone Census process until implementation of National Register of Citizen (NRC). “Bandh, blockade, strike and other form of agitation that affect normal life will only affect daily wage earners and students, all the demands can be negotiated at the table,” he said. Additionally, a government statement said that the returning cadres were encouraged to make constructive use of the opportunity, reintegrate with their families and communities, and contribute positivity to the development of the state. The government and security agencies reaffirmed their commitment in creating an environment conducive to lasting peace, while upholding the rule of law and ensuring the safety and security of all citizens. headline: Fishermen urge Tamil Nadu government to drop plan to build new Secretariat at Pattinapakkam
text: It was a battle cry that was heard on the sands of the Marina Beach in Chennai on Tuesday (September 15, 2026) when representatives of fishermen panchayats issued an ultimatum for the Tamil Nadu government to give up the proposal for building the Secretariat-cum-Assembly complex at Pattinapakkam (Foreshore Estate). “Having chosen the land, the government has issued the G.O. Even if there is a small movement in that direction [towards construction of the complex], we will not remain quiet. We are stakeholders and we were not consulted in any manner. This has left us with no choice but to stage massive Statewide protests against the project,” said K. Bharathi, a community leader. ‘Land belongs to locals’ Around 1,000 men and women gathered on the sands on a patch marked by black flags on the Marina. As all of them signed the register, they were given an opportunity to express themselves on the issue. Many said the community should not have waited so long as to retrieve the land rightfully belonging to the local residents. “A vast portion of the land marked for the Secretariat belongs to the Srinivasapuram/Mullikuppam fishing hamlet. We had been waiting for the government to construct homes for fishermen there. If the government drops the proposal, well and good. We will give some time to Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to return from his U.K. trip so that he can rethink the decision,” said V.R. Vijayan of Maylai Pagudhi Anaithu Meenava Grama Panchayat Sabhai. Another community leader, ‘Kabaddi’ Maran, said the construction of the Secretariat complex would amount to murdering all the 1,500 fishermen families in one go. “Because of security reasons, our lives and livelihood will be reduced to nothing. We won’t be able to step out of our homes or go fishing. While we accept that there is a need for a new Secretariat, this definitely is not the location. The anger among the community, especially the youngsters and women, is palpable. They want immediate action, but we are telling them to be patient as Mr. Vijay has our interests at heart,” he said. headline: Child rights panel orders probe into pregnancy of minor girl at tribal welfare school in Andhra Pradesh
text: The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (APSCPCR) has ordered a thorough inquiry into the pregnancy of a Class IX girl at a Tribal Welfare Residential School in Polavaram district. The girl, who was found to be two months pregnant, is undergoing treatment at a hospital. Following a report published in The Hindu, the APSCPCR directed the officials concerned to ensure the girl’s safety and take action against those responsible. The school principal, hostel warden and a teacher were suspended, while the police registered a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, against the hostel cook and arrested him, said APSCPCR member Vundavalli Gandhi Babu. “A detailed inquiry has been ordered into the sexual abuse of the inmate. The Commission will visit the institute soon,” Mr. Gandhi Babu said on Tuesday. headline: Punjab govt employees go on mass casual leave over unpaid DA arrears
text: Punjab govt employees go on mass casual leave over unpaid DA arrears Essential services unaffected; over 150 unions intensify protests despite a recent 60% DA hike and government warnings of legal action. Chandigarh: The Punjab government’s administrative functioning ground to a near-halt on Tuesday as secretarial, directorate, deputy commissioner, and tehsil office staff took a collective one-day mass casual leave, demanding the immediate release of ₹14,191 crore in pending dearness allowance (DA) and dearness relief (DR) arrears accumulated over several years. Protesting outside the Civil Secretariat in Chandigarh, workers raised slogans against the state government for ignoring their financial grievances. While hospital and transport workers exempted themselves to maintain essential services, this marks the second state-wide shutdown in 10 days. The unrest began on August 27 with an initial mass leave. Subsequent talks broke down when chief minister Bhagwant Mann refused to meet union leaders in Jalandhar unless they called off the strike unconditionally. In response, over 150 unions operating under the Sanjha Mulazim Manch umbrella escalated their agitation. Though a cabinet sub-committee, comprising Harpal Cheema, Aman Arora, and Baljit Kaur, convened talks last week—leading to a state announcement matching the central government’s 60% DA rate—employees insisted on full settlement of arrears in line with an August 3 Punjab and Haryana high court ruling. The high court had ordered the state to clear all ₹14,191 crore in pending dues within 14 days at a 6% simple interest penalty, while quashing the state’s proposed five-year phased payout plan. On Monday night, state industries and commerce minister Aman Arora termed the strike illegal, stating that the DA dispute remains sub judice in the Supreme Court. The state government has appealed against the high court verdict before the apex court, arguing that releasing ₹14,191 crore in a fortnight without legislative sanction from the consolidated fund is constitutionally impossible and would collapse public welfare spending. Arora urged staff not to become political tools or cause public hardship, warning that unlawful disruption would trigger disciplinary action. Union leaders, however, said that peaceful protest is a constitutional right and demanded the withdrawal of show-cause notices issued over the August 27 strike before further talks. They maintained that essential public operations remain unaffected. The Manch now plans to hold a mock Vidhan Sabha session on September 30, followed by coordinated blockades of ministers’ residences in October. - Gurpreet Singh Nibber is an Assistant Editor with the Punjab

headline: Assam Police Seize 50,000 Yaba Tablets Worth Rs 10 Crore From Truck in Cachar
text: Guwahati: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has praised Cachar Police and Assam Police for seizing 50,000 Yaba tablets worth an estimated Rs 10 crore at Digharkhal in Cachar district. The seizure was made at the Old MVI Check Point, where police intercepted a truck and allegedly recovered the tablets from a concealed chamber inside the vehicle. One person has been apprehended in connection with the seizure, and further investigation is underway to trace the source and intended destination of the consignment. Praising the police teams for the operation, Sarma said the successful seizure reflected the continued efforts of the Assam Police to crack down on the illegal drug trade. In a social media post, the Chief Minister wrote, “Humpty Dumpty had a great fall. So did this drug haul,” while appreciating the efforts of Cachar Police and Assam Police. The latest seizure is part of the state’s ongoing crackdown on drug trafficking and the movement of narcotic substances through Assam.

headline: TN CM C Joseph Vijay Apologises After Minister Omits Honorifics For M Karunanidhi | Outlook India
text: - Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay apologised in the Assembly after a cabinet colleague breached protocol. - State Forest Minister RV Ranjith Kumar referred to former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi by name without customary honorifics. - The controversy arose during an Assembly debate regarding funding requests for the Revenue and Health ministries. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay issued an immediate apology in the Assembly on Monday after a cabinet colleague broke protocol. State Forest Minister RV Ranjith Kumar referred to former Chief Minister M Karunanidhi by name, omitting traditional respectful honorifics. Vijay said, "I apologise on his behalf." Debate Triggers Assembly Row The controversy started during an Assembly debate regarding the funding requests for the Revenue and Health ministries. Kumar criticised historical cash-for-votes strategies, specifically citing the controversial "Thirumangalam formula". He said that political actors had previously handed out a maximum of Rs 1,500 for each ballot in his Kancheepuram electoral district, but added that the current administration secured its mandate without handing out cash to voters. While contrasting past electoral practices with the current administration, Kumar referred to the DMK patriarch simply as "Karunanidhi". He omitted customary titles normally used in the House, such as "former Chief Minister". Protocol Breach Sparks Protest The direct reference breached a historical convention within the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. The House traditionally requires formal protocol titles, such as "Kalaignar" (scholar), when addressing revered leaders. Vijay halted Kumar mid-speech before the debate could deteriorate. He acknowledged the reference was inappropriate and apologised to de-escalate the tension.

headline: Rajasthan govt restricts outsider entry, photography in schools soon after CJP announces inspections | Today News
text: The Rajasthan government has restricted the entry of outsiders in government schools without prior permission of the principal and barred photography and videography without written approval, news agency PTI reported on Monday, 17 August. The government order issued on Sunday evening also comes in the backdrop of protests in some government schools across the state over alleged lack of amenities and shortage of teachers. headline: Naga heritage preservation must go beyond physical objects, include traditional knowledge: Nagaland Guv - Mangalorean.com
text: Naga heritage preservation must go beyond physical objects, include traditional knowledge: Nagaland Guv Kohima: Nagaland Governor Nand Kishore Yadav has said that preserving Naga heritage should not be limited to safeguarding physical objects, but must also include preserving the traditional knowledge and cultural practices associated with them. The Governor and Chairman of North Eastern Zonal Cultural Centre (NEZCC) on Friday released two books, –“Nagas: The Knowledge Practitioners”, authored by Alok Kumar Kanungo and Alino Sumi, and ‘Nagaland Textiles – Threads That Weave Stories”, authored by Sentila T. Yanger, at the NEZCC Headquarters in Chumoukedima. Addressing the gathering, Governor Yadav added that the two publications, though dealing with different subjects, brought the rich cultural heritage and knowledge traditions of the Naga people into academic and public focus. He said both publications conveyed the importance of recognising culture as a body of knowledge created, practised, refined and transmitted across generations. Speaking on the book – “Nagas: The Knowledge Practitioners”, the Governor said indigenous knowledge should not be viewed merely as folklore, but as knowledge developed through observation, experience, experimentation and adaptation. The Governor added that traditional knowledge relating to agriculture, crafts, technologies, forests, natural resources, rituals and material culture represented valuable knowledge systems developed within communities. Referring to the publication on Naga textiles, Governor Yadav said that Naga shawls represented more than pieces of cloth and carried identity, memory, social meaning and artistic expression. He noted that colours, patterns, motifs and weaving techniques reflected knowledge and traditions developed within different communities. He also stressed the importance of proper documentation of indigenous knowledge, saying that documentation could provide an accessible record for researchers, students, artisans, museums and future generations and said that such documentation should be undertaken with sensitivity to the communities from whom the knowledge originated, with due recognition of their identity, ownership, dignity and intellectual rights. Speaking on the relevance of indigenous knowledge in the present context, the Governor said that technological advancement should not lead to cultural amnesia. He encouraged the younger generation to embrace modern education and technology while also understanding the traditional knowledge of their communities. Governor Yadav said that traditional knowledge could offer valuable insights into contemporary concerns such as climate change, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture, responsible use of natural resources and sustainable livelihoods. headline: CM Omar Abdullah defends NC MLA's 'Pajama remark', calls it historical fact
text: Srinagar, Sept 10 : Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Thursday defended the National Conference (NC) spokesperson and MLA, Tanvir Sadiq's controversial 'Pajama remark' by calling it a historical fact. Tanvir Sadiq had recently stirred the hornet's nest by saying that it was the NC founder late Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah during whose leadership it became possible for Kashmiris to wear Pajamas. Speaking to reporters on the 44th death anniversary of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah on September 8 here, Tanvir Sadiq said till that time an entire 'Mohalla' (locality) had just one Pajama which they would wear by turns. Speaking to reporters here today, Omar Abdullah said there was no need for Tanvir Sadiq or the NC to apologise for the remark since according to Omar Abdullah the statement was historically accurate. The Chief Minister told reporters that the poverty and hardships faced by Kashmiris in the past were well documented by historians and were not Tanvir's personal opinion. "What Tanvir said is historically accurate. He does not need to apologise or clarify what he said," Omar Abdullah said. He added that Walter Lawrence and several other historians had written about Jammu and Kashmir, particularly about the poverty of Kashmiris and the manner in which people were trapped under the system of landlords. "People did not have money. Tanvir did not talk about this first. Maybe there is a senior National Conference leader, from our President to General Secretary and others, who did not talk about this," the Chief Minister said. "There was a time when Kashmiris were so poor that they had to come to the city with their pajamas from the mosque. This is not Tanvir's own thinking. This is a historical fact," he added. The Chief Minister said Tanvir Sadiq's intention was perhaps to highlight the progress Kashmiris had made from those difficult circumstances, saying people were now educating their children and producing doctors and engineers. He added that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) had a common agenda in raising the issue. "Tanvir does not need to apologise for this. headline: J&K Govt Must Reconsider Power Tariff Hike: Mehbooba Mufti - Daily Excelsior
text: J&K Govt Must Reconsider Power Tariff Hike: Mehbooba Mufti SRINAGAR, Aug 27: PDP president Mehbooba Mufti on Thursday said the Jammu and Kashmir Government must reconsider the electricity tariff hike to give relief to the poor, who are already reeling under rising costs. SRINAGAR, Aug 27: PDP president Mehbooba Mufti on Thursday said the Jammu and Kashmir Government must reconsider the electricity tariff hike to give relief to the poor, who are already reeling under rising costs. headline: Protests Erupt in Jharkhand Over Cancellation of CGL Exams
text: Ranchi, August 19: Protests erupted in Jharkhand as employees affected by the cancellation of 22 recruitment exams by the state government demonstrated outside the Jharkhand Secretariat. The decision, which impacts the appointments of 2,628 selected candidates, was made in response to alleged irregularities in the JPSC and JSSC examinations. Chenna Kumari, a protesting employee, expressed her frustration, stating, “The government’s decision has forced us to take to the streets. Losing a job means more than just losing employment; it affects entire families.” Chandan Kumar questioned the fairness of the decision, saying, “Those who earned their jobs through hard work should not be punished. This reflects the government’s and the system’s failure. We prepare for exams based on government advertisements and recruitment processes, not on the agency’s reputation.” Archana highlighted the confusion surrounding the government’s notification, which mentioned evidence found during investigations by the CID and JPSC. “What are these so-called evidences? Are individual candidates to blame? The court had ordered the removal of those found guilty of irregularities, not the cancellation of the entire CGL exam,” she said. Kashish Kumari added, “We were working in the Secretariat until yesterday, and now we are on the streets. We will seek a stay on the government’s decision from the court. The government should have consulted employees before making such a decision.” Another protester emphasized the legitimacy of their appointments, stating, “Our appointments were based on the High Court’s decision. headline: HC refuses to interfere with Bengal Speaker appointing Ritabrata as LoP
text: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday (August 18, 2026) refused to interfere with the decision of the Speaker of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly, Rathindra Bose, to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of Opposition (LoP). A division bench of Justice Shampa Sarkar and Justice Ajay Kumar Gupta ruled that the single bench of Justice Krishna Rao will have to dispose of the case within two months. Earlier, Justice Rao had refused to grant a stay on the Speaker’s order appointing Mr. Ritabrata as the LoP, following which the petitioners approached the division bench. While the court noted that the best course of action for the Speaker would have been to invite both parties before making the decision, it said that at present no interim relief could be granted to “maintain orderliness of the House”. The court also mentioned that the order of the Speaker was temporary. A petition challenging Mr. Ritabrata’s appointment was filed by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay whom Trinamool Congress chairperson and former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee had nominated as the LoP. On June 18, Justice Rao refused to grant an interim stay on the petition filed by Mr. Chattopadhyay, saying the court did not find any prima facie case and “balance of convenience and inconvenience in favour of the petitioner for grant of interim order” as prayed. The Trinamool had won 80 of the 294 seats in the West Bengal Assembly polls. On May 9, its general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, sent a letter to the Speaker nominating Mr. Chattopadhyay as the LoP. Some MLAs, led by Mr. Ritabrata, said that their signatures in the letter were forged. Mr. Ritabrata and Sandipan Saha were expelled from the party after they formally complained, and, on June 3, Mr. Ritabrata was appointed LoP by the Speaker with the support of 58 MLAs. The LoP now claims the support of over 65 out of 80 MLAs. The appointment of the LoP caused a split in the Trinamool Congress legislature party, with one faction supporting Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee and another backing Mamata Banerjee. headline: Physically challenged seek increased monthly assistance depending upon nature of deformity
text: Seeking an increase in monthly assistance for differently abled persons based on the nature of their disability, they staged a demonstration here on Thursday. The protesters said the Tamil Nadu Government should increase the monthly assistance to ₹6,000, ₹10,000 and ₹15,000 based on the nature of disability, as being given by the Andhra Pradesh government. Since caregivers of persons with severe disabilities faced difficulties in taking care of them, the assistance should be increased proportionately, they said. The protesters also blamed the Union Government for being “indifferent” towards the welfare of differently abled persons. The United Nations Special Declaration and the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, had guaranteed dignified living conditions for the differently abled by ensuring a level playing field in education, employment, social security, healthcare and rehabilitation. The UN Declaration and the Act had mandated the Union Government to create funds exclusively for implementing special schemes for the welfare of the differently abled. However, even 10 years after the enactment of the Act, the Narendra Modi-led Union Government had not allocated sufficient funds for implementing special schemes for them. Consequently, the promises made in the UN Declaration and the Act continued to remain only on paper, they said. Even as the State Government was providing the monthly assistance, the Union Government’s contribution of ₹300, fixed 17 years ago by the then Congress Government, had not been increased under the BJP government that assumed office in 2014. After Mr. Narendra Modi came to power, the Union Government was allocating only 0.0025% of the Union Budget for the welfare of differently abled persons, they alleged. The protesters said the differently abled were running from pillar to post to obtain national identity cards and hence could not avail themselves of several benefits, including 35 kg of free rice or wheat a month. After the BJP government drastically cut the allocation for welfare schemes for the differently abled, they were also not hired under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee programme, they alleged. Hence, the Union Government, especially Mr. Narendra Modi, should implement the promises made in the Act and the UN Declaration, they said. Published - August 27, 2026 07:22 pm IST

headline: "Desperate PM-HM duo terrified of growing despair, anger": Jairam Ramesh accuses Centre of 'crackdown' on Congress against CEC protests
text: ANI 25 Sep 2026, 23:46 GMT+10 New Delhi [India], September 25 (ANI): Senior Congress MP Jairam Ramesh on Friday accused the Centre of unleashing a "brutal crackdown" on protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the government was "terrified" of growing public anger over the functioning of the Election Commission. In a post on X, Jairam Ramesh said, 'Today, citizens and Congress workers took to the streets to demand accountability for the subversion of their constitutional right to vote and the unscrupulous actions of the Chief Election Commissioner.' Ramesh further alleged, 'Facing the countdown to their exit, the desperate PM-HM duo is terrified of the growing despair, anger, and outrage among the public. The opposition parties' protests across several states come amid a political row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise of electoral rolls, following a report by The Indian Express claiming that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections multiple times over 10 months regarding decisions and procedures linked to electoral rolls and database access. The poll body has maintained that all final decisions related to the SIR exercise were unanimous. headline: Naga students’ body marches to assembly against Vande Mataram imposition
text: The Naga Students’ Federation on Tuesday protested and marched to the Nagaland Legislative Assembly, demanding a resolution against the imposition of Vande Mataram at official events. headline: Will withdraw candidate from Nandigram if Mamata decides to contest: Ritabrata Banerjee
text: Amid the dispute over the party symbol, the Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction of the Trinamool Congress on Saturday (September 12, 2026) said it would withdraw its candidate from the upcoming Nandigram Assembly bypoll if Trinamool Congress chairperson Mamata Banerjee decides to contest the election from the seat. The announcement came on the day the Election Commission met representatives of the two factions of the Trinamool Congress—one led by Ms. Banerjee and the other by Leader of Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee. “We want Mamata Banerjee to come to the Assembly. It will be better if she comes from Nandigram,” Mr. Banerjee said. He said his faction had more or less finalised its candidate for the bypoll but would withdraw the nominee if the former Chief Minister chooses to contest, even as an Independent. Of the Trinamool Congress’s 80 MLAs, more than 65 have backed Mr. Banerjee, while Ms Banerjee has the support of only a handful of legislators. Also Read : West Bengal by-elections to test Trinamool rival groups’ claim over party symbol Ms. Banerjee had lost the 2021 Assembly election from Nandigram to Suvendu Adhikari by 1,956 votes. In the 2026 Assembly election, Mr. Adhikari won from both Nandigram and Bhabanipur and subsequently gave up the Nandigram seat, necessitating the bypoll. The by-election is also scheduled in Rejinagar following the decision of Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) leader Humayun Kabir to vacate the seat. Mr. Mabir, who had won from both Naoda and Rejinagar, decided to give up Rejinagar. His son Golam Nabi Azad is the AJUP candidate from Rejinagar. The CPI(M)-led Left Front has nominated Sayeed Asad Aliu from Rejinagar and Shanti Gopal Giri from Nandigram. The Congress has nominated Mohd Abdullahil Kafi from Rejinagar and Milan Pradhan from Nandigram. The bypolls to Nandigram and Rejinagar are scheduled for October 6. The last date for filing nominations is September 16. Both the Trinamool factions are yet to field candidates. headline: Kapil Sibal calls for 10-year ban on politicians switching parties mid-term
text: Former Union Minister Kapil Sibal suggested that anyone who changes their political party during an active term should be disqualified from contesting elections and serving as an elected representative for the next five or ten years. He was delivering a talk on horse-trading and democracy at an event conducted by the Kerala State Committee of the All India Lawyers Union (AILU), on Sunday (September 13, 2026). “I have a confession, I am a Dimagi Naxal” he declared as he began his speech. The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, which deals with anti-defection, provides that a Member of Parliament would not be disqualified for defection if his political party merged with another political party and two-thirds of the party agreed to the merger. The clause, which was designed to protect political realignment, has now become the preferred instrument of wholesale defection, he noted. “Those in power will not hurry to close a loophole that benefits them. If one accepts that two-thirds of a legislative party may rewrite an election, it will subordinate the significance of the people’s will to post-poll arithmetic,” Mr. Sibal said. He proposed that the Tenth Schedule should be reworked so that a merger would simply mean a merger of political parties and not a mass walkout by legislators. “Any inducement, be it cash, office, contracts or the quashing of an enquiry, must be treated as corruption and not as the ordinary give-and-take of politics,” he pointed out. “The harm caused by the reality of political defection is not technical; it is foundational,” Mr. Sibal said. “The people’s mandate after an election ends up falsified, as the electoral verdict can change when legislators switch sides. When the citizens’ mandate is treated as a transferable asset, the promise of a democracy ends up dishonoured. Legislators changing political parties mid-term weakens their accountability, both to the citizens and within parties. Public faith declines in investigative agencies, Governors, Speakers of Legislative Assemblies and Courts when they are drawn into the making of majorities, while processing defection petitions. When regional parties, representing distinct political communities, are absorbed through defection, the different voices of the public are not just defeated; they are taken over,” Mr. Sibal stated. headline: Low-level operatives convicted, NIA court verdict does not deliver justice to victims families: Chhattisgarh Congress chief
text: | | | Low-level operatives convicted, NIA court verdict does not deliver justice to victims families: Chhattisgarh Congress chief Raipur (Chhattisgarh) \| September 6, 2026 10:59:22 AM IST Chhattisgarh Congress President Deepak Baij has said the verdict delivered by the NIA court in the Jhiram incident case has failed to deliver justice to the victims' families, the people of Bastar and Chhattisgarh, and the Congress party. | | Chhattisgarh Congress President Deepak Baij has said the verdict delivered by the NIA court in the Jhiram incident case has failed to deliver justice to the victims' families, the people of Bastar and Chhattisgarh, and the Congress party. He said the ten individuals convicted or accused are not key Naxal leaders but were merely low-level operativesinformers. The NIA itself had acknowledged the involvement of over 200 Naxals and registered FIRs against 40 individuals, including prominent leaders. While some leaders were killed, many others have surrendered and are currently under government protection; were they ever interrogated? This was not merely an incident; it was a conspiracya contract killing orchestrated to seize power," Baij told ANI. The case pertains to the deadly ambush on a Congress convoy on May 25, 2013, in Jhiram Valley in Bastar. The attack, carried out by armed Maoists, killed at least 29 people, including several senior Congress leaders and security personnel. The leaders were returning from a 'Parivartan Yatra' ahead of the 2013 Assembly elections. Special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Jagdalpur has convicted 10 surviving accused in the case. The court found all 10 accused guilty under various sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Arms Act. The court has reserved the announcement of the quantum of punishment for September 16. Congress leaders have alleged that the probe failed to uncover a larger political conspiracy and ignored security lapses. headline: KPSC chairman suspended for second time by Governor
text: After the Karnataka Cabinet decided to recommend the suspension of Karnataka Public Service Commission Chairman Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar, who is embroiled in controversy in recruitments, Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot on Tuesday suspended the Chairman again. This is the second time that the Governor has suspended the KPSC Chairman. The order cites provisions of Article 317 (2) of the Constitution, and the High Court of Karnataka’s order of August 18. The Governor has directed the senior-most member of the KPSC to act as the Chairman until further orders. Currently, B. Prabhudev is the senior-most member of the KPSC. Before Cabinet Earlier, on July 10, Mr. Sahukar was suspended by the Governor over submission of false income certificate by one of his two daughters, who claimed the annual income to be ₹40,000, while applying for the post of Industrial Extension Officer. However, the Cabinet’s approval for suspension had come later. Mr. Sahukar had challenged the Governor’s order that was taken without the aid and advice of the Cabinet in the High Court, which quashed the Governor’s order and directed Mr. Sahukar’s reinstatement. Meanwhile, the Karnataka Cabinet on Friday cleared the suspension, and recommended to the Governor to suspend the Chairman. Amid ED raids The order also comes at a time when the Enforcement Directorate has taken up the investigation of bribe and corruption in the recruitment of Veterinary Officers and has already searched over 20 premises, including the KPSC, residence of Mr. Sahukar and IAS officer and former Controller of Examination in KPSC Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, several middlemen among many others. headline: CM Mohan Yadav orders judicial probe into Sagar liquor deaths; transfers top officials
text: Bhopal/Sagar, Sep 9 : Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Wednesday ordered a judicial inquiry into the deaths allegedly caused by illegal liquor in Sagar district. In a late-night action, the Chief Minister also announced administrative changes, including the appointment of a new divisional commissioner and Inspector General, and directed that strict action be taken against those responsible for the incident in the Banda-Shahgarh area. Senior IAS officer Dilip Kumar has been appointed as the new Sagar divisional commissioner, while senior IPS officer Irshad Wali has been appointed Inspector General of Sagar division, according to the state government. Yadav directed officials to ensure accountability for any negligence or irregularities and said no person found guilty should be spared. The action came after the Chief Minister visited Bundelkhand Medical College in Sagar, where he met patients undergoing treatment and interacted with their family members. He personally enquired about the condition of those admitted to the hospital and assured their relatives that the government stood with them. During a meeting with police and administrative officials and public representatives at the medical college, Yadav directed authorities to maintain strict law and order and launch an intensive investigation into illegal liquor activities in Sagar and adjoining and border areas. "Ensure strict action against those responsible. No guilty person should be spared," he said. The Chief Minister directed officials to seize illegal liquor and related material and conduct prompt investigations wherever there was suspicion or any possibility of illegal activities. He said the government was following a zero-tolerance policy towards crime and anti-social activities, while stressing that action should be impartial and transparent and no innocent person should be targeted. "I have given the administration a free hand to take the strictest possible action against those involved, including those carrying out illegal encroachments or running such illegal empires," he said in a statement issued late on Wednesday. Yadav also directed officials to keep a close watch on people spreading rumours through social media and other platforms with an intention to disturb peace and communal harmony, and take strict action against them. On the wider issue of substance abuse, the Chief Minister also called for an intensive de-addiction campaign with the participation of religious institutions, social organisations and voluntary groups. "We will need collective social commitment to deal with this problem," he said.

headline: After Jharkhand protesters burn Soren, Rahul effigies, State Government calls for fourth round of talks

headline: Manipur shuts all educational institutions from Aug 20 to 23 amid unrest
text: Manipur shuts all educational institutions from Aug 20 to 23 amid unrest Manipur has ordered all schools, colleges and universities shut from August 20 to 23, citing the prevailing law and order situation amid a JFD shutdown. The Manipur government on Wednesday ordered the closure of all educational institutions across the state from August 20 to 23 in view of the prevailing law and order situation, according to an official order. The government order was issued by the commissioner-cum-secretary to the Government of Manipur, in which commissioner of education (school) Ningthoujam Geoffrey said that the closure would cover all schools affiliated with the Board of Secondary Education Manipur, Council of Higher Secondary Education Manipur, Central Board of Secondary Education or otherwise. The order, which said the decision was taken “in view of the prevailing law and order situation in the State,” also applies to colleges, higher education institutes and universities under government, aided and unaided sectors. Deep Dive The order further said that all deputy commissioners, zonal education officers and directors concerned had been asked to circulate the order to schools and institutions under their jurisdiction. Meanwhile, normal life remained paralysed across several valley districts in Manipur on Wednesday as the 48-hour shutdown called by the Campaign for Just and Fair Delimitation (JFD), a Meitei group, continued over its demand that the Census be conducted only after an NRC is done. Meitei groups have been pressing for an NRC to identify undocumented migrants who settled in Manipur after 1951 from neighbouring countries and pose a threat to the state’s original inhabitants. Kuki organisations have accused Meiteis of trying to label them all as undocumented immigrants. In neighbouring Assam, an NRC was updated in 2019 to identify undocumented immigrants who came to the state after 1971. As part of the agitation, the students’ wing of JFD has held a series of agitations over the last few days, including shutting down the Directorate of Census Operations office located in Imphal East and disrupting training centres for enumerators and supervisors involved in the Census process. Meanwhile, in a separate government order issued on Wednesday, charge officer/Sub-Divisional Officer, Lilong, Imphal West, Moirangthem Priyaroshni Devi said that “all the appointees of supervisors, enumerators and field trainer regarding Census Training Programme stand cancelled.”

headline: "Jharkhand will set example for tackling exam irregularities": State Minister Dipika Pandey assures aspirants of reforms
text: ANI 18 Aug 2026, 01:27 GMT+10 Ranchi (Jharkhand) [India], August 18 (ANI): As the Jharkhand government agreed to aspirants' demands and cancelled the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission - Combined Graduate Level (JSSC-CGL) examination, State Minister Dipika Pandey on Monday assured students of reforms to strengthen the examination system and ensure strict action against those involved in paper leaks. Earlier on Monday, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren announced that the state government had decided to cancel all activities associated with TSR Data Processing Private Limited (TDPL), including the examinations conducted, the results published and the candidates selected, and the state Cabinet also decided to cancel the JSSC-CGL examinations. Following the announcement, student leaders Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti ended their hunger strike in the presence of Jharkhand Ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari at the Sadar Hospital. Dipika Pandey said the government would consult students and incorporate their suggestions while bringing reforms, adding that Jharkhand would set an example for the entire country in tackling examination irregularities. She also assured the protesters that shortcomings in the existing system would be addressed and that agencies investigating the matter would ensure that those responsible for paper leaks are not spared. 'Since the first day, I have been telling you that Jharkhand will set an example; we have a model of legislation to ensure strict punishment for the culprits of paper leaks. I can confidently tell you that the reforms we will bring after consultation and taking suggestions from students will be a model for the entire nation... I would like to appeal to the students that through your efforts, a major issue which is not only Jharkhand-specific but is troubling students across the country today, with your efforts, we have led this movement towards a positive conclusion. We assure you that we will rectify the flaws in our system based on your suggestions, and the agencies involved will ensure that the culprits are not spared, and Jharkhand will become an example', she said. Meanwhile, Jharkhand Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu said a committee constituted to examine the students' concerns had discussed their issues and reached consensus on most matters. headline: 'BJP can't scare me with ED, CBI': B Nagendra slams 'manuwadis' after stepping down as Karnataka minister
text: 'BJP can't scare me with ED, CBI': B Nagendra slams 'manuwadis' after stepping down as Karnataka minister The Congress leader announced his resignation as the minister for planning and statistics in Karnataka as well as from his MLA seat. Congress leader B Nagendra, after stepping down as Karnataka minister less than a month after his induction, slammed who he referred to as “Manuwadis”, and criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party. Nagendra on Friday said the BJP could not “scare him” with ED and CBI, while claiming that he had been “targeted” by “Manuwadis” because they did not want a tribal man to grow, PTI news agency reported. The Congress leader announced his resignation as the minister for planning and statistics in Karnataka as well as from his MLA seat after allegations of his involvement in financial irregularities at the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribe Development Corporation. Nagendra, in tears while relaying his decision, said he was stepping down of his own will to avoid “embarrassment” to his party. “I am resigning of my own will to avoid the embarrassment that may cost my party because of unnecessary allegations made by the opposition party against me,” he said, while alleging that he was a “victim” of BJP's “Manuwadi” politics. His resignation came amid political pressure on him and the Congress party over the alleged Valmiki Corporation scam. The BJP has been demanding his resignation since his induction into chief minister DK Shivakumar's cabinet on August 3. BJP's resignation demand, Cong's backing of Nagendra Despite the BJP's repeated demands seeking Nagendra's resignation, the Congress and CM DK Shivakumar had backed him publicly. The BJP and its ally JD(S) had earlier this week mobilised large number of workers and taken out a protest march to the Vidhana Soudha, seeking Nagendra's removal as minister. Several protesters were detained, with BJP leaders B Y Vijayendra, R Ashoka and others taken into preventive custody. The BJP and JD(S) had also stalled proceedings in both Houses of the Karnataka legislature, calling for Nagendra's dismissal. However, the Congress in Karnataka took a firm stand to back Nagendra, stating that no court of law had convicted him. “Let the opposition parties give a notice to discuss the issue in the House. headline: Congress social media chief faces BJP heat over 'false' claims on flag hoisting during I-Day celebrations
text: Congress social media chairperson and Working Committee member Supriya Shrinate is in the eye of storm over circulation of two old videos pertaining to 80th Independence Day celebrations while alleging that the BJP leaders hoisted party flags instead of the Tricolour on the occassion. The BJP quickly fact-checked the claims, stating that neither of the videos were related to Independence Day events. Shrinate had claimed that one of the videos was from Chhattisgarh, while the other was from West Bengal. In the first instance, she shared a video purportedly showing BJP workers raising the party flag instead of the national flag at Swami Vivekanand Mangal Bhavan in Kurud, located in Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh. "For 53 years, their ancestors boycotted the Tricolour -- even today, they never tire of insulting the national flag," the Congress leader wrote in a post on X while sharing the video. Following the post, the BJP filed an FIR against Shrinate over the allegation and accused her of using an old video and presenting it as footage from the Independence Day celebrations. Former Chhattisgarh Minister and senior BJP leader Ajay Chandrakar strongly criticised Shrinate and said, "The Independence Day program is of national importance. It is celebrated in governmental and personal capacities both in the country and abroad. The Congress Party has used the national festival as a medium to defame the BJP." "The BJP organisation of Dhamtari district has, by filing an FIR, demanded action against Mallikarjun Kharge, Jairam Ramesh, Supriya Shrinate, and Pawan Khera as well. Immediate action should be taken on this," he added. Chandrakar himself hoisted the national flag at the official district-level Independence Day ceremony in Dhamtari. headline: Vice-chairperson poll puts ruling alliance in Kerala’s Pala to test
text: Two weeks after an alliance of Congress rebel councillors and the LDF came to power in Pala municipality, the civic body is bracing for another political test with the election of the vice-chairperson scheduled for September 16. While the election of Congress rebel Maya Rahul as chairperson passed off smoothly, the vice-chairperson election is expected to be more contentious, with differences within the ruling combine over the post remaining unresolved. Adding to the uncertainty, Congress rebels Biju Mathews and Tony Thaiparambil have staked claims to the post. In the 26-member council, the LDF-Congress rebel alliance enjoys a clear majority, with 12 LDF councillors and four Congress rebels. The Kerala Congress (M)-led LDF had earlier made it clear that it would not seek any position in the civic body, leaving the vice-chairperson post to the Congress rebels. However, the rebels have yet to reach a consensus on their candidate. Mr. Mathews argues that he deserves the post as he has not been given any position in the council, while other rebels, including Mr. Thaiparambil and Rejitha Prakash, already head various standing committees. Mr. Thaiparambil, however, has not made it clear whether he will press his claim. He said political stability of the council should be given paramount importance and that the chairperson needs strong support from the vice-chairperson. In the emerging political scenario, the stance of chairperson Ms. Rahul will be crucial. The LDF has 12 members, and her support would ensure a majority in the election. However, she too has refrained from disclosing her preference. “The ruling combine will convene a meeting to discuss the matter and take a decision before the vice-chairperson election. If the dispute persists, Ms. Prakash, another Congress rebel, may emerge as a consensus candidate, particularly as the Kerala Congress (M) is keen to avoid direct participation in the municipal administration,” a source said. Meanwhile, a Kerala Congress (M) source said the possibility of the party fielding a candidate for the post was unlikely at present, though the situation could change depending on future developments. headline: West Bengal government orders closure of 252 madrassas, sends show-cause notice to 100
text: West Bengal government orders closure of 252 madrassas, sends show-cause notice to 100 Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education Department Minister Kshudiram Tudu said madrassas that have requisite approvals will continue to function. The West Bengal government has ordered the closure of 252 madrassas and sent show-cause notices to around 100 others after a state-wide survey that found that several such institutions lacked requisite approvals and basic infrastructure, officials said on Sunday. Minority Affairs and Madrasah Education Department Minister Kshudiram Tudu said madrassas that have requisite approvals will continue to function. Also Read | West Bengal Govt to stop financial assistance to students to buy mobile phones The field-level survey was carried out by the department across all districts of West Bengal since early June to assess the infrastructure, approval status and management systems of government and private madrassas. Officials said the seminaries have been served a show-cause notice. Further action will be taken after examining their responses, they said. The exercise was initiated following directions from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari to ascertain the number of authorised and unauthorised madrassas in different districts, Tudu said. Also Read | Bars, liquor shops to remain shut, no DJ on Maha Ashtami in Bengal: CM Suvendu "As many as 252 madrassas have been ordered to close while 100 others have been sent show-cause notices for lacking requisite approvals and basic infrastructure," the minister added. State Panchayati Raj Minister Dilip Ghosh said there had been several controversies surrounding madrassas and claimed that in several cases people arrested for their alleged involvement in extremist activities were found to have been working as teachers in some such institutions. Also Read | West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari sets Vande Mataram mandate to ‘stay in state’ "Complaints against madrassas had repeatedly been received. There have been instances of people carrying out anti-national activities from seminaries," he said. "Madrassas being run in accordance with the law and with government permission will continue to function. But the government will not allow madrassas to be opened indiscriminately and cause trouble." The opposition Trinamool Congress's MLA Kunal Ghosh said all madrassas should not be painted with the same brush.

headline: U.P. Congress president urges PM Modi to review ethanol-blended fuel policy; questions rising sugar prices
text: Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai on Tuesday (August 24, 2026) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking an urgent review of the ethanol-blended fuel policy and steps to address “rising” sugar prices, arguing that the two issues are linked and need to be assessed from the perspective of consumers. Mr. Rai raised concerns about whether the anticipated savings in foreign exchange from decreased petroleum imports could be fully achieved if domestic sugar shortages necessitated imports of the commodity, which would also require foreign exchange expenditure. “The actual account of ethanol, sugar production, domestic prices, and imports should be clarified to the public,” added Mr. Rai, a former Minister, in his letter. In his letter, Mr. Rai reminded the Prime Minister that he had previously written to the latter on July 7, addressing “scientific, economic, environmental, and consumer interest-related inquiries” regarding ethanol-blended fuels. Mr. Rai pointed out that the government’s main argument supporting the ethanol policy from the Oil Ministry was that it would lessen reliance on petroleum imports and enhance the nation’s energy security. Mr. Rai added that Union Food Minister Shri Prahlad Joshi has also shown no responsibility for the steep rise in sugar and other food prices. “Unfortunately, he will now also oversee the Education Ministry,” Mr. Rai said. He said the government should undertake a comprehensive review of the ethanol policy, particularly in view of concerns among owners of older vehicles over E20 fuel. Mr. Rai referred to recent comments by Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran suggesting that lower-blend fuel such as E10 could again be made available alongside E20 to address concerns of owners of older vehicles. “When the government’s own senior economic adviser is talking about the need to provide consumers with an option, there should also be a comprehensive review of this policy,” Mr. Rai said. He also questioned the role of Union Ministers Nitin Gadkari and Hardeep Singh Puri in the policy and reiterated his earlier demand for their removal from the Union Cabinet, alleging that they had failed to protect consumer interests. “Carry out a Cabinet reshuffle if you wish, but in the interest of the people and a vigilant democracy, also answer questions concerning public interest,” Mr. Rai said. headline: West Bengal imposes 72-hour private practice restriction on doctors
text: The West Bengal Health Department decided to bar teacher-doctors serving under the West Bengal Medical Education Service from undertaking private practice on the day a patient is admitted to a government hospital and for the following 48 hours, a senior official said on Monday. The restriction, effectively covering a 72-hour period, came into force immediately, he said, adding that the order was aimed at ensuring that faculty members remained available for patients admitted under their care. “The restriction will apply from the day of admission and for the next 48 hours. The intention is to ensure continuity of care and the availability of the treating faculty for admitted patients,” the official said. The order is expected to directly affect private practice by faculty members of government medical colleges. Government doctors generally have a designated admission day each week. Under the new directive, they will not be able to undertake private practice on that day and the following two days, leaving them with fewer days in the week for such practice. In some cases, where faculty members have two admission days a week, the restriction could cover most of the working week. Some doctors have expressed concern that the sudden restriction could affect patients who are already undergoing treatment at private hospitals under government doctors. However, some patients have welcomed the move, saying ensuring the availability of doctors after admission to government hospitals could improve continuity and quality of care. headline: ‘13.5L families dropped from BPL list in 6 months’, Selja demands explanation
text: Chandigarh: Congress Working Committee (CWC) member and Sirsa MP Kumari Selja on Saturday questioned the removal of 13.5 lakh families from Haryana ’s BPL list within six months, alleging that the BJP govt had identified a large number of poor families before the assembly elections but was now questioning their eligibility. Selja said the number of BPL families had risen to around 52.50 lakh before the elections, but fell to 39.89 lakh within six months. She sought an explanation for what economic or social transformation had taken place during this period to make 13.5 lakh families suddenly ineligible for welfare benefits. The senior Congress functionary questioned whether the families’ incomes had increased substantially or whether BPL cards had been issued before the elections without adequate verification. Selja said a BPL card was crucial for accessing ration, healthcare, education and other welfare schemes and warned that genuine beneficiaries should not be deprived without transparent verification. She demanded the release of district-wise details of the 13.5 lakh families removed from the list and the disclosure of the criteria and reasons for their exclusion. She also called for gram sabhas, local bodies and affected families to be involved in the verification process, along with a simple, time-bound appeal mechanism. Selja also accused the BJP of attempting to divert attention from governance failures by raising religious and caste issues. She said Haryana’s real concerns included corruption, unemployment, youth migration, rising crime and growing insecurity about the future. “Govt should answer these questions instead of provoking religious and caste sentiments,” she said, adding that people were increasingly recognising such attempts to divert attention from governance issues.

headline: Farmers block Chandigarh entry point, launch weeklong protest over MSP demands - OrissaPOST
text: Chandigarh: Hundreds of farmers from Punjab blocked one of the prominent entry points of Chandigarh, the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana, Tuesday for their weeklong protest over demands, comprising guaranteed minimum support prices (MSP) for all crops as per the Dr Swaminathan Commission report. Heavy security has been deployed both by Chandigarh and Punjab to prevent any untoward incident. The farmers under the banner of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM) parked their tractor-trailers on one side of the busy road leading to Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport and pitched tents for their sit-in protest that will last till September 7. The gathering is expected to increase by the evening as hundreds of farmers are being ferried along with ration to the protest site. The SKM has been allotted a protest site in Sector 48 by the Chandigarh Administration, where a huge stage was erected to address protesters. People travelling between Mohali and Chandigarh, especially those heading to the airport, could face a harrowing time with the start of the seven-day agitation, despite protesters being allowed to park their vehicles on one side of the two-lane highway. Mohali Deputy Commissioner Komal Mittal said they would try to keep one side of the two-way traffic on the carriageway open. The SKM comprises 32 farmer organisations, comprising the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) Rajewal, the Kirti Kisan Union, and the Punjab Kisan Union. However, the BKU Ugrahan, an associate member of the SKM, is not part of this protest. The SKM has been demanding, among other demands, scrapping all previous agreements concerning Punjab’s river waters by convening a special session of the Assembly, the restoration of the state’s representation in the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), repeal of the Dam Safety Act, and the withdrawal of the Disaster Management Act of 2024. In Punjab, the BKU (Ugrahan) launched indefinite dharnas August 30 outside the deputy commissioners’ offices in 17 districts against anti-farmer decisions and policies by the state and Central governments. The BKU (Ugrahan) has been demanding cancellation of the India-US trade deal, and scrapping of Punjab’s land pooling policy, ownership rights to tenant farmers, and a complete waiver of agricultural loans for farmers and labourers.

headline: ‘We are Gen Z’ has become new ‘Do you know who my father is’: Omar Abdullah
text: A new video has surfaced online showing a young woman confronting Ladakh police at a checkpoint after a road was briefly closed by security personnel. “We are Gen Z, and we are not going to tolerate this,” the woman can be heard saying in the video. The incident reportedly took place on July 25 near Minimarg, a location known as a gateway between Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The woman, who is believed to be a tourist, claimed that people had been forced to wait for nearly five hours. “We pay from our pockets to visit, and they are doing this to us. Earlier, they used to do this to Kashmiris only; now they are doing it with tourists as well,” she said. The woman, whose identity has not been established, later staged a dharna at the checkpoint and reportedly prevented even an Army convoy from proceeding towards a transit camp. According to police, the road had been temporarily closed as Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi were travelling through the area. The restrictions led to delays for tourists and other travellers. The woman's remarks and conduct towards security personnel have triggered a debate on social media, with several former Army officers criticising her behaviour towards men in uniform. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah also weighed in, cautioning against using the “Gen Z” identity as a threat. “This ‘we are Gen Z’ has become the new ‘jaantay nahin ho mera baap kaun hai’. The quickest way to erode any Gen Z goodwill is to start using it as a threat at the slightest perceived affront,” Abdullah posted on X while sharing the video from his personal account.

headline: Mamata Banerjee niece Bristy Mukherjee death reason: What happened in Birbhum and what we know so far

headline: President Murmu returns Bengal anti-Goonda Bill, flags overlap with central narcotics law- Moneycontrol.com
text: President Droupadi Murmu has returned the West Bengal government’s proposed anti-goonda bill for reconsideration after objecting to a provision which may overlap with a central anti-narcotics law, an official told PTI on Friday. The West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-Social Activities Bill, 2026, or the anti-goonda bill, was passed in the assembly in June, substantially expanding the state’s powers to tackle organised crime, extortion, illegal mining, cybercrime and public disorder. The bill was sent to the President for assent, and she returned it for reconsideration over a provision related to the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, the official said. The provision in question is Section 2(d)(iii)(B), which brings within the definition of a “goonda” a person involved in committing, attempting, abetting, promoting, financing or facilitating an offence punishable under the NDPS Act, the note issued by the central government before returning the bill mentioned. The note also pointed out that the provision could cover ground already dealt with under the PITNDPS Act, 1988, a central law specifically providing for preventive detention of people involved in the illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. Section (B) of the bill may overlap with the preventive-detention framework provided under the PITNDPS Act, 1988, the note said. It further observed that having both provisions could result in two parallel preventive-detention mechanisms operating in relation to drug-related activities. The note also raised the question of possible repugnancy under Article 254 of the Constitution, which deals with the doctrine of repugnancy, resolving inconsistencies between laws made by Parliament and state legislatures on subjects in the Concurrent List. To prevent duplication and an overlap between the proposed legislation and the Central law, the note recommends removing the reference to offences under the NDPS Act, 1985, from Section 2(d)(iii)(B). A top state government bureaucrat told PTI that the note would be reviewed properly. "At the moment we cannot talk much about the development. We will go through the note before deciding the next step," he said. "But, as there is still a provision to again table the bill in the Assembly, we are hopeful that it could be sent to the President after amendment."
