text: Assam Cong opposes Kaziranga ESZ cut, alleges move to aid corporate mining The Assam Congress on Monday staged a protest near Kaziranga National Park against the state government's proposal to reduce the Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) around the World Heritage Site, alleging that the move was aimed at facilitating corporate mining. Scores of Congress workers, led by state party president and Deputy Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi, gathered at Kohora Range and raised slogans demanding protection of Kaziranga and withdrawal of the proposal. Addressing the protesters, Gogoi alleged that the move to shrink the ESZ was part of a "deep-rooted conspiracy" to benefit corporate groups, including the Adani and Ambani groups, and facilitate large-scale commercial mining in the neighbouring Karbi Anglong hills. He accused BJP leaders, ministers and MLAs of encroaching upon elephant corridors to build resorts and of forcibly dispossessing Adivasi families of land to construct hotels in Engle Pathar. Gogoi further said, "Rampant illegal coal, stone and sand mining patronised by the ruling dispensation has triggered catastrophic floods across Upper Assam, destroying over 4,000 houses and claiming more than 100 lives." He said unabated deforestation and hill mining have also forced tigers and elephants into human settlements, escalating man-animal conflict. Targeting Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Gogoi alleged that instead of cracking down on the 'mining mafia', the government was granting them legal protection. He demanded the immediate release of activist Pranab Doley, arrested under the NSA for opposing the government's "anti-people and ecology-destroying policies" of forcibly acquiring land to construct a five-star hotel near the Kaziranga National Park. Commercial activities in the Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) or the buffer zone of a forest is either prohibited, regulated or allowed as per the set norms. The controversy over Kaziranga National Park's ESZ stems from the Assam government's proposal to reduce the buffer area around the World Heritage Site from the default 10 km to 1 km. The opposition and activists allege that the cut is aimed at facilitating corporate mining and tourism in the forest area along with Karbi Anglong hills, which is also an elephant corridor. Environmentalists have also warned that a smaller buffer zone will increase man-animal conflict and threaten the fragile biodiversity. On the other hand, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has strongly defended the move to cut the buffer zone and said the reduction is to protect villagers living inside the ESZ

headline: Delhi govt achieves target of 100 Atal Canteens in 8 months
text: New Delhi, Aug 16 : The Delhi government's 'Atal Canteen' scheme achieved a major milestone on Sunday with the inauguration of the 100th facility, coinciding with the death anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, an official said. Former Vice-President M. Venkaiah Naidu inaugurated 25 new Atal Canteens on Sunday from the Vishwavidyalaya Metro Station in the presence of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Manoj Tiwari, Delhi Minister Ashish Sood, and other dignitaries, an official statement said. The scheme was launched on December 25, 2025, on the occasion of Vajpayee's 100th birth anniversary. Speaking on the occasion, former Vice-President Naidu said that launching 100 Atal Canteens in Delhi is a highly commendable initiative. "Its goal is to provide affordable and nutritious food to the poor, slum dwellers, labourers, and people arriving in Delhi from various parts of the country in search of employment," he added. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that achieving the target of 100 Atal Canteens is a major milestone for the Delhi government. headline: West Bengal government bans liquor sales on Maha Ashtami, DJ music during Durga Puja
text: NEW DELHI: West Bengal has announced a series of restrictions for this year’s Durga Puja, including a one-day ban on liquor sales, a complete prohibition on DJ music and curbs on the use of major roads for Puja-related activities. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari made the announcements on Monday at a coordination meeting with Durga Puja committees at Milan Mela Prangan. The measures are aimed at ensuring that celebrations remain peaceful and orderly. All liquor shops and bars across the state will remain closed on Maha Ashtami, when devotees offer anjali to Goddess Durga. "On the day when devotees offer anjali (Maha Ashtami) to Maa Durga, all liquor shops in the state will remain closed. There will be no liquor available in bars either," he said. The decision comes despite liquor traditionally seeing strong demand during the Puja period. DJ music banned, themes to face scrutiny The government will also prohibit DJ music during the celebrations and immersion processions. Adhikari asked Puja committees to ensure that their idols, pandals and themes do not offend religious sentiments or go against Sanatan traditions. Theme-based Pujas will still be allowed, but organisers have been asked to be more careful while choosing their concepts. The administration has also placed restrictions on roads being used for Puja activities. National highways cannot be blocked for organising Pujas, while 13 major roads in Kolkata, including Red Road and Cathedral Road, have been identified as areas where such activities will not be allowed. Puja inaugurations will also not be permitted before the start of Devi Paksha. Devi Paksha refers to the bright lunar fortnight in the Hindu month of Ashwin associated with the worship and invocation of Goddess Durga. The previous Trinamool Congress government under Mamata Banerjee had faced allegations over inaugurations being held before Devi Paksha began. Immersion deadline and special arrangements Adhikari said organisers would have to complete idol immersions within the stipulated period before Lakshmi Puja. "There will be no forcing or threatening anyone to change the immersion date," he said. The state has also planned cultural programmes in six major cities over two days, along with special events at six designated immersion ghats. text: Villagers push out CJP activists during Rajasthan school inspection Villagers in Jaipur's Bagru assembly constituency resisted a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) team's visit to a government primary school on Friday, allegedly pushing the activists out of the area as part of a confrontation over the group's "School Thik Karo" campaign, according to the sources. The incident occurred at Rampura Kanwarpura village in Jaipur district, where CJP workers had gone to inspect the school and speak with students and teachers. Bagru Deputy Superintendent of Police Dharmendra Sharma said he was unaware of any such development. Villagers reportedly barricaded the main approach road before the CJP team arrived and checked vehicles entering the area. A confrontation broke out shortly after, and the activists were pushed out of the village, sources said. The villagers later staged a sit-in outside the school, raising slogans against the CJP. The school building has been declared unsafe and closed for students with classes currently held in a nearby cattle enclosure. Villagers, joined by BJP workers, said the building could be repaired locally and claimed the government had already sanctioned funds for the work. The CJP team had planned to visit two government schools in Jaipur district on Friday to assess infrastructure and facilities. The visit came days after the Rajasthan government restricted entry of the public and media into government schools, following earlier CJP inspections. CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka criticised the restriction, accusing the state education minister of trying to conceal the poor condition of government schools. "The education minister is adopting an authoritarian approach to hide the poor state of education in Rajasthan. We will not be intimidated by the government's order. Our mission will continue until the condition of all government schools in Rajasthan improves," he said. As part of the campaign, the CJP plans to assess academic arrangements, student facilities, building conditions and other infrastructure in government schools across Rajasthan's rural belts, besides interacting with teachers and students. (Source: PTI)

headline: SC suspends life sentence of former NSCN-IM cadre in Manipur triple murder case
text: ANI 07 Sep 2026, 19:28 GMT+10 New Delhi [India], September 7 (ANI): The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the life sentence of former self-styled lieutenant colonel of NSCN-IM, Hopeson Ningshen, convicted for the 2009 abduction and murder of three government officials in Manipur, citing his incarceration of more than 17 years. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale granted conditional suspension of his sentence and directed that Ningshen remain within Delhi and not leave the national capital till the disposal of his appeal. The Manipur government opposed the plea, citing the sensitivity of the case, while the Centre said that if the court decided to suspend the sentence, adequate safeguards could be imposed. The bench noted that it had considered the sensitivity of the matter on several occasions but was now dealing with a case where the appellant had remained incarcerated for over 17 years and his appeal was still pending. Ningshen was convicted for the abduction and murder of Kasom Khullen SDO Thingnam Kishan Singh and his two subordinate officials, Yumnam Token and Aribam Rajen. The cases were transferred from Manipur to Delhi in 2010 by the Supreme Court amid concerns by the CBI over communal tensions and the possibility of a physical attack on Ningshen. A Special CBI Court convicted Ningshen in 2014 and sentenced him to life imprisonment. The Delhi High Court upheld his conviction and sentence in November 2019. His appeal against the High Court verdict is pending before the Supreme Court. text: "What happened between the 2 sides?": Congress' Salman Khurshid demands transparency on India-China bilateral talks after Jairam Ramesh poses 4 questions to PM Modi New Delhi [India], September 13 (ANI): Former External Affairs Minister and senior Congress leader Salman Khurshid on Sunday demanded transparency from the Union government regarding discussions between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping during the BRICS Summit, urging the Centre to brief the opposition on the outcome of the high-level engagement. headline: Husbands to face POCSO charges if wife becomes mother before 18: Bengal CM
text: Kolkata, Sep 7 : In a major crackdown on child marriage and teenage pregnancies, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has announced that husbands of girls who become mothers before attaining the age of 18 will be prosecuted under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, with the state government initiating suo motu cases against offenders. Speaking to the media persons here on Monday, the Chief Minister said, "Now West Bengal is notorious in terms of child marriage and childbirth before the age of 18. The previous Trinamool Congress government is responsible for this. So, henceforth, strong legal action will be taken under the POCSO Act against the husbands of girls who conceive before the age of 18. The government will file suo motu cases in such matters. The culprit can be imprisoned for a maximum of 20 years. They will also be deprived of all government opportunities and social welfare allowances." He also said that the priests or Kazis performing rituals of marriage between underage brides and grooms will also not be spared. The administration will also take action against the guardians concerned. "From January 1, 2016, to June 30 this year, about 60,000 girls under the age of 18 became mothers. Murshidabad tops the list. During that period, 12,847 girls from the district became mothers before attaining the age of 18. Next on the list is South 24 Parganas, where 4,178 girls under the age of 18 became mothers," the Chief Minister added. He informed that the State Health Department provided him with this information. "The law under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 specifies the prevention of child marriages. The number of child marriages is so high that there are not even enough jails in the state to house all those who are guilty on this count. But still, we will not allow this to continue. We will make arrests. We have to stop all these social evils. We will launch a bigger campaign on this issue in the coming days," CM Adhikari said.

headline: 'School Thik Karo' campaign: Rajasthan villagers clash with CJP workers during visit; accuse them of politicising education - Bilkul Online
text: Jaipur A confrontation broke out early on Friday morning in Rampura Kanwarpura near Jaipur’s Sanganer area after workers of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) arrived to inspect a government school under their ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign. Local villagers opposed their entry, claiming that the school premises should not be ‘politicised’. The situation escalated when CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka arrived at the spot. According to Ranka, his team members were manhandled and he was also subjected to physical assault. A video of the confrontation has circulated on social media. Residents stopped the CJP workers at the school gate and refused to allow them inside. They said the village did not need outside political groups to intervene in the school’s affairs. The villagers pointed out that Rs 12 lakh had already been sanctioned by the government for renovation of the school building. They said they were capable of carrying out the necessary improvements themselves and did not want the school to become a site of political activity. Some residents also alleged that certain groups attempt to exploit religious sentiments and create divisions in society, saying the village would prefer to manage its own affairs. After the confrontation, Ranka released a video on social media in which he described the villagers involved as “BJP goons.” He alleged that the government machinery was trying to prevent them from highlighting problems in government schools. Ranka claimed that children at the school were being made to study in conditions resembling a buffalo shed. “This government school in Rampura Kanwarpura has been in a dilapidated state for years, and children are forced to study in a place resembling a buffalo shed,” Ranka said. He further stated that members of his team were manhandled when they attempted to raise the issue. Earlier, the CJP team had planned visits to two government schools in Jaipur. At 8:00 a.m. they visited the government primary/upper-primary school in Rampura Kanwarpura, Sanganer and at 11:30 a.m., they planned to visit the government school on Vatika Road, where a roof collapse had reportedly raised concerns. The first visit was disrupted by the confrontation with villagers. The incident comes amid a recent Rajasthan Education Department order restricting the entry of outsiders into government schools, along with unauthorised videography and uploading of school-related videos to social media without prior approval. headline: West Bengal bypolls: ECI announces October 6 polling for Nandigram, Rejinagar | Today News
text: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced October 6 as the polling date for by-elections to two Assembly constituencies in West Bengal -- Nandigram and Rejinagar. The ECI announced the schedule for the two bypolls on Monday. The Nandigram seat became vacant after Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and incumbent West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari resigned as MLA. The Rejinagar constituency was also left vacant following the resignation of Humayun Kabir. The bypoll announcement is expected to trigger fresh speculation about whether Trinamool Congress (TMC) chief Mamata Banerjee will contest from Nandigram as she seeks to make a comeback to the West Bengal Assembly. headline: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari announces crackdown on child marriage after 60,000 underage deliveries
text: NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday announced a statewide crackdown on child marriage, ordering house-to-house drives to identify underage marriages and pregnancies and warning of arrests, imprisonment and withdrawal of government welfare benefits for those involved. Speaking to the media at Nabanna after a Cabinet meeting, Adhikari said the government would invoke the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 and the POCSO Act against those marrying minors as well as people who facilitate or solemnise such marriages. The announcement came after the state health department reported nearly 60,000 institutional deliveries involving underage girls between January 1 and June 30, according to figures cited by the chief minister. Nearly 60,000 underage deliveries reported in six months Adhikari said Murshidabad recorded the highest number, with 12,847 institutional childbirths by underage girls during the six-month period. South 24 Parganas followed with 4,178 cases. He said West Bengal tops the country in child marriages and childbirths involving girls below 18 years of age. The chief minister said every case of pregnancy and childbirth involving a girl below 18 must be reported. The health records would be used by authorities to identify suspected child marriages and initiate action against those responsible. The proposed house-to-house drives will involve coordination between the police, health and social welfare departments and district administrations, with records of underage pregnancies and institutional deliveries being used to identify vulnerable cases. Husbands, facilitators face legal action Adhikari said husbands of women found to have been married while underage would be issued showcause notices and asked to produce valid proof of their wife's age. "If they fail to provide valid proof of the age, strict action will be taken," he said. He warned that police would initiate criminal action and make arrests in cases detected during the crackdown. "Police action will be initiated, and arrests will be made," Adhikari said. The government will also withdraw welfare and other scheme benefits from people found to be involved in child marriages, he said. The chief minister issued a warning to priests, qazis and others who solemnise or facilitate underage marriages. Those found involved would face imprisonment and fines under the law. headline: Parliament panel questions delay in response to Baiga child deaths in Madhya Pradesh
text: Members of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Social Justice and Empowerment questioned the government over its response to the deaths of Baiga tribe children in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat district, asking why there were no clear answers on the cause of the deaths several months after the first cases were reported. The panel met representatives of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, the Ministry of Jal Shakti’s Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, and the Department of Telecommunications to review the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN). The PM-JANMAN scheme was approved by the Union Cabinet following the announcement of the Pradhan Mantri PVTG Development Mission in the Union Budget for 2023-24. The scheme has an outlay of ₹24,104 crore for three years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, and aims to improve the socio-economic conditions of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs). According to sources, Opposition members questioned why, despite the government’s claims of service saturation in villages identified under the PM-JANMAN, it did not have clear answers on the causes of the deaths. The health crisis in remote tribal settlements of Balaghat has raised concerns over infectious diseases, malnutrition and access to healthcare, with children bearing the brunt of the illness. As per the Union Health Ministry, the first cases emerged in late June in villages in Birsa block, where several children developed fever, rashes and other symptoms. The official death toll between June and August is six, with officials stating that malaria and measles, including possible co-infection, were among the illnesses identified. Local representatives, however, have claimed a higher death toll. A Congress MP, however, pointed out that the first death was reported in the Birsa block on May 18 and that the toll could exceed 25. He claimed that the government acknowledged it only by July 20. Members sought an explanation for the delay in intervention despite provisions for mobile medical units under the scheme. According to sources, representatives of the Jal Shakti Ministry told the panel that they were not aware of the incident. The Tribal Affairs Secretary later informed the committee that Balaghat, which remained affected by Left-Wing Extremism until 2025, could not fully benefit from the scheme. headline: Maharashtra gives taxi and tuk-tuk drivers a year to learn Marathi language
text: - Published An Indian state has given taxi and tuk-tuk drivers one more year to learn the local language after a new rule making it mandatory sparked protests. Transport officials in the western state of Maharashtra had begun testing drivers' ability to conduct basic conversations in Marathi, the state's official language, on 20 August. Those who failed were given a month to learn the language, after which they risked having their licences suspended or cancelled. The government said the requirement was meant to improve communication between drivers and passengers and ensure safer journeys. But the rule alarmed drivers' unions, who argued that workers should not risk losing their livelihoods while they were still learning the language. Many of the drivers are migrants who came to Maharashtra from other parts of India in search of work, including the populous Hindi-speaking states of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Amid protests, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced last week that the drivers would be given another year to learn Marathi, as many had been out of the formal education system for years and needed more time. State Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has said that drivers will be expected to learn Marathi during the year and that there will be no more extensions. Maharashtra has almost 979,000 valid tuk-tuk and taxi permits, nearly half of them in the Mumbai metropolitan region. The extension has brought some relief to drivers who had feared losing their ability to work. "We were worried that if our licences were suspended, our daily income would be affected," says Lakhan Pandey, a taxi driver in Mumbai. "Now we feel somewhat relieved." But the row has reopened a much older debate in Maharashtra, where questions of language, migration and jobs have shaped politics for decades. "The issue is not simply about communication between drivers and passengers, but about Marathi identity, migration and employment," says Prakash Akolkar, a journalist, author and political analyst. Those tensions stretch back to the creation of Maharashtra itself. The state was formed in 1960 after a long campaign for a Marathi-speaking state. As Mumbai grew into India's financial centre, it drew generations of migrants from across the country in search of work. Language became increasingly entwined with arguments over jobs and opportunities for Marathi speakers. headline: Bengaluru: FIR against Uttarakhand BJP men over 'purification'
text: Bengaluru: A zero FIR was registered on Friday, September 4, against Uttarakhand BJP members and others in connection with the alleged “purification” ritual held at a venue after AICC chief Mallikarjun Kharge addressed a rally there, police said. The case was registered following a complaint lodged by T R Ramappa, former vice-chairman of the ST Department (Adivasi Congress) of the Indian National Congress at Vidhana Soudha Police Station on August 31, they said. A Zero FIR is a case that can be filed in any police station, regardless of the place where the crime is committed or the jurisdiction of the police station, officials said. According to the FIR, the complainant stated that on August 8, the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha and National President of the Indian National Congress, Mallikarjun Kharge, attended and addressed a large public rally at Ramlila Ground in Haldwani, Uttarakhand. The said rally was a peaceful and democratic public assembly, duly conducted in accordance with the law and without any unlawful incident, it said. The FIR stated that after the public rally, certain members and functionaries of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) allegedly orchestrated and conducted a so-called “purification ritual” on August 10 (Shuddhikaran) at the very venue where the said rally was held. ‘Ritual intended to convey casteist notion’ “The said ritual was purportedly intended to convey the deeply offensive, derogatory and casteist notion that the presence of Sri. Mallikarjun Kharge, a member of a Scheduled Caste community, had rendered the said place ‘impure’ and that the venue consequently required ritualistic cleansing,” the complainant alleged. Such conduct, if established, the complainant alleged, is not merely “objectionable” but constitutes a “deliberate” and “deeply insulting” act directed against the dignity and social status of Kharge and is liable to attract the consequences prescribed under the applicable provisions of law. Complaint registered after seeking legal opinion “That, compounding the gravity of the aforesaid egregious act, Sri Mahendra Bhatt, in his capacity as the President of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttarakhand, has, through public statements made to the media, brazenly defended, justified and endorsed the aforesaid purification ritual. headline: Pune: Hinjawadi, Maan & Marunji Residents To Protest On 6th Sept Over Traffic, Roads & Water Crisis
text: Pune: Residents of Hinjawadi, Maan and Marunji have announced a peaceful protest on 6th September 2026 over worsening civic and infrastructure problems in the rapidly developing IT corridor, residents told The Free Press Journal on Sunday. The protest is being organised by local residents, farmers, IT employees and various regional welfare associations. The Resident Welfare Association (RWA), Maan, has submitted a formal representation to the Maharashtra government. The association has demanded immediate and time-bound action on traffic congestion, road widening, water shortages, urban planning and administrative issues. The residents have sought clear deadlines for the government to resolve the problems. They have also warned that the protest could be intensified if concrete decisions are not taken. One of the key demands is an immediate meeting at Hinjawadi under the chairmanship of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. The residents want major potholes to be filled within seven days and temporary traffic measures to be introduced at major congestion points. ‘Open Metro, Widen Roads, Solve Traffic’ The residents have also demanded that the entire Maan-Shivajinagar Metro Line 3 be opened on priority by 31st October. They said this would provide an alternative to road travel and help reduce pressure on the busy IT corridor. They have also sought a decision on the long-pending Wakad-Balewadi transit hub within six months. Land acquisition and compensation for road widening have emerged as another major concern. The residents have demanded that compensation issues involving farmers be resolved immediately, along the lines of the model used for the Purandar airport land acquisition. They have sought completion of the land acquisition and tender process within 30 days. The proposed road widening works should then be completed within six to nine months and before the 2027 monsoon, according to the representation. The residents have also called for a permanent traffic plan involving the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) and the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI). The plan should cover major congestion points such as Wakad-Hinjawadi Flyover, Bhumkar Chowk, Tathawade and the Punawale underpasses. Officials also informed the CM that another student, Salmon Raj, was injured in the accident and is currently undergoing treatment at Tekkali District Hospital (DH). The Chief Minister directed authorities to ensure Salmon Raj receives better medical care and instructed officials to support and assist the affected families. As per reports, four youths were killed, and another was injured after they were struck by the Rajadhani Express near Burma Colony on the outskirts of Tekkali when they were crossing the railway track and the speeding train hit them. They were reportedly going to attend to nature’s call at the time of the incident.

headline: Two state laws (and one proposed law) with constitutional implications
text: April 17, 2016 · 6:52 am Last month, Punjab passed the Indian Penal Code (Punjab Amendment) Act, which inserts a new Section 295AA into the IPC. 295AA, according to reports, prohibits “sacrilege” to the Guru Granth Sahib, and imposes life imprisonment as a punishment. I haven’t yet been able to obtain a text of the law, but if indeed the term used is “sacrilege”, it seems to me that there is a clear over-breadth problem with respect to Article 19(1)(a). It would also be interesting to see whether Section 295AA has a mens rea requirement, since that was precisely the ground on which the Supreme Court upheld Section 295A in Ramji Lal Modi’s Case – reasoning that an “intentional” insult to religious sentiments can cause public disorder, bringing the section within the scope of Article 19(2). It also seems to me that the sentence of life imprisonment is highly disproportionate, and can constitute cruel and unusual punishment, violating Article 21. On April 11, the Maharashtra Legislative Council cleared a bill to “regulate” dance bars in the State of Maharashtra. The Hindu has an account of some of the stringent conditions imposed by the bill. Apart from the fact that the bill imposes prior restraint by subjecting all performances to the approval of the censor board, it also allegedly prohibits “vulgar” performances. Once again, this seems to be a textbook case of over-breadth under Article 19(1)(a) – quite apart from the fact that the Supreme Court itself, on more than one occasion, has specified that mere vulgarity (if it lacks a “prurient interest”) does not constitute obscenity. Last week, Maharasthra enacted a law against social boycotts (a previous draft may be accessed here). The law prohibits social boycotts (which are defined in numerous ways, ranging from expulsion from the community, to obstructing regular business and social relations, to obstructing the performance of marriage) within communities. It is therefore applicable horizontally, and – naturally – impacts the freedom of association (which, as the Court has held, carries with it the freedom not to associate). Social boycotts – and legislative action against them – have a long history in India, as we have often discussed on this blog. headline: Jalandhar: Gangster injured in police firing during escape bid - The Tribune
text: A gangster was shot at while allegedly trying to escape from custody of the Jalandhar Commissionerate Police on Saturday. The accused, Sukhjinder Singh, alias Prince, a resident of Kakke Kandiala village in Tarn Taran, was associated with the Doni Bal gang. He was arrested along with Sahajdeep Singh, also from the same village, after they attempted to open fire in the Model Town area recently. The police had taken Sukhjinder near the Dairy Complex in Jamsherpur for the recovery of the weapon. During the operation, he allegedly broke free and tried to escape. According to the police, after he opened fire at the police team, an officer retaliated. Investigating Officer ASI Raj Masih had arrested both the accused on Thursday. During interrogation, Sukhjinder Singh had disclosed that they had concealed the weapon near a bridge. During recovery proceedings, the accused took out the pistol buried in the ground and pushed ASI Raj Masih to the ground and opened fire. The ASI had a narrow escape and the bullet hit the wall of the bridge. In self-defence, the ASI fired at the accused with his service pistol. The injured accused was shifted to the Civil Hospital. Model Town ACP Manmohan Singh said another person involved in the conspiracy, Jashanpreet Singh, also a resident of Kakke Kandiala village, will be arrested shortly. During the investigation, Daljit Kaur, mother of one of the accused, was also arrested for providing shelter to Jashanpreet Singh. The police have recovered a country-made .32 bore pistol, one magazine, one live .32 bore round and one empty cartridge.

headline: NIA court to deliver verdict on Sept 5 in Jhiram Ghati Naxal attack case that wiped out Chhattisgarh Congress top brass - The Tribune
text: NIA court to deliver verdict on Sept 5 in Jhiram Ghati Naxal attack case that wiped out Chhattisgarh Congress top brass CPI (Maoist) cadres on May 25, 2013, surrounded and killed 29 Congress leaders and security personnel, including Salwa Judum founder Mahendra Karma, who took 50 bullets Thirteen years after one of the deadliest Naxal attacks in Chhattisgarh wiped out the state Congress leadership, a Special NIA court will deliver its verdict on September 5. Earlier, the verdict was expected on Monday but later it was deferred to September 5. The case came to be known in the annals of Chhattisgarh history as the Jhiram Ghati massacre. On May 25, 2013, just after 4 pm, CPI (Maoist) cadres killed 29 Chhattisgarh Congress leaders and security personnel after planning the attack for months and allegedly hoodwinking the entire intelligence and security apparatus of the state. Who all were killed The killings involved Chhattisgarh Congress stalwarts, including former Union Minister Vidya Charan Shukla, then state unit chief Nand Kumar Patel and his son Dinesh, then MLA Yogendra Sharma, and former MLAs Uday Mudaliyar and Mahendra Karma, founder of the volunteer anti-Naxal force Salwa Judum. Even today, a memorial in the name of those killed stands on the national highway in Sukma's Jhiram Ghati, where the attack took place. It is widely believed that Mahendra Karma, founder of the anti-Naxal civilian force Salwa Judum, was the prime target of the 2013 attack. He took 50 bullets and was also axed to death. Only one survivor that day Curiously, one Congress leader, Konta MLA Kawasi Lakhma, escaped unhurt that day and contested his sixth election in 2023. He again won the seat. Conspiracy theories surfaced after Lakhma survived the attack, with locals telling this correspondent, when she visited the Jhiram Ghati memorial in Bastar during the Chhattisgarh election tour in 2023, that former Chhattisgarh Industry Minister Kawasi Lakhma's writ ran large in Bastar's Maoist belt, where he inspired both fear and awe. The National Investigation Agency probed the matter and filed a closure report terming the ambush as a Naxal attack and naming few cadres of the outlawed CPI (Maoists). headline: CM sets Aug 24 deadline for farmer registration on AgriStack
text: Chandigarh: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Friday set Aug 24 as the deadline for targeted farmer registration on AgriStack, directing districts to work on a “war footing” and assign targets to revenue and agriculture officials. He said he would personally review the progress that day, ahead of PM Narendra Modi’s review on Aug 25, and sought explanations from districts reporting slow progress. AgriStack, a central govt initiative, will provide each registered farmer a unique Farmer ID and digitally link agricultural land parcels with land records. It will also maintain digital records of crops sown on individual fields and facilitate geo-mapping of villages and agricultural land. Saini said the platform would help ensure faster delivery of benefits under schemes such as PM-KISAN, crop insurance, agricultural credit, MSP-based procurement, and distribution of fertilisers and seeds. He also directed DCs to prioritise digital crop survey and auto-mutation so that people do not have to make repeated visits to govt offices for routine land and agriculture-related services. Additional chief secretary, revenue, Sumita Misra said farmers should register on Agri Stack on priority, cautioning that those who do not register could face difficulties in accessing agriculture-related schemes. The GPS-based Digital Crop Survey-2026 began across Haryana on Aug 16 and will continue till Sept 30. Agriculture officials and patwaris are conducting field-level surveys to record crop-sowing details along with geo-referenced data.

headline: Test Of Democracy Is The Book We Dislike
text: Test Of Democracy Is The Book We Dislike Bans are admission of fragility Recent tumult over whether a book written by a leader of an opposition party should be published has brought to centre stage a larger and more uncomfortable question i.e., what does India's experiment with democracy really mean when confronted with speech that is inconvenient, provocative or politically disagreeable? Freedom of speech is rarely tested by opinions with which we agree. It is tested when an expression irritates us, challenges our political loyalties, unsettles our social assumptions or contradicts the version of history we have come to accept as truth. It is perfectly legitimate to disagree passionately with a published perspective. One can expose its factual inaccuracies, challenge its interpretation, question its motives or demolish its arguments. But the appropriate response to disagreement in a democracy should be more argument, not less expression. It should be a counter-book, a scholarly rebuttal, a fact-based critique, a public debate, or simply the freedom to ignore the book. Suppression, bans and violence are altogether different responses. They do not defeat an argument; they prevent the argument from being heard. India has, unfortunately, acquired a long and somewhat dated legacy of responding to uncomfortable books through prohibition and political pressure. From Lady Chatterley's Lover to Jaswant Singh's Jinnah: India, Partition, Independence, and from the controversies surrounding Nathuram Godse's writings to Salman Rushdie's The Satanic Verses, books have repeatedly become battlegrounds for competing claims of morality, nationalism, religious sentiment and constitutional propriety. The literary merit, intellectual seriousness or factual accuracy of these works can, and should, be passionately debated. Some may be profound; others misguided, offensive or historically questionable. But that is precisely the point: they should be debated rather than disappeared. Jaswant Singh understood this instinctively when his book on Jinnah and Partition was banned by the Gujarat government in 2009. His response was memorable: “The day we start banning books, we are banning thinking.” That sentence deserves to be remembered well beyond the controversy that produced it. A book is an argument made public. To prohibit it because its argument is politically inconvenient is therefore to move beyond disagreement and towards controlling the boundaries of permissible thought. headline: Kasturirangan Report: Both Houses of Karnataka Legislature adopt resolution urging Centre to confine ESA to notified forests
text: The Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Council on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) adopted unanimous resolution urging the Centre to confine the Ecological Sensitive Area (ESA) identified as per the Kasthurirangan report on conservation of Western Ghats to only the notified forests. It also sought a year’s time for the State to help take up a physical survey of the areas coming under ESA. “The draft notification issued by the Centre regarding the ESA in Karnataka should not be finalised till the next one year when the physical survey would be completed. The final decision on ESA should be taken only after the State submits its report to the Centre and only after detailed discussion by the Centre with the State,” said the resolution, which was tabled by Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar. The resolution said that Karnataka would constitute a high-level committee led by a retired judge to suggest measures to correct the “lacunae” in the Kasthurirangan report through appropriate modifications. The committee would comprise officials from the Revenue and Forest Departments besides representatives of farmers, industrial units and experts from academic institutions that have expertise in the sectors of forest and ecology. Report to be submitted The State government would submit the report of the high-level committee and the physical survey of the ESA, the resolution said. The government would also form committee comprising people’s representatives at village panchayat level to help assist the high-power committee. The Centre had, on July 27, issued the seventh draft notification on ESA based on the Kasthurirangan report, which comprises 20,668 square km of area spread over 1,449 villages across 10 districts of the State. The State’s stand on ESA would mean reducing it to about 16,000 square kms. The unanimous resolution demanded that agricultural/horticultural/plantation lands, human settlements and areas of public activities should not be included in the ESA. The experts’ committee should demarcate the boundary of forests and human settlements through a physical survey which is based on the revenue survey numbers of the property, the resolution said. headline: Manisha Koirala supports Gen Z's fight against corruption, urges youth to have ‘a vision’: ‘Just because you’re young doesn’t mean you’ll be a good leader’
text: Over the past few years, Gen Z has emerged as a powerful force in politics, raising questions about accountability, corruption and governance across countries, including Nepal and India. Speaking at the NDTV World Anvishka Summit in Kathmandu, Manisha Koirala reflected on the role of the younger generation in politics and offered advice to young people stepping into leadership. In September 2025, Nepal witnessed Gen Z-led protests that reportedly contributed to the fall of then Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli’s government. A new government under Prime Minister Balendra Shah subsequently took over. In India, young people have also participated in protests over issues including National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET), Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) paper leaks. Manisha Koirala backs Gen Z’s fight against corruption Talking about the younger generation’s political activism, Manisha said she supports their energy and applauded their decision to speak out against corruption. “I support the younger generation's energy. I support and I salute the fact that they stood up against corruption, against a political class failing to address corruption,” the actor said. Manisha added that it was too early for her, or anyone else, to discredit the movement. However, she also cautioned against assuming that youth alone automatically translates into effective leadership. “I also believe that only because you're young doesn't mean you'll be a good leader. You know, there is a wisdom, there is an experience, there is something which is also very much a country needs,” she said. The Heeramandi star stressed that ultimately, the performance of any government should be judged by its accountability and ability to deliver. “At the end of the day, accountability matters. At the end of the day, delivery matters. So let's see,” she said. ‘Nepal has examples of young people taking leadership’ Manisha also pointed out that young people taking up political leadership is not a new phenomenon in Nepal. “In Nepal's political history, this is not the first time the younger generation has taken a leadership,” she said. She cited her grandfather, Bishweshwar Prasad Koirala, Nepal’s first democratically elected Prime Minister, who assumed the leadership role at a relatively young age. headline: Modi Hails Bengal Women’s Assistance Scheme
text: Nearly 1.5 crore women receive the fourth instalment of Rs 3,000 monthly aid New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday said the Centre and the West Bengal government were committed to giving women the confidence and decision-making power to move forward, with the Annapurna Yojana playing a crucial role in achieving that goal. Virtually addressing an “Annapurna Divas” programme organised by the West Bengal government, Modi said a major grievance among the state’s people over the past 12 years was that the benefits of several Central schemes had not reached them on time. Without naming the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamul Congress government, he said poor families had suffered the most because they were denied the benefits of Central schemes. The BJP government had now accelerated the stalled schemes, he said. “Our vision is that the women of Bengal should have both the power to make decisions and the courage to move forward. The Annapurna Yojana plays a crucial role in this. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the beneficiary mothers and sisters,” Modi said. Earlier, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced at a programme in Salt Lake, near Kolkata, that Mr Modi’s birthday on September 17 would be observed annually as Annapurna Divas in the state. He said the Prime Minister had guaranteed the monthly assistance of Rs 3,000 to women. The fourth instalment of the BJP government’s Annapurna Yojana was credited to the bank accounts of nearly 1.5 crore women on Thursday. Eligible women receive Rs 3,000 a month under the scheme. Modi said the assistance could help a mother pay for her child’s education or enable a woman to buy medicines and other household essentials. “When their worries about essential household expenditure are reduced, their confidence naturally grows. The Annapurna Yojana is a major initiative aimed at strengthening the confidence of Bengal’s women,” he said. The Prime Minister said a fixed amount was deposited directly into the beneficiaries’ bank accounts every month without their having to depend on anyone. “This is a tremendous help,” he said. Modi said addressing the needs of women and girls at every stage of their lives had been among the BJP’s highest priorities. Referring to the BJP’s victory in the West Bengal elections earlier this year, he said the state had chosen the path of change and that women had played the most important role in bringing about the transformation.

headline: Congress ignoring Mamata outreach depicts turning wheel of political fortune after West Bengal polls
text: New Delhi, Sep 17 : Trinamool Congress leaders, owing allegiance to Mamata Banerjee, have reportedly confirmed a Congress outreach before next month's bye-elections with a proposal to share one seat each, and the subsequent turndown -- a development indicating trading positions, with the latter now acquiring high political grounds after this year's Assembly poll results in West Bengal. In the Assembly polls held in April this year, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won 208 seats and Trinamool 80 in the 294-member West Bengal Assembly. Later, Rejinagar and Bhabanipur were left vacant after the winning candidates, which included Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, opted out and retained the other they had simultaneously won. Reeling from electoral setbacks in West Bengal, followed by several leaders and elected representatives walking out of its folds and many under investigation over alleged malpractices, Trinamool's top leadership had contacted Congress General Secretary (Organisation) K.C. Venugopal with the seat-sharing proposal. According to a Trinamool MP, the Congress never reverted, rather went on to announce candidates for both seats. When asked later, Venugopal apparently pointed to strong objections from regional party members. Congress leaders are also said to have cited Mamata's earlier decision to end alliances with Congress and allegations of attacks and harassment against its workers under the previous Trinamool Congress government in the state. Reports quoted West Bengal Congress President Shubhankar Sarkar having said the Trinamool Congress should rather support its candidates in both seats and that only then the possibility of a future alliance could be considered. Incidentally, when Sarkar replaced Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury as the party leader ahead of state election, it was assumed that the Congress high command intended to send a show of softening in stand in Congress ranks towards Mamata Banerjee. Since the parting of ways began, another bitter war of attrition between the two parties, which escalated with the appointment of Chowdhury as the state Congress Chief. A known Mamata-baiter, Chowdhury upped the ante against the then ruling Trinamool Congress in West Bengal, with the party frequently lodging protests in with Central Congress leaders, including Sonia Gandhi. The Congress by then had successfully held hands with the Communists against a common political foe at the State Secretariat, forgetting the pitched verbal and physical battles of almost three-and-a-half decades. It was this animosity that made Mamata Banerjee walk out of the Congress fold in 1997 and form the Trinamool Congress next year.

headline: ‘Flip-flop': BJP mocks CM Satheesan, claims he deleted post slamming cleric's remarks on women
text: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday launched a sharp attack on Kerala CM VD Satheesan, alleging that he deleted a social media video in which he had criticised Grand Mufti of India Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar’s remarks on women’s participation in public life. The BJP accused Satheesan of “flip-flops” and alleged that he had backed down after initially taking a strong stand against the Sunni cleric’s comments. “The Chief Minister V D Satheesan is not the prince of principles, but the prince of flip-flops,” the Kerala BJP said in a social media post. The party alleged that Satheesan’s stand changed after pressure from political and religious groups, and accused him of “surrendering before religious extremist forces”. BJP alleges Satheesan ‘backtracked’ The BJP claimed that Satheesan had deleted his video hours after criticising Kanthapuram’s remarks. It also alleged that the chief minister’s position was influenced by the Jamaat-e-Islami and Indian Union Muslim League. “The Chief Minister of Kerala is nothing but a playing card in their hands,” the BJP said, alleging that Satheesan was “dancing to their tune”. Satheesan rejects restrictions on women Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Satheesan said the Kerala government did not agree with the cleric’s position. “We don't agree with his statement that women should stay home. It's not a suitable stand in our developing Keralam. It's not the 19th century that one should make such statements. Even Islam doesn't say that. Women should not stay home, but join the mainstream. That is our stand,” he said. Satheesan’s comments came amid criticism of Kanthapuram over his defence of directives issued by his faction of the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama regarding women’s participation in religious celebrations.

headline: Grant cut, DJs banned, liquor outlets shut on Maha Ashtami: Big announcements in Bengal ahead of Durga Puja
text: Grant cut, DJs banned, liquor outlets shut on Maha Ashtami: Big announcements in Bengal ahead of Durga Puja The BJP government also waived electricity charges and fire-clearance fees for puja committees, while liquor shops and bars will shut on Maha Ashtami. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal on Monday slashed the grant for Durga Puja committees from ₹1.10 lakh provided last year by the previous Mamata Banerjee-led government to ₹1 lakh this year, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said, announcing a complete ban on DJs during the festivities and closure of liquor outlets and bars on Maha Ashtami. Addressing reporters after a meeting with representatives of Durga Puja committees, Adhikari also announced a 100% waiver of electricity charges for puja committees across the state and said they would not have to pay fees for obtaining fire safety clearances. Urging large-budget puja committees to not avail the grant, the CM said the government would provide the assistance to committees that need financial aid. “I do not want to misuse the powers of the chief minister. I would request those who are capable (of organising pujas without government assistance) not to take the financial aid. Those who cannot organise the puja without this money will be given ₹1 lakh by the government,” Adhikari said. First Puja season under BJP government This is the first Durga Puja season under the BJP, which stormed to power in the eastern state earlier this year. Adhikari also took a swipe at former chief minister Banerjee, who in 2025 increased the state’s grant for community pujas from ₹85,000 each to ₹1.10 lakh. In 2018, when the TMC started the scheme, the amount was fixed at ₹10,000. “The manner in which the former chief minister announced grants for puja committees last year was similar to bargaining in a morning fish market,” he said. “This didn’t help (her) in the elections though.” TMC leaders refused to comment on the development. headline: The Identity Project
text: The Identity Project A study of pockets in Bihar where the demographic balance between communities appeared to have changed noticeably revealed an unexpected trend that took officials by surprise. Illegal immigrant families were actively seeking institutional deliveries, and this was not just a concern rooted in a desire for safe births. headline: What does the newly passed inter-university transfer Bill mean for teachers in West Bengal? | Explained
text: The West Bengal Assembly on Thursday (September 10, 2026) passed a Bill that empowers the State government to transfer teaching and non-teaching staffers from one State university to another. The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was tabled by State’s Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay during a special session of the State Assembly with 171 MLAs voting in support and 15 against. The State cabinet had approved the Bill on September 8. The statement of objects and reasons of the Bill states that the State, through the legislation, intends the government to optimise the utilisation of human resources in the higher education sector while protecting the service conditions, seniority, and other rights of university employees. While the objects of the legislation may appear praise worthy, the MLAs from the Opposition flagged that the Bill will lead to selective targeting of academicians critical of the State government. What legal provisions does the Bill entail? The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the 2017 Act by empowering the Chancellor, in consultation with the State government, to transfer employees “for administrative reasons”. Section 11 of The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Act, 2017 provided for the transfer of employees of colleges (teachers, librarians, officers and non-teaching employees) from one college to another. However, there is no corresponding provision for the transfer of employees of universities from one university to another. The 2017 Act was enacted to provide for better administration and to improve the quality of education in the State-aided higher education institutions in West Bengal. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari’s stance on the Bill During the Trinamool Congress regime, the State government has set up several universities and many of them lacked basic infrastructure, teachers and even students. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, while participating in the discussion on the Bill in the Assembly said that the State government’s aim is to make weaker universities stronger and independent by applying the provisions of the Bill. Mr. Adhikari said that if anyone wants to call this misuse of power, they can keep doing it. “We don’t care. We have come to power for five years with a two-thirds majority,” he said. Pasha pointed out that the Kerala High Court had disposed of a writ petition concerning the film after observing that the plea was not maintainable against the grant of a certificate to a movie by the CBFC. text: ‘No FIR, no move' : Rahul Gandhi stages dharna over student’s pellet injuries A demand for an FIR turned into a political standoff on Friday, August 21, as Congress leader Rahul Gandhi sat on a dharna at the Parliament Street police station with 19-year-old Sahil Lochab, who was allegedly injured by pellets during a protest last month. Gandhi said he would not leave until a case was registered over Lochab's complaint. Gandhi arrived at the police station with Lochab after first visiting the Mandir Marg police station, where they sought registration of an FIR but failed to get a response. headline: JMM workers clash with protesting students in Ranchi, flee with Hemant Soren’s effigy
text: A scuffle broke out between protesting students and JMM workers in Ranchi on Friday as the agitators marched towards Albert Ekka Chowk to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, amid allegations that the Jharkhand government had misled them into withdrawing their earlier agitation. The students, protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, were marching under the banner of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch. They have accused the state government of "deceiving" and "betraying" job aspirants after the Jharkhand High Court stayed notifications cancelling appointments linked to several recruitment examinations. The students alleged that they were marching peacefully towards Albert Ekka Chowk when a group of JMM workers suddenly confronted them and misbehaved with female protesters, leading to a scuffle. BJP State President Aditya Sahu, the Leader of the Opposition Babulal Marandi and former Chief Minister Raghubar Das took part in the protest and gherao of the Deputy Commissioner (DCs) and Superintendent of Police (SPs) offices in the five districts, including the state capital Ranchi on the first day of the agitation. headline: BSEB Matric, Inter Toppers 2026: Bihar Government To Felicitate 168 Students With Up To ₹2 Lakh Cash Prize And ₹51,000 Laptop Incentive
text: The Bihar government will felicitate 168 meritorious students who secured positions in the topper lists of the Bihar School Examination Board (BSEB) Intermediate and Matriculation Annual Examinations 2026. The felicitation ceremony is scheduled to be held on September 9 at 12 noon at Nek Samvad, Patna, according to the Education Department's official programme notice. The selected students, along with their family members, will be honoured at the ceremony. The awards include cash prizes based on the students' ranks, along with an additional incentive for purchasing a laptop. Bihar Board Toppers 2026 Felicitation Ceremony The programme will be organised under the chairmanship of Mithilesh Tiwari, Minister, Education Department, Bihar. Bihar Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav have been listed as distinguished guests for the event. The programme is being organised by the Bihar government and Education Department to recognise students who performed exceptionally well in the 2026 board examinations. Bihar Government's Incentive For Meritorious Students The felicitation programme is part of the state government's efforts to recognise academic achievement among students. The combination of rank-based cash awards and the additional laptop incentive is aimed at rewarding high-performing students and supporting their continued education. The ₹51,000 laptop incentive will be provided to every student being felicitated, irrespective of whether the student secured first, second, third or another eligible position in the topper list.

headline: Many UP dists ‘ban’ unauthorised entry and filming in govt schools
text: Many UP dists ‘ban’ unauthorised entry and filming in govt schools At least six district level education officers issued circulars asking all school staff in their districts not to allow outsiders and YouTubers to enter school premises and record videos, which they said would tarnish the image of government schools LUCKNOW After a series of viral videos of poor quality mid-day meals served to students in some UP government schools, district education officers have issued orders prohibiting the entry of outsiders, including YouTubers, into government-run primary and upper primary schools across the state to ensure smooth functioning of teaching and learning activities. The directives have coincided with the CJP’s (Cockroach Janata Party) nationwide #SchoolThikKaro (fix the government schools) campaign on social media to improve government schools, as well as student protests over poor school facilities in different parts of UP over the last two weeks. On Wednesday, students in Unnao district blocked traffic to protest poor quality food and lack of drinking water facilities at their school. On Monday, hundreds of girl students in Lucknow blocked traffic for hours to protest shortage of teachers in their school. Additional chief secretary (basic and secondary education) Partha Sarthi Sen Sharma claimed that no government order was issued (to stop entry of outsiders in schools). He said: “Many decisions are taken by BSAs in their districts depending upon local situations, like for example, closure of schools due to local festivals or extreme weather conditions. All decisions don’t require state government’s approval or consent.” In contrast, at least six district level education officers recently issued circulars asking all school staff in their districts not to allow outsiders and YouTubers to enter school premises and record videos, which they said would only tarnish the image of government schools. Farrukhabad’s basic education officer, Vishwanath Pratap Singh, was the first to issue an order barring outsiders from entering schools on April 17. In a circular, he accused “certain individuals or groups of individuals” claiming to be journalists of entering schools unauthorisedly, photographing children in classrooms, attempting to inspect records and demanding information to tarnish the education department’s image. It began in Bihar in 2025 and was subsequently expanded to other states and Union Territories. The exercise has become politically contentious, with opposition parties alleging that eligible voters could be excluded and accusing the Election Commission of favouring the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). text: FIRs, dismissals, suspensions: How Haryana govt forced sanitation workers to end strike Sanitation workers end longest strike in three decades despite govt refusing to regularise contractual workers After striking a deal with the Haryana government on Friday, sanitation workers under the Nagar Palika Karamchari Sangh called off their longest-ever strike in three decades. The 37-day strike ended despite the government not agreeing to their key demand of regularising contractual sanitation workers. The sanitation workers had also gone on strike from May 1 to May 14. The 2022 strike lasted 11 days, while the 2018 agitation continued for 16 days. Before these, the 1996 strike during the Bansi Lal regime was the longest. As many as 13,091 sanitation workers on the Palika rolls (contractual workers) had been on strike since August 6. Supporting them, 3,418 regular sanitation workers also joined the agitation, severely affecting garbage collection across the state. Heaps of municipal waste accumulated along roads in cities across Haryana. Most local bodies tackled the situation by collecting garbage at night. Several FIRs were also registered against sanitation workers for disrupting garbage lifting. How the Haryana government won the last round After announcing several benefits for sanitation workers, the Urban Local Bodies Department (ULBD), headed by Commissioner and Secretary Ashok Meena, had given the workers September 5 as the deadline to return to work, failing which legal and disciplinary action would be initiated. The department conveyed that all demands had been accepted except the regularisation of contractual workers, citing a legal hurdle. From September 7, the ULBD began issuing dismissal orders. By September 11, as many as 73 contractual workers had been dismissed and 12 regular workers suspended. Most of those facing action were office-bearers against whom FIRs had been registered. A total of 34 FIRs were lodged against 342 workers. Some arrests were also made. Talks between the government and the union had remained stalled since August 26, with Nagar Palika Karamchari Sangh president Naresh Shastri refusing to budge on the demand for regularisation of contractual workers. headline: SSB seizes over 325 kg ganja in Arunachal Pradesh, one arrested
text: Kolkata/Itanagar, Sep 20 : The Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), in a coordinated operation with the Arunachal Pradesh Police, seized nearly 325.5 kg of cannabis (Ganja) from the West Kameng district of the state on Friday. The operation was carried out by troops of the 61 Battalion SSB, Bhairabkhunda. One person has been arrested in this connection. The seizure comes weeks after the Assam Police seized over 307 kg of ganja near the state's border with Arunachal Pradesh. text: MPSC paper leak: Aaditya demands chairman, secretary’s resignation Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray met Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma on Friday to demand the immediate resignation of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) chairman and secretary over the recent paper leak. text: Indian police to query Google over 500,000 fake Gmail IDs linked to bomb hoax GOOGLE-INDIA/ (PIX, URGENT):Indian police to query Google over 500,000 fake Gmail IDs linked to bomb hoax * Police to press Google over security lapses * Emailed bomb threat targeted Gujarat government offices * India already scrutinising Google for Firebase-linked scams By Munsif Vengattil NEW DELHI, Sept 15 - Indian police will question Google over a lack of safeguards after smashing a criminal network that set up and managed more than 500,000 fake Gmail accounts to send hoax bomb threats to government offices, a police official told Reuters on Tuesday. India is one of Google's largest markets by users, where the U.S. tech giant is already under scrutiny after authorities found a pattern of criminals misusing its web development platform, Firebase, for financial scams. Police in the western state of Gujarat broke up an email network this week that they described as sending "inter-state" bomb threats and arrested two individuals, uncovering 513,847 Gmail IDs and passwords being used since 2022. Reuters is the first to report that Google itself figures in the investigation. The scale of fake Gmail accounts in use is unprecedented, Vivek Bheda, a senior cybercrime official of the Gujarat police, told Reuters. "We will write to Google, ask them to make some policy changes so cannot be bypassed," Bheda said, adding that police planned to formally designate Google as a subjectof the investigation soon. Google, owned by Alphabet Inc, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It was not immediately clear what legal charges or penalties, if any, Google could face. It also threatened countries cooperating with India during the summit, police said in a statement. headline: Modi And The Return Of The Vajpayee Numbers
text: The BJP knows that there is no leader in its ranks who can match Modi's popularity or have his cult following, and what awaits is a return to the Vajpayee numbers, when allies called the shots, argues Saisuresh Sivaswamy. Key Points - Till Modi came along, the BJP had not won an election solely on the strength of its Hindutva campaign. - The Sangh Parivar has no one who is being groomed as Modi's successor. There is no one in the organisation, RSS and BJP, with mass appeal. - There is an added urgency over Modi's successor because even though he will lead the BJP's 2029 election, he himself will step down after two years in office. Speculation about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's future plans -- which received a boost when the Bharatiya Janata Party did not secure a majority of its own in 2024, received fresh impetus over the government capitulating to the Cockroach Janta Party's demand for Dharmenda Pradhan's resignation -- has now developed further legs following reports of muted public response to his 76th birthday celebrations which we were told will be massive in scale. Alongside is the spectacle of Modi and the BJP's bete noire Rahul Gandhi's continued criticism of the government -- which shouldn't faze anyone in the ruling circles except for the fact that many in the neutral space who once jumped in with relish to ridicule him are now not so sure if they were right and he was wrong, or if he was right and they were wrong. headline: Govt. announces promotions for Swarna Ward employees in Andhra Pradesh
text: The Andhra Pradesh Government has issued orders enabling promotions for four categories of Swarna Ward Secretariat functionaries following the recent approval by the State Cabinet. The order covers Ward Administrative Secretaries, Ward Data Processing Secretaries, Ward Sanitation and Environment Secretaries (Grade-II), and Ward Planning and Regulation Secretaries (Grade-II). Junior Assistant posts As part of the Cabinet-approved restructuring, the government has approved the creation of 815 Junior Assistant posts by rationalising 915 identified surplus and vacant posts, comprising 458 Ward Amenities Secretary Grade-II posts and 457 Ward Planning & Regulation Secretary Grade-II posts. The newly sanctioned Junior Assistant posts will facilitate promotions for eligible Ward Administrative Secretaries. The resultant vacancies in the Ward Administrative Secretary cadre will, in turn, provide promotional opportunities for eligible Ward Data Processing Secretaries. Posts upgraded Further, the government has approved the upgradation of 815 posts each in the Ward Sanitation and Environment Secretary, and Ward Planning and Regulation Secretary cadres from Grade-II to Grade-I, thereby creating 1,630 promotional positions across these two categories. The decision addresses a longstanding issue affecting employees recruited in 2019, many of whom have completed more than six years of service without receiving a promotion despite the promotional hierarchy having been notified by the government. The decision is expected to benefit eligible employees working across Swarna Ward Secretariats functioning in the Urban Local Bodies. Municipal Administration and Urban Development (MAUD) Principal Secretary S. Suresh Kumar said the restructuring would strengthen the supervisory framework in municipal administration, particularly in sanitation, revenue administration, town planning and digital service delivery. headline: ESA row heats up in Keralam; Kerala Congress (M) demands village-wise data, White Paper
text: Even as the Keralam government has sought to exclude more than 30 villages covering over 1,500 sq km from the Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) proposed by the Centre, the political row over the issue is showing no signs of easing. The Kerala Congress (M) has now trained its guns on the United Democratic Front (UDF) government, demanding an explanation for the discrepancy between the findings of a five-member government committee in 2014 and the figures submitted to the Centre in September 2026. Party chairman Jose K. Mani, MP, said the inclusion of agricultural land in 25 villages across nine districts on the latest ESA list was a matter of serious concern. “Even with the ESA affecting 36 Assembly constituencies, including those represented by five Ministers and the Chief Whip, and 15 Lok Sabha constituencies, the UDF leadership has failed to adopt a clear political position,” he alleged. Special Assembly session Mr. Mani said the State should have convened a special Assembly session before September 25 and passed a resolution making it clear that inhabited and agricultural areas outside existing reserve forests should not be included in the ESA. He also demanded that the government publish village-wise details of the forest area identified by the five-member committee in 2014 and compare them with the figures submitted to the Centre in 2026. headline: HC Denies Relief To Eatery For Serving Analogue Paneer; Cites Poetic Justice
text: Restaurant also needs to suffer for some time just as it made people suffer by making them eat something rotten, judge said. Mumbai: The Bombay High Court on Friday refused to grant any urgent relief to a Thane-based restaurant facing action from the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) while coming down on it heavily for serving banned analogue paneer to customers. "poetic justice", a bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad, said the restaurant- 'Udupi Swaad' - also needs to suffer for some time just as it made people suffer by making them eat "something rotten". Earlier this month, the Maharashtra government banned the manufacture and sale of analogue or non-dairy paneer for one year over public health concerns and widespread violations of food safety norms. As per a government order, offenders could face life imprisonment and a minimum fine of Rs 10 lakh in cases where consumption of unsafe food results in death. Analogue paneer is a non-dairy substitute made using vegetable oils, starches, emulsifiers and other additives instead of milk fat. It is cheaper to produce than conventional paneer and generally contains lower protein levels. The eatery had filed a petition in the HC against the August 11 order of the FDA suspending its licence after it was found that it had been serving customers the banned analogue paneer. In its plea, the restaurant said the FDA ought to have first issued them an improvement notice. The court, which has time and again pulled up the FDA for its drastic action against eateries and hotels, on Friday, however, noted that the petitioner hotel needs to suffer. "You need to suffer first as you have made people suffer by eating this (analogue paneer). This is poetic justice. We will take a different strict view this time," the court said. The bench questioned the restaurant if it had mentioned clearly in its menu card that the paneer served in their dishes was analogue and not the actual paneer made from milk. "You are making people eat something rotten by making them believe that it is paneer and you are saying improvement notice should be given to you? Why don't you advertise on your signboard that original food is not available with us," it asked. The petitioner restaurant assured the court that it would not use analogue paneer again.
