headline: Sowjanya case: What the Supreme Court said while ordering fresh investigation
text: The Supreme Court has ordered a de novo investigation into the 2012 rape and murder of 17-year-old Sowjanya in Karnataka’s Ujire, questioning why key leads were not pursued by the three agencies — local police, CID and CBI– that investigated the case. The apex court also pointed to DNA evidence that can still be used to identify the perpetrators. In a strongly worded judgment on Monday, September 21, the Supreme Court said the manner in which the investigation was conducted had caused “injustice to the victim” and that the possibility of the real culprit or culprits manipulating the investigation could not be ruled out. The Court ordered the Karnataka government to constitute a fresh Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by a senior police officer and comprising investigators familiar with modern investigative technology. Officers who were part of the earlier investigations by the Belthangady police, Karnataka CID or CBI have been barred from being part of the new team. The fresh investigation must be completed within three months, and a police report must be filed before the concerned court. A key factor in the Supreme Court’s decision was the existence of potential witnesses and physical evidence that could still help the investigation. The Court noted that on April 29, 2026, it directed Karnataka to protect eight potential witnesses identified by Sowjanya’s family. The state located the witnesses within three weeks. The Supreme Court said the state’s ability to locate the witnesses within three weeks “raises questions on the inability of 3 investigative agencies to examine these leads when it was timely.” The Court also referred to the evidence of Vinod J Lakkappan, Assistant Director of the Toxicology Division, Madivala, Bengaluru, who had conducted the DNA analysis in the case. Lakkappan had testified that hairs belonging to persons other than Santhosh Rao, who was earlier prosecuted for the crime, were found on Sowjanya’s churidar top, marked as Material Object 15. He had also stated that if suspicious persons were identified, their blood samples could still be collected and compared with the DNA material. The Supreme Court said this evidence showed that useful forensic evidence was still available. It held that the Karnataka High Court was wrong in concluding that evidence that had not been collected at the “golden hour” was unlikely to be available now. The Court also took note of the fact that Santhosh Rao was acquitted by the Sessions Court

headline: Rajya Sabha polls for 10 UP, 1 Uttarakhand seats on October 16
text: New Delhi, Sep 22 : The Election Commission of India (ECI) has announced the biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, along with a by-election for one seat from West Bengal, on October 16. Of the 11 seats going to the polls in the biennial elections, 10 are from Uttar Pradesh, and one is from Uttarakhand. The West Bengal election will be held to fill a casual vacancy in the Upper House. According to the schedule announced by the Election Commission, the notification for the elections will be issued on September 29, while the last date for filing nominations will be October 6. The scrutiny of nominations will be conducted on October 7, followed by the last date for withdrawal of candidature on October 9. Polling for the Rajya Sabha seats will be held on October 16 from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., while counting of votes will begin at 5 p.m. on the same day. In Uttar Pradesh, the terms of 10 sitting Rajya Sabha members are coming to an end. The members whose terms are expiring include Arun Singh, Geeta alias Chandraprabha, Brij Lal, Ram Gopal Yadav, Ramji Gautam, B.L. Verma, Seema Dwivedi, Dinesh Sharma and Hardeep Singh Puri. In Uttarakhand, the by-election is necessitated by the completion of the term of sitting Rajya Sabha member Naresh Bansal. The West Bengal seat is being filled through a by-election following the resignation of Rukmini Mallick from the Rajya Sabha. Mallick's resignation was the fourth such resignation by a Trinamool Congress MP since the Mamata Banerjee-led party was ousted from power in West Bengal. The October 16 elections will therefore cover both scheduled retirements and a casual vacancy in the Upper House. The ECI has laid out the complete election process from notification and nomination to polling and counting.

headline: Nagaon Bypoll: Congress-BJP Clash Erupts in Samaguri
text: A Correspondent Nagaon: Tension gripped Barma under the Samaguri Assembly segment on Sunday after a confrontation broke out between Congress and BJP supporters during the Congress campaign for the October 6 Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. The incident occurred when a Congress convoy carrying APCC president Gaurav Gogoi, MP Rakibul Hussain and party candidate Sibamoni Bora was passing through Barma on its way to an election rally at Lorimukh. BJP supporters allegedly waved black flags and raised "Go Back" slogans, following which stones were reportedly hurled at vehicles in the Congress convoy by unidentified persons. Police and paramilitary personnel intervened to control the situation. During the ensuing commotion, journalists covering the incident were allegedly assaulted, leaving media workers Bhaskar Das and Gulzar Hussain injured. Journalists subsequently staged a road blockade in protest, demanding action against those responsible. Tension continued in the wider Barma area following the incident. Later, former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister and Assam Congress observer Bhupesh Baghel, along with Gaurav Gogoi, Rakibul Hussain and Sibamoni Bora, reportedly lodged complaints at Nagaon Sadar Police Station seeking stringent action against those allegedly involved. Speaking outside the police station, Gogoi and Hussain sharply criticised the Assam government over the incident, with Hussain launching a strong attack on Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. The incident has added to the political tension surrounding the Nagaon Lok Sabha by-election. Police investigation into the alleged stone-pelting and assault is awaited. headline: Gurgaon spa crackdown: Probe widens to trafficking network, Jharsa couple held
text: GURGAON: What began as a crackdown on illegal activities at spa centres in Sector 90 has widened into a probe into an alleged organised trafficking network, with Gurgaon police tracing the trail to a Jharsa man who allegedly used websites, WhatsApp chats, PGs, guest houses and vehicles to facilitate the racket. Based on the leads provided by her, police apprehended Sahil, a Jharsa resident, along with his wife. headline: Coal Ministry rejects inadequate coal supply as cause of Punjab power crisis
text: New Delhi, Sep 13 : The Ministry of Coal on Sunday clarified that adequate coal has been made available to power plants in Punjab and attributed the state's reduced power generation to factors including low utilisation of its own plants, reported breakdowns at independent power plants and inadequate lifting of coal already offered by Coal India Limited (CIL). The clarification came after media reports attributed reduced generation at Punjab's thermal plants to plant outages and inadequate coal supply. The ministry said the government has already enabled coal movement to Punjab's independent power plants (IPPs) from PSPCL's captive mines and that CIL remains committed to ensuring uninterrupted coal supply for power generation in the state. It said higher utilisation of PSPCL's own plants, monitoring of breakdowns at IPPs and timely lifting of coal offered by CIL subsidiaries would help optimise power generation and address Punjab's requirements. The ministry said it has enabled supply of coal from PSPCL's captive Pachhwara Central Coal Mine to IPPs, subject to fulfilment of statutory payment obligations to the Jharkhand government. Coal from the Pachhwara mine can also be used by IPPs not owned by PSPCL, including Nabha Power Limited (Rajpura) and Talwandi Sabo Power Limited (Mansa), up to 50 per cent of annual production after meeting the requirements of specified end-use plants. The ministry said CIL supplies to Punjab's IPPs remain adequate. Against Nabha Power's average consumption of around 4.3 rakes per day over the last three days, rake supply averaged around five rakes per day. For Talwandi Sabo Power, against consumption of around 3.8 rakes per day, supply averaged around five rakes per day. During September 2026 so far, average supply has been around 4.9 rakes per day for Nabha Power and 4.1 rakes per day for Talwandi Sabo Power, higher than their average consumption, it said. Between April 2026 and September 11, production at the mine stood at 83.67 per cent of the annual target, while despatch was 68.44 per cent of the target. As of September 11, coal stock at PSPCL's plants stood at around 114 per cent of the normative requirement, indicating adequate coal availability, the ministry said.

headline: ‘Cage-like’ school: Days after attack, CJP inspects Jaipur schools, gives 7-day ultimatum to govt
text: ‘Cage-like’ school: Days after attack, CJP inspects Jaipur schools, gives 7-day ultimatum to govt CJP warned that it would launch a public agitation with local residents if the problems were not resolved within the stipulated period. The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Sunday inspected two government primary schools in the Shastri Nagar-Bhatta Basti area and alleged that both lacked basic infrastructure, giving the administration seven days to address the deficiencies. This comes after members of the group were allegedly attacked while visiting a government school in Bagru. In a statement, the CJP claimed that the completed building of one government primary school had remained closed for several years, forcing children from the area to travel long distances to attend classes. The group said the second school was operating from a makeshift, cage-like structure without a proper building or essential amenities. “Children cannot be expected to study in such deplorable conditions. The administration must provide safe and adequate educational facilities at both schools within seven days,” the CJP said. The group warned that it would launch a public agitation with local residents if the problems were not resolved within the stipulated period. It demanded the immediate reopening of the closed school building and the provision of a safe and adequate building, along with essential facilities, for the other school. The inspection came amid a controversy over a Rajasthan government directive restricting unauthorised entry into government schools. The order also cited legal provisions, including the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, that could be invoked in cases involving violations of children’s safety and privacy.

headline: KPSC ‘scam’: CID arrests IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar
text: The Criminal Investigation Department (CID) of the Karnataka Police on Saturday arrested IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in connection with the alleged irregularities in the recruitment of 400 veterinary officers, making him the first accused to be arrested. Mr. Gangwar, who served as Controller of Examinations at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) from February 2024 to March 2026, was taken into custody after two days of questioning. CID officials are likely to make several more arrests as the investigation progresses and the alleged roles of other officials, KPSC members, and candidates are also examined. The IAS officer was produced before the magistrate at his residence on Sunday evening and he was remanded in judicial custody. The CID will likely seek his custody on Monday. Investigators have allegedly found prima facie evidence pointing to Mr. Gangwar’s role in the alleged irregularities, including material relating to suspected manipulation of OMR sheets. The CID is also probing allegations that certain candidates were provided training at hotels and resorts as part of the recruitment process. The examination was held on January 8, 2026, and the final selection list was released on July 17. Following allegations of malpractice, the CID sent 329 OMR sheets of candidates who appeared for the examination to the State Forensic Science Laboratory for examination. Mr. Gangwar’s arrest follows days of scrutiny after the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) conducted searches in connection with the alleged KPSC scam. He had subsequently appeared before the CID and was questioned extensively regarding his tenure as Controller of Examinations. The CID has also questioned suspended KPSC Chairman Shivashankarappa S. headline: MPSC scraps drug inspector exam amid paper leak scandal, Opposition demands stern action
text: Mumbai, Aug 26 : Upping the ante over paper leak scandal, the Opposition parties, including NCP SP and Congress in Maharashtra announced that their fight against paper leaks will continue in future. Their demand for action against culprits followed an announcement by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) on late Tuesday evening, when it cancelled the recruitment process for the post of Drug Inspector (Group-B) under the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) department. The decision to cancel exams came in wake of a preliminary investigation into allegations of malpractices during the screening examination held on March 22. Both parties demanded that the guilty should be punished. They also made a strong case for the resignation of the MPSC chairman. NCP SP MLA Rohit Pawar said that the paper leak in the commission is not an ordinary incident but an extremely serious matter, and this is a question of the commission's credibility. "Therefore, the chairman of the commission should take moral responsibility and resign immediately. The government should also appoint a person with a clean image to the position of chairman of the commission. The ministers of the General Administration Department should also take a stand on behalf of the government and inform the people of the state about the facts," he added. He stated that the paper leak incident in the Drug Inspector exam has finally been cancelled by MPSC, adding that he had raised the issue of paper leak with full evidence, followed up with all necessary actions with the investigation agencies. He remarked that finally the investigation has concluded that there was indeed a paper leak. "Even though the commission has canceled the paper, their explanation that the paper was only with one student is absolutely unacceptable. According to the information we have received, the fact is that papers were sold for 40-40 lakhs through an agent racket operating across the state, and the commission is also aware of this fact," he said. He demanded that "Instead of trying to suppress this matter, the commission should make the inquiry report public, and what happened to the agent people whose names we had provided? Is anyone from the commission involved? Whose blessings are at play? They should also reveal this. If the commission tries to cover up this matter, we will not remain silent." headline: Two TMCP workers arrested for tearing Swami Vivekananda's poster at college in Bengal's Malda; one still absconding
text: Kolkata, Aug 26 : Two activists of Trinamool Congress' student wing, Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (TMCP), have been arrested for allegedly tearing up a poster with Swami Vivekananda's picture and also kicking that poster publicly at a college in Malda district of West Bengal. Recently, a video clip went viral on social media, where the three TMCP activists associated with Samsi College in Malda district, were seen tearing a poster of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) first and then trampling on it. As the video clip went viral, there were severe reactions over the actions of the TMCP activists. The police started an investigation in the matter and identified the three persons involved in the act. Thereafter, the police have arrested two of the three people involved in the matter namely Debojit Saha and Arijit Ravidas. The third accused in the matter, Tariq Anwar is still absconding. A police search has been launched to find him. Meanwhile, seeing the situation as untenable, Tariq had already posted a video message on social media apologising for his action. Giving his reactions in the matter, the ABVP's organisation president in Malda (North), Prasun Chowdhury, alleged that during the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress regime, TMCP activities had burnt down the picture of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore at Chanchal college also in Malda district. "They are yet to get over such nasty habits. On August 22, they tore the picture of Swami Vivekananda. They tried to send a bad signal by tearing and trampling on the ABVP flag. They also proudly uploaded this video on social media. On August 23, we filed a written complaint against the accused at Chanchal police station. The police took immediate action. Both of them have already been arrested. The main accused, Tariq, is still absconding," Chowdhury said. Demanding immediate arrest of Tariq, he also said that Swami Vivekananda is the idol of the nation and ABVP will never tolerate an insult of his picture. To recall, in 2024, TMCP activists had burnt down the picture of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore at Chanchal college in Malda district. The development resulted into massive protests led by then Leader of the Opposition in West Bengal Assembly and the current West Bengal Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari Facing all-round criticisms, the police were forced to arrest the then president of the TMCP's Chanchal College unit.

headline: Police Raid 18 Spa Centres In Gurugram, Detain 50 People, Including 30 Women - Daily Excelsior
text: Police Raid 18 Spa Centres In Gurugram, Detain 50 People, Including 30 Women Gurugram, Sep 19: Police have raided 18 spa centres at Sapphire 90 Mall in Gurugram and detained 30 women and 20 men, officials said on Saturday. The joint raid by the Haryana State Commission for Women and Gurugram police began... Gurugram, Sep 19: Police have raided 18 spa centres at Sapphire 90 Mall in Gurugram and detained 30 women and 20 men, officials said on Saturday. The joint raid by the Haryana State Commission for Women and Gurugram police began on Friday at 10:00 pm and continued until 3:00 am on Saturday, officials said. According to police, during the simultaneous raids, they found prima facie evidence of suspected illegal activities in 8 of the 18 spa centres. Police are now examining seized electronic, digital, physical, and documentary evidence to uncover the network and the roles of the owners, operators, managers and facilitators. Police said some spa centres were locked, but officers managed to open them and discovered men and women in compromising positions. "Thirty women and twenty men were found at the premises. Police are questioning the women to ascertain their circumstances and identify any possible chain, network, or facilitators of such activities," a senior police officer said. Police said they are also verifying the role of the men present at the spas, and appropriate legal action will follow based on the evidence. Gurugram Police said they maintain zero tolerance towards organised illegal activities carried out under the guise of legitimate commercial establishments. They said police acted on suo motu cognisance of suspected illegal activities in spa centres. Police said the joint raid was conducted in the presence of Gurugram Police, Haryana State Commission for Women Chairperson Usha Priyadarshini and her team, and the Duty Magistrate. Police said further investigation is underway. (AGENCIES)

headline: BJP protests in Shikaripura; accuses Karnataka government of neglecting farmers
text: Shivamogga : , Sep 18 (IANS) The BJP staged a protest in Shikaripura town in Shivamogga district against what it alleged were the Karnataka government's anti-farmer policies. BJP State President, B.Y. Vijayendra, accused the government of failing to understand and address the problems faced by farmers in the state. Addressing the protest, Vijayendra claimed the agitation was aimed at warning the government about the hardships faced by farmers and demanding that it take steps to resolve their problems. Referring to the problems faced by farmers living along forest fringes in the context of the Gadgil and Kasturirangan committee reports, Vijayendra said it could not be accepted that these committees were constituted only on the basis of orders from the High Court or Supreme Court of any state. He said the Gadgil and Kasturirangan committees were constituted during the tenure of the previous Congress-led UPA government. As a result of the impact of these reports, farmers living in forest-fringe areas are now forced to come onto the streets and protest, he alleged. headline: Wanted Jharkhand Maoist Brijesh Ganjhu killed in encounter with UP ATS
text: RANCHI: The chief of the banned Maoist organisation 'Tritiya Prastuti Committee' (TPC), Brijesh Ganjhu (also known as Gopal Singh Bhokta), in Jharkhand, was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh ATS. IG (STF) Prem Gautam briefed Jharkhand Police on the entire matter and confirmed the killing on Sunday. A combined reward of Rs 30 lakh had been announced for Brijesh’s arrest by the Jharkhand government and the National Investigation Agency (NIA) before he died. The Jharkhand government had placed a bounty of Rs 25 lakh, while the NIA had announced a reward of Rs 5 lakh. According to senior Police officials in Jharkhand, the encounter between the ATS and Brijesh took place early Sunday morning at Lanka Maidan near Tengra More in the Ramnagar police station area of Varanasi. After sustaining a gunshot wound, he was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. According to the UP ATS, they received intelligence inputs that Brijesh was in Varanasi and was expected to pass through a specific route on a motorcycle in the morning. Acting on the information, the ATS team laid a trap in the Tengra Mor area. At around 5:00 AM, the team signalled Brijesh, who was approaching on a motorcycle, to stop. Instead of stopping, Brijesh allegedly opened fire on the ATS team, triggering a gun battle. He was hit during the ATS's firing in retaliation. The team rushed him to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The UP ATS also informed that an accomplice managed to flee the spot during the encounter. The ATS recovered two pistols, several live cartridges, and spent shell casings from Brijesh at the site. During the exchange of fire, bullets fired by Brijesh struck the bulletproof jackets of ATS DSP Vipin Rai and Head Constable Nitendra Krishna. Both are reported to be safe. Brijesh had long been on the radar of security agencies. He was declared wanted about eight years ago in connection with a terror-funding case investigated by the NIA. Following the ATS operation, investigations are now underway regarding the cases registered against him and the network linked to his Maoist activities. The police are also trying to ascertain how long Brijesh had been living in Varanasi and who his contacts were. headline: J-K minors rape & abortion death: CM Abdullah directs expedited inquiry - The Tribune
text: J-K minor's rape & abortion death: CM Abdullah directs expedited inquiry The 15-year-old was 'raped repeatedly' by a teacher in her school for the last few months, resulting in pregnancy and her death following an abortion bid Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday directed the school education department to expedite its inquiry into the Kishtwar schoolgirl rape case so that stringent and exemplary action can be ensured. “Chief Minister today directed the School Education Department to complete its inquiry into the heinous Kishtwar incident concerning a young schoolgirl expeditiously, so that stringent and exemplary action can be ensured in this matter,” Abdullah posted on his official X handle. A 15-year-old girl was allegedly raped repeatedly by a teacher in her school for the last few months, resulting in pregnancy and her death following an abortion bid in Jammu and Kashmir’s Kishtwar district, prompting police to arrest the accused and his brother on Friday. The girl’s death late Thursday evening triggered protests across Chatroo and several other parts of the district. Police have arrested accused Khalid Ahmed Sheikh, a Teacher Grade-II and the in-charge headmaster of the Middle School Bumalpora in Inderwal, along with his brother, officials said. The girl died while being taken towards Jammu for an abortion, sources said. Her body and that of the stillborn child were subsequently taken to her village, triggering protests in Chatroo and other parts of Kishtwar on Friday.

headline: Nationwide protests on August 26 in support of Haryana municipal employees’ strike - The Tribune
text: Nationwide protests on August 26 in support of Haryana municipal employees’ strike AISGEF condemns arrests of striking workers, accuses Haryana Government of failing to implement May 13 agreement The All India State Government Employees Federation (AISGEF) has strongly condemned the Haryana Government for allegedly failing to implement the agreement reached with the Municipal Employees Union Haryana on May 13 and for arresting striking employees at various places. The Federation has announced demonstrations across all states on August 26 against what it termed the government’s “breach of promise” and the arrests, and to express solidarity with the ongoing strike by municipal employees in Haryana. AISGEF national president Subhash Lamba said the demonstrations would protest against the Haryana Government’s “extremely neglectful and hostile attitude” towards sanitation workers, who, he said, were among the most socially and economically marginalised sections of society. “Instead of implementing the May 13 agreement and bringing an end to the stalemate with the Urban Local Bodies and Fire Department employees, the government resorted to police repression and arrests. Hundreds of striking employees have been arrested in different districts, including a large number of women employees,” he said. AISGEF general secretary A Sreekumar said there was no legal impediment to regularising employees who had been working on contract for 10 to 15 years. “The contract system could not be abolished for want of political will,” he said.

headline: Unauthorised entry won’t be allowed in Haryana govt. schools: Education Minister
text: Haryana Education Minister Mahipal Dhanda on Monday said unauthorised entry will not be allowed in government schools in the State. His remarks came after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists visited government schools in several villages in the State over the past two weeks as part of its ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign. They alleged deficiencies in infrastructure, cleanliness, availability of teachers, and quality of midday meals. Addressing reporters in Hansi, Mr. Dhanda termed government schools a “national heritage” and said the “safety of students cannot be compromised for political publicity”. He said anyone visiting a government school should do so in coordination with members of the panchayat and the school management committee (SMC). “The sarpanch is there, elected representatives of the panchayat are there. There is an SMC in all schools. Anyone visiting must take along SMC and panchayat members,” the Minister said, adding that responsibility would be fixed if disturbances occur on the school premises during such visits. Mr. Dhanda said people with genuine complaints about a government school should first approach the sarpanch and other responsible authorities. CJP national core committee member Sudhir Sangwan told The Hindu that the group had so far visited 16 to 17 schools across districts such as Jhajjar, Bhiwani, Charkhi Dadri, and Fatehabad. ‘Teacher suspended’ He claimed that a teacher was suspended in Bhiwani after a CJP activist raised concerns over the quality of foodgrains supplied for the midday meal. He added that CJP activists plan to visit 100 more schools in the State over the next fortnight, with the objective of highlighting shortcomings and demanding greater accountability and better execution. ‘Invited by villagers’ Reacting to the Minister’s remarks, Mr. Sangwan said CJP activists entered schools only after they were invited by villagers who wanted improvements in their schools. He questioned the effectiveness of the SMCs, saying though they were set up to function as watchdogs, their members were often inactive or lacked the capacity to monitor schools effectively. Mr. Sangwan also shared on X an order issued by the Hansi district administration restricting unauthorised entry into schools and criticised the move as an attempt to prevent people from documenting the condition of government schools. headline: Karnataka to hold special Assembly session on drought, Kasturirangan report on September 21-23: Dy CM Parameshwara
text: ANI 04 Sep 2026, 00:28 GMT+10 Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], September 3 (ANI): Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara on Thursday said the state Cabinet has decided to convene a special Assembly session on September 21, 22 and 23 to discuss the severe drought situation, problems faced by farmers and the contentious Kasturirangan report. Parameshwara said farmers in the state are facing difficulties due to several ongoing issues and that there have not been sufficient opportunities to discuss them in the legislature. 'The Cabinet has decided to call a special session on September 21, 22 and 23. The farmers of the state are facing difficulties due to several ongoing issues, and there have not been enough opportunities to discuss these matters in the House,' he said. He added that Karnataka is facing a severe drought this year, describing it as an unprecedented situation whose impact extends beyond agriculture to the state's wider economy and food security. 'This year, the state is facing a severe drought. After nearly 150 years, such a drought has occurred. Its impact is not only on the lives of farmers but also on the wider community of the state, including the economy and food security. Therefore, we want to have a detailed discussion on these issues, and that is why we are holding this special session,' Parameshwara said. The Deputy Chief Minister said the Kasturirangan report would also be taken up for detailed discussion during the special session. He said the Karnataka government has rejected the report on several occasions, but the debate surrounding its recommendations continues. We will also use this special session for the purpose of discussing the Kasturirangan Report,' he said. headline: Suvendu leads Vande Mataram rally, vows crackdown on JU 'threat culture'
text: Suvendu leads Vande Mataram rally, vows crackdown on JU 'threat culture' West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Friday warned a section of Jadavpur University (JU) students against what he described as a “threat culture” prevailing on the campus and said his government would end it. The chief minister said his government would restore nationalism and the state's cultural traditions inside and outside the university campus. He accused the erstwhile TMC government of allowing nationalism to fade from public consciousness during its 15-year rule, while alleging that West Bengal’s traditions had been destroyed in the 34-year-long Left Front era. The chief minister was addressing a programme in which ‘Vande Mataram’ was sung by 10,000 people outside the JU's south Kolkata campus. Adhikari alleged that the university had long been influenced by communists who, according to him, had distanced students from Independence Day, Republic Day, Indian and Bengali traditions and the country's cultural heritage. “In their homes, you would never find pictures of Rabindranath Tagore, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay or Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar," he claimed. The CM also criticised the TMC, alleging that the party had reached an understanding with sections of students for electoral gains. headline: Rift, dissent and more: The many Election Commission controversies over the years
text: Rift, dissent and more: The many Election Commission controversies over the years The latest ECI controversy is not new: the poll panel has faced scrutiny under successive governments over internal rifts and alleged overreach. India's three-member poll panel finds itself embroiled in a controversy amid speculations of rift between chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (CEC) and two election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. After a news report that Sandhu and Joshi had objected to certain key decisions of the Election Commission of India (ECI), including those related to the contentious Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, opposition parties called for Kumar's resignation and the Supreme Court's intervention, also questioning the integrity of the poll process. The poll body rejected charges of one-sided decision-making, saying differences are part of the deliberation process but all ECI decisions are unanimous. The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) distanced itself from the controversy. Deep Dive It's not the first time ECI is in the eye of the storm. In its journey through successive governments—from a one-member commission to three members and beyond— the poll panel and some of India's CECs have drawn constant scrutiny over allegations of internal rift and overreach. The TN Seshan episode One of the major controversies broke out in the 1990s, when TN Seshan was the CEC. Previously, the Election Commission had traditionally functioned as a one-member body, with the CEC effectively exercising the institution's authority. Two election commissioners were appointed in October 1989, but the arrangement lasted only until January 1990. The commission returned to a single-member structure until 1993. Then the Narasimha Rao government appointed MS Gill and GVG Krishnamurthy as election commissioners. Seshan challenged the move, arguing that the additional commissioners diluted the CEC's authority. The Supreme Court rejected his challenge in July 1995, holding that Article 324 of the Constitution permits a multi-member Election Commission and that the other commissioners were not merely advisers to the CEC but members of the Commission with a role in its decision-making. The tensions did not end there. In 1995, while Seshan was away in the US, he authorised a deputy election commissioner to hold the "current charge" of the commission. Gill and Krishnamurthy objected, arguing that Seshan could not effectively bypass the other constitutional commissioners by handing charge to a subordinate official. Kolkata, Aug 29 (IANS) West Bengal Minister for Municipal Affairs and Urban Development Agnimitra Paul on Saturday evening called for custodial interrogation of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee in connection with the conspiracies behind the rape and murder of a junior doctor at state‑run R.G. Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata in August 2024. Paul's remarks came on the same day Kolkata Police registered a suo motu FIR against Mamata Banerjee at Hastings Police Station in South Kolkata over alleged violation of a Calcutta High Court order during the foundation day rally of Trinamool Congress' student wing, Trinamool Chhatra Parishad (TMCP), on Friday. Paul attended an administrative review meeting at the Kolkata Municipal Corporation headquarters on Saturday afternoon. Speaking to media afterwards, she said custodial interrogation of Mamata Banerjee was necessary in the R.G. Kar case. "The FIR registered at Hastings Police Station is justified. One of the major wrongdoings committed by the previous Chief Minister was the attempt to cover up the death of the junior lady doctor at R.G. Kar. In the FIR filed at Hastings Police Station, Paul said Mamata Banerjee could not disregard court orders. Such blatant disregard towards law cannot be tolerated," she said.

headline: Assam Congress holds Statewide Padayatras against proposed Kaziranga ESZ reduction
text: Assam Congress holds Statewide Padayatras against proposed Kaziranga ESZ reduction The Assam Congress on Saturday held padayatras across the state to protest the proposed reduction of the Eco-Sensitive Zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park. Congress leaders and workers took part in demonstrations across several districts, including Sonitpur, Lakhimpur, Hailakandi, Karimganj, Tinsukia, Karbi Anglong and Golaghat. Protesters marched through district headquarters, raising slogans against the government and demanding that the proposal to reduce the ESZ be withdrawn. In Guwahati, Leader of Opposition in the state Assembly Wazed Ali Choudhury, former MP Ripun Bora, state women's wing president Mira Borthakur and other Congress leaders participated in the protest. Police stopped the protesters from leaving the Congress office in Dispur. Party workers subsequently attempted to cross the barricades and move onto the streets. Choudhury said the protests would continue until the government reverses its decision. “We will not allow the BJP-led government to damage Kaziranga National Park, which is our pride. We will not relent till the decision is reversed,” he said. Bora and Borthakur said the Congress would continue raising the issue across Assam and seek to increase public awareness. They also accused Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of compromising the interests of Kaziranga to benefit large corporate groups. The controversy centres on the Assam government’s proposal to approach the Centre seeking a reduction in the ESZ around Kaziranga from the default 10-km zone to between 1 km and 3 km. Activities within an ESZ are prohibited, regulated or permitted under prescribed rules depending on their nature. Opposition parties and environmental activists have alleged that reducing the buffer zone could encourage commercial mining and tourism around Kaziranga and the adjoining Karbi Anglong hills, an important elephant corridor. Environmentalists have also warned that a narrower ESZ could increase human-animal conflict and put pressure on the biodiversity of the UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sarma has defended the proposal, saying it is intended to protect the interests and livelihoods of villagers living within the ESZ. with inputs from PTI

headline: Kerala Congress (Joseph) Opposes Proposal for Muvattupuzha District
text: Recently, at an event in Muvattupuzha, Congress MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan urged Chief Minister V D Satheesan to consider forming a new district comprising parts of Ernakulam, Idukki and Kottayam districts Idukki: The Kerala Congress (Joseph) faction has opposed a proposal to form a new Muvattupuzha district by including Thodupuzha, with Water Resources Minister Mons Joseph saying on Saturday that the issue has no relevance at present. Recently, at an event in Muvattupuzha, Congress MLA Mathew Kuzhalnadan urged Chief Minister V D Satheesan to consider forming a new district comprising parts of Ernakulam, Idukki and Kottayam districts. Satheesan, in his reply, said the request would be considered and that the government would appoint a Delimitation Commission. The proposal, however, has been opposed by the Kerala Congress (Joseph) faction, which has a strong presence in Thodupuzha, currently part of Idukki district. Kerala Congress (Joseph) is a key constituent of UDF. Speaking to reporters, Mons Joseph said removing Thodupuzha from Idukki would amount to "tearing away the very soul and heart of Idukki district". He said party chairman P J Joseph had opposed the proposal when it was first raised. "Earlier, when former Muvattupuzha MLA Joseph Vazhackan raised this issue in the Assembly, it was discussed and dropped as an abandoned matter," he said. Joseph said there was no objection to examining whether there was any possibility of reconsidering the proposal, but such a matter should not be discussed on a public platform. He said the MLA had the right to submit a proposal to the chief minister and the CM had the right to respond to it. "However, all these matters must be examined in detail by the UDF leadership and the state-level UDF committee. When it is discussed in the UDF, the Kerala Congress will state its opinion. At present, this issue has no relevance," Joseph said. Muvattupuzha is part of the Ernakulam district, located on the eastern side, close to Idukki district. Earlier, MLA Kuzhalnadan had said that a Muvattupuzha district is necessary for the development of the region, as the funds granted to the Ernakulam district mostly concentrate on urban development, including Kochi city.

headline: No room for speculation in Disha Salian death case, CBI will investigate: CM Fadnavis
text: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said the CBI will investigate the death of Disha Salian and cautioned against speculation after the agency registered an FIR in the case. Speaking to reporters after a state Cabinet meeting, Fadnavis said he had not yet seen the FIR but noted that the Bombay High Court had directed that the case be transferred to the CBI. "We should now see what the CBI investigates. It is not appropriate for us to engage in speculation," he said. The CBI registered the FIR without naming any accused, in compliance with the high court's directions on a petition filed by Salian's father, Satish Salian. On September 2, the high court ordered a CBI probe into Salian's death and criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR for six years. The court observed that the police investigation had raised more questions than answers. Salian, who had worked as the manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 12th floor of a building in Mumbai's Malad area. Six days later, on June 14, Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence, triggering a nationwide uproar and a subsequent CBI probe into his death. In his petition, Salian's father named several senior politicians, Bollywood actors and police officials whom he wanted investigated in connection with his daughter's death. (With inputs from PTI)

headline: Indian Candidate Sanghani registers historic victory at ICA elections
text: IFFCO Chairman Dileep Sanghani has been elected as an At-Large Director on the Global Board of the International Cooperative Alliance (ICA), marking a significant achievement for India and its rapidly expanding cooperative movement. Sanghani secured 526 votes in the ICA Global Board election held on September 15 at the ICA General Assembly in Panama City. He was India’s sole candidate in the At-Large Director election, which featured cooperative leaders from several countries competing for 15 positions on the 30-member ICA Global Board. With 526 votes, Sanghani emerged as the third-highest vote-getter overall and the top vote-getter among candidates from Asia, Europe and Africa. His election gives India direct representation on the highest governing body of the global cooperative movement and is being seen as an important recognition of the country’s growing role in international cooperation. Sanghani’s candidature was backed by a sizeable Indian cooperative delegation, with India carrying around 25 votes. The campaign also received support from cooperative organisations and leaders across several countries. His international profile received a major boost following the ICA Global Cooperative Conference and General Assembly hosted in New Delhi in 2024. Sanghani played a prominent role in the event, which brought cooperative leaders from across the world to India. The New Delhi gathering was also associated with the launch of the International Year of Cooperatives 2025. A cooperative leader with more than four decades of public and institutional experience, Sanghani served two terms as a Member of the Gujarat Legislative Assembly before being elected to the Lok Sabha from Amreli, where he served four terms. He has also held several ministerial responsibilities in the Gujarat Government. He has also served as President of the National Cooperative Union of India (NCUI) and currently heads IFFCO as its Chairman. The ICA candidate profile highlights his leadership of IFFCO, which comprises 35,700 primary cooperative societies representing more than 50 million farmers. Sanghani entered the Panama election with a campaign centred on strengthening global cooperation through collaboration, innovation, digital transformation and inclusive growth. He also emphasised the need to ensure that technological advancement remains rooted in the basic values of the cooperative movement. The ICA Global Board consists of 30 members, including the President, four regional Vice Presidents, representatives of eight sectoral organisations, the Presidents of the Youth and Gender Equality Committees, and 15 At-Large Directors elected directly by ICA members. headline: India's citizen-led school audits test limits of activism
text: The Indian activist movement dubbing itself the "Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)" shot to national prominence in May by leading weeks-long protests over a scandal involving highly competitive entrance exams. The student-led campaign put the government under intense political pressure and ended with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July. Now, the CJP is taking aim at India's government schools, organizing volunteer visits to classrooms, documenting conditions and demanding accountability for problems. Launched on August 15, Independence Day in India, the campaign asks parents, students and volunteers to inspect schools and record basic facilities including toilets, drinking water, electricity, classroom furniture and school buildings. The CJP has said the findings will be used to pressure authorities to make improvements. The initial target is to audit 100 rural government schools over two months. It has also proposed giving recognition to village leaders who improve their schools. Unlike the first campaign, which was based on street protests, the school audits require a more sustained form of local activism. Volunteers are expected to work consistently at the local level, document conditions and follow up with officials, parents and communities. The organization is dealing with different layers of the Indian administration. Responsibility for government schools is divided between state governments, local administrations and elected village bodies. The CJP is therefore set to tackle different rules and political interests across the country. India has over a million government schools, according to Education Ministry data. They make up nearly 70% of all schools in the country but serve less than half of its 247 million schoolchildren. CJP: 'We are not afraid' That scale has given CJP a vast field for its campaign. But it has also brought a new set of challenges. The authorities are raising questions regarding rules and locations for the CJP scrutiny, as well as safeguards when children are present. The response is already varying from state to state. Some authorities have ordered their own inspections, while others have restricted access or taken police action against CJP volunteers. Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan states have objected to school visits carried out without permission. headline: WATCH: Mumbai Auto Drivers Celebrate As Maharashtra CM Fadnavis Gives One-Year Extension To Learn Marathi
text: Non-Marathi auto-rickshaw drivers in Mumbai broke into celebrations on Friday after the Maharashtra government granted them an additional year to learn Marathi. Drivers were seen dancing and expressing gratitude towards Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, calling the decision a major relief. The extension comes after representatives of auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers' organisations met Fadnavis and raised concerns about the difficulties many drivers were facing in meeting the Marathi language requirement within the earlier deadline. Drivers dance in celebration Videos from the celebrations showed groups of auto-rickshaw drivers dancing and cheering after the announcement. Many described the extension as an opportunity to learn Marathi without the pressure of having to complete the requirement immediately. The government has maintained that people working in Mumbai should have functional knowledge of Marathi. However, driver representatives argued that a large number of non-Marathi-speaking drivers were willing to learn the language but faced difficulties related to access to teachers, certification and other administrative requirements. BJP Dhadak Kamgar Union leader Abhijit Rane welcomed the decision and said the drivers had never opposed learning Marathi. Speaking to ANI, Rane said, "I feel that more than 50 per cent of people still had to learn Marathi." He claimed that representatives had highlighted the challenges faced by drivers across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), where, according to him, around 3.5 to 4 lakh people drive rickshaws, with the number of drivers rising further because of multiple shifts. 'They want to learn Marathi' Rane stressed that the extension should not be viewed as an attempt by drivers to avoid the language requirement. "All our non-Maharashtrian rickshaw and taxi drivers and owners have a great enthusiasm that they want to learn Marathi, and now they will learn it in a good way," he said. He also praised Fadnavis for considering their concerns, saying, "Devendra ji is a sensible leader; he understands our hard work, labour and our enthusiasm to learn Marathi. There was no hesitation from our side to learn Marathi. Marathi is a simple language." Language rule faces legal questions The one-year grace period comes amid a legal challenge to the Maharashtra government's notification making working knowledge of Marathi compulsory for auto-rickshaw, taxi and app-based cab drivers. Trinamool Congress leader Majeed Memon welcomed the extension but questioned whether language requirements could affect a person's constitutional right to earn a livelihood. headline: Is Fadnavis shifting to national politics? He says...
text: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has firmly denied speculation about a move to national politics, reiterating his dedication to state development and his role in Maharashtra. Key Points - Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis denied rumours of a shift to national politics. - Fadnavis affirmed his commitment to serving the people of Maharashtra. - His Delhi visit was focused on discussing state development projects with the Centre. - He stated that Prime Minister Modi has entrusted him with Maharashtra's responsibility. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday dismissed speculation about a possible shift to national politics following his visit to Delhi, saying he was in the capital to pursue the state's development projects. Speaking to reporters in the national capital after meeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Fadnavis maintained that the people of Maharashtra and the central leadership had entrusted him with the state's responsibility, which he would continue to fulfil. Fadnavis On Political Speculation And State Focus "Whether I am in Delhi or Mumbai, people keep speculating. I feel many have nothing else to do, so they enjoy discussing me. Let them enjoy it," he said. He said that the people of Maharashtra and Modi have handed him the responsibility of the state, and he will continue to serve the state. Asked about the Bharatiya Janata Party's new national team, Fadnavis said, "I have not seen the team yet, to be honest. You know that I have just come out of a meeting. But if the team has been announced and someone from Maharashtra is in it, we are happy. I will look at the entire team once and then speak about it." The chief minister said he was in Delhi to discuss several Maharashtra projects with the Centre, including infrastructure, industrial development and pending approvals. When asked who was behind the speculation that he should be sent to Delhi, he said, "Many people feel that I should go to Delhi. I tell everyone that I am in Mumbai only."

headline: Jharkhand Cancels Recruitment Exams: Why Govt Took The Call As DN Mahto Ends Hunger Strike
text: The Jharkhand government’s decision to cancel the JSSC-CGL examination and all examinations conducted by TDPL has brought an end to a prolonged student agitation, with student leader Devendra Nath Mahto ending his hunger strike at Sadar Hospital in Ranchi. Mahto called off the strike in the presence of Jharkhand Ministers Dipika Pandey Singh and Irfan Ansari after Chief Minister Hemant Soren announced the cancellations. The move came after students raised concerns over the recruitment examination process, paper leaks and irregularities. Mahto said the hunger strike had entered its 16th day, while the wider struggle began on July 2. He said a CID inquiry was launched on July 28 following a July 20 meeting with Soren. “The investigation is being conducted thoroughly, sparing no one, not even high-profile figures like the former Chief Secretary and the JPSC Chairman.” He thanked the Jharkhand government, Soren, Rahul Gandhi, Dipika Pandey, Irfan Ansari, students, media, social activists and people who supported protesters during the agitation. Jharkhand cancellation decision follows prolonged student agitation Mahto said cancelling the JSSC-CGL examination was a difficult decision because the recruitment process had already reached the joining stage and many candidates may have secured positions. He, however, described the government’s move as a bold step taken in the interest of students. He said, “Today marks a huge victory for Jharkhand. While I am now suspending my protest, my struggle for reform will continue.” He demanded stronger laws and reforms to prevent paper leaks and ensure every examination is monitored and audited. “Every examination must be monitored, every examination must be audited, and there must be a clear certificate for every examination and at every stage; we will continue to struggle for this,” Mahto said, adding that legislative or constitutional changes should be considered if required. Jharkhand ministers confirm hunger strike has ended Minister Irfan Ansari said Mahto, Umme Habiba and Rahul Kranti voluntarily ended their hunger strike and were given juice to break their fast. “The government has accepted all their demands; these were significant demands and a major issue. He said all three were healthy, with normal blood pressure and blood sugar levels, and that there were no issues. headline: WB CM Suvendu crushes cough syrup bottles with roadroller
text: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari made a powerful statement against drug trafficking by crushing 2 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup in Balurghat, reinforcing the state's commitment to a drug-free India and improved border security. Key Points - West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari crushed 2 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup in Balurghat. - The action sends a strong message against drug smuggling and aims to combat youth drug addiction. - Improved coordination between BSF and state police has led to significant drug seizures along the Bangladesh border. - The seized Phensedyl cough syrup was intended for smuggling into neighbouring Bangladesh. - CM Adhikari also announced the establishment of a new medical college in Balurghat. West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on September 2, Wednesday, drove a roadroller over nearly 2 lakh bottles of banned cough syrup in Balurghat, in a stern message against drug smuggling. Accompanied by Union minister and Balurghat MP Sukanta Majumdar, Adhikari drove the road roller and crushed the bottles lined up outside the SP office of the Dakshin Dinajpur district. State Health Minister Shardwat Mukhopadhyay was also present during the programme. Combating Drug Addiction Among Youth The CM said the destruction was part of efforts to keep the country's youth away from drug addiction. "My first message through this is that we have to bring the youth out of drug addiction," he said. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's campaign for a drug-free India, Adhikari said the initiative was "extremely relevant and timely". "We have seized a large quantity of narcotics since our government came to power. Over the past four months, these drugs have been seized in joint operations by the BSF and the police. "We destroyed them symbolically today. We will make West Bengal drug-free -- that is the message," he said. Enhanced Border Security and Coordination The chief minister said that coordination between the BSF and the state police had improved along the Bangladesh border, stating that the seized Phensedyl cough syrup bottles were allegedly meant to be smuggled into the neighbouring country. "Earlier, there was no coordination between the BSF and the police in Dakshin Dinajpur because the BSF was treated as an enemy. In the last four months, these narcotics have been recovered through joint operations," he said. text: Mumbai, Sep 2 : Maharashtra's Senior Nationalist Congress Party minister Chhagan Bhujbal, along with Shiv Sena ministers Sanjay Rathod and Gulabrao Patil, on Tuesday walked out of the meeting of the cabinet sub-committee on OBC issues, boycotting the gathering, claiming lack of funds and administrative bias against the community. The walkout led to the committee chairman and BJP minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule reprimanding officials, stating that the Finance Department must immediately disburse the budget-approved funds for OBCs to the OBC Department. Suvendu Adhikari defended Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, also known as Bageshwar Baba, in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly on Thursday, days after the preacher urged vegetarian food during the upcoming Durga Pujas. He also asked police to arrest people who burnt the preacher’s photographs outside Bhawanipore police station. Adhikari said Shastri had put forward his views but had not imposed them on anyone. “A saint had come to Liluah, he spoke like a saint about nationalism, Akhand Bharat and on culture. Those who want to accept will accept, and those who do not want will not. He did not impose it on anyone. I saw a number of people burning his photographs outside Bhawanipore police station. I am directing the CP (Commissioner of Police) from here that these people need to be arrested,” Adhikari said in the Assembly as The Hindu reported. Shastri’s comment triggered debate over food choices during Durga Puja festivities. People across the State objected, saying those from outside the region could not lecture Bengalis on dietary preferences. Shastri’s Puja Appeal The self-styled godman made the appeal on September 6. He said, “I want to appeal to the Hindus of Bengal that during Navratri, even if you don’t keep the idols of the Goddess, do not sell non-veg near the idols,” during a religious event at Liluah in Howrah. headline: Karnataka assembly adjourned over BJP uproar on poacher killing
text: Karnataka assembly adjourned over BJP uproar on poacher killing The killing of three people in an alleged exchange of fire with Forest Department personnel on August 15 in Chamarajanagar led to uproar in the Karnataka Legislative Council on Monday followed by adjournment. The opposition BJP termed the killing of three suspected poachers as a murder committed by the government. Seeking an immediate discussion and a reply from the state Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy, Leader of the Opposition Chalavadi Narayanaswamy demanded justice for the families of the victims. "Three precious lives were snatched. It is a murder committed by the government only. Those killed were minorities. Justice should be done to the families," he said. In reply, Minister Basavaraj Raya Reddy said the state government was ready to discuss this, but the opposition has to give a notice for it. Chairman Saleem Ahmed's appeal to the opposition BJP to stay calm could not fetch any result. The BJP was adamant for a detailed discussion and resorted to sloganeering inside the House. Finding the Council not in order, Ahmed adjourned the House. Three alleged poachers were killed in an exchange of fire with forest personnel in the Datti forest area under the Shagya range here on Saturday, prompting Chief Minister D K Shivakumar to order a magisterial inquiry into the incident. The incident occurred in the dense forest area falling under the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary when forest personnel, acting on information about hunting, encountered four men, Minister Ramalinga Reddy had said. Two of them died on the spot. One person was injured and was taken to hospital, where he reportedly died. One person allegedly fled the spot, the minister said.

headline: Congress rejects Mamata Banerjee’s alliance pitch for Bengal bypolls
text: The Congress has reportedly rejected an alliance proposal from former West Bengal Chief Minister and Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee for the upcoming bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar, deciding instead to contest the elections on its own. According to reports, Mamata Banerjee had reached out to Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal with a proposal for an electoral understanding. However, there has been no official confirmation from either party regarding the reported conversation. The Congress has already announced its candidates for the high-stakes bypolls, signalling its decision to go solo in both constituencies. ‘Trinamool is a liability’ West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee chief Subhankar Sarkar said the party remained open to working with political forces ideologically opposed to the BJP. However, he indicated that an alliance with the Trinamool Congress could prove detrimental to the Congress at this stage. Sarkar pointed to the ongoing dispute surrounding the Trinamool’s party symbol and suggested that any adverse development in the matter could affect the political momentum of a potential alliance. He also said the Congress had witnessed the Trinamool’s recent political challenges and internal turmoil following its defeat in the West Bengal Assembly elections earlier this year. According to reports, Mamata Banerjee had proposed that the Congress contest the Nandigram seat while seeking Congress support in Rejinagar, a minority-dominated Assembly constituency in Murshidabad. Bypolls scheduled for October 6 The Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls are scheduled to be held on October 6 and are expected to be closely watched political contests. Nandigram, in particular, is likely to witness an intense battle after the seat was vacated by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who retained the Bhabanipur seat in Kolkata, where he defeated Mamata Banerjee. The bypolls will be the first major electoral test in West Bengal following the BJP’s rise to power in the state, with the Congress, Trinamool Congress and BJP expected to closely assess the political mood ahead of the contest.

headline: MP Hooch Tragedy: 11 Dead, 35 Hospitalised; 3 Officials Suspended, Probe Ordered
text: At least 11 people died and 35 were hospitalised in Sagar after consuming suspected toxic liquor, prompting official suspensions and a probe. At least 11 people, mostly aged 28 t0 50, died in Madhya Pradesh’s Sagar district after consuming suspected toxic liquor, officials said on Sunday. Around three dozen people have been battling for life in the district hospital in Sagar and Bundelkhand Medical College Hospital, officials said. The incident took place in the villages of Nauroja and Dogra under Banda police station limits. “The incident came to light around 4.30 am on Sunday”, Sagar district collector Pratibha Pal said. Preliminary investigation suggested that the deaths were caused due to the consumption of toxic methyl alcohol, suspected to be supplied by Uttar Pradesh-based illicit liquor manufacturing gang, officials said. Sagar district superintendent of police Anurag Sujaniya said that the source of the spurious liquor has been found to be Lalitpur in Uttar Pradesh. Probe is on to identify the local supply chain and the people involved in the operation, police said. Sagar district borders Lalitpur district of Uttar Pradesh. According to the police officer, around a dozen people have been detained for interrogation in connection with the incident. Doctors have started screening people in these two villages to identify such cases to provide them treatment, officials said. The deceased have been identified as Golu alias Chaman Lodhi (45), Digvijay Lodhi (28), Kartar Singh Lodhi (30), Ajyar Singh Lodhi (56), Roshan Lodhi (30), Rajendra Lodhi (32), Harnam Ray (42), Uttam Nathyu Nayak (42), Sumer Singh Dangi (47), Raj Kumar Lodhi (47), and Surendra Ahirwar (35). Three excise officials have been suspended following the incident. The excise officials who were suspended are Kirti Dubey, Assistant Commissioner (Excise), Sagar, Dilip Khandate, Assistant District Excise Officer, and Roshni Ureti, Excise Sub-Inspector. This apart, local Deputy Excise Commissioner Neeraj Srivastav has been transferred and shifted to Gwalior Headquarters. Chief minister Mohan Yadav who left for four-day visit to Dubai to take part in the Global Investment Summit, organized by the Madhya Pradesh government to attract foreign investment on Sunday, ordered a probe into the incident. Madhya Pradesh Congress unit president Jitu Patwari slammed the state government for the recurring incidents of hooch tragedies in the state and demanded a judicial probe into the incident.

headline: Nine-judge Constitution Bench of Supreme Court hears arguments on right to privacy: Updates from day 5
text: by | August 1, 2017 A historic nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India has been hearing arguments for and against the right to privacy in the matter of K.S Puttaswamy v. Union of India for four days (day 1, day 2, day 3, day 4). On the first two days of the hearing (July 19 and July 20), the petitioners presented their arguments in favour of a right to privacy in India. On the third day (July 25) Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal took a pro-privacy stance on behalf of the State Governments of Karnataka, West Bengal, Punjab and Puducherry. A brief submission was made by the Counsel for the State of Himachal Pradesh, while the Attorney General of India (K. K. Venugopal), on behalf of the Government of India initiated arguments against the right to privacy being a fundamental right. On day four (July 26), the Attorney General continued his arguments and Senior Advocate C.A. Sundaram began his submission for the State of Maharashtra. Today, Senior Advocate C.A. Sundaram continued his submissions before the Court, followed by submissions from Additional Solicitor General Tushar Mehta on behalf of the State of Madhya Pradesh and Unique Identity Authority of India (UIDAI), and Senior Counsel Rakesh Dwivedi for the State of Gujarat. Mr. Sundaram stated that the framers of our Constitution had expressly left out the right to privacy from the ambit of fundamental rights, and only the Parliament had the power to introduce it through a constitutional amendment, if they deem it necessary to have such a right. Privacy can only be protected by way of statutes and legislation, he said, and cannot be elevated to the level of fundamental right. headline: Assam Police seize contraband valued at Rs 12 crore, two held
text: Guwahati, Aug 24 : Assam Police seized around 2,098 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth Rs 11-12 crore, during a major antiâ€‘narcotics operation in Kokrajhar district, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Monday. Guwahati, Aug 24 (IANS) Assam Police seized around 2,098 kg of ganja, estimated to be worth Rs 11-12 crore, during a major anti‑narcotics operation in Kokrajhar district, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Monday. Taking to X, Sarma praised Kokrajhar Police for the seizure and said the contraband was recovered at the Damrapara Checking Point. According to the Chief Minister, the ganja had been concealed beneath bamboo in an attempt to evade detection during transportation. Two persons allegedly involved in transporting the contraband were apprehended during the operation. Sharing details of the seizure, Sarma wrote: "Raat gayi, baat nahi jaane di," while appreciating Kokrajhar Police for their action. He estimated the value of the seized ganja at around Rs 11–12 crore, underlining the scale of the consignment and the significance of the operation. The seizure is part of the Assam government's continuing crackdown on the trafficking and transportation of narcotic substances through the state. Assam shares international and inter‑state borders and has emerged as an important transit route for the movement of various types of contraband. Authorities have stepped up checking and surveillance at vulnerable points to prevent the transportation of narcotics. The Damrapara Checking Point operation also highlights the role of police checkpoints in intercepting consignments being moved through the state. Police are expected to investigate the source of the seized contraband, its intended destination, and the wider network allegedly involved in its transportation. The two apprehended accused are likely to be questioned as part of the investigation to establish their links with other persons involved in the alleged drug trafficking network. Sarma congratulated Kokrajhar Police for the operation and encouraged Assam Police to continue their efforts against narcotics trafficking. "Keep up the good work, Assam Police," the Chief Minister said in his post. The Assam government has in recent years maintained a strong focus on its anti‑drug campaign, with police regularly conducting seizures of narcotics and arresting alleged traffickers across districts. Monday's seizure is among the major narcotics recoveries reported from the state and is expected to provide investigators with leads into the movement of large consignments through Assam. The authorities are continuing their probe into the case. --IANS tdr/dan

headline: AKSSA to launch protest in Dharwad today despite police denying nod
text: Despite the police denying permission citing law and order concerns, the All Karnataka State Students Association (AKSSA) has announced an indefinite satyagraha from Tuesday near the Michigan Compound in Saptapur of Dharwad demanding action on issues concerning students and job aspirants. AKSSA president Kanthakumar told presspersons in Dharwad on Monday that students from across the district will participate in a peaceful protest and remain at the venue until their demands are addressed. The association has sought a re-examination for candidates affected by irregularities in the examination conducted for the recruitment of police constables. It has also demanded an inquiry into irregularities in recruitment conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) and stringent action against those found responsible. The association has also raised concerns over the implementation of announcements made in the State Budget. The proposals, including the establishment of Indira Canteens and digital libraries for students, are yet to be implemented, Mr. Kanthakumar said. He also urged the State government to issue a notification for the recruitment of 10,000 additional teachers, over and above the 15,000 teacher posts for which recruitment has already been notified. Permission denied Police Commissioner N. Shashikumar told presspersons that permission for the protest near Michigan Compound has been denied as the area has several hospitals and is home to a large number of senior citizens and students. The police have also taken into consideration the violations of the conditions laid down by them during the students protest in September last year. Mr. Shashikumar said that the association has not furnished some of the details sought for by the police regarding the proposed agitation. Referring to an earlier High Court order related to an earlier denial of permission for protest by the police, Mr. Shashikumar said that the court subsequently permitted only 100 people to participate in a protest at Nehru Stadium in Hubballi at a designated time, subject to certain conditions. headline: TMC chief Mamata Banerjee to attend INDIA bloc meeting on September 30
text: TMC chief Mamata Banerjee to attend INDIA bloc meeting on September 30 Addressing a rally in Hooghly, Banerjee said, "Why was the SIR conducted? It was forced upon us solely to capture Bengal, as they couldn't win otherwise." Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee will attend the INDIA bloc meeting on September 30. The meet, which is set to discuss the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), will bring political rivals CPI(M) and TMC together. In a rare show of solidarity, the All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) chief held talks with CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby, along with Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, over holding a meeting of the INDIA bloc. Addressing a rally in Hooghly, Banerjee said, "Why was the SIR conducted? It was forced upon us solely to capture Bengal, as they couldn't win otherwise. Under the guise of SIR, the names of 92 lakh people were struck off." Banerjee said TMC was the first party to raise this issue. "We went to court and managed to get 32 lakh reinstated. Yet, 27 lakh names remained excluded...you removed the names of 92 lakh people in Bengal alone. And across the country, nearly 13 crore people have fallen victim to this SIR process," news agency ANI quoted her as saying. INDIA bloc formed in 2023 The INDIA bloc was formed in 2023 ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. It brought together parties with different ideological positions and competing regional interests. The bloc held its first meeting in Patna in June 2023, followed by a meeting in Bengaluru in July, where it was formally named. In West Bengal, the TMC and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections separately, while the CPI(M)-led Left Front also fought the polls on its own. Banerjee's latest appeal is notable as she seeks to bring different opposition parties together around a common institutional issue. Banerjee questions arrest of Milan Pradhan She also questioned the arrest of Congress's Nandigram by-election candidate Milan Pradhan in cases linked to the 2007 Nandigram anti-land acquisition agitation. The TMC's Mamata faction candidate withdrew from the contest after meeting West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Banerjee then extended her support to Pradhan.

headline: Teacher recruitment: Government ignores vacancies in linguistic minority schools
text: While the Karnataka government is recruiting to fill 15,000 vacant teacher posts in government schools across the State, many have objected to this not including vacancies in government linguistic minority schools. The government issued an order on August 10 for the recruitment of 15,000 teachers, which is primarily limited to government Kannada and English medium schools. There are 3,947 Urdu medium schools, where about 2,73,573 students are studying. In addition, there are 881 Marathi medium schools, 53 Tamil medium schools, 53 Telugu medium schools, and five Hindi medium schools in the State. These schools are said to have over 5,000 teaching vacancies, which are not being filled through the present recruitment drive. Job aspirants’ long wait “We have been waiting for recruitment for many years. The government has disappointed us,” said Kaleem Ahmed, a job aspirant. Another job aspirant, Imran Sharif, said that a large number of candidates who have completed BEd, DEd, and TET qualifications have been waiting for recruitment for many years. Many are working as guest teachers, while some are unemployed. “The dream of getting a government job before reaching the age limit is not fulfilled,” he rued. Flagged in Council During the ongoing Legislative session, members of the Legislative Council, Balkis Banu and Abdul Jabbar, raised the issue and drew the government’s attention. “Many districts with a large number of linguistic minority schools, including Kalaburagi, Bidar, Belagavi, Bagalkote, and Vijayapura, are in the Kalyan Karnataka region. These areas are also identified as backward districts based on the SSLC results. The shortage of teachers and the poor infrastructure in these schools is already serious compared to other parts of the State. In such a situation, ignoring them in recruitment can lead to further problems,” Ms. Banu said. Meanwhile, a delegation of job aspirants from linguistic minority schools met Minority Affairs Minister U.T. Khader, Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad and Chairman of the Legislative Council Salim Ahmed, appealing to them to convince the government to also fill vacancies in these schools. The Ministers are said to have assured job aspirants that they would take up the issue with the Chief Minister. Published - August 20, 2026 09:16 pm IST

headline: Bombay HC Clarifies July 24 Order Allowing PoP Idol Immersion In Natural Water Bodies Remains In Force
text: Mumbai, August 20, 2026: The Bombay High Court on Thursday clarified that its July 24, 2025 order permitting immersion of Plaster of Paris (PoP) idols measuring over six feet in natural water bodies will remain in force until it delivers its final judgment on the issue. A bench of Justices Ajay Gadkari and Kamal Khata issued the clarification after Advocate General Milind Sathe sought clarity on the effect of the court’s earlier orders. The clarification became necessary after the court, on August 14, reserved its judgment in a batch of petitions challenging the manufacture, sale and immersion of PoP idols. While reserving the judgment, the bench had said its June 9, 2025 interim order would continue until the final verdict. However, the June 9 order specifically stated that PoP idols could not be immersed in natural water bodies without the court’s permission. This raised questions over whether the subsequent July 24 order, which permitted immersion of PoP idols above six feet in natural water bodies subject to certain conditions, would continue. The bench on Thursday clarified that the July 24 order will remain operative until the final judgment. PoP Restrictions And CPCB Stand The June 9 order had lifted restrictions on the manufacture and sale of PoP idols after the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) revised its earlier stand. For nearly five years, the CPCB had maintained that the manufacture and sale of PoP idols were prohibited. It later clarified before the court that its guidelines were only “advisory”. While allowing the manufacture and sale of PoP idols, the High Court had imposed conditions on their immersion in natural water bodies. The petitions before the bench seek implementation of the CPCB’s 2020 guidelines, which prohibit the immersion of PoP idols in natural water bodies. The petitioners have also challenged the Maharashtra government’s August 1, 2025 immersion policy, which permitted immersion of PoP idols above six feet in natural water bodies while requiring smaller idols to be immersed in artificial ponds. Also Watch: The state’s policy expired in March 2026, but the government has sought to continue with the same arrangement. After hearing the petitioners, the state government and other intervenors, the bench reserved its judgment.
