headline: Bombay High Court takes minutes on record, converts plea to PIL on Adivasi ashram schools
text: The Maharashtra Government informed the Bombay High Court on Monday (September 1, 2026) that the 17-day hunger strike by tribal students from Ashram Schools in Pune's Manjari area has concluded. The development followed a meeting between Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, the Tribal Development Minister, and representatives of the protesting students. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad recorded the submission made by Chief Government Pleader Neha Bhide. The bench was told that the Chief Minister assured the student representatives that their demands would be examined. "Medical care was provided to the protesting students. No student is hospitalised. All students are stable. The hunger strike ended after the Chief Minister met the representatives," Mr. Bhide told the court. The Bench received a copy of the minutes of the meeting between the Chief Minister, the Tribal Development Minister, and the student representatives. According to the document, the government agreed to constitute a Special Investigating Team (SIT) to probe the death of a student from food poisoning. The government also decided to implement mess services in hostels instead of the Direct Beneficiary Transfer (DBT) scheme for food supplies. The court took the minutes on record and directed the state to file an affidavit detailing the implementation of these decisions. The Bench converted the writ petition into a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) to monitor the infrastructure of Ashram Schools across Maharashtra. The court had previously intervened last week after being informed that the health of one protester had declined. Acting Chief Justice Ghuge had stated that the court did not want any student to lose their life. The Bench had directed the state to provide medical facilities to the protesters and ordered hospitalisation if required. The authorities were also instructed to provide food to the students if necessary. The hunger strike originated from grievances over facilities in Ashram Schools, particularly those in tribal regions. headline: Mamata Banerjee's niece found dead at her residence in West Bengal's Birbhum, say police
text: Mamata Banerjee's niece found dead at her residence in West Bengal's Birbhum, say police The 31-year-old's body was found in a room on the second floor of her house in Rampurhat's Kusumba village. Trinamool Congress supremo Mamata Banerjee's niece has been found dead at her residence in West Bengal's Birbhum, police said on Tuesday. The 31-year-old's body was found in a room on the second floor of her house in Rampurhat's Kusumba village on Tuesday afternoon. The deceased is the daughter of Mamata's cousin brother. According to her family members, she had been suffering from depression for the past few years and was undergoing treatment for the same, PTI news agency reported. She had lost her job following the Supreme Court order cancelling recruitments for government-aided schools over alleged corruption, the family members added. Her body was sent for a post-mortem examination, and an investigation into the incident is underway, the officer said. “The circumstances leading to the death will be established after the post-mortem and other procedural inquiries,” PTI cited him as saying. headline: Congress objects to UN map depiction of Arunachal Pradesh
text: In a statement, Arunachal Pradesh Congress Committee (APCC) president Bosiram Siram said any international map that creates ambiguity about the state's territorial status is unacceptable. He asserted that no foreign claim, map or nomenclature can alter India's sovereignty over Arunachal Pradesh. Siram said the party supports the Centre's objection to any inaccurate or misleading representation of the country's territory. He said India's support for a UN General Assembly resolution on equal-area cartographic representation was aimed at improving the accuracy of world map projections and should not be interpreted as acceptance of any particular boundary or territorial claim. Siram said India's response should go beyond diplomatic objections and focus on strengthening its presence in frontier areas through better roads, communication networks, logistics, security infrastructure and economic development. The APCC reiterated that Arunachal Pradesh is a vital frontier of India and said stronger development and national presence in border areas would provide the most effective response to cartographic and territorial assertions. "The position that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of India is non-negotiable," Siram said, stressing that the state must remain secure, connected, developed and constitutionally protected. In response to media queries regarding the UN General Assembly resolution on equal-area world map, the government's official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal recently said the resolution neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names. "India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation of vote, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation. We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries. India's sovereign territory...must be depicted in accordance with India's official map. Any inaccurate or misleading depiction is unacceptable. Our position on India's sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable," he stated.

headline: MHADA To Showcase Kamathipura Cluster Redevelopment Plan To Residents On September 11
text: Mumbai: The proposed layout of the ambitious Kamathipura Cluster Redevelopment Project will be presented to local residents and stakeholders on Friday, September 11, as the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) moves to take the redevelopment plan forward through greater public participation. Layout presentation planned The presentation, being organised jointly by MHADA's Mumbai Building Repairs and Reconstruction Board (MBRRB) and the Kamathipura Vikas Samiti, will be held at 6 pm at Akhil Padmashali Samaj, Bhavna Baug, Kamathipura, 6th Lane. The cluster redevelopment project, planned across approximately 34 acres, covers around 943 cessed buildings and 349 non-cessed buildings. More than 8,000 residents and tenants are associated with the project, including around 6,625 residential and 1,376 commercial tenants apart from approximately 800 landlords. Redevelopment plan details The project is aimed at replacing the area's ageing and dilapidated structures with safer and modern housing while undertaking comprehensive redevelopment of the neighbourhood. The Government of Maharashtra has proposed an integrated redevelopment mechanism for both cessed and non-cessed properties in Kamathipura under a Government Resolution issued on January 12, 2023. The redevelopment is being undertaken by the MBRRB under Regulation 33(9) of the Development Control and Promotion Regulations (DCPR), 2034. Bhagirathi Housing Pvt. Ltd. and Mathi Developers Pvt. Ltd. have been appointed as the Construction and Development Agencies (C&DA), while MHADA has been designated as the Nodal Agency as well as the Special Planning Authority (SPA) for the project. Residents to receive project briefing During Friday's presentation, MHADA is expected to explain the proposed layout and provide details about the rehabilitation strategy, beneficiaries, infrastructure, civic amenities, environmental measures and future development plan for the area. The initiative is also intended to give tenants, landlords, landholders and other local stakeholders an opportunity to understand how the proposed redevelopment will be structured and how rehabilitation will be carried out. Also Watch: Focus on planned transformation Kamathipura, one of Mumbai's oldest and historically significant neighbourhoods, has evolved over several decades and contains a mix of residential and commercial establishments. Given the area's dense development and ageing building stock, the cluster approach is intended to facilitate redevelopment on a larger scale rather than relying on individual building-wise redevelopment. The authority is also positioning the redevelopment as an opportunity for the planned, sustainable and inclusive transformation of Kamathipura. headline: ‘Not everyone in NDA agrees’: Omar Abdullah questions Centre’s UCC plan amid JD(U)'s opposition
text: NEW DELHI: Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday questioned the Centre’s plan to implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in all 21 BJP-led NDA-ruled states before 2029, citing the Janata Dal (United)’s opposition to implementing the law in Bihar and questioning whether the government can secure the numbers to pass it in Parliament. Abdullah’s remarks came a day after JD(U) leader Shyam Rajak said the party was opposed to implementing the UCC in Bihar, despite supporting the UCC Bill in Parliament. The JD(U), which has 12 Lok Sabha MPs, is a key NDA ally and shares power with the BJP in Bihar. Speaking to reporters in Srinagar, Abdullah also questioned the state-wise rollout of the UCC, arguing that civil legislation should be dealt with by Parliament. "In this regard, the National Conference has issued its statement. Our Rajya Sabha MP Shammi Oberoi has said that it is Parliament's job to do this. Why are you doing it from different states? Not everyone in their NDA agrees with this. JDU has straight-up raised its hands and said it won't be implemented in Bihar. If their own people aren't ready for UCC, how can these people say that it should be implemented across the entire country? I don't think these people will be able to pass it in Parliament," Abdullah said. Rajak said on Monday that the party’s position on implementing the UCC in Bihar remained unchanged, despite its support for the legislation in Parliament. "Our stand on the issue was made clear by our leader way back. He had said that although our party was supporting the UCC Bill in the Parliament, it was not in favour of implementing the same in Bihar," Rajak said. "The chief minister may be of the BJP but the government is being run with the help of allies... our stand is clear, the question of implementing UCC in Bihar does not arise," he said. JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha said the party would soon meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the implementation of the UCC in states. “We will soon meet Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the issue,” Jha told PTI. headline: SC asks Election Commission to set timeline for deciding TMC name, symbol dispute
text: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Election Commission to apprise it of the time frame within which it can finally decide the dispute between the two rival factions of the All India Trinamool Congress over its name and "flowers and grass" election symbol. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee against the Election Commission's (EC) decision to freeze the TMC's name and party symbol. Referring to the delay in deciding the Shiv Sena dispute, the bench said the dispute should be decided expeditiously and asked the poll panel to suggest a "reasonable" time frame that would allow both sides a fair opportunity to present their evidence while enabling the EC to reach a final decision. It asked senior advocate D S Naidu, appearing for the poll panel, to apprise it of the timeline for finally deciding the row over the ownership of TMC's name and election symbol and posted Banerjee's plea for hearing on September 28. "Find out, for final adjudication, how much time are you expected to take? Only for this limited purpose... reasonable time in which parties are given fair opportunity and you have time to apply your mind... but not too long," the CJI said. At the outset, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Banerjee, questioned the timing of the EC's interim order, saying that it had been passed after the bye-election process had commenced and consequently, it denied Banerjee an opportunity to avail legal remedies. "Can the Election Commission delay matters, and then pass orders in the midst of elections knowing that I won't have a remedy," Sibal asked. He said the dispute had reached the poll panel in July and that the Commission could have passed an order earlier, before the election process began. "The intent of the Election Commission is to leave me without a remedy," Sibal said. The bench, however, questioned what the EC could have done after receiving nominations from candidates belonging to both factions, each claiming to be the genuine TMC. headline: 111 sitting MPs and MLAs changed their political parties after being elected: ADR
text: A total of 111 sitting MPs and MLAs changed their political parties after being elected to the current Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha and State Assemblies since 2022. Among them, 26 were members of the Lok Sabha, seven were of the Rajya Sabha and 78 were of Legislative Assemblies, according to an analysis by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and National Election Watch. The analysis was based on the elections and byelections held between 2022 and 2026. Nagaland recorded the highest number of party switches, with 32 (29%) MPs/MLAs changing sides, followed by West Bengal with 20 (18%). Also Read | Kapil Sibal calls for 10-year ban on politicians switching parties mid-term As far as political parties were concerned, the Nationalist Democratic Progressive Party (NDPP), All India Trinamool Congress and Indian National Congress together accounted for 64 (58%) of the 111 MPs/MLAs who changed parties. The highest number of party switches was recorded among representatives originally elected from the NDPP (25, 23%), followed by the Trinamool (20, 18%) and the Congress (19, 17%). The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) accounted for nine (8%) party switches, while the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) each accounted for seven (6%). The Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) accounted for six (5%), followed by Janata Dal (United) with five (5%) and the National People’s Party (NPP) with four (4%). It is noteworthy that the recent fall of governments in some State Assemblies was attributed to defections by their MLAs, the report said. As far as parties that received the maximum number of lawmakers within their fold were concerned, the Naga People’s Front (NPF) led the list, with 32 (29%) joining the party, followed by the BJP with 29 (26%) and the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) with 20 (18%). The Congress received nine (8%), Shiv Sena eight (7%), the NPP six (5%) and the People’s Party of Arunachal four (4%). Overall, the NPF, BJP and NCPI together accounted for 81 (73%) of the 111 MPs/MLAs who joined other political parties. Published - September 24, 2026 09:35 pm IST

headline: One Manipur Deputy CM seeks action against another
text: Manipur Deputy Chief Minister Losii Dikho has urged the Centre to take punitive measures against fellow Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen for “colluding” with a Kuki insurgent group allegedly involved in the killing of Naga civilians. Mr. Dikho and eight other Naga MLAs also threatened to pull out of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led government in Manipur if no action is taken against Ms. Kipgen and the leaders of Kuki-Zo extremist groups. Five of these MLAs, including Mr. Dikho, are from the Naga People’s Front (NPF), two are from the BJP, one from the National People’s Party, and one is an Independent. They listed their demand in a letter to Union Home Minister Amit Shah on August 29. “The letter was hand-delivered today (Monday),” Mr. Dikho said. In the letter, the MLAs demanded the arrest of Kuki-Zo leaders, who publicly claimed responsibility for the killing and dismemberment of six Naga civilians, whose mutilated bodies were recovered on June 10, almost a month after they were abducted. They also demanded the arrest of Thangboi Kipgen, the head of the extremist Kuki National Front (Presidential) faction and Ms. Kipgen’s husband. “Initiate action against Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen as her office is colluding with the Kuki militant group led by her husband Thangboi Kipgen…” the letter read. The Naga MLAs further demanded the immediate abrogation of the Suspension of Operation agreement that the Centre had signed with 25 Kuki-Zo rebel groups in 2008, citing alleged repeated violations and acts of terror against civilians. “When the mutilated bodies of the six Naga men are still unclaimed in protest against the non-arrest of the perpetrators, another four Naga men were mercilessly killed in the IT road ambush on August 27, carried out by the Kuki militants,” the MLAs wrote, citing some other incidents of violence. They warned that if action were not initiated, they would be “unable to defend or adequately respond to the challenges raised by the public concerning our continued support to the Government of Manipur.” “This step is being taken solely in the larger interest of the people of Manipur, and out of absolute necessity,” they further wrote. Manipur had 10 Naga MLAs. One of them, N. Kayisii of the NPP, died in January 2025. Published - September 01, 2026 01:40 am IST

headline: Govt. failed to respond to drought-like conditions in Andhra Pradesh, says Jagan
text: YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy on Wednesday alleged that the TDP-led NDA government in Andhra Pradesh has failed to respond to the worsening drought-like conditions in the State. “The government is neglecting the farmers and agricultural labourers, and is indulging in political drama over Backward Classes (BC) reservations in the local bodies,” Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said while addressing the media on Wednesday. Against the normal rainfall of 384 mm between June and August 23, the State had received only 189.62 mm, he said. Of the 688 mandals, 625 received deficient rainfall, while 25 of the 28 districts were facing a rainfall deficit, he said, adding that kharif cultivation was about 20% below normal. Farmers had invested in seeds, fertilizers and nurseries after being assured of irrigation water, but many crops and nurseries dried up, the former Chief Minister said, and accused the government of failing to provide adequate water to the Rayalaseema projects and farmers under the Nagarjuna Sagar and Krishna delta systems. He also accused the government of weakening crop insurance and farmer-support systems, and claimed that crop insurance coverage had declined sharply after farmers were required to bear the premium burden. headline: Maharashtra Steps Up Efforts To Trace Tourists Stranded In Flood-Hit Nepal
text: Mumbai: The Maharashtra government has stepped up efforts to trace and assist tourists from the state stranded in flood-hit Nepal, with authorities maintaining close coordination with the Centre amid disrupted communication networks and road connectivity in Nepal. At least 114 tourists from Maharashtra are estimated to be stranded in Nepal, of whom 53 have been confirmed safe, state officials said on Thursday. The figure is likely to change as district administrations continue collecting and verifying information about residents who travelled to the Himalayan nation. Rescue efforts underway Disaster Management Minister Girish Mahajan said the state government was in continuous contact with the Union government and was making efforts to establish contact with all Maharashtra tourists. So far, contact has been established with four tourists, who were confirmed to be safe. “Relatives should not panic. The Centre and the state government are making every possible effort to contact all tourists from Maharashtra,” Mahajan said, pointing out that telephone services and mobile networks had been disrupted in several areas following floods and landslides. According to the State Emergency Operations Centre (SEOC), around 61 Maharashtra tourists were travelling through Richa Tours Pvt Ltd, while others had travelled independently. Of those travelling through the tour operator, nearly 37 people in one vehicle were confirmed safe in the Saga Mansarovar area. Tourists await evacuation Officials said several Maharashtra tourists were located at three separate places in Nepal. Many of them had undertaken the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage and were returning when floods and landslides disrupted road connectivity. With the road to Kathmandu reportedly closed, authorities are coordinating efforts to move tourists towards the nearest safe and accessible locations. Vinita Vaid Singal, Principal Secretary, Disaster Management, Relief and Rehabilitation Department, said the state was in touch with the Ministry of External Affairs and the Union Home Ministry, which are coordinating efforts to trace Indian citizens in Nepal. The state government is also contacting private travel operators that regularly take tourists from Maharashtra to Nepal. Officials said the state was currently in touch with 11 travel agencies to obtain details of Maharashtra residents who may have travelled to Nepal recently. headline: Six Assam youths missing in Nepal floods, CM Himanta Biswa Sarma says figures may rise- Moneycontrol.com
text: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Friday said six people from the northeastern state were reported missing after devastating floods struck Nepal on August 26, 2026, while cautioning that the number was not yet final. “Six people from Assam were missing in the devastating flood in Nepal. The figures may rise but till afternoon we have got the figures of six people. I cannot say it was the authentic figure but it may change,” Sarma told reporters. Among those reported missing are two youths from Langhin in Assam’s Karbi Anglong district, according to NDTV. They have been identified as 24-year-old Rituparna Brahma and 28-year-old Mantri Basumatary. The two, from Doidak village under Langhin, had travelled to Nepal around two weeks before the disaster in search of employment. According to an official quoted in the report, both were working at a hydroelectric project near the Trishuli River in Nepal. “The duo had gone to Nepal two weeks ago in search of work. Both were working in a company named Hydro Electrical Project located near the Trishuli River in Nepal.However, since the catastrophic flood in Nepal, the families have not been able to establish any contact with them. Their mobile phones have been switched off since the day of the incident,” the official reportedly said. Rituparna and Mantri have remained untraceable since the natural disaster hit Nepal on August 26. Their families have informed Dokmoka Police Station about their disappearance and have also sought intervention from the Government of India, the Assam government and Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council Chief Executive Member Tuliram Ronghang. The families have appealed for the missing youths to be rescued at the earliest and are currently relying on government authorities and rescue teams for assistance. Another missing person from Assam has been identified as Shatadal Nath, a resident of Hindu Block village in Doboka in Hojai district. Reports said Nath was also among those who went missing following the disaster in Nepal. Meanwhile, Someswar Narzary, 37, who was a colleague of Rituparna Brahma and Mantri Basumatary, survived the incident. Narzary was able to contact his family by phone and inform them about what had happened. The Assam government has also opened helpline numbers to provide emergency assistance, coordination and information concerning people from the state who may be stranded in Nepal. The latest information comes as families of the missing Assam youths continue to wait for updates

headline: J&K Set for Showdown Between Ruling NC and Opposition BJP on Wednesday

headline: Bihar warns people against eating ‘unfamiliar’ fish caught in Nepal floodwaters - The Tribune
text: Bihar warns people against eating ‘unfamiliar’ fish caught in Nepal floodwaters Fisheries Department issues advisory amid reports of strange-looking fish in flood-hit districts; contamination and infection risks flagged In a strict warning, the Bihar government on Tuesday cautioned people against the consumption of “unfamiliar and unusual” fish caught in floodwaters flowing into the state’s rivers from Nepal. In recent days, people living in East and West Champaran districts, Gopalganj, Bagaha and Saran have reported catching “strange-looking” large fish. Bihar Fisheries Minister Nand Kishor Ram said a comprehensive advisory had been issued against catching, consuming, buying or selling unfamiliar fish to “avoid any contamination”. Following flash floods in Nepal, water from the Trishuli river has been flowing into Bihar via the Gandak and Kosi rivers, both major waterways in the northern part of the state. As river levels rise, unfamiliar varieties of fish have been turning up in flood-affected areas, and some people are reportedly said to have fallen ill after consuming them. The Animal and Fisheries Resources Department has advised people not to buy, sell or consume fish caught from floodwaters, warning that such fish may carry sewage contamination, bacteria, viruses and other pathogens. Nepal Police have also issued a similar warning for residents. The advisory, issued by Bihar’s Department of Dairy, Fisheries and Animal Resources, states that during floods, fish move out of ponds, rivers, lakes and reservoirs and spread widely with floodwaters. It notes that continuous exposure to polluted drains, dead animals and other contaminants can make these fish unsafe for consumption and that people should avoid eating fish caught from floodwaters until environmental conditions stabilise. “Do not treat any unfamiliar fish as fit for consumption without checking with the concerned department. Seek immediate medical help at the nearest health centre if symptoms such as vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, dizziness or breathing difficulty appear after eating such fish. Report sightings of unusual fish to the local District Fisheries Officer or administration. Do not pay attention to rumours, and avoid consuming unknown fish for the sake of safety,” the advisory said. headline: Haryana: 11 bills passed on session’s last day
text: Haryana: 11 bills passed on session’s last day The House passed the Haryana State Commission for Women (amendment) Bill, 2026, to increase the number of non-official members of the commission including several more bills The Haryana assembly on Tuesday passed 11 Bills including the Haryana State Commission for Minorities Bill for setting up a state minorities commission to provide an institutional arrangement for evaluating the safeguards provided in the Constitution and laws for the protection of minorities. According to the statement of objects and reasons, the commission will make recommendations to ensure effective implementation of safeguards and laws in Haryana. “The commission with statutory status would infuse confidence among the minority communities about its working and effectiveness. It would also carry greater weight with the state government, its departments, boards, corporations, local authorities and other organisations concerned with the welfare and development of minorities,’’ the statement said. The commission will consist of a chairperson and a vice-chairperson. The main task of the commission shall be to evaluate the progress of the development of minorities in the state, monitor the working of the safeguards provided in the Constitution and in laws enacted for the protection of the interests of minorities, and look into specific complaints regarding deprivation of rights and safeguards of minorities. The commission shall also undertake studies, research and analysis on issues relating to the socio-economic and educational development of minorities and make recommendations for effective implementation of safeguards and for appropriate measures to be undertaken by the state government. The House passed the Haryana State Commission for Women (amendment) Bill, 2026, to increase the number of non-official members of the commission. The statement of objects and reasons of the Bill said that there has been an increase in the number of complaints, memoranda and other matters relating to women in the past few years. “As a result, the workload and responsibilities of the commission have increased considerably. At present, there are five non-official members in the commission. In view of the increased workload, this number is not sufficient for the effective and expeditious disposal of the commission’s functions. Therefore, in order to strengthen the efficiency and institutional capacity of the commission, it has been considered necessary to amend section 3(2)(b) of the Haryana State Commission for Women Act, 2012. Under this, it is proposed to increase the number of non-official members from five to seven,” the statement said.

headline: SC issues notice on Tejpal's appeal against rape conviction
text: The Supreme Court on Friday issued notice to the State of Goa on an appeal filed by former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal against a Bombay High Court judgment sentencing him to 10 years’ imprisonment in a 2013 rape case. A bench headed by Justice MM Sundresh took up the appeal in a brief hearing. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, for Tejpal, described the case as one of reversal of conviction and imprisonment. Sibal said his client had already surrendered. The Supreme Court directed Tejpal to surrender within three weeks in an order passed on August 25. A single-judge bench of Justice Alok Aradhe observed that his appeal would be heard once the certificate of his surrender is filed in the Supreme Court on or before September 22, 2026. Tejpal’s appeal had followed a separate appeal filed by the State of Goa in the apex court for enhancement of his punishment to life imprisonment. The State had said the sentence was manifestly inadequate but clarified that it did not want to challenge or reopen the High Court’s findings on the merits. The Bombay High Court Bench had sentenced him to 10 years’ imprisonment on August 6 after setting aside a five-year-old Goa sessions court decision acquitting him. While Tejpal pleaded for leniency, claiming he was a “political victim” and the father of two daughters, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa, had demanded the maximum punishment to send a strong message. The State has said that the 10-year prison sentence pronounced by the High Court was “grossly disproportionate to the nature and gravity of the offence” committed by Tejpal. “The present case warrants enhancement of sentence to imprisonment for life, or such enhanced sentence as this court may deem appropriate, and the sentences ought not to have been directed to run concurrently,” the State petition had said. The High Court had termed the trial court’s 2021 order as “perverse”. Tejpal was convicted of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in 2013 during an event organised by the magazine in Goa. Published on September 25, 2026

headline: “Ritwick Chakraborty Is Stunning As A Political Anomaly In Winkle Twinkle” – A Subhash K Jha Review
text: Winkle Twinkle (Bengali) Starring Ritwick Chakraborty, Parambrata Chattopadhyay, Rajatava Dutta, Sohini Sarkar Directed by Srijit Mukherji What happens when you are declared dead in 1976 and you wake up from the dead in 2002? When people around talk about Hrithik, you think it is Ritwick Ghatak they are referring to. “Is he still making films?” wonders Sabyasachi Sen, back from the dead, and trying to come to terms with the radically transformed socio-political scenario. Coincidentally, Sabyasachi is played by another Ritwick… Ritwick Chakraborty, one of the finest actors of the country, tragically not known much outside Bengal. As the time-challenged traveller from Buddhadeb Bhattacharya’s CPM to Mamata Banerjee’s TMC, Ritwick has before him the daunting task to bridge two eras. He straddles the world he cannot leave behind, and the world that won’t accept him, with a sobering fluency. The performance is a textbook of naturalistic acting, yet not in any showy way. In comparison, Parambrata Chatterjee as the son comes across weak, trying too hard to get into the skin of the loutish politically scrambled egghead determined to defy and drown Daddy’s idealism into rubbles of nihilism. He is especially ineffectual when scoffing at his screen father, as though his heart is not in it. The supporting cast feels like an intrusion. The conversation with Stalin feels forcibly positioned in a film that feels like a father-son drama with a political slant sliding into the conflict. The film is based on the critically acclaimed stage play by Bratya Basu. Srijit doesn’t take the play out of the film, which is a fine place to be, as long as the characters don’t appear excessively discursive. In its audacious blend of time-travel and Bengal’s politics Winkle Twinkle reminded me of Mrinal Sen’s early political non-dramas Interview (1971) Calcutta 71 (1972) and Padatik (1973). Srijit’s film about a dormant political traveller awakening to a new reality is an intriguing whodunnit where the slain entity is political idealism. What if a man who goes missing from his own memory to wake up to a world where politics is no longer about idealism, but opportunism? headline: Fist fights in J-K Assembly as CM moves statehood resolution
text: Jammu and Kashmir's political landscape witnessed significant turmoil as Chief Minister Omar Abdullah's resolution for urgent full statehood restoration, referencing past autonomy demands, ignited fierce protests and chaos in the assembly. Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday moved a resolution in the assembly to seek urgent restoration of full statehood to the union territory, leading to ugly scenes in the House and even fist fights. headline: 100 days of BJP Government in West Bengal | Balancing trust and mistrust
text: On August 17, the Bharatiya Janata Party Government in West Bengal came out with full page advertisements in leading national dailies titled ‘100 days of Bhorosha — 8 pillars for Bikosito Poschimbongo (100 days of trust: 8 pillars for a developed West Bengal). The BJP fought the West Bengal Assembly elections 2026 on the promise of bringing in ‘bhorosa’ (trust) and the assurance that they will drive ‘bhoy ‘(fear) out. In the advertisement, the eight pillars of trust refer to industrialisation, good governance, law and order, national security, health, education, and empowerment of people among others. One of the biggest challenges of the West Bengal government is to bring in big industrial capital in the State, something which the Trinamool Congress government had miserably failed to do. In the past 100 days, the Suvendu Adhikari government has announced a single window clearance for investment over ₹100 crore and promised to bring in a new industrial policy. While there is some enthusiasm among the industrialists over change of regime, for real investment to flow in, the BJP government will have to do something path-breaking particularly when West Bengal has lost decades to States in the south and west of the country as far as attracting private investment is concerned. headline: CJP to join Maharashtra PSC aspirants' protest
text: The Cockroach Janta Party and its founder Abhijeet Dipke are now backing MPSC aspirants' protests across Maharashtra, demanding accountability and transparency amidst alleged paper leaks and irregularities in crucial online examinations. The Cockroach Janta Party said on Sunday that its members and founder Abhijeet Dipke will join students in their protests over alleged paper leaks in various online examinations conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC). headline: Massive fire at Kolkata hotel: 9 people, including 5 Bangladeshi nationals, killed
text: At least nine people, including five Bangladeshi nationals, were killed after a massive fire broke out at a hotel in Kolkata on Wednesday. A child was among those killed in the blaze. Four out of the five Bangladeshi victims belonged to the same family. They had travelled to Kolkata for medical treatment. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered the formation of a five-member special investigation team (SIT) immediately to conduct a comprehensive inquiry into this incident. The fire broke out at around 2 a.m. on Wednesday inside the hotel, located at central Kolkata’s Mirza Ghalib Street under New Market Police Station area. According to Kolkata Police, around 60 people were rescued from the hotel premises. “Extremely pained to learn about the loss of lives due to a fire mishap in Kolkata. My condolences to those who have lost their loved ones in this tragedy. May the injured recover at the earliest. The local administration is assisting those who are affected,” Prime Minister Narendra Modi said in a post on X. While we remain focused on the rescue and relief operations and conduct investigations regarding what went wrong, it is impossible to ignore the reality we are facing today. This tragedy is a grim reminder of the legacy of negligence left behind by the previous regime, the Chief Minister said. “legacy of negligence” Blaming the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government’s “legacy of negligence” for the tragedy, he alleged that for years Kolkata and West Bengal’s infrastructure was allowed to grow unchecked, with structures being permitted to be built and operated as hotels and other businesses while completely ignoring mandatory fire safety norms. “My heart goes out to the families who have lost their loved ones in this heartbreaking tragedy. I have instructed the administration to ensure that the injured receive the absolute best medical attention and support,” Adhikari said. The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has contacted the families of the deceased and is in contact with hospitals and police to extend necessary assistance. The Bangladesh Foreign Ministry is also in contact with the Indian authorities. Published on August 19, 2026

headline: Rajasthan CM passes popularity test as BJP widens lead in urban body polls - The Tribune
text: Rajasthan CM passes popularity test as BJP widens lead in urban body polls Independents trounce BJP, Cong in CM’s hometown Bharatpur Under scrutiny over governance issues, particularly the state of infrastructure in government schools, Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma today passed the popularity test, with the BJP widening its lead over the Congress in the results of the urban local body elections. The BJP won more than 4,171 wards, while the Congress secured over 3,597, with results declared for 10,200 wards by 8 pm. In all, 10,245 councillors are to be elected across 10 municipal corporations, 51 municipal councils and 248 municipalities in the state. Polling was held on September 9 and 11. CJP leaders had also alleged that they were targeted by goons hired from outside the state when they went to inspect schools. Apart from the CJP, the Congress, led by Rahul Gandhi, had separately organised a “Chhatron ki Goonj” rally in Kota, where the BJP won the municipal corporation, securing 53 of the 100 wards today. BJP leader Sudhanshu Trivedi said the party was headed for a “spectacular victory” in Rajasthan’s 309 local bodies, alleging that the results had exposed Rahul’s “jhooth ki goonj” (lies). headline: Jagan fires another salvo at Chandrababu over DSC scam
text: Amaravati, Sep 14 : Continuing to fire salvos at Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu over alleged irregularities in the appointment of teachers through DSC, YSR Congress Party president Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy said on Monday that when exams lose credibility, dreams get clipped. "Lakhs of aspirants sacrifice prime years of their lives and their families' hard-earned money for a fair chance. When the system fails them, it doesn't just affect the results, it shatters their faith in the entire recruitment process, resulting in disillusionment," the former Chief Minister said in a post on X "Chandrababu Naidu Garu, fairness is not an option; it is a duty! Don't you feel their hard work deserves fairness and future accountability? Will you assume responsibility for the current scam in DSC?" asked YS Jagan. This is the latest in a series of social media posts by the YSRCP chief, questioning the alleged irregularities. He has been highlighting the irregularities and reiterating his party's demand for a thorough probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the resignation of Education Minister Nara Lokesh, son of Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu. "One teacher post. A rollercoaster of twists & turns in this DSC scam," he had posted on Sunday. He told Chief Minister that the explanations keep changing, and every new explanation gives rise to even more questions for teacher aspirants. The YSRCP chief explained various twists in the appointment of a teacher. The post was reportedly awarded with 65 TET marks, after the candidate passed through 7 stages of verification. "The DEO confirmed the candidate to be ineligible. So the obvious question is: What actually was verified in those 7 stages?" According to YS Jagan, the third twist was that the candidate got the job but didn't know. The candidate himself reportedly said that he did not know how he got the job. "And now, the biggest question of all: Can this, by any means, be called fair and transparent? Has this not enabled the DSC scam? Will you not assume moral responsibility for this?" he questioned Chandrababu Naidu. In a post on Saturday, the YSRCP chief had told the Chief Minister that teacher aspirants' careers have become a joke for him.

headline: Zomato analogue paneer ban: Gurgaon restaurants tighten checks, verify dairy supplies- Moneycontrol.com
text: Restaurants across Gurgaon are tightening checks on their dairy supplies after Zomato introduced a zero-tolerance policy against analogue dairy products on its platform, as per The Indian Express. Over the past two weeks, representatives of food aggregators have been visiting partner restaurants for regular discussions. Analogue dairy products have also become part of these conversations, with restaurants being asked to ensure their kitchens are free of synthetic dairy substitutes and to verify their suppliers and ingredient declarations. At Harish Bakery in Sector 56, staff said Zomato representatives visited the outlet last week to explain the new guidelines. “They came by to discuss, among other things, any use of analogue paneer. We use natural paneer, so we didn’t face any issue,” a member of the management said. In Sector 23, Grills manager Pramod Kumar said the restaurant's operations had not been affected because it uses standard dairy products. Staff at nearby Ananda Cafe, a South Indian restaurant, also said they had never faced a situation where their supplier delivered analogue paneer instead of regular paneer. The Haryana government has separately imposed a one-year ban on analogue paneer. Under food safety norms, products made by completely or partially replacing milk fat or milk solids with vegetable oil, vegetable fat or other non-dairy ingredients are classified as analogue or non-dairy paneer. Restaurants are also strengthening their own checks amid growing scrutiny of dairy substitutes. At Khadak Singh Da Dhaba, the management is reviewing its vendor supply chains and tightening verification procedures. “Some of our competitors were undercutting us by using analogue paneer; now, there will be a more level playing field. Yes, the costs of paneer have been rising in recent times, though, but we had already hiked prices earlier to account for this,” said Akshit Behl, the restaurant’s growth and investment head, as quoted by The Indian Express. Akshit said the enforcement could also address price differences between restaurants using natural paneer and those using cheaper substitutes. He added, “All our dairy vendors are registered with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). We have asked them to ensure compliance from their end. All the checking (for analogue dairy) happens at a local/restaurant level only than in a centralised way.” Behl said. Other restaurants said verifying invoices and sourcing from certified dairies has become increasingly important, even as wholesale prices rise. headline: This might be my last meeting: Manoj Jarange Patil's emotional appeal as he announces solo march to Mumbai
text: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Sep 14 : Entering the 17th day of his hunger strike, Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange Patil on Monday issued a highly emotional appeal to the Maratha community. Having discontinued IV fluids and medical treatment, Jarange Patil stated that his physical condition was rapidly deteriorating, warning that his upcoming journey to Mumbai might be his last encounter with the people of Maharashtra. "Today is the 17th day of my fast. Removing the IV saline has caused a burning sensation in my stomach again. I will be heading to Mumbai virtually alone, accompanied by just four or five associates. "I am unable to stand up, so please do not organise welcome ceremonies along the route. If I have the energy, I will speak. While there are no restrictions on coming to meet me, this could likely be our final meeting. Come to the roads to bless me, but do not march to Mumbai just yet. This may be my final goodbye to the Godavari belt and to Maharashtra," Jarange Patil expressed during his Press conference. Refusing to bow down, Jarange Patil called upon the community to stand firm. "We cannot let the Maratha community lose. Wherever my body falls, it falls. But Marathas must fight with such pride that future generations hold their heads high, saying that 'he died but never backed down'. I don't want to rot and die. I want to die giving rights to my community. We must not let the dignity of the community slip even by an inch," he declared. Warning the community to stay vigilant, Jarange Patil targeted Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, alleging a political strategy to suppress the Maratha agitation. "We have to counter Devendra Fadnavis' moves step for step. Their strategy has been to use the cover of deities to defame the Maratha movement, instigate riots through infiltrators, and then use police force to crush the protest. Marathas do not lack leaders. If not one leader, there will be another. Vote for whoever gives us reservationâ€"your personal preference for a party or leader is useless if they do not secure your children's future," he remarked. He added that the 5.5 crore working-class Marathas could block Mumbai at any moment, contrasting them with political and wealthy elite who make up a small fraction of the population. Jarange Patil had briefly accepted medical aid following appeals from the government and community members.

headline: Manipur Violence: Home Minister Vows Firm Action After Four Killed
text: Guwahati: Today, the manipur Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam said violence would not be allowed to derail the state’s path towards peace and normalcy, a day after four people were killed in separate attacks in Tamenglong and Noney districts. Reacting to the killings, Konthoujam said the government would take firm action against those responsible and directed authorities to establish the facts surrounding the incidents. “Violence against innocent civilians is unacceptable and will be dealt with firmly,” the minister said in a post on twitter. He also expressed deep anguish over the attack at Tollen Kuki village, where Lhingjangai Singsit was killed and her husband, Seineih Singsit, and their infant son were injured after suspected militants opened fire at their residence. Seineih later succumbed to his injuries while being taken to a hospital in Silchar, Assam. In a separate incident, a woman and a man were shot dead by armed militants at Longpi village under Nungba police station at around 3.30 pm. The killings coincided with Sahnit Ni, or Black Day, observed by the Kuki community on 13th September to remember victims of the Kuki-Naga conflict of the 1990s.

headline: Three Newborns Die In Amravati Hospital NICU Fire As Maharashtra Orders High-Level Investigation
text: Mumbai: Three newborn babies died after a fire broke out in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) of the District Women’s Hospital in Amravati in the early hours of Monday, prompting the Maharashtra government to order a high-level inquiry into the tragedy. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis expressed grief over the deaths and said the government would provide financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh to the family of each deceased child. He also directed the Amravati district administration to ensure that the medical treatment of injured children was provided entirely at government expense. Families of deceased newborns to receive ₹5 lakh assistance from state government Fadnavis said a high-level investigation would determine the exact cause of the fire and establish whether all required safety procedures had been followed. He questioned whether the hospital’s mandatory fire audit had been properly conducted and whether any lapses had been recorded only on paper. “Those responsible for the deaths of these innocent children will face stringent action,” Fadnavis said, stressing that no one found responsible would be spared. Seven-member committee formed to investigate circumstances behind NICU fire Public Health and Family Welfare Minister Prakash Abitkar, who visited the hospital and inspected the site, said the incident was extremely unfortunate and warranted a detailed investigation. He announced the formation of a seven-member committee headed by Health Department Commissioner Sanjay Katkar to investigate the circumstances surrounding the fire. The committee will include senior officials from the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, AIIMS and the Directorate of Medical Education and Research. It has been asked to submit its report within eight days. According to Abitkar, the committee will examine several aspects, including possible faults in ventilators and electrical systems, the fire audit conducted at the hospital and any other administrative or technical irregularities that may have contributed to the tragedy. The Health Minister said the hospital had been opened only two years ago and was equipped with modern medical facilities. He said such an incident should not have occurred and stressed the need to identify the lapses and implement corrective measures to prevent similar tragedies. Abitkar also visited Dr Panjabrao Deshmukh Medical College to review the condition of newborns who were undergoing treatment after being rescued from the fire. headline: At grievance meet, Haryana minister orders closure of illegal Panchkula gym - The Tribune
text: Haryana Development and Panchayats Minister Krishan Lal Panwar on Tuesday chaired a meeting of the District Public Grievance Redressal Committee at the PWD Rest House in Sector 1 here, where all eight complaints placed before the committee were resolved on the spot, including one concerning an illegally operating gym that was ordered to be shut. Kalka MLA Shakti Rani Sharma and Deputy Commissioner Satpal Sharma were among those present at the meeting. Panwar lauded the Deputy Commissioner and the district administration for resolving all eight complaints. As Chairperson of the committee, he said his priority was to ensure that every grievance was addressed promptly so that complainants received timely relief. He directed officials to resolve each complaint at the earliest so that Panchkula’s committee could become a model for other districts. During the meeting, a complainant from Bagwali village said a gate erected on National Highway land had blocked access to his plot. In this regard, the NHAI Project Director said an inspection had found both permanent and temporary encroachments. Officials said a woman police Inspector and an ASI had been suspended for negligence in the investigation, adding that the case was on trial in court. Panwar directed the Police Department to pursue the case effectively before the court. A resident of Ratpur Colony in Kalka complained about an illegally operating commercial gym near Radheshyam Gaushala, which, the resident said, lacked a fire NOC, CLU and other required approvals. headline: Uttarakhand govt steps up crackdown on adulterators, hoarders ahead of festive season
text: Dehradun, Aug 25 : The Uttarakhand government, led by Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, on Tuesday intensified its crackdown on food adulterators and hoarders ahead of the upcoming festive season, launching an extensive inspection and enforcement campaign across the state. Acting on the Chief Minister's instructions, authorities have been directed to conduct a special weeklong campaign in all districts. Divisional Commissioners have been made responsible for monitoring the drive and ensuring strict action against those involved in food adulteration, hoarding and other violations. Raids, inspections and sampling of food establishments are being carried out across Uttarakhand. Officials have also been directed to destroy expired, spoiled and substandard food items on the spot. Notices are being issued to erring shopkeepers, while court cases have been initiated in several instances. The authorities are also keeping a close watch on the hoarding of essential commodities, particularly sugar, as well as the commercial use of domestic LPG cylinders. In Dehradun, 11 food samples were collected on Monday. Since August 1, officials have inspected 70 establishments in the district and collected 48 samples for testing. In Haridwar, 47 establishments were inspected and 27 samples collected. Similar action has been reported from other districts. In Nainital, 10 shops were inspected and six samples collected, while 10 kg of substandard sweets were destroyed. Ten samples were collected in Pauri, three in Bageshwar, two each in Almora and Pithoragarh, six in Tehri and four in Uttarkashi. In Champawat, 21 locations were inspected, and 10 samples were sent to laboratories for examination. The intensified drive comes ahead of a series of major festivals, including Raksha Bandhan, Krishna Janmashtami, Navratri and Diwali, when the demand for sweets, dairy products and other food items increases significantly. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) enforces a zero-tolerance nationwide framework alongside state authorities to curb food adulteration through strict inspections, mobile testing labs, and heavy legal penalties. The FSSAI prioritises audits and random sampling via a Risk-Based Inspection System (RBIS) targeting high-risk categories like dairy, spices, and edible oils. Over 305 Mobile Food Testing Laboratories (MFTLs), known as Food Safety on Wheels (FSW), operate across states and union territories for instant on-site screening. headline: Haryana Congress to gherao Election Commission office today - The Tribune
text: Haryana Congress to gherao Election Commission office today Hooda alleges irregularities in voter lists, turnout data The Haryana Congress will gherao the State Election Commission’s office in Chandigarh on Friday, demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, former Chief Minister and Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda said on Thursday. Addressing public meetings during his ongoing village outreach programme in the Garhi Sampla-Kiloi Assembly constituency, Hooda alleged that “one disclosure after another” had raised questions over the functioning of the Election Commission. “Following Rahul Gandhi, media reports have now also made it clear that the BJP formed governments in Haryana and several other states by stealing votes,” he alleged. Hooda said the Congress had raised several questions regarding the Haryana Assembly election results but had not received satisfactory answers. He questioned the revision in voter turnout figures, saying the Election Commission had put the turnout at 61.19% on polling night, which increased to 65.65% the following day and 67.9% on October 7, a day before counting. “It is beyond comprehension how the number of votes could increase so much overnight,” he said. Hooda also alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, citing instances where 501 voters were registered at one house, 223 votes in the name of a single woman and 22 votes against the photograph of a foreign woman. He claimed such irregularities involved millions of votes and occurred in both constituencies won and lost by the Congress. Hooda accused the BJP of “stealing” not only votes but the Haryana Government, calling it an attack on democracy and the Constitution.

headline: Mahua Moitra writes to LS Speaker over house eviction order, seeks safety and dignity for women MPs
text: A day after she was asked to vacate a room at a circuit house in her Krishnanagar constituency, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra on Saturday wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, seeking intervention to safeguard the dignity and security of women parliamentarians. Moitra alleged that the administration in West Bengal’s Nadia district ordered her to leave the state-run guest house late on Friday night, despite having initially allotted her accommodation there. She said a crowd gathered outside the circuit house and raised slogans, including “Jai Shree Ram”, after she declined to leave. According to Moitra, she arrived at the circuit house at around 6.15 pm. At 9.47 pm, she received a call from the Nadia additional district magistrate asking her to vacate the premises. She said she later received a WhatsApp message at 10.52 pm containing an order stating that reservations could not be honoured because of “annual cleaning”. In her letter to Birla, Moitra said asking a woman MP staying alone to leave her allotted accommodation late at night raised serious concerns about her rights and security. She urged the Speaker to urgently examine the matter and take steps to uphold the dignity of women MPs, arguing that efforts to increase women’s representation would be meaningless unless elected women representatives were adequately protected. Moitra also approached the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), describing the incident as a threat to democratic norms and alleging that a crowd was gathered outside the circuit house. Several Opposition leaders expressed support for Moitra. TMC Rajya Sabha leader Derek O’Brien questioned the developments in West Bengal, while Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav asked whether the incident amounted to a breach of parliamentary privilege. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas also condemned the incident and called on Birla to intervene, describing the late-night eviction order as “unacceptable and deplorable”. Moitra, the TMC MP from Krishnanagar, has faced several protests and confrontations in Nadia since her election. In recent months, she has alleged that BJP workers targeted her during incidents involving protests outside a district court and a TMC office. The BJP has denied involvement and attributed one such incident to internal factionalism within the TMC. The latest incident comes days after the Supreme Court declined to entertain Moitra’s plea against a Calcutta High Court direction in a case concerning alleged remarks, observing that an MP should not be afraid of facing political backlash. headline: Amravati Hospital Fire: Fadnavis Announces Rs 5 Lakh Ex-gratia
text: The state government will provide Rs 5 lakh in financial assistance to the family of each deceased child, Fadnavis said in a statement. Mumbai: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday expressed grief over the death of three infants in a fire at the District Women's Hospital in Amravati and ordered a high-level inquiry into the incident. The state government will provide Rs 5 lakh in financial assistance to the family of each deceased child, Fadnavis said in a statement. A ventilator in the government hospital's NICU, which houses premature and critically ill babies, caught fire at around 3.15 am, claiming the lives of three children, officials said. Fadnavis said the incident was "extremely tragic and heartbreaking" and expressed solidarity with the families of the deceased. Fortunately, 36 children were rescued safely from the hospital during the incident, he noted. The health administration has been directed to conduct a high-level inquiry, the CM said, and assured that the strictest action would be taken against those found responsible for the tragedy. He directed the state health minister and health secretary to visit Amravati on Monday to take stock of the situation. Fadnavis also directed the Amravati district administration to ensure that the injured children receive treatment at government expense. ( Source : PTI ) Next Story

headline: Congress MLAs protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in J&K Assembly
text: Congress MLAs protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in J&K Assembly Noisy scenes were witnessed in the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly on Friday as Congress MLAs protested against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Soon after the House proceedings began, Congress members stood up, raised slogans against Kumar and displayed banners carrying messages such as “Protect the vote, protect the democracy” and “No democracy without fair elections”. Congress MLAs Nizamuddin Bhat, Irfan Hafiz Lone and Iftikhar Ahmad raised slogans against the CEC. “This is an attack on democracy,” Lone said. Bhat urged Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather to allow the Congress members to speak. However, the Speaker asked them to return to their seats and disallowed the protest. As the Congress MLAs continued raising slogans and attempted to move into the well of the House, the Speaker warned them of action. The members also demanded Kumar's resignation and arrest. The Speaker told the protesting MLAs that the Election Commission of India “is not in our control”. The Congress members later returned to their seats, following which the Question Hour continued. The protest comes amid opposition parties' criticism of the CEC following an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders they said were taken without their knowledge. According to the report, their concerns included changes to statutory Form 6, the addition and deletion of names from electoral rolls and centralised control of the electoral-roll database. The Election Commission has said that differing views and observations are a normal part of institutional deliberations and that its orders have full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures. It also said all three commissioners and other EC officials are authorised to offer suggestions to improve the electoral system. (with inputs from PTI)

headline: Democracy’s Last Mile: Why local journalism matters where public policy meets everyday life
text: Democracy is often imagined in grand settings. Parliament, elections, courts, television studios and national headlines. But for most citizens, democracy is experienced much closer to home: in the government school, the district hospital, the panchayat office, the police station or the block office. That is where a road is sanctioned or abandoned. Where medicines reach a hospital, or do not. Where a school has teachers or exists largely on paper. Where a government scheme reaches its intended beneficiary or disappears somewhere along the way. And that is where someone needs to be watching. In May this year, 60 students at a government school in Nalanda, Bihar, fell ill after consuming their midday meal. Media reporting brought the incident to wider attention. Five days later, the National Human Rights Commission took suo motu cognisance of the report and sought a detailed report from the district administration. The incident was a serious failure of a public service. But what followed also showed why journalism close to the ground matters. A problem that might have remained confined to one school entered the public domain and prompted an institutional response. This is what local journalism does at its best. It takes something that may otherwise remain an allegation, a rumour or a private grievance and turns it into a public record. A social-media post can bring attention to a problem. A reporter can verify what happened, ask who is responsible, seek an answer and, when necessary, return to the story. That persistence is what separates visibility from accountability. It creates a feedback loop between citizens and institutions. Remove the reporter, and the loop breaks. The consequence is not simply that fewer local stories appear in newspapers or on websites. Citizens increasingly have to navigate public life without a reliable record of what is happening around them. This is how news deserts emerge: places where events continue to happen but fewer people are professionally present to record them. A news desert is not a place where nothing happens. It is a place where too little gets recorded. Local journalism is therefore not simply national journalism on a smaller scale. Its importance lies in proximity. headline: AAP Chief Arvind Kejriwal Reacts To Satyendar Jain's Arrest, Calls Case 'Fabricated'
text: AAP chief and former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday, August 18, criticised the arrest of former Delhi minister and party leader Satyendar Jain, alleging that the action was taken at the BJP's behest and calling the case politically motivated. Kejriwal said Jain had once again been arrested despite having previously faced imprisonment in what he described as a fabricated case. He claimed the latest allegations would also eventually be proven false. Questioning the BJP over what he termed "dictatorship", Kejriwal alleged that opposition leaders were being targeted through false cases and sent to jail at the government's discretion. He said that although the allegations would eventually be exposed, the time spent behind bars and the mental distress faced by those arrested could not be compensated. Kejriwal further said the BJP had reached a point where its actions had exhausted the public's patience, claiming that the "end of the Modi government" was inevitable regardless of how much pressure was exerted. He also expressed solidarity with Jain, saying that the Aam Aadmi Party and people across the country stood firmly behind the former minister. Satyendar Jain arrested in Delhi Jal Board case The Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) of the Delhi government arrested Satyendar Kumar Jain on August 18 along with five other accused in connection with discrepancies in the tendering process for projects involving the expansion and modernisation of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) under the Delhi Jal Board (DJB). The other accused include Udit Prakash Rai, a former IAS officer and former CEO of the Delhi Jal Board; Ankit Srivastava, a former contractual consultant with the DJB; and three private individuals: Nagendra Yadav, proprietor of AN Enterprises, Raja Kumar Kurra, owner of Euroteck Environment Pvt. Ltd., and Pankaj Verma, proprietor of Srijanhar. The arrests relate to FIR No. 10/2024, registered at the Anti-Corruption Branch police station on May 11, 2024. The case invokes provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, as amended in 2018, along with IPC sections concerning cheating, criminal breach of trust, cheating by a person bound to protect an interest and criminal conspiracy. The case originated from a complaint filed by the Directorate of Vigilance, Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi, regarding irregularities in the tendering process for the augmentation and upgradation of DJB sewage treatment plants.

headline: Delhi court grants 4 weeks’ interim bail to ex-DGHS Vatsala Agarwal in Rs 600-crore medical scam - The Tribune
text: Delhi court grants 4 weeks’ interim bail to ex-DGHS Vatsala Agarwal in Rs 600-crore medical scam Delhi court notes that the applicant is suffering from hypertension, Type II diabetes mellitus, bronchial asthma, lower backache and right shoulder pain A day after a Delhi court rejected the bail plea of former DGHS official Dr Vinod Kumar Ranga, the court granted relief to Ranga’s co-accused, Dr Vatsala Agarwal, granting her four-week interim bail in connection with the alleged Rs 600-crore medical equipment procurement scam. Special Judge Vidya Prakash allowed interim bail subject to conditions, including furnishing a bail bond of Rs 1 lakh and two sureties of a like amount. The court noted that, after examining the applicant’s medical reports in their entirety, the Medical Officer In-Charge of the Jail Dispensary opined that she complained of breathing difficulty and palpitations. She is suffering from hypertension, Type II diabetes mellitus, bronchial asthma, lower backache and right shoulder pain. She is under regular follow-up by doctors posted at CJ-06 Dispensary, as well as visiting specialists from the Endocrinology, Ophthalmology, Pulmonology and Cardiology departments of Safdarjung Hospital. “In view of the above-noted facts and circumstances and considering the present medical condition of the applicant and without going into the merits of the case or seriousness of the allegations levelled against her, and purely on humanitarian grounds, this Court is of the opinion that the accused deserves to be granted interim bail on medical grounds,” the court noted. “Accordingly, the accused, Dr Vatsala Aggarwal, is hereby admitted to interim bail on medical grounds for a period of four weeks from the date of her release, subject to furnishing a personal bond of Rs 1,00,000 with two sureties of the like amount,” the order stated. The court also laid down several conditions for the bail, including directing her to undergo medical examination and treatment at a hospital of her choice. Further, the court directed her not to leave the NCR region during the period of interim bail without its prior permission. She was also directed to join the investigation, if required by the Investigating Officer, upon written notice during the period of interim bail. The Delhi government's Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) arrested her on June 27 in connection with an alleged multi-crore procurement scam involving medicines, surgical items and medical equipment. headline: 'Dimaagi Naxal' Jibe To Women's Quota: PM Modi’s I-Day Speech Sparks Fresh BJP-Opposition Clash
text: New Delhi: Opposition parties on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his "dimaagi Naxal" remark, saying he should not have used his Independence Day speech for politics, and claimed his pitch on 33 per cent women's reservation in legislatures displayed the ruling BJP's "hypocrisy" after not implementing the quota in the 2024 general elections. Senior BJP leaders, however, hailed the prime minister's speech as a roadmap for achieving the goal of a developed nation, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah terming it a resolve for indigenous development, prosperity and self-reliance. BJP chief Nitin Nabin said the 'Saptdhara' (seven streams of strength) listed by Modi will become new foundations of India’s development journey. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that PM Modi's resolve "is firm and clear: reform with conviction, empower the youth, strengthen our nation and make India a global powerhouse". In his 13th consecutive address on the 80th Independence Day, the prime minister urged political parties to rise above differences to help secure 33 per cent reservation for women in legislatures, called upon the youth to take the lead in building a developed India and warned against being misled by "dimaagi Naxals". The day also saw a row over leaders of opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha - Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge -- not attending the official Independence Day event at the Red Fort. The BJP also attacked the Congress over its former president Sonia Gandhi's alleged objection to the full rendition of 'Vande Mataram' during the Independence Day event at the Congress office. On the other hand, the Congress took a swipe at PM Modi over the sequencing of his tri-coloured pocket squares, saying it seems he is celebrating the Independence Day of Ireland instead of India's. Attacking PM Modi for his 'dimaagi Naxal' remark, leaders of several opposition parties said it was intended to stigmatise his opponents and those questioning the government, with the Congress terming it a "sure sign of desperation". Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged that the prime minister was claiming credit for all that the Congress has done and warned that "he may bring the national flag down one day". headline: Nandigram Congress candidate sent to judicial custody till Oct. 3; no time to canvass for Oct. 6 bypoll
text: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan for the Nandigram byelection in West Bengal was produced at the Haldia district court on Saturday (September 19, 2026) and sent to judicial custody till October 3. This will leave the candidate with no time to campaign for the byelection scheduled for October 6. The cases against him are 19 years old. Mr. Pradhan was was arrested on Friday (September 18) within an hour of Mamata Banerjee extending her support to the candidate, after her own candidate Sanchita Pradhan (De) withdrew her nomination for the bypoll. Ms. Pradhan met with the Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari late on Thursday (September 17) night after which she announced her decision. On Saturday evening, Congress leaders and workers in Kolkata organised a protest march against the arrest of Mr. Pradhan. Police officials said that the arrest of the Nandigram Congress candidate was only a lawful step. “Milan Pradhan was arrested in four cases dating back to 2007 during the Nandigram protests. Some of the charges include murder, attempt to murder, abduction with intent to murder, causing disappearance of evidence, house trespass, rioting with arms and deadly weapons,” an official statement from the West Bengal police said. “Execution of long-pending non-bailable warrants is a standing instruction of the Election Commission of India in respect of all elections/bye-elections. The arrest of Shri Pradhan is a lawful step towards compliance with the same during the course of an ongoing special drive,” the statement said. headline: Will uproot anti-nationals from JU campus: CM Adhikari
text: Will uproot anti-nationals from JU campus: CM Adhikari West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday warned the forces raising the “free Kashmir” slogan inside the Jadavpur University campus, saying he would uproot such elements in the days to come. Adhikari, who led a massive 3-km Gerua Sanman Yatra from Golpark to the JU gate, joined by hundreds of monks, seers and BJP workers, said there was no place for anti-national elements inside the campus and those raising slogans demanding “freedom for Kashmir” would be uprooted. “We will not allow anti-national elements to flourish in the University campus... The forces raising slogans like ‘Kashmir mange azadi’ will be uprooted,” he said, adding he knows “how to teach lessons to those people who insult Gerua (the Saffron flag).” The Chief Minister earlier said that general political slogans like Inquilab Zindabad (long live revolution) or those criticising the Government policies were allowed to be raised. Jadavpur University campus is usually dominated by the Left students’ unions. In a related development, the Chief Minister also said that the Government was proposing to bring a Bill on higher education. According to sources, the Bill could include provisions regarding transfer of college and university teachers. The Left opposition promptly questioned Adhikari’s intentions, saying the Bill was aimed at victimising the college and university teachers for their ideological leanings. “The Chief Minister earlier had threatened to teach the Jadavpur University Teachers’ Association (JUTA) a lesson... By armtwisting them because they have been firmly standing behind the students... But this ploy of the Government will not be successful... Instead of further improving the quality of the University, which is already bringing international laurels, the Government is playing saffron politics ... They will not be successful in their designs... The people will reject their game plan anyway,” said Srijan Bhattacharya, national president of Students Federation of India, a CPI(M) students’ arm. The JU imbroglio started following a midnight ruckus inside the university campus when Left-wing students and alleged ABVP supporters clashed inside the campus.

headline: INDIA bloc parties likely to meet on September 30 to discuss EC related concerns: Report
text: Listen to this article in summarized format The proposed meeting comes amid a political row over the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Congress workers staged protests across several states on Friday demanding the resignation and removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Demonstrations were reported in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Chandigarh, Manipur and West Bengal. The protests followed a directive from the All India Congress Committee to state units to march to Election Commission offices and demand action against Kumar. The Election Commission has rejected the characterisation of the objections as evidence of institutional dissent.
