headline: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke alleges money power in DUSU polls: 'They come in Rolls Royce, BMW'- Moneycontrol.com
text: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) convenor Abhijeet Dipke alleged money power drives the Delhi University Students’ Union elections, pointing to the ABVP’s recent poll victory. The ABVP, an affiliate of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), on Saturday won three of the four central panel posts of DUSU in the polls that unfolded after recent CJP-led Gen Z protests. The Congress-backed National Students' Union of India (NSUI) failed to secure any of the four central panel posts, with the ABVP winning the president, secretary, and joint secretary positions. The VP position was won by an Independent. Dipke claimed campaigners travel in luxury car when asked about the DUSU polls. He said, "Money works in elections and nothing else. Those who campaign in DU come in Rolls Royce, which is worth crores of rupees. They come in Audi, BMW. So money works there." On Congress MP Rahul Gandhi’s claim that the BJP‑led government was promoting people with ideological affiliations, Dipke echoed similar concerns. "In Amravati, I saw that Vice Chancellor Kumud Sharma (VC of Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya, Wardha, located near Amravati) comes from the RSS ideology. Since she became VC, FIRs have been registered against more than 50 students," he claimed, PTI reported. "When students protest for something, an FIR is registered against them. But when ABVP opposes something or locks any gate, no FIR is registered against them. Only Dalit, Adivasi (tribal) students who oppose the ideology are booked. It is a roadmap to make institutions (universities) a shakha of RSS," Dipke charged. The CJP founder further claimed students were losing faith in the education system. headline: CJP team pushed out of Rajasthan village; Dipke claims BJP 'goon' behind attack - OrissaPOST
text: Jaipur: A scuffle broke out at a village in Rajasthan when villagers, allegedly accompanied by BJP workers, put up barricades and forcibly pushed back a Cockroach Janta Party team that had gone there to inspect a government school as part of its “School Thik Karo” campaign. Rampura Kanwarpura village in Jaipur district became the latest trouble point for the CJP, which alleged that its workers were attacked and pelted with stones, with co-convener Ashutosh Ranka accusing the state police of failing to intervene. Ranka alleged that members of the CJP team were assaulted, vehicles were damaged and women supporters were roughed up. Founder Abhijeet Dipke asked what is happening in Rajasthan and said in a post on X, “Goons of BJP are after the blood of Ashutosh and other CJP volunteers. How can @PoliceRajasthan allow this kind of attack?” Bagru DSP Dharmendra Sharma, however, said he was unaware of any such development. Videos of the incident showed a large number of people engaging in a heated exchange with the CJP team, pushing and shoving its members as they tried to enter the village. Some clips also showed smashed windows of cars, believed to belong to the visiting CJP team. “All levels of disgust were crossed today. For the past several years, the school at Rampura Kanwarpura has been running from a buffalo shed. “But when we reached there for an inspection, we were openly assaulted, pelted with stones. Car windows were smashed, stones were rained down on the team. Clothes were torn. My clothes were also torn.” Ranka told reporters. The school building was closed for students after being declared ‘unsafe’, with classes being held in a cattle enclosure close to it. The villagers, however, claimed that the government had already sanctioned funds for the repair work, which could be carried out with local efforts. Ranka alleged that the CJP team was attacked on the orders of Rajasthan Education Minister Madan Dilawar. “Madan Dilawar finds it acceptable for children to study in a buffalo shed. But fixing the school? That’s not acceptable,” he said. “Mr Dilawar â€“ you sent goons today and shamed the entire state of Rajasthan in the eyes of the country. But we are not the kind of people who get intimidated by such thuggery,” he added. “Today, the entire country has seen BJP’s hooliganism live. This is a black day for democracy in Rajasthan,” he said.

text: Arrested Nandigram Congress candidate Milan Pradhan’s wife has appealed to all Opposition parties on Thursday (September 24) to support her husband. headline: Waris Punjab De protests outside AAP ministers’ houses in Ludhiana - The Tribune
text: With Assembly elections approaching, political protests against the AAP government in Punjab have intensified, with members and supporters of Akali Dal Waris Punjab De staging demonstrations outside the residences of AAP ministers in Ludhiana district. Supporters, mostly youngsters, protested outside the residences of Cabinet Ministers Tarunpreet Singh Sondh and Hardeep Singh Mundian. The protests were part of the statewide agitation being carried out by Waris Punjab De against the AAP government. The demonstrations in Ludhiana were held under the guidance of party leader Manpreet Singh Ayali. Protesters waved black flags and raised slogans against the government, demanding action and justice in several matters. Ayali told The Tribune that the alleged police brutality against Mohanjit Singh Sheron was intolerable. Sheron was allegedly subjected to physical and mental torture after being detained for showing black flags to the Chief Minister near the residence of Punjab Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr Balbir Singh in Patiala recently. “Besides, the Chief Minister’s wife too has been named in Rs 5 crore bribery act against a rapist and the tragic death of farmer Gulzar Singh was another example about the atrocities being done by the ruling party in Punjab. We want accountability by the state government on all these matters. Black flags were shown to the ministers of AAP by Waris Punjab De all over,” said Ayali. The protesters sat outside the ministers’ residences and raised anti-government slogans, demanding a proper probe into the matters. Protest outside Gajjanmajra’s residence In another incident, protesters gheraoed the residence of AAP MLA Jaswant Singh Gajjanmajra at Begowal village in the Amargarh area last evening. A video of the incident is also circulating on social media. The protest followed allegations of torture of a village woman by the police and AAP workers. The protesters alleged that instead of taking action against the AAP workers, the MLA turned a blind eye and decided to hold a rally against the victim. Police stopped the protesters from entering the MLA’s residence.

headline: Shocking classroom death: 6-year-old boy collapses after being scolded, slapped by teacher in Andhra Pradesh - The Tribune
text: Shocking classroom death: 6-year-old boy collapses after being 'scolded', 'slapped' by teacher in Andhra Pradesh Family alleges that the child's fatal collapse was triggered by extreme panic and distress following the alleged assault A six-year-old boy died in a classroom at a private school here after being allegedly slapped by a teacher, police said. According to a video which went viral on Thursday, the kindergarten student was seen standing near the teacher's desk in a queue with a slate while his homework was being checked. The boy appears distressed and was seen crying before the teacher, waving his hands as the teacher handled his uniform. The teacher then pulls the child closer and allegedly slaps him while the boy stood still for a brief moment before suddenly collapsing unconscious onto the teacher's lap. headline: Over a year after resignation, ex-VP Jagdeep Dhankhar yet to get official residence- Moneycontrol.com
text: Jagdeep Dhankhar’s temporary post-retirement address has stretched into a year-long stay, with the former vice-president continuing to live at a private farmhouse in Delhi as he awaits government accommodation. Dhankhar has been staying at a farmhouse owned by Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) leader Abhay Singh Chautala in Chhatarpur since September 1, 2025. The arrangement was initially described by people close to the former vice-president as temporary, but he has continued to reside there nearly a year later. As per a Hindustan Times report, no government residence has been allotted to Dhankhar so far. His office did not respond to queries on whether any accommodation had been proposed or sought since his resignation. The former vice-president is entitled to government accommodation for life under the rules governing pension, housing and other facilities for retired vice-presidents. The rules provide for a furnished residence without rent, water or electricity charges. Under the existing framework, a retired vice-president is ordinarily entitled to a Type-VIII government residence at a location of their choice. If such accommodation is unavailable, the rules provide for the highest category of government housing available at that location. In cases where government accommodation is not available, the Centre can arrange leased accommodation with a living area of up to 2,000 square feet, according to the rules. The accommodation is to be drawn from the General Pool Residential Accommodation stock administered by the Directorate of Estates under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). A former vice-president has to approach the ministry to exercise the entitlement. The delay in Dhankhar’s case comes despite indications last year that a Type-VIII bungalow had been readied for him. Officials in the estates administration had then indicated that accommodation suitable for the former vice-president was available in Lutyens’ Delhi. Dhankhar had resigned from the vice-presidency on July 21, 2025, citing health concerns. In his resignation letter to President Droupadi Murmu, he said he wanted to prioritise healthcare and follow medical advice. His resignation came hours after he admitted an Opposition-backed motion in the Rajya Sabha seeking a probe into former Delhi High Court judge Justice Yashwant Varma. The Lok Sabha had also admitted a similar motion backed by parties across the political spectrum. Opposition leaders subsequently alleged that Dhankhar had been compelled to resign, a claim that was not established. headline: Supreme Court suspends sentence of NSCN(M) militant convicted in 2009 Manipur killings
text: Supreme Court suspends sentence of NSCN(M) militant convicted in 2009 Manipur killings The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the sentence of self-styled NSCN(M) "lieutenant" Hopeson Nignshen, convicted in connection with the abduction and killing of three Manipur government officials in the state's Ukhrul district in February 2009. A bench comprising Justice M M Sundresh and Justice P B Varale noted that Nignshen has been in jail for more than 17 years. "We are dealing with a case where the appellant has been incarcerated for more than 17 years and therefore, he is relying only on the ground of suspension of sentence, particularly when his appeal is pending. We grant suspension of sentence on the following conditions: the applicant shall stay within the boundaries of Delhi and not leave until the appeal is disposed of," the bench said. The counsel appearing for the Manipur government opposed the plea. The Delhi High Court on November 20, 2019 had upheld trial court's order convicting Nignshen for kidnapping and killing three government officials in Manipur in 2009 and handed him life imprisonment. The trial court in 2014 had awarded the jail term to Hopeson Nignshen, holding him guilty of abducting Dr Thingnam Kishan Singh and two others, and killing them after conspiring with other National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Isak Muivah (NSCN-IM) militants. Nignshen, who was also held guilty of looting the deceased's belonging, was asked to pay a fine of Rs 35,000. The case was transferred to Delhi from Manipur on the Supreme Court's direction in May 2010 after CBI had apprehended a threat to Nignshen's life and chances of unrest in the state if he was presented in a Manipur court. According to CBI, on February 13, 2009, Nignshen and other NSCN-IM militants had abducted Kishan Singh, SDO-cum-BDO of Kasom Khullen in Manipur's Ukhrul district, and five members of his personal staff. The agency had said that on the next day, the militants allegedly let off three of the abducted people -- Ram Singh Siro, Ramthing Singlai and Kapangkhui Jajo, who belonged to the Naga community -- while killing Kishan Singh, Y Token Singh and A Rajen Sharma. headline: J&K’s political paradox: The Battle between Demanding Power and Pinning Blame
text: Amid the humid September weather, Jammu and Kashmir's summer capital last Wednesday witnessed the NC and BJP staging counter-protests. The protests by the National Conference (NC) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Srinagar on Wednesday have exposed a contradiction at the heart of Jammu and Kashmir’s post-2019 political arrangement. The party in power in the Union Territory is demanding more powers to govern, while the principal opposition, which, ironically, also wields the actual power via New Delhi, is questioning its performance in office. The National Conference, which runs the government in Jammu and Kashmir, protested near the BJP office demanding restoration of statehood. The BJP, in turn, held a counter-protest targeting the Omar Abdullah government over governance and its record in office. The confrontation is more than another round of political mobilisation. It raises a fundamental question that has remained unresolved since Jammu and Kashmir lost its special constitutional position and was downgraded from a state to a Union Territory on August 5, 2019. The question is who should ultimately be held responsible for governing the region? Ideological Differences and Power-Sharing Anomalies The ideological differences between the BJP and the NC lie at the centre of this confrontation. For the BJP, the political reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir in 2019 was part of a larger project to integrate the region more firmly with the Union and move away from the special constitutional arrangement that existed before August 5, 2019. For the NC, restoration of statehood has become a central political demand and a measure of whether the Centre is prepared to return the political and administrative powers that the region enjoyed as a state. Political analysts believe the two parties have fundamentally different political ideologies. “While the BJP believes in greater centralisation, the NC’s belief system is historically rooted in a stronger federal structure,” said Shahnawaz Hussain, a political analyst. That ideological contest has deep roots. In October 1983, then Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah convened a landmark opposition meeting in Srinagar, bringing together 17 political parties and nearly 60 prominent opposition leaders. headline: 'School Thik Karo' Campaign: Rajasthan Govt Tightens Entry Rules, Sparks Political Row Over Media Access
text: Jaipur: Citing the state’s special responsibility for the safety, dignity, privacy, and well-being of children, the Rajasthan Education Department has issued guidelines restricting the entry of outsiders, including media personnel, into government schools without prior permission. Order Triggers Political Row However, the timing of the order has triggered a political controversy as it comes amid the Cockroach Janata Party’s “School Thik Karo” campaign, under which party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka has announced inspections of dilapidated government schools. The order, citing the state’s special responsibility for the safety, dignity, privacy, and well-being of children, refers to the principle of in loco parentis and right to life, dignity, and privacy under Article 21 of the Constitution. It also cites Supreme Court judgments on privacy and guidelines issued by the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) that have existed for years. Reacting to the development, Ranka challenged Education Minister Madan Dilawar and the state government, saying that the campaign would continue despite the restrictions. “Either fix all the dilapidated schools in Rajasthan, or file an FIR against us in advance,” Ranka said in a social media post, adding that the party would not stop inspecting schools until their condition was improved. Under the new directives, no outsider will be permitted to enter a government school without prior permission from the principal or head of the institution. Government officials authorized to perform official duties have been exempted from the restriction. The Education Department’s order makes it mandatory for visitors to register their details in the school visitor register before entering. Outsiders will not be allowed to enter classrooms, laboratories, libraries, dormitories, playgrounds, restrooms, or other areas where students are present unless accompanied by the principal, a teacher, or an authorized school official. The guidelines also impose restrictions on photography, videography, interviews, audio recording, and live streaming involving students, teachers, or school activities. Such activities will require prior written permission from the principal. The department has further prohibited the collection, publication, or dissemination of photographs, videos, or personal information of students where such use could compromise their privacy, dignity, or safety. School administrations have been instructed to ensure that students’ identities and personal information are not used in ways that could adversely affect their well-being. headline: Watch | BJP worker eats mud in protest over Cauvery water dispute in Karnataka's Mandya- Moneycontrol.com
text: In an unusual protest over the Cauvery water dispute, BJP worker Shivakumar Aradhya ate mud in Karnataka's Mandya, alleging that the state government had “put soil in farmers’ mouths.” Aradhya staged the protest near the Visvesvaraya statue in Mandya, raising slogans against the Karnataka government and the Cauvery Water Management Authority. The protest came amid continued concerns among farmers over the sharing and release of Cauvery water. The Cauvery water dispute remains a decades-old and politically contentious issue between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over the river’s allocation. While the Cauvery originates in Karnataka and eventually flows through Tamil Nadu into the Bay of Bengal, the two states have differing water needs. Karnataka has maintained that it must meet the requirements of its drinking-water supply and farmers, while Tamil Nadu relies heavily on the river for irrigation in its Cauvery delta. The latest protests followed a direction from the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) asking Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. Groups in Karnataka have opposed the order, arguing that the state is itself dealing with water shortages and should first meet its domestic and agricultural requirements. Mandya, a key centre of the Cauvery agitation, witnessed demonstrations by farmers and pro-Kannada organisations at Sanjay Circle and other parts of the district. Protesters carried empty vessels and horse gram, raised slogans including “Our water, our right” and disrupted traffic on the old Bengaluru–Mysuru highway. The horse gram was meant to highlight how farmers could be compelled to shift away from paddy to less water-intensive crops amid the shortage. headline: PM Modi pays tribute to Bhagat Singh on birth anniversary, calls him
text: PM Modi pays tribute to Bhagat Singh on birth anniversary, calls him "source of inspiration for every Indian" New Delhi [India], September 28 (ANI): Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday paid tribute to freedom fighter Shaheed Bhagat Singh on his 119th birth anniversary, describing him as a "source of inspiration for every Indian", particularly for the youth of the country. In a video message shared on X, PM Modi recalled Bhagat Singh's fearlessness and unwavering commitment to India's freedom struggle, saying his life and sacrifice continue to inspire generations. "Amar Shaheed Bhagat Singh for every Indian, especially the youth of the country, is a source of inspiration. Fearlessness was ingrained in his nature," PM Modi said. The Prime Minister also recalled a letter Bhagat Singh had written to the British authorities before his execution, in which he demanded that he and his fellow revolutionaries be treated as prisoners of war. "Before dangling from the gallows for the country, Bhagat Singh ji had also written a letter to the British. He had said that I want you to treat me and my companions like prisoners of war. Therefore, our life should be taken not by hanging, but directly by shooting. This is proof of his indomitable courage," he added. PM Modi further highlighted Bhagat Singh's sensitivity towards the suffering of people and his willingness to help others. "Bhagat Singh ji was also very sensitive to people's pain and always stayed ahead in helping. I respectfully pay tribute to Shaheed Bhagat Singh ji," he said. In a separate post on X, PM Modi said Bhagat Singh's indomitable courage and valour had infused new vigour into India's freedom movement. "Millions of salutations to Shaheed Bhagat Singh on his birth anniversary. With their indomitable courage and valor, he infused new vigor into the freedom movement. His spirit of sacrificing everything for the honor of the nation is a symbol of the courage and resolve of India's youth," he said. Bhagat Singh was born on September 28, 1907, in Banga, in present-day Pakistan's Punjab province. He emerged as one of the most prominent revolutionaries of India's freedom struggle. On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs inside the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi in protest against colonial legislation. headline: Manipur CM Urges Delhi Government for Swift Probe into Musician’s Death
text: Guwahati: Today, manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh has urged Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta to ensure a swift, transparent and time-bound investigation into the alleged assault and subsequent death of Manipuri musician C. Vikram Singh in New Delhi. In a letter to Gupta dated 8th September , Khemchand said the 54-year-old musician was allegedly assaulted outside his residence in Kilokari Village in the early hours of 7th September after objecting to disorderly conduct, shouting and public consumption of alcohol. Singh later succumbed to injuries sustained in the alleged attack. The Chief Minister said the incident had triggered widespread grief, anger and anxiety among people in the state and the wider Northeast community. He warned that any perception of delay, bias or delay in delivering justice could further worsen public unrest, particularly amid concerns over the safety of people from the Northeast living in the capital of India. Chongtham Vikram Singh’s wife, Joshna Chongtham, said she was struggling to come to terms with the sudden loss of her husband, describing him as a father, son, brother, musician and a deeply loved member of the family. “At these difficult times, I ask that my family be allowed to grieve in peace and privacy,” Joshna said. “We are not seeking revenge. We are seeking justice,” she said, stressing that her husband had a family, a name and a life that mattered. Khemchand sought Gupta’s personal intervention to ensure that the investigation was conducted fairly and transparently under the supervision of senior police officials and completed within a stipulated timeframe. He also urged Delhi police to arrest all those allegedly involved . Till now, Delhi Police have arrested seven men and also arrested a juvenile in connection with the alleged assault.

headline: Man slapped by Delhi minister Parvesh Verma was out on bail in MCD worker abduction, assault case
text: NEW DELHI: The controversy over Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma slapping a man during a road inspection took a fresh turn on Monday after details of an earlier assault case involving the man emerged. Sahib Singh, 22, who was seen filming road work when Verma confronted and slapped him, had allegedly been arrested in a case registered at Tilak Nagar over the assault of a municipal worker, according to police records and documents shared by the minister. The case dates back to June, when MCD worker Dhan Bahadur alleged that he was assaulted after objecting to garbage being thrown from a building into a collection vehicle. According to his complaint, several men allegedly dragged him from the vehicle and beat him. He was taken to Deen Dayal Upadhyay Hospital, where he underwent a medico-legal examination. A FIR was subsequently registered under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Bahadur later in a video said that Singh was among those involved in the assault. Singh has also been identified by the BJP as the man who allegedly abused Verma's family before the minister slapped him. The incident has triggered a political confrontation between the BJP and AAP, with AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal likely to visit the area on Monday.

headline: Water war between AP And TG : KRMB defers decision on drinking water sharing
text: Water war between AP And TG : KRMB defers decision on drinking water sharing The three member – committee of Krishna River Management Board (KRMB) has once again deffered a decision on Krishna water sharing between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for drinking purposes. Officials said that since the two states are not accepting each other for the proposed sharing. In the previous meeting on August 24, the committee deferred its decision due to the both states did not come into consensus on water sharing. The committee met again on Friday in Hyderabad for which the Irrigation officials from the both states attended. According to the officials, during the meeting, the Telangana government has proposed sharing of Krishna water on a 50:50 percent basis, for which the Andhra Pradesh government has objected. In contrast, the Andhra Pradesh government has proposed 66 percent of water for Andhra Pradesh and 34 percent for Telangana. Officials of Telangana government has objected to the proposal submitted by Andhra Pradesh. Sources said that the officials of both states have made allegations against each other on utilization of krishna water. While, Andhra Pradesh alleged that Telangana government is utilizing water from Nagarjuna Sagar project for power generation, Telangana government alleged that Andhra Pradesh is illeagally withdrawing water from Pothireddypady project. Andhra Pradesh government urged the KRMB to direct Telangana government to stop power generation immediately. Telangana Irrigation Officials, speaking to reporters, said that they have demanded allocation of 200 TMC of water to Telangana, due to the prevailing El – Nino conditions. They also made it clear that they have objected to 66: 34 percent sharing proposed by Andhra Pradesh. For the last three year Andhra Pradesh government is repeatedly proposing the same percentage of sharing despite the Telangana government objecting, they added.

headline: Gauhati HC tells Assam govt to pay Rs 2 lakh each to kin of two women expelled to Bangladesh
text: Gauhati HC tells Assam govt to pay Rs 2 lakh each to kin of two women expelled to Bangladesh The Gauhati High Court has directed the Assam government to pay interim compensation of Rs 2 lakh each to the families of two women who were declared non-citizens by a foreigners tribunal and sent to Bangladesh without their families being informed or being allowed to exhaust their legal remedies. In separate orders passed on September 3, a division bench of Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund also impleaded the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to facilitate the repatriation of Mumtaz Begum and Jahanara Begum from Bangladesh. Both women were declared non-citizens by the Foreigners Tribunal in Nagaon’s Juria. Mumtaz’s husband Mujammel Hoque and Jahanara’s son Mujahidul Islam approached the High Court seeking relief. The court observed that Article 21 of the Constitution, which guarantees protection of life and personal liberty, applies to non-citizens as well as Indians. It said the women had been deprived of the opportunity to challenge the tribunal’s opinions before the High Court. The amount will be in addition to any compensation the petitioners may seek before a civil court. The bench directed the MEA to help locate the two women in Bangladesh and bring them back to India so they can pursue their legal remedies against the tribunal orders. In both cases, the court found that the authorities had failed to provide the women with copies of the tribunal’s opinions or inform adult members of their families about their detention and expulsion. headline: Shiv Sena ministers trying to engineer riots: Jarange Patil
text: Mumbai: Tensions between Maratha leader Manoj Jarange Patil and the state government escalated, with Patil accusing Shiv Sena ministers of trying to engineer riots in the state. There were sharp exchanges between the Shiv Sena ministers and Patil, with the latter threatening to lead thousands of Marathas to Mumbai if the state government does not issue a government resolution to give Kunbi caste certificates to the Marathas. "Eknath Shinde ministers are planning to create riots in the state. It's a conspiracy. They do not want Marathas to get Kunbi caste certificates... We will crush them. We are going to Mumbai on September 12," Patil said. He has claimed that Shinde's ministers have been instrumental in cancelling the Kunbi caste certificates issued to the Marathas. Patil, who till recently was only attacking the CM, has turned his focus on Shinde also and has been relentlessly attacking him and his ministers. "He should focus on his stir, which is on the reservation issue. Why is he attacking our leader? He should not teach us. We can give him a befitting response. We are also Marathas. If he continues his attacks, then we will respond in the same manner," said Shiv Sena minister Bharat Gogawale. On Wednesday, protesters blocked traffic on the Beed-Parli national highway for two hours. The Hingoli market was shut while Maratha protesters were fasting for the last three days in Nanded. Roads were also blocked in Dhule. Sena minister Uday Samant and BJP MLC Prasad Lad said 3.16 lakh Kunbi caste certificates have been issued to eligible Marathas. On Patil's claim that several applications for Kunbi certificates were rejected, Samant said, "21,051 applications were submitted for caste validity verification, out of which 16,110 were issued. Out of this, 64 applications were found invalid, which is just 0.3% rejection. He has been misguided by people close to him that there is mass rejection of caste certificates."

headline: Karnataka: Report on plugging exam and recruitment loopholes sought
text: The Cabinet sub-committee on student issues and education reforms has asked S.R. Niranjana, Vice-Chairman of the Karnataka State Higher Education Council, to submit a report on conducting examinations without paper leaks and ensuring transparency in examinations and recruitment processes for various posts, U.T. Khader, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, who heads the sub-committee, said on Thursday after its first meeting. This comes in the wake of widespread student protests across the country over the NEET paper leak and the recent controversy surrounding the alleged scam in the recruitment of 400 veterinary officers by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). The Jharkhand government faced similar protests, as seen in Delhi, over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The sub-committee was also formed in response to Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi’s student interaction programme, Chatron Ki Goonj, and recent student protests across the country. The committee also discussed the recruitment process of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). There was a discussion on KPSC’s inability to adopt a Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)-style examination system and how this may have prevented deserving candidates from securing coveted posts in the State government. “A permanent solution should be found to the irregularities and problems in the KPSC recruitment process. Necessary reforms should be undertaken to put an end to such cases,” said Madhu Bangarappa, Minister for School Education and Literacy and a member of the sub-committee. The sub-committee also announced that it would launch a website for students, parents and other stakeholders to submit suggestions on education reforms. The committee will also tour the State to interact with students and teachers and understand their problems firsthand. Published - September 04, 2026 12:46 am IST

The case was registered following a complaint lodged by TR Ramappa, former vice-chairman of the ST Department (Adivasi Congress) of the Indian National Congress at Vidhana Soudha Police Station on August 31, they said. headline: Karnataka Congress Protests Against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Demands Resignation
text: Terming the alleged actions of the CEC as being against democracy and the Constitution, Congress leaders and workers staged the protest, holding placards and raising slogans demanding Kumar's resignation and action against him Bengaluru: Karnataka Congress on Saturday staged a protest at Freedom Park here against the Election Commission's SIR exercise, demanding the resignation and arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Citing media reports, party leaders alleged that Kumar had taken several decisions without the concurrence of the other two Election Commissioners despite their objections. They alleged that the exercise had resulted in the deletion of a large number of voters' names. Terming the alleged actions of the CEC as being against democracy and the Constitution, Congress leaders and workers staged the protest, holding placards and raising slogans demanding Kumar's resignation and action against him. Several senior party leaders, such as Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, State Congress President B K Hariprasad, former Chief Ministers Siddaramaiah and Veerappa Moily, AICC Secretary Gopinath Palaniyappan, state ministers and legislators, participated in the protest. The Congress has also held protests in Mysuru and several other parts of the state. The protest demanding the CEC's resignation came in the wake of an Indian Express investigation which reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the last 10 months to decisions and orders they said were issued without their knowledge. The objections included changes to statutory voter registration Form 6 and the centralisation of control over the electoral roll database, according to the report. The Election Commission, however, has asserted that its official orders, decisions and administrative directions have full legal sanction, and that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations within any institution.

headline: Assam Government Encroaches Into a World Heritage Site in India’s Northeast
text: Manas National Park in the northeast Indian state of Assam is in danger. The Assam government, which should be protecting this 1,176-acre World Heritage Site, has encroached on the park for several years. Originally part of the North Kamrup Reserve Forest, the land under contention, which is spread over 9.3 sq km, was given on a 30-year lease to the Indian government for setting up a seed farm. After the lease expired in 2001, the area became part of the Manas National Park and Tiger Reserve, the Assam forest department said in a letter to the Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) that governs this region. In the letter, the Assam forest department pointed out that the BTC had leased the encroached land for cultivation. Sources claimed that local farmers are engaged in farming in the area, which is officially not permitted inside a wildlife sanctuary, national park or World Heritage Site. The letter made a case for its handover to the forest department. The forest department also urged the Assam government to convince the BTC to return the encroached area to the Assam forest department The area that has been allegedly encroached by local farmers with the BTC’s consent is part of the Manas National Park’s core tiger and Bengal florican habitats. This falls in the Bhuyanpara Range of the park, which is also where the erstwhile government-owned Kokilabari Seed Farm was located. Concerned about the encroachment and its devastating impact on the park, the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has also been reminding the Assam government to initiate action over the past few years. In a communique dated July 30, 2026, which was also posted on social media, the NTCA asked the chief secretary of the Assam government to “intervene” and facilitate the “handing over” of the encroached area to the Manas Tiger Reserve authorities. It also reminded the government that a directive on the issue had been sent on June 11, but the authority was “not aware about the progress made in the matter so far.” Manas National Park was designated as a reserve forest in 1907 and declared a wildlife sanctuary in 1928. In 1973, it became India’s first tiger reserve. Spread across an area of 2,837 sq km, the park was the largest in the country. The date has a particular significance for India as it marks the launch of the Government’s ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign in 2024. The UN recognition could provide an additional impetus to state-level campaigns by bringing greater international attention to prevention, education, community mobilisation and enforcement of the law. text: By Kritika Bhardwaj Following from the five-judge bench’s decision yesterday, a nine-judge bench was constituted today to determine the existence of a fundamental right to privacy. Arguments were advanced on behalf of some of the petitioners today. A background to this hearing, and the larger Aadhaar case can be found here. Senior counsel appearing for Mr. Mathew Thomas commenced arguments today. He began by arguing that both M.P. Sharma v. Satish Chandra (MP Sharma) and Kharak Singh v. State of Punjab (Kharak Singh) were decided when AK Gopalan v. State of Madras (Gopalan) held the field. The view adopted in AK Gopalan was that different fundamental rights operated in individual silos and were to be read separately. This decision was overruled by an eleven-judge bench in R. C. Cooper v. Union of India (RC Cooper). It was argued that neither of the two decisions in question could be considered good law with respect to their interpretation of fundamental rights, given that the basis for these judgments i.e. AK Gopalan was overruled. Further, the observation in MP Sharma that there is no right to privacy within Article 20(3) of the Constitution could not extinguish a general right to privacy. With respect to Kharak Singh, it was pointed out that the minority view in the case applied had the correct test and consequently, liberty was not a residuary expression and inherently contemplated privacy. It was argued that the concepts of privacy and liberty could not be separated. If life and liberty were considered inalienable, so was privacy, as the former could not exist without the latter. Characterising the American jurisprudence on privacy as being rooted in the concept of liberty, and the continental understanding emerging from dignity, he argued that the Preamble to the Indian Constitution considered both to be inalienable values. He contended that privacy was the essence of liberty, and that human development and exercising choice required internal privacy. It was pointed out that pursuant to the Court’s decision in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (Maneka Gandhi), Articles 14, 19 and 21 had to be read together. Indian Youth Congress National Secretary Tariq Bagawan, along with Youth Congress office-bearers and students, participated in the protest. The Youth Congress alleged that the police resorted to caning to disperse the protesters in New Delhi. Karnataka Pradesh Youth Congress Committee president H.S. headline: CPI(M), Congress leaders trade barbs over rail division split
text: The row over the proposed bifurcation of the Palakkad railway division has triggered a political slugfest between CPM and Congress leaders, with both sides challenging each other over protests against the Centre. CPM district secretary E.N. Suresh Babu challenged Congress MP V.K. Sreekandan to stage an indefinite hunger strike in front of the Railway Ministry in Delhi if he was serious about opposing the transfer of Mangaluru from Palakkad rail division. He also called on the Congress to launch a strong agitation against the Centre. Mr. Sreekandan hit back, saying those with the courage to protest should take on the BJP instead of targeting him. He accused CPI(M) leaders of being afraid of the BJP and said they were attacking him instead of protesting against the Centre. Mr. Sreekandan also accused the CPI(M) of trying to mislead people over railway development in Palakkad. The BJP, meanwhile, criticised both the Congress and CPI(M) for trading accusations over the issue. The BJP said the two fronts were trying to turn the matter into a political controversy instead of explaining the facts behind the Centre’s decision. With protests against the division continuing, the railway issue is emerging as a new point of confrontation among the political parties in the State. Published - August 24, 2026 08:24 pm IST

headline: Manoj Jarange stands firm on hunger strike, urges Marathas to apply for Kunbi certificates- Moneycontrol.com
text: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Thursday refused to end his indefinite hunger strike despite fresh assurances from the Maharashtra government. However, he urged members of the Maratha community to begin applying for Kunbi caste certificates from September 4, saying the process should not be delayed. Jarange has been on an indefinite fast for the past six days at Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district, demanding reservation for the Maratha community. A government delegation comprising Ministers Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil and Uday Samant, along with MLC Prasad Lad and MLA Makarand Patil, met Jarange to persuade him to withdraw or postpone his protest. Appealing to Jarange to end his fast in view of his deteriorating health, Vikhe Patil said the government was committed to resolving the Maratha reservation issue. He added that officials had traced nearly 58 lakh Kunbi records and the process of issuing Kunbi certificates would be expedited. Nodal officers would also be appointed to oversee the process and resolve issues faced by applicants. Although Jarange remained firm on continuing his protest, he asked eligible Marathas to start submitting applications for Kunbi certificates, especially based on records identified in the Hyderabad Gazette. The activist said the 58 lakh records would help eligible families obtain Kunbi certificates and validity certificates. Applications, he said, could be made using family, blood or clan links with people whose Kunbi records have already been traced. Kunbi, an agrarian community, falls under the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category. Jarange has been demanding Kunbi certificates for eligible Marathas to enable them to claim reservation under the OBC quota. He also urged people facing difficulties in submitting applications to approach their respective district collectors. Making it clear that the government's assurances were not enough, Jarange said he would continue his hunger strike until all the demands of the Maratha community were accepted. "I will drink water and take IV fluids, but I will not break my fast," he said, while also urging Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde to take a "sincere and concrete stand" in support of the Maratha community. headline: ‘It Is A Matter Of Great Joy’: Piyush Goyal Wishes PM Modi On 76th Birthday, Hails 25 Years Of Service
text: Mumbai: Union Minister Piyush Goyal on Thursday extended birthday wishes to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as he turned 76, highlighting his nearly 25 years of service across fields and expressing hope that he would continue to guide the country towards the goal of a developed India by 2047. Speaking to reporters in Mumbai, Goyal said Modi's birthday was being marked through various service-oriented programmes across the country. “It is a matter of great joy for all of us today that we are celebrating the birthday of Prime Minister Narendra Modi through acts of service at various locations across the country,” Goyal said. Goyal highlights Modi's development vision Goyal said Modi's vision extended beyond individual projects and encompassed creating opportunities for young people, empowering women, expanding access to healthcare and education, generating employment and strengthening India's position globally. He also highlighted the Prime Minister's stated goal of making India a developed country by 2047. Goyal expressed confidence that India would achieve the Viksit Bharat goal and prayed for Modi's health and long life. “I pray to God to grant PM Modi a long and healthy life, so that he may continue to guide and lead us for years to come, inspiring and motivating us all to dedicate our lives to the nation,” Goyal said. PM Modi turns 76 Born on September 17, 1950, Narendra Modi turned 76 on Thursday. The occasion also comes close to the completion of 25 years since Modi first assumed executive office as Gujarat Chief Minister in October 2001. He served as Gujarat Chief Minister before becoming Prime Minister in 2014 and began his third consecutive term as PM in 2024. Moreover, birthday greetings poured in from political leaders across the country, with several leaders wishing Modi good health and a long life. 25-foot sand art at Puri Beach Subsequently, marking Modi's 76th birthday, Padma Shri awardee and renowned sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik created a 25-foot sand art installation at Puri Beach in Odisha. headline: ‘Not on our to-do list’: Andhra Pradesh minister Nara Lokesh rejects proposal for airport near Chennai
text: AMARAVATI: The Andhra Pradesh IT and industries minister Nara Lokesh has rejected a suggestion that the state could develop a new airport at Sri City to cater to passengers from Chennai. He denied the idea, saying the state already has enough development projects on its plate. Responding to a post suggesting that Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu could ensure a new airport at Sri City if he secures another term, the minister said the proposal was not among the state’s priorities. “Between Amaravati, Polavaram and three economic regions, we have enough development to do in AP already! This is not on our ‘to-do’ list. Respectfully, we will pass on this,” he said in a post on X. The remarks came shortly after Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay’s government dropped the proposed Parandur greenfield airport project in Kancheepuram district. The exchange comes amid a political debate over Chennai’s second airport project, after the Tamil Nadu government dropped the proposed Parandur site and announced plans to identify an alternative location. Why was Parandur airport scrapped? Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay announced in the Assembly on Monday that the state government had dropped the proposed airport at Parandur and would look for an alternative site. A technical feasibility study will be conducted before a new location is finalised. The TVK government said it was opposed to the Parandur site because the project would require relocation of a large number of people and affect agricultural land. Vijay had earlier visited Eganapuram and other villages around Parandur and met residents protesting the proposed airport. The state government plans to instead expand the existing Chennai airport by constructing a fifth terminal, which is expected to add capacity for around 20 million passengers annually. The decision has triggered a political row, with the Opposition questioning the impact of abandoning the Parandur project on Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth and investment prospects. The Parandur project had been proposed as Chennai’s second airport, with the site covering Parandur and surrounding villages. The project faced prolonged opposition from residents concerned about land acquisition, relocation and the impact on agricultural land.

headline: Top Maoist commander with ₹30 lakh reward killed in encounter in UP's Varanasi
text: Top Maoist commander with ₹30 lakh reward killed in encounter in UP's Varanasi Brijesh Ganjhu was the commander of the Jharkhand-based Tritiya Sammelan Prastuti Committee (TSPC), a banned outfit. Top Maoist leader, Brijesh Ganjhu alias Gopal Singh Bhokta, wanted in at least 44 cases of murder, extortion and under provisions of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) was shot dead in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) in Varanasi early on Sunday, police officers said. Ganjhu was the commander of the Jharkhand-based Tritiya Sammelan Prastuti Committee (TSPC), a banned outfit, and carried a combined reward of ₹30 lakh on his arrest by the Jharkhand government as well as the National Investigation Agency (NIA). Ganjhu was a resident of Lootu village in Chatra district of Jharkhand. Also Read I Jhiram Valley massacre: Maoists planned ambush months in advance, rehearsed attack, court order reveals A release by the Uttar Pradesh Police said the ATS had received information about Ganjhu’s movement towards Mughalsarai (adjoining Varanasi). He was travelling on a motorcycle with an associate from Tengra Mod towards Mughalsarai via Ramnagar when an ATS team tried to intercept him near Lanka Maidan under Ramnagar police station. As soon as he spotted the police, Ganjhu abandoned the motorcycle and opened fire at the police team while trying to evade arrest, the police said. Cops intercept, arrest Ganjhu Deputy superintendent of police (DSP) Vipin Rai and head constable Nitendra Krishna of the ATS were hit by the Ganjhu’s bullets, but their bulletproof jackets protected them, the statement said. During the retaliatory firing, Ganjhu was shot and was subsequently taken to a nearby hospital, where doctors declared him dead, it said. His associate, however, managed to escape and has not been identified yet, it added. “Acting on an informant’s tip-off, police attempted to intercept and arrest him. Instead of stopping, he jumped off the vehicle and opened fire on the police personnel. In the ensuing crossfire, he was shot,” Rai said. The encounter comes amid intensified surveillance by UP security agencies over the movement of Naxal operatives and their associates into Uttar Pradesh. The ATS has been monitoring the possible movement of ultras through the Sonbhadra-Mirzapur corridor. First came the dispute over the colors of the national flag, and now it is the controversy surrounding the singing of Vande Mataram. This is a transparent attempt by the BJP to deflect focus from ongoing civic protests and the glaring exposure of deteriorating government-run schools. What makes these recent protests remarkable is that young girls—from primary school levels upwards—are leading the charge. Yet, the BJP government has offered nothing in response, not even an apology. text: Did love make Bhagat Singh a weaker revolutionary? In a heated argument once, Sukhdev accused him of allowing his fascination with a woman to come in the way of revolutionary duty. Bhagat Singh's answer, in a letter days later, was a defence of love as a revolutionary's strength, not a weakness. On Bhagat Singh's 119th birth anniversary, Utkarsh Mishra looks at the friendship, arguments and ideas that bound him and Sukhdev together. headline: Jharkhand Congress holds march in Ranchi, seeks separate OBC column in caste census
text: Ranchi, Sep 16 : The Congress on Wednesday organised a march to Lok Bhavan in Jharkhand 's capital Ranchi, demanding a separate column for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in the upcoming Caste census. A delegation of the party later submitted a memorandum addressed to the President of India through the Governor, urging the Centre to include the demand in the census exercise. The march began from Bapu Vatika and saw participation from Congress leaders, party workers, and OBC representatives from various districts of the state. The procession was led by Nishant Jaiswal, President of the Pradesh Congress OBC Department. Congress leaders said reliable data on the OBC population and its socio-economic status was essential for effective policymaking. They noted that the party has been consistently demanding a separate code and clear identification of OBCs in the forthcoming caste census. State Congress President Keshav Mahto Kamlesh said the caste census should not be viewed merely as an exercise to collect statistics. He added that accurate data on the actual OBC population and its socio-economic conditions would help in framing policies and welfare schemes more effectively. Rural Development Minister Deepika Pandey Singh said the demand was linked to social justice and equal opportunities. According to her, comprehensive and credible data is crucial for formulating policies related to education, employment, healthcare and economic empowerment. Health Minister Irfan Ansari said a clear enumeration of OBCs in the caste census would reveal the community's actual population and facilitate the formulation of targeted development programmes. Leader of the Congress Legislature Party in the Jharkhand Assembly, Pradeep Yadav, also described the demand for a separate OBC column as an issue linked to policy formulation and adequate representation. Yogendra Yogi, In-charge of the Pradesh Congress OBC Department, said the party would continue to pursue the demand through democratic and constitutional means. Former MP Dhiraj Prasad Sahu and former State Congress President Rajesh Thakur also supported the demand for authentic data on the OBC population and its socio-economic status. Through the memorandum submitted to the Governor, the Congress delegation urged the Central government to include a separate column for OBCs in the upcoming caste census and ensure the community's actual population is accurately recorded. The party had earlier announced the September 16 march as part of its campaign on the issue.

headline: HIGHLIGHTS | Rahul Gandhi ends dharna after Delhi Police registers FIR over pellet injuries to youth

headline: Kerala ministers slam Muslim cleric’s ‘confine women to homes’ remark
text: Kerala ministers slam Muslim cleric’s ‘confine women to homes’ remark The remark came days after a circular issued by the AP faction of Samastha that sought to restrict the participation of Muslim women in public events. A Kerala-based Sunni Muslim leader, 95-year-old Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar, ignited a controversy on Sunday by urging women to remain confined to their homes and claiming their entry into the public sphere would “lead to destruction”—remarks that were sharply condemned by the state ministers for home and women and child development. headline: Nepal flash flood kills 8 near Tibet border: UP, Bihar on alert as Bhote Kashi river flows downstream- Moneycontrol.com
text: Flash floods in Nepal on Wednesday that killed at least eight people and caused widespread damage near the Tibet border has raised concerns downstream in India, as the Bhote Koshi river eventually flows into the country as the Gandak. As flash floods ravaged Nepal, the Central Water Commission (CWC) under the Ministry of Jal Shakti issued a special flood advisory after a sudden rise in the water level of Nepal’s Trishuli river, warning authorities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh to closely monitor the situation along the Gandak river. According to the advisory, a sharp rise in the Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal---around 160km from the Indian border---has been reported and the rise is suspected to be linked to glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) activity near the Nepal-China border. A GLOF occurs when water accumulated in or around a glacier or glacial lake is suddenly released, potentially sending a powerful surge downstream. Such events can cause rapid rises in river levels and pose a significant risk to downstream communities and infrastructure. The flood wave is expected to travel downstream into the Gandak river, although the CWC said it would undergo “peak attenuation” as it moves downstream. The commission has advised local authorities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, particularly areas near the India-Nepal border along the Gandak, to remain alert and closely monitor the situation. The advisory further recommends that precautionary measures be taken along the Gandak river if required. It has also asked authorities to ensure that the gates of the Gandak Barrage are operated in a manner that allows the anticipated floodwaters to pass through safely. The warning comes as at least eight people were killed after massive flash floods swept through villages in Nepal's mountainous Rasuwa district near the Tibet border on Wednesday, damaging roads, bridges and power projects. Nepal deployed helicopters for rescue operations, but water levels were too high for them to land in the worst-hit areas of Syapru Besi and Timure, Reuters reported, citing officials who warned that the number of casualties could rise. headline: MPSC paper leak: Aspirants protest in Pune
text: MPSC paper leak: Aspirants protest in Pune A large number of MPSC aspirants staged a protest march in Pune on Monday, demanding transparency in the recruitment process and action against the alleged paper leaks and irregularities in various examinations. The protesters demanded the resignation of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) chairman and secretary and the immediate appointment of officers with a “clean image” to the posts. The march began at Omkareshwar Temple Chowk and proceeded to the Pune District Collectorate, where protesters raised demands related to the functioning of the MPSC and examination procedures. NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar and Congress legislator Vishwajit Kadam joined the protesters, extending support to their demands. Pawar said the Government must fulfil the protesters’ demands.The protesters demanded that the commission provide, within eight days, an explanation on objections raised about the Drug Inspector (Group-B) examination and initiate an inquiry into alleged irregularities. Among other demands, the aspirants sought an inquiry into alleged errors in the evaluation of descriptive papers of the 2025 State Services Main Examination and Agricultural Services examination. They also demanded that the preliminary inquiry report submitted by the Mumbai Crime Branch to the MPSC be made public.

headline: Bengal govt orders reverification of birth certificates issued between 2021 to 2026
text: Kolkata, Aug 21 : The West Bengal government on Friday issued a notification ordering reverification of birth certificates issued in the state between 2021 and 2026, covering the last five years of the previous Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress regime. In the notification issued by the office of the West Bengal Chief Secretary, Manoj Kumar Agarwal, the reverification will cover birth certificates issued in both "digital" and "offline" modes. Sub-divisional officers (SDOs) and block development officers (BDOs) have been entrusted with the task. After the new Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-ruled government, led by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, came to power in West Bengal, it said it had noticed several irregularities in birth certificate issuance under the previous regime, especially in the last five years. A large number of fake birth certificates came to the notice of the Election Commission of India (ECI) during the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise in the state before the recently concluded assembly elections earlier this year. That is why the new state government decided to reverify all the birth certificates issued during the last five years of the previous regime. As per the notification, BDOs will verify certificates in rural areas, while SDOs will handle urban areas. If necessary, BDOs and SDOs will have the authority to form investigation teams for that purpose. An officer from the state secretariat at Nabanna said special emphasis will be placed on delayed registrations. The state government has also said it will conduct a thorough investigation to examine the documents verified while issuing birth certificates and whether the laid-down rules were followed. As per the notification, the documents checked during the reverification process and their results must be uploaded to the 'Birth-Death Information Portal'. The Chief Secretary's office has also instructed the preparation of a detailed report for each birth certificate. The reports should mention whether the birth certificates in question were original, fake or defective. In addition, the BDOs and SDOs have been asked to consider the authority of the person who issued the certificate. "If any certificate is found to be fake or illegal, then the specific reason must be documented. The BDOs and SDOs have been instructed to complete this verification process by September," said a state secretariat insider.

headline: BJP workers not part-time politicians: Nitin Nabin slams Rahul Gandhi
text: Saharanpur, Sep 22 : In what appears to be a veiled jibe at Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) President Nitin Nabin on Tuesday said that the party's workers "are not part-time politicians". This comes days after Tamil Nadu BJP chief Nainar Nagenthran called the Congress leader "a part-time politician, condemning him for the purported mimicry of Prime Minister Narendra Modi during Gandhi's 'Chhatron ki Goonj' event in Indore. Speaking to reporters in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, Nitin Nabin, without taking any name, said: "A Bharatiya Janata Party worker works round-the-clock; our workers are not part-time politicians. I am delighted by the zeal and enthusiasm visible among the workers everywhere, and by the firm resolve they demonstrate to form a BJP government in Uttar Pradesh once again." The BJP chief expressed optimism that the party will return to power in the 2027 Assembly polls. "After visiting western Uttar Pradesh, interacting with workers, and discussing matters with senior leaders, I am confident that the Bharatiya Janata Party will successfully achieve its mission for 2027," he stated. Nabin added: "We believe—whether considering Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's tenure over the past years or Prime Minister Modi's tenure spanning the last 12 years—the public has clear faith in our approach to development and our foreign policy. The people trust that this government will transform India into a developed nation and turn Uttar Pradesh into an 'Uttam Pradesh' (an exemplary state)." Nitin Nabin is on a two-day visit to Uttar Pradesh from Monday. A day before, he began his visit by paying tribute at Kargil Martyrs Memorial Park in Meerut. In a message on X, Nabin said: "Today, during a visit to Uttar Pradesh, upon reaching the Kargil Martyrs Memorial Park in Meerut, I paid floral tributes and bowed in homage to the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation's defence, and planted a tree in their memory." "The courage of our soldiers, their dedication to the nation, and their supreme sacrifice made while defending the country's borders will forever remain a source of inspiration for every Indian," he said. During Nabin's visit to the state, the party leadership is set to focus on reviewing organisational preparedness across booths, 'Shakti Kendra' (cluster of booths), mandals, and district levels, and engaging in direct dialogue with party workers.

headline: “Satluj” – When the State Bans Memory, The River Becomes the Archive
text: Say Satluj and you hear winter fog settling on wheat. You smell wet earth, diesel, and old paper. In geography it is Shatadru, the Rigvedic river of the land of five waters. Rivers do not speak. They file. They keep the record. 1947: it heard trains cut in half at the border, whistles carrying grief across new cartography. 1984: it watched night burn in Delhi and in Punjab’s villages, and mirrored the glow. 6 September 1995, 9:20 am, Kabir Park, Amritsar: it saw a red Maruti stop. Men in uniform took a man washing his car. His name was Jaswant Singh Khalra. Bank manager. His job was to make accounts add up. On 3 July 2026, Honey Trehan’s ’Satluj’ arrived on ZEE5. Diljit Dosanjh played Khalra. Not the pop star. A gaunt, quiet man with rage folded under his shirt. By the night of 5 July, the Ministry of Electronics and IT invoked Rule 3 of the IT Rules, 2021. Forty-eight hours later the film was gone from India. Within a week it vanished from ZEE5’s international catalogue too. In August 2026 it survives on Telegram, WhatsApp, and “guerrilla screenings” in gurdwara halls and college rooms across Punjab. The platform erased it. The river didn’t. The Accountant Who Asked For Bodies Khalra was not a politician. He was not a militant. He was a citizen with an accountant’s discipline and a Sikh’s sense of seva. From the late 1980s to 1994, Punjab was crushed between two fires: armed insurgency and a counter-insurgency that increasingly operated outside law. The word in print and in whispers was “encounter.” Young men were lifted. Then silence. But where were the bodies? That question would not let Khalra sleep. From around 1992 he began visiting cremation grounds across Amritsar district: Tarn Taran, Patti, Majitha, Sarhali. He carried two government registers. One recorded body brought for cremation. The other recorded wood purchased. An adult cremation takes roughly 30-35 kg of wood. The math did not match. The gap was filled with entries marked ‘laawaris’ — unclaimed, unidentified. headline: Why Aga Ruhullah Is Quitting As Srinagar MP On November 3 After Farooq Abdullah’s Ultimatum
text: Trouble has started to mount for the National Conference (NC) as its firebrand leader and Member of Parliament from Srinagar, Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, is set to resign from both the basic membership of the party and his Lok Sabha seat on November 3. The move comes after NC patron and former Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah openly challenged the leader to step down and seek a fresh mandate if he believed his 2024 victory was based on his personal political standing rather than the party’s backing. Mehdi has publicly accused his party of abandoning key election promises, particularly regarding the fight for the restoration of Article 370, special constitutional status, and statehood for Jammu & Kashmir. He openly questioned why the NC leadership made these pledges during the 2024 assembly elections if they intended to back away shortly after coming into power. headline: Mamata Banerjee's niece found dead in West Bengal; was disturbed after losing job
text: KOLKATA: Bengal's former chief minister and Trinamool Congress President Mamata Banerjee's niece Bristi Mukherjee was found dead at her residence in Birbhum district on Tuesday, police said. She allegedly died by hanging herself. "Bristi Mukherjee's body has been sent for post-mortem examination. An investigation is underway. The circumstances leading to the death will be established after the post-mortem and other procedural inquiries," a senior officer said. The deceased woman's family members said she had been suffering from depression for the past few years and was undergoing treatment. The family said Mukherjee was struggling with depression after experiencing several distressing events in her life. She had lost her Group C job following a court order cancelling recruitments in government-aided schools over alleged corruption while also going through a divorce proceeding. Mukherjee was among the 26,000 employees who lost their jobs as non-teaching staff at Bolpur’s Upper Primary School in March 2023. The Supreme Court invalidated her appointment in April 2025, holding that the West Bengal School Service Commission (WBSSC) recruitment process during Mamata Banerjee’s tenure as chief minister was tainted by alleged favouritism and cash-for-jobs transactions. The cash-for-jobs case was among the major corruption cases to emerge during Mamata Banerjee’s 15-year rule. Mukherjee (28) was the daughter of Banerjee's maternal cousin Nihar Mukherjee who had previously served as the TMC president of Rampurhat-I block. The niece's body was recovered from a room on the second floor of her house at Kusumba village in Rampurhat area Tuesday afternoon. "It could be a case of suicide. An investigation has been launched to ascertain the exact cause of death," an officer said. headline: Delhi court reserves order on ACB plea for Satyendar Jain’s judicial custody - OrissaPOST
text: New Delhi: A Delhi court Wednesday reserved its order on an Anti-Corruption Branch’s plea seeking 14-day judicial custody of former minister Satyendar Jain, ex-Delhi Jal Board CEO Udit Prakash Rai and three others in the alleged corruption case involving the tendering process for sewage treatment plant projects of the DJB. The court also reserved its order on ACB’s another application seeking police custody of Ankit Srivastava, a former contractual consultant with the DJB. Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh is likely to pronounce the order shortly. Other accused in the case are private persons Nagendra Yadav, Raja Kumar Kurra and Pankaj Verma. During the proceedings, counsel for Jain said that after the FIR was registered “way back May 10, 2024”, his client was called once on August 5, 2026, and then a second time through a phone call Tuesday, after which he was arrested. The advocate claimed there was no material to justify the arrest. Counsel for ex-DJB CEO Rai also challenged his client’s arrest, saying Rai was presently posted as secretary in Mizoram government. Advocates for other accused also assailed the grounds of arrest. The case was registered in May 2024, on a complaint by the Directorate of Vigilance, over alleged large-scale irregularities, manipulation of tender conditions and criminal conspiracy in the tendering process related to augmentation and upgradation of sewage treatment plants of the DJB.

headline: Congress holds protest in Uttarakhand, demands resignation of EC Gyanesh Kumar
text: ANI 26 Sep 2026, 02:28 GMT+10 Dehradun (Uttarakhand) [India], September 26 (ANI): The Uttarakhand Congress on Friday staged a massive protest and gheraoed the Election Commission office and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee president Ganesh Godiyal, AICC state in-charge Kumari Selja, Leader of Opposition Yashpal Arya, former Chief Minister Harish Rawat, CWC member Karan Mahara, Deputy Leader of Opposition Bhuvan Kapri, former Assembly Speaker Govind Singh Kunjwal, former MP Pradeep Tamta, Discipline Committee chairman Vikram Singh Negi, along with party MLAs and senior leaders took part in the protest. The protesters marched from the Pradesh Congress office to the Secretariat, raising slogans, and later 'gheraoed the Election Commission office'. They also burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protest was organised as part of programmes being held across the country on the call of the All-India Congress Committee. The Congress submitted a memorandum addressed to the President of India demanding removal and arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The Uttarakhand Congress alleged that several serious questions have emerged in recent days regarding the electoral process, revision of electoral rolls and transparency in elections. It particularly raised concerns over the process of adding and deleting names from voter lists and disposal of objections. The party alleged that complaints by opposition parties regarding alleged discrimination in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process were not being taken into consideration by the Election Commission. It said that under such circumstances, complete transparency, accountability and equal treatment of all political parties in the functioning of the Election Commission were essential. Congress leaders further alleged that despite disagreement from the two Election Commissioners, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was taking unilateral decisions, which they termed unconstitutional and a violation of democratic principles. headline: JNU V-C Santishree Pandit’s tenure: reform, rupture or repetition?
text: One night in November 2025, a scuffle broke out at the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Central Library of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) over facial recognition entry gates, which students viewed as a tool for surveillance. By February 2, 2026, JNU administration had rusticated all four elected office-bearers of the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students Union (JNUSU) from the university. President Aditi Mishra, Vice President Gopika K. Babu, General Secretary Sunil Yadav, Joint Secretary Danish Ali and former union president Nitish Kumar were each rusticated for two semesters, fined ₹20,000 each and declared out of bounds from the entire campus. This marked the first time in JNU’s history that an administrative order dissolved an entire elected union. This is one episode in Vice-Chancellor Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit’s tenure, which has been defined by recurring disputes over discipline, recruitment and caste politics. Even as these controversies have played out, the university has sustained its second-place ranking among universities in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) and resumed regular convocations, including its sixth convocation, addressed by President Droupadi Murmu. A student who witnessed the expulsion incident noted that staging protests within a 100-meter radius of the administrative building is no longer feasible, a restriction which was formalised when the administration barred protests near academic complexes and imposed a ₹20,000 fine on violators in 2023. The student said surveillance has altered the day-to-day functioning of student politics. Ms. Pandit has been the V-C since February 7, 2022. Before her, M. Jagadesh Kumar had headed JNU from 2016 until his appointment as UGC Chairman in early 2022. He was also accused of cracking down on dissent and protests at multiple instances. On recruitment, the administration stakes its stronger claim to legacy on the scale of appointments made. Officials state that since February 2022, JNU has conducted over 400 interviews and filled more than 200 positions. Approximately 70% of these appointments have been made from reserved categories, and officials report receiving no complaints from candidates regarding the interview process. They alleged that subject-expert screening committees had rejected some candidates for failing UGC eligibility criteria, but selection panels later reinstated them. headline: Will stay in opposition: NCP (SP) leadership to functionaries
text: PUNE: The senior NCP (SP) leadership, according to its district functionaries, has clarified that the party will remain in the opposition, after they sought clarity on speculations over the outfit joining NDA . NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar addressed the district presidents and other functionaries of the party from western Maharashtra, Marathwada and north Maharashtra in a two-day meet in Mumbai last weekend. Amid speculations that NCP (SP) was tilting towards NDA and might join the govt in coming months, the party functionaries urged Pawar and the party’s working president, Supriya Sule , to clear the outfit’s stand on the possibility of joining NDA. According to the functionaries of NCP (SP), the party’s leadership clarified to them that it would not join NDA and continue to raise the voice of common citizens in the opposition. “Pawar Saheb clarified that his meetings with the BJP seniors were for official purposes and those did not mean his party would join NDA. Even Supriya said she had been witnessing similar speculations since 2014 but the party would not join BJP,” another functionary said. One of the party functionaries who attended the meeting told TOI,“Party gets support from all sections of the society, including the minority. Some functionaries said uncertainty was growing among the party workers at the grassroots because of these speculations. They feel that if the party joins NDA, a large section of the party supporters will shift to Congress. Therefore, some of the functionaries urged the party seniors to clear the stand on whether the party will join NDA or not.” Senior Pawar told the NCP (SP) functionaries in the meeting to make efforts for the party’s growth in their respective districts. He also advised them to enroll more members before the next elections. Speaking about the meet, working president Supriya Sule said, “It shows that we have democracy in our party. Party seniors spoke the least, while the district presidents spoke their heart out and gave honest feedback. After some reports about the speculations, they had some doubts. They told us about these and we addressed each and every doubt.”

headline: ‘We are the worst storytellers’: Suhel Seth on India’s failure to market itself at 'Kitaab' book launch | Indiablooms - First Portal on Digital News Management
text: ‘We are the worst storytellers’: Suhel Seth on India’s failure to market itself at 'Kitaab' book launch Author and columnist Suhel Seth was in Kolkata for the latest edition of ‘Kitaab’, a signature literary initiative of the Prabha Khaitan Foundation (PKF), in association with Rotary International and Ehsaas Women of Kolkata at Taj Bengal. Seth was present to launch his book WTF India: Are We Losing the Plot?, engaging in a candid conversation on India’s politics, governance, urban development, culture and the responsibilities of citizens. IBNS correspondent Souvik Ghosh reports... Q. You have been using your platform to talk about India for decades, often highlighting the contradictions of a rising India. How did that journey begin?
