headline: Cauvery row: Karnataka to move Supreme Court against order to release 6,000 cusecs to Tamil Nadu
text: Bengaluru, Sep 9 : Karnataka will approach the Supreme Court challenging the orders issued by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) directing the state to release 6,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu, Water Resources Minister N. Cheluvarayaswamy said on Wednesday. Speaking to reporters at Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru, Cheluvarayaswamy said the issue had been discussed at length with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and that preparations were underway to file a petition before the Supreme Court on Thursday after consulting the team of legal experts. He said the Karnataka government had also directed officials to file a review petition before the CWRC against its order. "The CWMA has also upheld the order of the CWRC. However, the situation in our reservoirs is extremely difficult and we are facing a situation where there is hardly enough water to release. At present, priority has to be given to drinking water, while there is also a need to fill up dried lakes and tanks," he added. The Minister expressed concern over the prevailing water situation and said conditions could improve only if Karnataka received good rainfall within a week of the Gowri-Ganesha festival. "We (Karnataka) will not support the CWRC order under any circumstances. Earlier, 100 TMC of water had been released, while this year we have released only 30 TMC. Despite this, the Tamil Nadu government has continued to put pressure on Karnataka," Cheluvarayaswamy said. He also added that the Karnataka government would seriously consider appointing a Special Advocate to represent the state in Supreme Court in the Cauvery matter, as suggested by former Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai. The Karnataka government would also discuss the proposal with Bommai, he added. Reacting to the Enforcement Directorate (ED) raids on the residences of Minister Satish Jarkiholi and his aides, Cheluvarayaswamy accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of politically targeting opposition leaders through central investigative agencies. "Let them do whatever they want according to the law. But targeting Opposition leaders through such raids has become the BJP's practice," he alleged. The Minister questioned why similar ED raids were not being conducted against Ministers in Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and other states where the BJP or its allies are in power. He accused the Centre of adopting a discriminatory approach in the use of central investigative agencies and questioned the rationale behind selectively targeting leaders of opposition parties.

text: SC suspends sentence of Naga militant in triple murder case, directs him to stay in Delhi New Delhi, The Supreme Court on Monday suspended the sentence of self-styled NSCN "lieutenant" Hopeson Nignshen, convicted in connection with the abduction and killing of three Manipur government officials in the state's Ukhrul district in February 2009. A bench comprising Justice M M Sundresh and Justice P B Varale noted that Nignshen has been in jail for more than 17 years. "We are dealing with a case where the appellant has been incarcerated for more than 17 years and therefore, he is relying only on the ground of suspension of sentence, particularly when his appeal is pending. We grant suspension of sentence on the following conditions: the applicant shall stay within the boundaries of Delhi and not leave until the appeal is disposed of," the bench said. The counsel appearing for the Manipur government opposed the plea. The Delhi High Court on November 20, 2019 had upheld trial court's order convicting Nignshen for kidnapping and killing three government officials in Manipur in 2009 and handed him life imprisonment. The trial court in 2014 had awarded the jail term to Hopeson Nignshen, holding him guilty of abducting Dr Thingnam Kishan Singh and two others, and killing them after conspiring with other National Socialist Council of Nagaland-Isak Muivah militants. Nignshen, who was also held guilty of looting the deceased's belonging, was asked to pay a fine of ₹35,000. The case was transferred to Delhi from Manipur on the Supreme Court's direction in May 2010 after CBI had apprehended a threat to Nignshen's life and chances of unrest in the state if he was presented in a Manipur court. According to CBI, on February 13, 2009, Nignshen and other NSCN-IM militants had abducted Kishan Singh, SDO-cum-BDO of Kasom Khullen in Manipur's Ukhrul district, and five members of his personal staff. headline: Partition, Bor Porong and the Chakmas’ unfinished struggle for belonging
text: Partition, Bor Porong and the Chakmas’ unfinished struggle for belonging The 1947 Partition fundamentally reshaped the political map of South Asia, creating the independent nation-states of India and Pakistan, and subsequently Bangladesh. Driven by a hasty division along religious lines, it precipitated the largest mass migration in human history, forcing an estimated 15 million people from their ancestral homes and turning them into refugees. While historical narratives often frame this event as a singular political milestone, critical Partition studies emphasise that its impact extends far beyond political boundaries and state formation. For the Buddhist Chakma people of Arunachal Pradesh, the wound inflicted by Partition continues to bleed, manifesting itself in their ongoing struggle for national identity, citizenship and political recognition. The abrupt transformation of neighbours into enemies, ancestral homelands into foreign territories, and established identities into contested ones created an enduring trauma for the Chakma community. The radio announcement on the evening of August 17, two days after independence, declaring that the CHT would be incorporated into Pakistan, represented the ultimate betrayal for this community. That solitary voice over the radio suddenly changed the fate of a people who had once been a dominant group with an autonomous kingdom during the pre-colonial period and enjoyed semi-autonomous status under British rule, only to be reduced to stateless refugees in the postcolonial period. Partition as an unending historical chapter: Subalternity and indigenous reality “Years of genocide have desensitised us.” — Sneha Kumar Chakma (The Indian Post, 1987) The postcolonial Chakma experience aligns closely with a theoretical framework that redefines Partition from a single event in the past into an ongoing historical process. Early scholarship on the 1947 Partition of South Asia focused heavily on “high politics”, particularly the closed-door negotiations between British colonial administrators and nationalist elites. This macro-historical approach mapped out how the borders were drawn while largely ignoring the human cost of the event. The lived experiences of the millions caught in the crossfire were largely omitted from the “history from above”. From the late 1980s through the 1990s, subaltern, feminist and critical historians such as Urvashi Butalia, Ritu Menon, Kamla Bhasin, Veena Das and Gyanendra Pandey radically challenged this methodological silence by embracing oral histories and survivor narratives. This approach recognised that the trauma of Partition, including sexual violence, massacres and the displacement of millions from their homelands, cannot be understood through official state archives alone. headline: BJP demands Sonia Gandhi's apology as Vande Mataram row turns political in Bengal
text: BJP demands Sonia Gandhi's apology as Vande Mataram row turns political in Bengal The controversy over the singing of the full version of "Vande Mataram" at the Congress headquarters in New Delhi has taken a political turn in West Bengal, with the BJP demanding an apology from Sonia Gandhi and threatening protests across the state. West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday, August 16, alleged that Gandhi had objected to the singing of the complete version of the national song during the Independence Day function, saying the incident had deeply offended people in the state, where Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay is revered as "Sahitya Samrat." He accused the Congress leadership of trying to explain away the episode and said video footage would establish what happened. "As Chief Minister, I feel that insulting Vande Mataram is an insult to Bankim Chandra himself. The BJP's Yuva Morcha announced a protest rally in Kolkata, with a proposed march from Esplanade to Moulali, adding a street-politics dimension to the row in Bengal. The Congress has denied the BJP's allegation that its senior leaders showed disrespect to the national song or attempted to stop the singing of its full version. headline: Pappu Yadav joins student protesters in Bihar, stages hunger strike
text: Independent MP Pappu Yadav, who supports the INDIA bloc, on Sunday (August 16, 2026) sat on a hunger strike at a protest site in Patna over alleged irregularities in the 70th Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) exams, and other issues. Research scholars, along with BPSC and Bihar Staff Selection Commission (BSSC) aspirants, are protesting in Patna's Gardanibagh area over a multitude of issues, ranging from new rules regarding recruitment of assistant professor to inconsistencies in the state civil services exam. Mr. Yadav said the 70th BPSC exam should be scrapped and re-conducted afresh. "Research scholars have been on hunger strike for the last 13 days, but there is nobody to listen to them. Neither the chief minister nor Bihar's education minister is paying heed to their grievances. The Education Minister talks about introducing the UPSC mains pattern in BPSC exams, which is bereft of any logic. The entire system is in a mess," he told reporters. He alleged there were marking inconsistencies in the 70th BPSC exam, frequent question paper leaks, police brutality against protesting students in the state, and disproportionate weightage to the English language in government exams. "The government itself accepted that the question paper of the 70th BPSC examination had leaked. Such incidents have happened even before. However, when students protest against such inconsistencies, they are beaten up and sent to jail," the MP said. He charged the government with "continuously committing injustice" against students and "refusing to listen to them". "Students are seriously concerned about TRE-4 exam notification. Additionally, the government accords disproportionate weightage to English-medium candidates vis-a-vis those opting Hindi, which is contrary to UGC and NET rules," Mr. Yadav said. He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of labelling all educated youth of the country as 'intellectual Naxals'. Mr. Modi had, during his Independence Day speech on Saturday (August 15), said that "while armed Naxals are eliminated in the country, we will have to identify and isolate intellectual Naxals". The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), won three of the four central panel posts in the DUSU elections held after the recent CJP-led Gen Z protests. The Congress-backed National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) failed to win any of the four posts. “Money works in elections and nothing else. Those who campaign in DU come in Rolls Royce, which is worth crores of rupees. They come in Audi, BMW. So money works there,” Dipke told reporters. He also alleged that ideological affiliations were influencing appointments and functioning in educational institutions, echoing Congress MP Rahul Gandhi’s criticism of the BJP-led government. Dipke claimed that Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya Vice Chancellor Kumud Sharma was associated with RSS ideology and alleged that more than 50 FIRs had been registered against students since she took charge. “When students protest for something, an FIR is registered against them. But when ABVP opposes something or locks any gate, no FIR is registered against them. Only Dalit, Adivasi (tribal) students who oppose the ideology are booked. It is a roadmap to make institutions (universities) a shakha of RSS,” he alleged. On protests by Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) aspirants seeking the resignation of MPSC Chairman Vivek Bhimanwar over alleged corruption, Dipke said students had lost faith in the examination system. “How can the students keep faith that exams will be conducted transparently until Bhimanwar resigns?” he asked. He said the CJP, along with MPSC aspirants, would soon launch an online campaign, “Bhimanwar Rajinama Dya” (Bhimanwar, resign), to explain the allegations against the commission chairman, his alleged links with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and why, according to them, his resignation was necessary. On the recent death by suicide of an IIT Bombay student, Dipke said the incident highlighted the need for greater mental health support for students. The student was found hanging in his hostel room on Friday evening, hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone and ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination, officials said. “The suicide incident at IIT Bombay is painful. This is a result of students losing faith in the education system. Children are dying in backward areas as well as big cities.

headline: Maharashtra minister urges Jarange to call off planned quota agitation in Mumbai during Ganesh fest
text: Maharashtra minister urges Jarange to call off planned quota agitation in Mumbai during Ganesh fest Maharashtra minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil on Wednesday urged Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange to call off his proposed agitation in Mumbai during the ongoing Ganesh festival, saying the reservation issue can be resolved through dialogue. “There is absolutely no plan to use force to stop the agitation. The issue can be resolved through dialogue and discussion. We are talking to those who have studied the quota issue,” Vikhe Patil said. The Water Resources Minister, who heads the state government's cabinet sub-committee on the Maratha reservation issue, said the government was ready to hold discussions with the community and its representatives whenever required. Vikhe Patil also referred to criticism of former chief minister Eknath Shinde by some members of the Maratha community, who have alleged that he “betrayed” them after they placed their trust in him. “If they feel that they have been betrayed, I think they should put that feeling aside,” he said, asserting that Shinde had taken considerable initiative on the reservation issue. Vikhe Patil claimed that around 5,500 children had been given an opportunity at the time despite the possibility of contempt of court proceedings, and that the process for the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) category was also initiated. “Many things were done. I don't think the community gains anything by feeling that it has been betrayed,” he said. He said the government had introduced several schemes while respecting the sentiments of the community and had kept the door open for further discussions. “Our only expectation is that devotees should not face inconvenience during Ganeshotsav. They are going to travel from Pune to Mumbai, and we do not want any untoward incident to take place,” Vikhe Patil said. He appealed to Jarange to suspend his agitation in view of the festival. Jarange, whose fast entered its 19th day on Wednesday, reached Patoda in Maharashtra's Beed district around 11 am, nearly 14 hours after leaving Antarwali Sarati village in Jalna district. He is scheduled to reach Mumbai on September 19 after travelling through Ahilyanagar, Pune and Khopoli in Raigad district. Last year, Jarange's hunger strike at Azad Maidan brought parts of south Mumbai to a standstill as thousands of supporters gathered in the city. The agitation was called off on September 2, 2025, after the government accepted six of his eight demands

headline: Delhi winter pollution plan: Real estate developers seek balanced approach, clear timelines for construction curbs
text: Delhi winter pollution plan: Real estate developers seek balanced approach, clear timelines for construction curbs Reacting to the Delhi govt’s construction curbs, real estate developers said pollution-control measures are necessary, but called for a balanced approach The Delhi government has announced a series of measures to curb winter air pollution in the national capital, including a complete ban on construction and demolition activities during the peak pollution period. headline: Doubled parking fees, WFH for 50% workforce, construction ban & more: Delhi govt ahead of winter air pollution | Today News
text: In an attempt to get a head start on the winter air pollution situation in the national capital, the Delhi government on Monday announced a complete ban on construction and demolition activities starting December. From November 1, the Rekha Gupta government has also doubled parking fees to discourage the use of private vehicles, and announced work-from-home for 50% of the workforce. Delhi’s air quality has begun to deteriorate over the past few days, with the AQI remaining in the moderate category amid dry weather and low wind speeds, which have contributed to the accumulation of pollutants. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Monday chaired a meeting at Paryavaran Bhawan to review measures aimed at tackling air pollution in the national capital. Union environment, forest and climate change minister Bhupender Yadav and Delhi food and supplies minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa were also present at the meeting. The Delhi Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said the government is working to address pollution from various major sources through enforcement measures, regular monitoring and coordination between different departments. “Clean air remains a year-round priority for the Delhi Government. Focused action is being taken across major sources of pollution through strict enforcement, continuous monitoring and coordinated efforts across departments,” CMO Delhi said in a post on X. Following the meeting, Sirsa said efforts to improve air quality should continue throughout the year rather than being limited to the winter months. “Providing clean air and a healthy environment to the residents of Delhi is our responsibility, and this responsibility is not limited to any one season. The Delhi government is continuously working in a technical and scientific manner, 365 days a year, 24×7, for pollution control,” Sirsa said in a post on X after the meeting. Sirsa said the Chief Minister will inspect areas identified as air pollution and traffic hotspots during the winter season. He added that ministers will also monitor the various sources contributing to pollution and assess the situation on the ground. As part of the winter preparedness measures, the government plans to work on reducing congestion and vehicle-related emissions. The proposed steps include regulating the entry of vehicles that contribute significantly to pollution, along with improving public transport and last-mile connectivity. The measures are aimed at strengthening Delhi’s pollution-control efforts ahead of the winter months, when the city typically faces deteriorating air quality.

headline: Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson receives charge sheet in assault case from Puducherry court
text: Tamil Nadu Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson on Friday (September 4, 2026) received, from the Puducherry District Court, the additional charge sheet filed against him and his father in a 2022 assault case. On the directions of the court, Mr. Wilson appeared before the Second Judicial Magistrate Chandrasekharan on Friday morning and received a copy of the charge sheet. His father Nestor, who is the second accused in the case, was also present. After the Minister received the copy of the charge sheet, the judge posted the next hearing of the case to September 9. The JM-1 court had been hearing the case pertaining to the assault in its initial stages. As the JM-I was recently transferred, the accused appeared before JM-II to receive a copy of the charge sheet. The court had previously directed the Minister to appear “in person without fail” to receive the charge sheet and a pen drive, which was produced by the complainant as evidence for the offence allegedly committed by Mr. Wilson. Recently, the Madras High Court had also pulled up the Minister for failing to appear before the Puducherry court in connection with the case. What is the case about? The case was filed in 2022 by Careline Claude, wife of the Minister’s brother, who resides in Ezhil Nagar in Puducherry town. She had complained that Mr. Wilson had trespassed into her house and assaulted and abused her over a property dispute. A case was registered by the Lawspet police. However, she had challenged the FIR, saying that it invoked only the soft provisions of the law against Mr. Wilson. On the directions of the court, a fresh charge sheet invoking more serious provisions was later filed by the police. Published - September 04, 2026 03:55 pm IST

headline: AAP's Saurabh Bhardwaj, other party workers detained during protest over Parvesh Sahib Singh slapping row
text: ANI 28 Sep 2026, 01:33 GMT+10 New Delhi [India], September 28 (ANI): Delhi Police on Sunday detained AAP Delhi President Saurabh Bhardwaj, AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar and other party workers during a protest against the Delhi government and PWD Minister Parvesh Verma over an alleged slapping incident during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar. The protest was held after AAP leaders shared a purported video claiming that Delhi PWD Minister allegedly slapped a local youth during a road inspection. During the protest, an AAP worker said, 'Until an FIR is registered against Parvesh Verma, we will not move from here. Parvesh Verma should resign...' Bhardwaj, in a post on X, said, 'Under the protection of the Delhi Police, BJP minister Parvesh slapped a young man in broad daylight. The police did not even register an FIR in this matter. When we went to the DCP office to demand answers about this, the senior officers misbehaved with the women activists and arrested me along with hundreds of workers. In the end, who should we now turn to for hope in justice?' Earlier, speaking to ANI, Bharadwaj said, 'In front of the police SHO, that boy was slapped by Parvesh Verma. All video evidence is present, everything is available on social media, and the SHO is saying they will investigate, but no FIR is being registered. We will go to the DCP office and get the FIR registered. If the FIR is not registered, we will sit on a dharna right there.' Addressing the gathering, Saurabh Bharadwaj said he had spoken to the SHO. 'The SHO called me a short while ago asking if I was on my way, and I confirmed that I was. I asked if an FIR had been registered yet. The SHO said, 'Sir, I am conducting an inquiry.' I told him, 'It happened right before your eyes; what is there to inquire about? It all took place in your presence.' Yet, the police still haven't registered an FIR,' Bharadwaj said. He said the issue was not limited to the registration of an FIR and alleged that failure to take action would encourage 'hooliganism' by BJP members.'It's not just about the FIR; if BJP members engage in hooliganism like this, even getting caught on camera and while acting as thugs right in front of the police, and no FIR is filed, their hooliganism will only escalate,' he said.

headline: TN minister Marie Wilson appears before Puducherry court after Madras HC’s reprimand
text: PUDUCHERRY: Tamil Nadu finance minister N Marie Wilson appeared before the Puducherry second judicial magistrate on Friday in connection with an ongoing assault case involving his brother Marie Claude. The magistrate served him a copy of the additional charge sheet along with a pen drive containing case details and adjourned the hearing to Sept 9. The minister appeared before the Puducherry court after the Madras high court rejected his request to exempt him from personal appearance and issued a stern reprimand, questioning, "Is finance minister Marie Wilson the King of England to claim he won't appear before the court?" The minister’s counsel filed two separate petitions before the magistrate, one seeking permanent exemption from personal appearance during trial, and another praying for discharge from the case. The magistrate will hear both petitions on Sept 9. The case stems from an incident on Aug 8, 2022, at Ezhil Nagar in Puducherry. Wilson was accused of forcibly entering his brother Claude’s residence by breaking open the door and allegedly assaulting both Claude and his wife, Caroline. The Lawspet police registered a case against Wilson following a complaint from Claude and initiated an investigation. Speaking to reporters outside the courtroom, Claude said, “This is not a case about child adoption or property issues. This case was filed because he assaulted me and my wife. We are still receiving threats. We are attending the court proceedings without revealing our current location to anyone.”

headline: IIT-Bombay protesters demanding Director's resignation, professor's arrest detained
text: Mumbai, Sep 21 : Mumbai Police on Monday detained members of a student organisation and students who had gathered outside IIT Bombay to stage a peaceful protest, demanding the resignation of the institute's Director Shireesh B. Kedare and the arrest of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla in connection with the death of student Sahil Wakode. "Four murders have happened so far! And the Director says that we will not accept the demands? The director himself is the murderer," a protester told reporters. Earlier in the day, the Mumbai Crime Branch took over the investigation into the death of IIT Bombay student Wakode. Investigators are examining his mobile phone for any suicide note or other digital evidence, as no such note was found in his hostel room. Meanwhile, IIT Bombay on Monday refuted reports claiming that its Director Kedare had resigned following the student's death, stating that the reports were false. The institute, however, confirmed that Professor Doolla had been suspended from his position as Dean with immediate effect. A few videos have also been circulating on social media, purportedly showing Kedare's resignation. In a post on X, IIT Bombay said: "Director IIT-Bombay has NOT resigned. We categorically state that the related news is false." In another post, the institute apologised for statements made in its earlier communication regarding the circumstances surrounding Wakode's death. "We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil. The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities," the institute said. "In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," it added. Meanwhile, Kedare said that Doolla had been suspended from his position as Dean with immediate effect. Doolla has been suspended only from his position as Dean (Administrative Affairs), while further action will be taken following the completion of the investigation, Kedare said.

headline: Two UKNA militants killed, two injured in joint ops by Army-Assam Rifles
text: Two UKNA militants killed, two injured in joint ops by Army-Assam Rifles Two UKNA militants were killed and two others injured in an exchange of fire with a joint team of the Indian Army and Assam Rifles in Manipur's Churachandpur district, officials said. The security forces launched an operation at Phaibong village in the Henglep subdivision on the night of August 29 after receiving intelligence inputs, officials said. The forces kept surveillance on a UKNA camp before beginning a tactical closing-in operation at around 5 am on September 2, they said. At around 5.30 am, UKNA cadres allegedly opened "indiscriminate firing", following which the troops responded with controlled fire, officials said. "Intel confirms 2 UKNA cadres neutralised and 2 injured," the Assam Rifles said in a social media post on Saturday night. The United Kuki National Army (UKNA) is not a signatory to the Suspension of Operations (SoO) agreement between the Centre, the Manipur government and several Kuki and Zomi armed groups. Following the exchange of fire, security forces searched the camp and recovered two MA rifles, one AK-56 rifle, one lathode gun, seven lathod grenades, 15 AK magazines, 371 AK-56 rounds, 601 MA rifle rounds, 172 SLR rounds, 15 combat uniforms and seven ammunition pouches, the Assam Rifles said. The operation was continuing in the surrounding jungle areas, it added. (with inputs from PTI)

headline: Karnataka Vande Mataram row: PIL challenges state order limiting singing to first two stanzas- Moneycontrol.com
text: A public interest litigation has been filed before the Karnataka High Court challenging the state government's decision to restrict the singing of the National Song 'Vande Mataram' to its first two stanzas at government functions, except events attended by the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister or Governor. The plea challenges the Karnataka government's September 8 order issued by the Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms following a Cabinet decision taken on September 3. The petitioner has relied on a July 9 communication from the Ministry of Home Affairs, which, according to the plea, mandates that the official six-stanza version of 'Vande Mataram' be sung on all occasions. The PIL contends that the National Song does not fall under either List II or List III of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution and is therefore within Parliament's exclusive legislative domain under Entry 97 of List I read with Article 248. The petition further argues that "What the State Legislature cannot do by statute, the Government cannot do by executive order under Article 162". It alleges that the Karnataka order is also contrary to Articles 256 and 257(1), as well as the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, which extends protection to the National Song. The plea has also raised questions over the procedure followed before the state government's decision. It alleges that the Cabinet took an "Informal Discussion" without a Cabinet Note or advice from the Law Department, which, according to the petitioner, violated the Transaction of Business Rules, 1977, and infringed Article 19(1)(a). Earlier, on September 10, the Karnataka government issued an order directing that the first two stanzas of 'Vande Mataram' be sung at all state government programmes. However, the order specified that all six verses would be sung at functions attended by the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Governor. The state government said the decision was based on guidelines issued by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs through its letter. The ministry has issued the official version of 'Vande Mataram' along with guidelines governing its playing and singing at various official and public functions, with separate provisions for playing and mass singing. The Karnataka government said the song had played a significant role in India's national movement and helped foster nationalism, unity and patriotism among citizens. headline: Andhra govt failed to respond to drought in Rayalaseema, says YSRCP
text: Amaravati, Aug 28 : The coalition government in Andhra Pradesh has completely failed to respond to the severe drought gripping Rayalaseema, leaving farmers without irrigation water, drinking water or fodder support, alleged the YSR Congress Party. YSR Congress Party leader Anantha Venkatarami Reddy and former minister Sake Sailajanath said that kharif cultivation in the region had been restricted to just 39â€"40%, groundwater levels had fallen by 12â€"20 metres, and milk production had declined by nearly 75% due to shortage of green fodder. They were addressing the media at the YSRCP district office in Anantapur on Friday. According to a party release, Ananta Venkatarami Reddy said the government had no contingency plan despite warnings over El Nino and rainfall deficit. He said Telangana had released nearly 53 TMC from Srisailam for power generation while Andhra Pradesh remained silent, even as Rayalaseema faced a growing water crisis. He recalled that the YSRCP government paid around Rs 8,600 crore towards crop insurance premiums and Rs 11,000 crore as input subsidy, whereas farmers were now being forced to pay insurance premiums themselves even for crops drying up in drought conditions. Sailajanath said electricity could be purchased, but lost water could not be recovered. With Srisailam storage declining to around 160 TMC, continued releases for power generation would leave Rayalaseema projects and Handri-Neeva without water, he warned. He demanded immediate diversion of water from Srisailam to Telugu Ganga, Handri-Neeva, drinking-water systems and other Rayalaseema projects, including at least 30â€"40 TMC through Pothireddypadu. The leaders demanded that the government restrain wasteful water releases for power generation, provide compensation to affected farmers and urgently address fodder and drinking-water shortages. They assured farmers that YSRCP would stand with them and warned that if the government failed to act, the party was prepared to intensify its agitation, including a protest at the Srisailam project.

headline: Assam govt destroyed drugs worth Rs 300 crore in 100 days of crackdown - Mangalorean.com
text: Assam govt destroyed drugs worth Rs 300 crore in 100 days of crackdown Guwahati: The Assam government has destroyed narcotic substances valued at around Rs 300 crore during the first 100 days of the BJP-led administration, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Friday, underlining the state’s intensified campaign against drug trafficking. The seized contraband was destroyed at Daulasal in Nalbari district at Assam’s first dedicated narcotics incineration facility. The Chief Minister said the action reflected the government’s continued efforts to dismantle drug supply chains and prevent seized narcotics from re-entering circulation. “Tick tock on the clock, the crackdown doesn’t stop. 100 days, 100% action,” Sarma said in a post on X. He said the government’s anti-drug drive was focused not only on seizures and arrests but also on eliminating trafficking networks operating across the state. “Seizures, arrests, destruction of drug networks, we are sending one message loud and clear: There is no place to hide,” Sarma said, reiterating the government’s commitment to taking strict action against drug peddlers and trafficking syndicates. Giving details of the enforcement drive under the theme “100 days of Surakshit Assam”, Sarma said narcotics worth approximately Rs 300 crore had been destroyed at the Nalbari facility. The Chief Minister also highlighted a series of anti-narcotics operations carried out across nine districts over a 10-day period. According to him, drugs estimated to be worth Rs 472.51 crore were seized during these operations. The seizures included around 30.7 kg of heroin and 5,499 kg of ganja, besides other prohibited substances, he said. The Assam government has stepped up its campaign against narcotics trafficking since Sarma became Chief Minister in May 2021, with enforcement agencies conducting sustained operations against drug suppliers, peddlers and trafficking networks. The state government has repeatedly described the fight against drugs as a key priority, combining seizures, arrests and destruction of confiscated contraband with efforts to disrupt organised trafficking networks.

headline: Sonia Gandhi as an author: Right to publish a book
text: The Supreme Court of India established a powerful standard for freedom of expression in S. Rangarajan v. P. Jagjivan Ram judgment. The court ruled that anticipated public anger or protest is not a valid reason to ban or suppress a work. The judges famously stated that expression cannot be held hostage to a “hostile audience,” and the state’s duty is to protect freedom, not bow to intolerance. For decades, India banned imports of this book under a 1988 customs notification (see The Salman Rushdie Satanic Verses Precedent). However, in a landmark move, the Delhi High Court effectively dismantled the ban because the government could not produce the original notification order. The court ruled that citizens cannot be bound by a phantom ban they are not permitted to see, reinforcing that administrative opacity cannot restrict a citizen’s right to read. Undeclared pre-censorship is far harder to fight because it happens behind closed corporate doors. Publishers often choose to pulp or withdraw books quietly to protect their business interests from political or legal harassment. Similarly, the Pulping of The Hindus: An Alternative History (2014) also can be quoted. Scholar Wendy Doniger’s book faced a civil lawsuit from a right-wing group claiming it hurt religious sentiments. Instead of fighting the case in court, the publisher, Penguin India, chose to settle out of court, withdraw all copies, and pulp the remaining stock. This caused mass outrage in the literary world, as it showed a major publisher giving in to legal intimidation before a court had even ruled the book unlawful. When veteran politician Jaswant Singh wrote a book praising Pakistan’s founder Mohammad Ali Jinnah, he was expelled from his political party (the BJP), and the state government of Gujarat officially banned the book (See the Withdrawal of Jinnah: India-Partition, Independence (2009). Even though the Gujarat High Court later struck down the ban, the political backlash created a massive “chilling effect” where bookstore owners across the state voluntarily refused to stock it out of fear of vandalism. Difference between Banning vs. Pre-Censorship | Feature | Official Book Banning | Undeclared Pre-Censorship / Self-Censorship | | Who enforces it? | The State (via laws, court orders, or customs notifications). | The Publisher or Author (via internal corporate decisions). | | Visibility | Public and transparent. A gazette notification or law is issued. | Invisible and hidden. Happens during editing or legal reviews. | | Recourse |

headline: Fight over neem tree ends with son killing father in Telangana
text: Hyderabad: A dispute over a neem tree that had continued between two families for nearly 25 years allegedly ended in a double murder at Erragadda Thanda in Mellacheruvu mandal on Saturday, August 29. According to the police, Bhukya Ram Naik allegedly killed his neighbour, Manda Venkateshwarlu Yadav, following a confrontation over the disputed tree. He then allegedly killed his own father in an attempt to make the incident appear to be a clash between two groups. Dispute over neem tree turns violent Venkateshwarlu brought some people to the area on Saturday morning and had the neem tree beside his house cut down. Ram Naik allegedly objected to the move and confronted Venkateshwarlu, referring to the long-running dispute between their families. The argument reportedly escalated, following which Ram Naik allegedly attacked Venkateshwarlu with an axe. Police said Venkateshwarlu suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. Man allegedly kills father after neighbour’s death Ram Naik’s father, Bhukya Saida, reportedly witnessed the attack and tried to intervene. Naik then reportedly attacked his father with the same weapon. His father died on the spot too. It is alleged that the second killing was carried out to make the first death appear to have occurred during a confrontation between the two groups. The incident triggered anger in the village. Members of Venkateshwarlu’s group attacked Ram Naik’s house. Police personnel reached Erragadda Thanda to control the situation. Following the incident, Ram Naik was taken into custody for questioning. A case has been registered and investigation is going on, the police said.

headline: Only 2 Vande Mataram Stanzas at Govt Event, Karnataka BJP MLA Walks Out
text: As the national song stopped after reciting two paragraphs, the MLA demanded that the full song be played but the administration went by state government's directive Shivamogga: A BJP MLA has walked out of a government programme here protesting against the rendition of only two stanza of Vande Mataram instead of the full length of the national song. The Shivamogga district administration had hosted a programme on the occasion of International Democracy Day on Tuesday where the national song was played. Shivamogga MLA S N Channabasappa was presiding over the function, which was organised at the Dr B R Ambedkar Bhavan. Senior officers of the district including the Deputy Commissioner of Shivamogga attended it. As the national song stopped after reciting two paragraphs, the MLA demanded that the full song be played but the administration went by state government's directive. In January, the Union Home Ministry directed that all 6 stanzas of Vande Mataram be sung before the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana, when both are played together. The directive was issued as the Centre marked the 150th year of Vande Mataram. However, the Congress-led Karnataka government issued an order on September 10, 2026, restricting the singing of Vande Mataram to its first two stanzas at routine state functions, in line to the 1937 Congress Working Committee decision taken by Rabindranath Tagore, Mahatma Gandhi, Subhash Chandra Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru, which is now in contradiction to the new union government guidelines.

headline: Bihar Police arrest govt. school headmaster, teacher under POCSO Act
text: The Bihar Police arrested a headmaster and a teacher of a government school in Dumraon in connection with a case of alleged sexual abuse of schoolgirls, including minors. Headmaster Mohammad Imam Ali Ansari and teacher Arvind Kumar have been arrested. One accused teacher from the same school, Virendra Prasad, is still absconding. Both teachers have been charged with sexually abusing the girls, circulating objectionable videos of them and threatening them through audio messages. The incident occurred under Krishnabrahmn Police Station in Buxar district. An FIR has been lodged on the complaint of the victim’s mother — her daughter is a minor — under several sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The headmaster was to receive the State Teacher Award 2026 on September 5, on the occasion of Teacher’s Day. Mr. Ansari allegedly aided and abetted the two main accused; following the police action, the Bihar Education Department has withdrawn his name from the State award. The department has also suspended the two accused teachers. In a press statement, the Buxar DM’s office said the Block Education Officer, Dumraon, had reported serious allegations against Assistant Teacher Virendra Prasad and School Teacher Arvind Kumar, both posted at the Middle School in Dumraon. The allegations included molestation of girl students, circulating objectionable videos and threatening them through audio clips, among others. Buxar Superintendent of Police (SP) Shubham Arya visited the police station to review the case details with officials and the actions taken so far. Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Arya said: “The headmaster was arrested yesterday, and another accused teacher, Arvind Kumar, has been arrested today (September 4, 2026). As the matter is very old and happened months back in January, it is hard to medically confirm the rape, but we are trying our level best to gather all possible evidence. Police have also conducted raids at the hotel where a girl was sexually abused.” He added: “Police teams are continuously conducting raids to arrest the remaining accused teacher. Preliminary information suggests that the girl is a former student of the school. We are investigating matters concerning other students as well. Information has come to light regarding three former students. One student is a minor.” Following the SP’s directives, police have stepped up operations and are conducting continuous raids at suspected hideouts to locate the remaining accused teacher. headline: Assam detains 27 Bangladeshi nationals in joint operation with railway police
text: Assam detains 27 Bangladeshi nationals in joint operation with railway police Assam Police and GRP detained 27 Bangladeshi nationals in Guwahati and Rangia. Officials have begun the process to send them back to Bangladesh. Assam Police, in a joint operation with the Government Railway Police (GRP), detained 27 Bangladeshi nationals who had allegedly entered the state illegally, from Guwahati and Rangia on Wednesday, officials said on Thursday. The process to send them back to Bangladesh has begun, they added. Police said the Bangladeshi nationals included men, women and minors. Initial investigations suggest they came from several districts of Bangladesh, including Dhaka, Sunamganj, Gopalganj, Bagherhat, Khulna and Mymensingh. “They are citizens of Bangladesh and were travelling without valid documents, so we detained them. Now we’ll examine how they entered Assam and where they were trying to go,” a senior police officer said. Deputy commissioner of police (border) for Guwahati Kulendra Nath Deka said on Thursday that 12 of them were detained at the Assam State Transport Corporation (ASTC) campus in Guwahati’s Paltan Bazar area on Wednesday. He said that during questioning, the 12 detainees told police that another group of 15 people was travelling on the Jammu Tawi Express, and border police immediately alerted the GRP. “We immediately informed the GRP at Rangia but the train had left the station by that time. The GRP identified and detained them on the moving train and they were handed over to us at Bongaigaon Railway Station,” he said. The detained individuals told police they had entered India through a secret route in Meghalaya and that a racket had helped them do so in exchange for money, officials said. Deka said the border department had started the process of sending the detainees back to Bangladesh and had placed a request before the concerned deputy commissioner for an expulsion order. The Assam government follows the Immigrants (Expulsion from Assam) Act, 1950, to deport suspected illegal migrants. In September last year, the Assam Cabinet approved an SOP under the 1950 Act, empowering district commissioners (DCs) to issue an expulsion order to any person who, in the view of the DC, is a foreigner.

Asked about statehood, Abdullah said, “You all know what happened with us. We were told that statehood would be restored after the (J&K) elections. text: In a significant political development, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Friday announced that her faction of the Trinamool Congress would support the Congress candidate in the Nandigram Assembly bypoll, hours after her party's nominee withdrew from the contest following a meeting with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The move came a day after the Election Commission froze the use of the Trinamool Congress' name and its traditional 'Jora Ghash Phul' (twin flowers and grass) symbol by the rival factions amid an ongoing dispute over the party's identity. The poll panel on Friday allotted the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'Football Player' symbol to the Banerjee-led faction, while the rival group led by Arup Roy was given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'Envelope' symbol for the October 6 bypolls. "How can they (EC) freeze my symbol, which has been with us since the beginning for the last 28 years?" she said. She alleged that the BJP had sought to weaken opposition parties in Maharashtra by splitting the Shiv Sena and the NCP and was now targeting the Trinamool Congress. headline: Rs 30 lakh bounty Naxal leader Brijesh Ganjhu killed in encounter with UP ATS in Varanasi- Moneycontrol.com
text: A senior Naxal leader of the banned Jharkhand-based Tritiya Prastuti Committee (TPC), carrying a combined bounty of Rs 30 lakh, was killed in an encounter with the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) in Varanasi on Sunday morning, police said. Brijesh Ganjhu, also known as Gopal Singh Bhokta, was wanted by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in several cases and was a senior commander of the TPC, a banned outfit considered a splinter group of the Maoist movement. Jharkhand Police spokesperson and IG (Operations) Narendra Singh confirmed that Ganjhu was killed during an encounter in Varanasi. The Jharkhand government had announced a reward of Rs 25 lakh for information leading to his arrest, while the NIA had announced an additional Rs 5 lakh bounty. According to UP ATS DySP Vipin Rai, the operation was launched after the team received information about Ganjhu's presence in Varanasi. He was travelling on a motorcycle with an associate from Tengra Mor towards Mughalsarai through Ramnagar when police attempted to intercept him. Police said Ganjhu got off the motorcycle and opened fire when the team tried to stop him. An exchange of fire followed, during which he sustained gunshot injuries. The encounter took place in the Lanka Maidan area under the Ramnagar police station limits, officials said. Two members of the UP ATS team, including DySP Vipin Rai and head constable Nitendra Krishna, were also targeted during the exchange. Bullets allegedly fired by Ganjhu hit their bulletproof jackets, but both officers were unharmed, police said. Ganjhu was taken to a hospital after being injured in the firing, where doctors declared him dead. The UP ATS had been tracking his movements for some time and launched the operation after receiving information about his arrival in Varanasi, officials said. In a letter dated September 16 from Patiala Central Jail barrack, Rajoana said he had spent more than three decades in prison and had been living under a death sentence for nearly two decades. headline: Jharkhand CM skips court appearance in money laundering case in Ranchi, next hearing on Sep 21
text: Ranchi, Sep 19 : Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren did not appear in person before a special PMLA court in Ranchi on Saturday in connection with a money laundering case linked to 8.86 acres of land in the Bargain area of the city. His counsel informed the court that the Chief Minister was occupied with pre-scheduled constitutional responsibilities. The court has fixed September 21 as the next date of hearing and directed Soren to appear either physically or through virtual mode at 4 p.m. on that day. The proceedings in the special court resumed after the Jharkhand High Court on Friday rejected Soren's discharge petition, refusing to grant him relief in the case. The High Court upheld the special PMLA court's earlier order dismissing his discharge plea, thereby clearing the way for further proceedings before the trial court. Soren had challenged the PMLA court's order rejecting his discharge application and had also sought a stay on the ongoing proceedings before the lower court. After hearing arguments from both sides on September 16, the High Court had reserved its verdict, which was delivered on Friday. The case pertains to 8.86 acres of land in Ranchi's Bargain circle area. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) is investigating allegations that the land was acquired through illegal means and that the transactions associated with it involved irregularities. According to the agency, land-related documents and procedural records were allegedly manipulated. Soren has denied the allegations, maintaining that there is no sufficient direct evidence against him. The ED, however, has contended that documents recovered during the investigation, witness statements and other circumstantial evidence establish a prima facie case. On June 8, the special PMLA court rejected Soren's discharge plea, observing that the material available on record was sufficient at the prima facie stage to proceed further with the case. The court had clarified that no conclusion regarding guilt had been reached at that stage. The ED has filed a charge sheet against Soren and around 18 other accused persons in the matter. The special court has already framed charges against several of the co-accused. --IANS snc/skp/

headline: Nearly 3 decades on, SIA reopens Wandhama massacre investigation - The Tribune
text: Nearly 3 decades on, SIA reopens Wandhama massacre investigation Agency also begins probes into killings of Kashmiri Pandit leaders Sarwanand Koul Premi and Tika Lal Taploo Jammu and Kashmir’s State Investigation Agency (SIA) has reopened the investigation into the 1998 Wandhama massacre in which 23 Kashmiri Pandits were killed in central Kashmir’s Ganderbal district, officials said. The agency has also begun investigations into the killings of Kashmiri Pandit poet and journalist Sarwanand Koul Premi and BJP leader Tika Lal Taploo, officials said. A senior official said the reopening of the cases was part of a wider effort to pursue long-pending cases of targeted killings during the peak of militancy in the Valley. “The investigation is part of the cases that are being reopened to take the older cases to their logical conclusion and ensure justice for the victims,” the official said. On the night of January 25, 1998, 23 members of the Kashmiri Pandit community were killed by unidentified terrorists in Wandhama village. According to officials, a group of armed men entered a family’s house on the pretext of asking for tea before opening fire on the family and neighbours. Among those killed were 10 women, nine men and four children. Sources said investigations have also been initiated into the killings of Premi and Taploo. Premi, a Kashmiri Pandit poet and journalist, was abducted and killed along with his son on the night of April 30, 1990. Taploo, a prominent BJP leader and its vice-president in Jammu and Kashmir, was killed in 1989. The SIA has recently stepped up efforts to reinvestigate old militancy-related cases. Earlier this month, the agency conducted searches at nine locations across the Union Territory in connection with the 1990 murder of a Kashmiri Pandit writer and his son. The agency has also recently filed a chargesheet against Jammu Kashmir Liberation Front chief Yasin Malik and four others in connection with the 1990 abduction and killing of Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat.

headline: Dehing Patkai home to 165 butterfly species, including 37 endangered ones: Sarma
text: Guwahati, Aug 25 (IANS) Assam Chief Minister, Himanta Biswa Sarma, on Tuesday highlighted the rich butterfly diversity of Dehing Patkai, describing the biodiversity-rich region as a safe haven for the state’s rare and endangered butterfly species. Taking to social media platform X, Sarma shared a message celebrating the region’s remarkable biodiversity and said that Dehing Patkai is home to 165 recorded butterfly species, including 37 endangered species. “Butterfly, fly away… ,” the Chief Minister wrote in his post, highlighting the ecological significance of the region and the importance of protecting its natural habitat. Sarma said the presence of such a large variety of butterfly species reflects the rich biodiversity of Dehing Patkai, which is known for its dense forests and diverse wildlife. He further underlined the role of conservation initiatives in preserving the fragile ecosystem and creating conditions where rare species can survive and flourish. “Conservation efforts are helping create a thriving habitat where rare species can continue to flourish,” Sarma said. Butterflies are widely regarded as important indicators of the health of an ecosystem, as their populations are closely linked to vegetation, climate and the overall condition of natural habitats. The Dehing Patkai landscape, located in Assam’s eastern region, is recognised for its rich forest ecosystem and diverse flora and fauna. The area forms an important part of Assam’s wider efforts to conserve its natural heritage and protect wildlife habitats. The Chief Minister’s post comes amid growing emphasis on biodiversity conservation and sustainable management of Assam’s forest resources. The state has, in recent years, stepped up efforts to promote wildlife conservation, protect forest landscapes and raise awareness about the ecological importance of its natural habitats. The identification of 165 butterfly species in Dehing Patkai, including 37 endangered species, further underscores the ecological value of the region and the need to safeguard its habitat. The conservation of butterfly populations can also contribute to the protection of wider ecosystems, as preserving their habitats helps maintain plant diversity and supports several other species dependent on the same ecological environment. Sarma’s message sought to draw attention to the biodiversity of Dehing Patkai while highlighting ongoing conservation efforts aimed at ensuring that rare species continue to thrive in their natural surroundings. --IANS tdr/rad

headline: Not taking political 'sanyas', will not stop till I force BJP into obscurity: Mamata Banerjee- Moneycontrol.com
text: Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee on Monday ruled out taking political ‘sanyas’ (retirement), saying she would continue her political fight until the BJP was pushed into obscurity. In a Facebook Live, Banerjee said people in West Bengal had understood the “true face” of the BJP within four months of the change in government. She also raised concerns over the ongoing Census exercise, alleging that it was a backdoor attempt to enforce the National Register of Citizens (NRC). According to Banerjee, the exercise was carried out without consulting political parties. Urging people to be cautious while filling out Census forms, Banerjee warned against sharing personal information, saying it could potentially result in people’s savings being wiped off. ‘BJP is cheating women’ Amid protests by women in different parts of the state over an alleged delay in the disbursement of funds under the Annapurna Bhandar financial aid scheme, Banerjee accused the BJP-led state government of reducing the number of beneficiaries by citing ineligibility. "We had launched Lakshmir Bhandar to make women financially self-sufficient but the BJP is considering religion and race to provide Annapurna Bhandar money. It is violating its pre-poll promise of providing Annapurna Yojana money to all women, and is now cheating them," the former chief minister alleged. Jadavpur University clashes Reacting to clashes between ABVP and Left students at Jadavpur University, Banerjee accused the BJP of orchestrating vandalism on the campus. She said the Trinamool Congress may have differences of opinion with some students, but maintained: "despite our differences of opinion with some students there, we respect them". Mamata on electoral roll revision Mamata Banerjee also criticised the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, alleging that lakhs of genuine voters had been illegally deleted from the voter list. She said she would approach the Supreme Court again, if required, for the inclusion of those voters. *With Agency Inputs Find the best of Al News in one place, specially curated for you every weekend. headline: Congress's Jully slams Rajasthan govt's school entry curbs, flags graduate unemployment
text: Congress's Jully slams Rajasthan govt's school entry curbs, flags graduate unemployment Congress leader and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajasthan Assembly, Tikaram Jully, on Sunday, August 23, accused the state government of attempting to conceal the poor condition of government schools by restricting entry and photography on school premises, and called for a broader overhaul of the education system with greater emphasis on skill development. Jully's remarks come a week after the Rajasthan government restricted outsiders' entry into government schools without prior permission from the principal, and barred photography and videography without written approval. The order, issued on August 16, followed an announcement by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that it would inspect schools across the state found to be in "poor" condition. Recounting a recent visit to a government school in Jaipur, Jully said students had first raised concerns about their school's condition on social media, prompting his visit. "After I went there, I was promised that the problems would be rectified within 15 days. When I returned after 15 days, I found a new order displayed outside saying that people and the media could not enter," he said, alleging that the restrictions were introduced specifically to keep the state of schools out of the public domain. The Congress leader argued that the education system requires fundamental reform, saying that handing out degrees without corresponding employment opportunities does little to address the underlying problem. He claimed that 26 per cent of graduates remain unemployed and questioned the methodology used by the government to calculate unemployment figures, alleging that joblessness has risen while the government has failed to adequately tackle the issue. "The education system has to change. Along with education, we also have to focus on skills. Only then will we be able to overcome this challenge," he said. (With inputs from PTI)

headline: CAT directs Chandigarh Education Dept to release DA arrears to contractual teachers within 2 months - The Tribune
text: CAT directs Chandigarh Education Dept to release DA arrears to contractual teachers within 2 months CAT’s time-bound direction come after the teachers filed contempt proceedings seeking payment of DA arrears along with the prevalent Basic Pay from their initial dates of appointment Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT), Chandigarh Bench, has directed the Education Department, Chandigarh Administration, to release arrears of Dearness Allowance (DA) to contractual teachers of schools from their respective dates of appointment within a period of two months and to file a compliance affidavit. More than 300 teachers, appointed between 1998 and 2002, filed contempt petitions seeking compliance with judgments passed by the CAT in 2018 in three Original Applications (OAs), directing the Education Department to release the arrears of DA. During the contempt proceedings, the Chandigarh Education Department finally issued an order dated August 11, 2026, granting the arrears of DA along with the prevalent Basic Pay from the initial dates of appointment to the teachers, in compliance with the 2018 judgments. In support of their claim, the counsels referred to a judgment of the Central Administrative Tribunal, Chandigarh Bench, decided on March 31, 2011, as well as other judicial pronouncements, including those of the Supreme Court, holding that contractual teachers are entitled to Basic Pay along with Dearness Allowance, as revised from time to time. Although the OAs were allowed in 2018 by quashing the letter dated February 10, 2016, the benefit was not granted by the Chandigarh Administration on the ground that the judgment was under judicial review before the Punjab and Haryana High Court in a petition filed by the Chandigarh Administration in 2011. headline: Why UP Govt Is Sending Senior Officials To Schools After 'Gen Alpha' Protests | Outlook India
text: - A wave of 'Gen Alpha' protests across Lucknow, Azamgarh, Mahoba, Hamirpur, Unnao, Kannauj and Fatehpur pushed the UP government to order tighter school monitoring. - The Chief Minister's Office has appointed nodal officers across five departments to track school conditions. - Officials have been told to identify the causes of deficiencies and fix responsibility . A wave of student protests, led by children as young as Class 6, has pushed the Uttar Pradesh government into an unusual position: appointing senior officials to personally monitor its own schools. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered tighter oversight of educational institutions after a string of demonstrations by students over teacher shortages, broken infrastructure and administrative delays spread across the state through July and August 2026, forcing bureaucrats out of their offices and onto school campuses. The response marks a shift from the state's usual pattern of local, one-off damage control at individual schools to a structured, top-down monitoring exercise spanning multiple government departments. What Triggered This Direct Administrative Intervention? The wave began in late July 2026, when roughly 1,500 students at Sarvodaya Inter College in Fatehpur staged a six-hour sit-in demanding clean drinking water, functioning fans and toilets, prompting officials to agree in writing to seven of their eight demands. Similar protests broke out in the same period across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Rajasthan, with children invoking the recent Gen Z protests in Delhi as inspiration. By mid-August, Uttar Pradesh alone had recorded six such protests in 20 days, including two demonstrations within four days by girls of the Jai Prakash Narayan Sarvodaya Vidyalaya in Lucknow over a shortage of Physics, Chemistry and Biology teachers ahead of board exams, students in Azamgarh and Hamirpur, and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya students in Kannauj who boycotted mess food and locked themselves in their hostel rooms. Adityanath ordered the tighter monitoring on August 20, following a review meeting on the management of the state's Sarvodaya residential schools. What Does The Government Want Officials To Check? The Chief Minister's Office has appointed nodal officers to oversee institutions across the basic and secondary education, higher education, technical and vocational education, social welfare and labour departments. These officials have been asked to identify the causes of deficiencies — from vacant teaching posts and faulty infrastructure to poor sanitation, unreliable mid-day meals, and hostel food quality — and to fix responsibility wherever negligence is established. headline: Maratha Reservation: Manoj Jarange-Patil Refuses Medical Check-Up On Day 4 Of Hunger Strike In Jalna; Govt Delegation To Meet Him Today
text: Jalna: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange-Patil, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike since August 29 at Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district, refused a medical examination on Monday, with doctors saying he did not respond to repeated requests to check his blood pressure and other health parameters. Jarange Refuses Medical Examination Jarange-Patil has been demanding action on Maratha reservation and the issuance of Kunbi caste certificates to eligible Marathas. His protest entered its fourth day amid growing concern over his health. A medical team that arrived at the protest site attempted to wake him and sought permission to conduct a check-up, but Jarange reportedly indicated with his hand that he did not want to undergo the examination. Medical officer Dr Vijay Wakode said the team would continue requesting Jarange to undergo regular health checks. “We are repeatedly requesting him, but he has refused the examination. Our medical team is here and we will come every two hours and request him,” Wakode said, as reported by TV9 Marathi. According to the doctor, Jarange's health parameters checked the previous day showed his blood pressure at around 130 and blood sugar at around 70. Cabinet To Discuss Jarange's Protest Jarange's indefinite fast has put pressure on the Maharashtra government, with the state Cabinet scheduled to meet on Tuesday. The ongoing agitation and Jarange's demands are expected to come up for discussion during the meeting. Govt Delegation Set To Meet Jarange Today A government delegation is also likely to meet Jarange after the Cabinet meeting. According to reports, BJP MLA Prasad Lad will meet him at Antarwali Sarati at 11:30 am, while Ministers Shambhuraj Desai, Uday Samant and Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil are also expected to meet Jarange-Patil later today. The delegation is expected to present the government's position and hold discussions with him. headline: Mr Singh poster row: Showing any community in poor light uncalled for: SGPC - The Tribune
text: A day after the US Department of Homeland Security took down an AI-generated poster asking "Mr Singh" to self-deport, SGPC president Advocate Harjinder Singh Dhami alleged that the post had unfairly targeted the Punjabi and Sikh community. Dhami has written to the US Embassy in New Delhi, objecting to the content of the poster. He has also urged External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar to take up the matter with the US authorities through diplomatic channels. While welcoming the withdrawal of the poster, Dhami said such references could create a negative perception about an entire community by associating an individual’s alleged conduct with his religious or ethnic identity. He said Punjabis and Sikhs had made significant contributions to the economic and social development of the United States through their hard work and skills. He particularly referred to the community’s presence in the trucking sector and other fields. According to the SGPC statement, Dhami said mentioning “Mr Singh” in the poster and highlighting his identity in connection with a driving-related matter reflected bias against the Punjabi and Sikh community. “Targeting any community on the basis of its religious identity, name or attire is against the values of a civilised society,” he said. Dhami said the Sikh community was known globally for its contribution to society and humanitarian service. An issue involving an individual, he said, should not be projected in a manner that casts aspersions on the wider Punjabi or Sikh community. He said attempts to portray immigrant communities negatively were inconsistent with the multicultural character of the United States and could affect social harmony. The SGPC president urged Jaishankar to raise the issue with the US and seek appropriate action, saying such incidents required greater sensitivity towards the religious and cultural identities of immigrant communities.

headline: Assam government to go paperless from January 1 , 2027
text: Guwahati, Sep 23 : Assam government has set January 1, 2027 as the deadline for all state government offices to shift to paperless office system, marking a major expansion of its ongoing digital governance programme, officials said. The Chief Minister's Office made the announcement on Wednesday, describing it a new phase in Assam's efforts to modernise administrative functioning and make public services more efficient and transparent. "Save the Date: 1 January 2027. A new chapter in Assam's digital governance," the CMO said in a post on X. It said that under the leadership of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, all government offices would transition to the paperless e-Office system, with the objective of making public services "more transparent, efficient and citizen-centric". Assam has already adopted the National Informatics Centre (NIC)-developed e-Office platform in the state Secretariat. According to NIC, all 58 departments in the Secretariat are currently using the system, while implementation is also being extended to selected directorates and Deputy Commissioners' offices. The e-Office platform replaces conventional paper-based file processing with digital workflows. Government offices can receive and diarise documents electronically, create and move files digitally, prepare notes and drafts online, and digitally sign and archive official records. The system also enables officials to track the movement and status of files, creating an electronic trail of administrative processes and decisions. According to NIC, the platform is intended to make government functioning more responsive, effective, accountable and transparent while reducing dependence on physical files. Assam has been working towards expanding e-Office adoption for several years. The state-initiated implementation at the district level and established a dedicated state-level steering mechanism in 2021. In 2026, the government launched e-Office District to further extend digital file management and paperless administrative processes across district-level government machinery. The January 1, 2027 deadline will therefore mark the expansion of an existing digital framework to government offices across the state rather than the introduction of e-Office in Assam. The statewide rollout will require government departments and field offices to adopt the system uniformly. Its effectiveness will depend on infrastructure, digital capacity and the extent to which electronic file movement helps reduce delays, improve monitoring and streamline delivery of public services. --IANS tdr/mr

headline: DMK rejects Vijay’s free cars for 59 MLAs, Udhayanidhi Stalin says ‘government in debt’
text: DMK rejects Vijay’s free cars for 59 MLAs, Udhayanidhi Stalin says ‘government in debt’ Leader of Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin said all 59 DMK legislators had decided not to avail Vijay’s offer. Days after Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced free official vehicles for every legislator in the state, the opposition DMK on Friday rejected the offer, citing the state’s mounting debt. Leader of Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin said all 59 DMK legislators had decided not to avail Vijay’s offer, news agency ANI reported. "Since the TVK government has been saying from day one after assuming power that the government is in debt, all 59 DMK MLAs have decided not to avail this offer. headline: CJP School Inspection Drive Turns Violent In Jaipur Village
text: Jaipur: The school inspection drive by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) turned violent in Rampura Kanwarpura village near Jaipur on Friday when a team led by party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka was allegedly confronted and attacked by villagers. Inspection drive turns violent The CJP workers had reached the village to inspect the condition of the government school as part of the party's ongoing campaign against alleged poor infrastructure and mismanagement in government schools. The team faced strong opposition from local residents and was allegedly beaten and chased out of the village. Their vehicles were also reportedly pelted with stones. Ranka alleged that villagers damaged mobile phones and vehicles belonging to the CJP workers and assaulted a woman party worker accompanying the team. Five CJP workers, including Ranka, were reportedly injured and taken to SMS Hospital for treatment. The party had planned to inspect Bhattawala Government School on Vatika Road, but the visit was cancelled following the confrontation. headline: Karnataka: Cabinet again recommends suspension of Karnataka Public Service Commission chairperson
text: The Karnataka Cabinet on Friday (August 21) is learnt to have decided to again recommend the suspension of Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar, who has been accused of favouring his two daughters for selection as Industrial Extension Officers. One daughter has been accused of providing a false income certificate showing the family’s annual income as ₹40,000. Earlier suspension Sources said that the Governor had earlier suspended Mr. Sahukar and then sent the decision to be ratified by the Cabinet, which cleared it. However, this was seen as a procedural lapse. “The Cabinet took the decision again to overcome the lapse and has sent it to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot, who will take further action,” sources said. Mr. Gehlot is expected to refer the matter to President Droupadi Murmu. The development comes after the Karnataka High Court on August 18 set aside the Governor’s order of suspending Mr. Sahukar and had ordered reinstatement. The court had observed that the Governor’s order was “illegal” in the absence of aid and advice from the Council of Ministers. The advocate-on-record for the Governor had told the court that the President, acting on the Governor’s recommendation, on August 14, had referred to the apex court to hold an inquiry into the allegations against Mr. Sahukar. However, the court had then said that the issue raised in Mr. Sahukar’s case was on a different legal point. For industries In another decision, the Cabinet is learnt to have cleared the amendment to Karnataka Industries (Facilitation) Act, 2002, in a bid to strengthen the single window system for clearance and introduce “Know Your Approvals” for applicant industries besides bringing in a “once only” system for document submission. The affidavit-based clearance has been extended from 15 services to 20 services, and affidavit-based clearance certification for MSMEs to three years and big industries to five years. The amendment proposed a “deemed approval” system if the applications are not cleared within the stipulated period, among many other proposals. The Cabinet has also approved tabling of the Karnataka Gram Swaraj and Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to replace an ordinance promulgated earlier to amend the rules that deal with taxation, rates and fee.
