headline: Ex-Haryana minister's son dies after shooting self at farmhouse
text: PATIALA/JIND: Gaganjot Sandhu, son of the late former Haryana agriculture minister Jaswinder Singh Sandhu, died by suicide on Friday after shooting himself with a licensed firearm at his farmhouse in Punjab’s Ropar district, police said. He was 45. Sandhu, a resident of Gumthala Garhu village of Pehowa town in Kurukshetra district, served twice as the village sarpanch. Initial inquiries indicated that Sandhu had arrived at his farmhouse in Purkhali village from Kurukshetra early Friday morning and was alone at the property when the incident occurred. Police received information about the incident around 2:30 pm, after which law enforcement personnel and forensic specialists secured the site and collected ballistic evidence. The body is kept at Ropar civil hospital for post-mortem. Deepinder Singh, DSP, Ropar, confirmed that Sandhu used a licensed weapon. He said Sandhu had reportedly been suffering from depression related to an attempt-to-murder case recently registered against him in the nearby town of Khanna. In recent years, Sandhu faced multiple legal disputes and criminal charges. In Nov 2021, two separate cases were registered against him at the Pehowa police station involving allegations of assault and an attempt to run over a local political worker’s relative. On March 29, 2026, Sandhu was arrested in connection with a shooting over a property dispute in Gumthala Garhu, where he allegedly injured a land dealer. Sandhu’s late father, Jaswinder Singh Sandhu, was a senior leader in the Indian National Lok Dal (INLD), serving four terms as an MLA from the Pehowa constituency and as the state’s agriculture minister in Om Prakash Chautala ’s govt. The elder Sandhu passed away in 2019. Police have initiated formal inquest proceedings under Section 194 of BNSS to verify the full sequence of events surrounding his death. Sandhu is survived by his wife, Simranjit Kaur, and two sons.

headline: Communication between CEC, ECs shows functioning democracy: BJP
text: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday (September 23, 2026) said communications between the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners, which the Opposition parties cited as evidence of internal dissent in the institution, instead demonstrated its democratic functioning. He accused the Congress of being associated with multiple controversies concerning the independence and impartiality of the ECI during its rule in the past. headline: Jharkhand: Protesters call off agitation over exam irregularities in Indian state
text: - Published Protesters in the eastern Indian state of Jharkhand have called off their 26-day agitation over alleged irregularities in government exams after the state agreed to several of their demands. Thousands of students and job seekers had been seeking an overhaul of the state's recruitment system, with some also going on hunger strike. The breakthrough came after the government cancelled 22 of these exams and ordered investigations into several others. On Wednesday, student leaders said they had given the government two months to fulfil its remaining promises. The protest site in the state capital, Ranchi, where hundreds had been camped out since late July, has since been cleared. Before leaving, protesters held celebrations, exchanging garlands and bursting crackers. "This marks a major victory in the struggle that Jharkhand's students have endured," student activist Ravindra Paswan told news agency ANI. But protest leaders stressed that the agitation had only been suspended and could resume if the government failed to act. One issue that had prolonged the stand-off was the students' demand for an investigation by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal investigative agency. The state government had resisted that demand, instead ordering its Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to investigate alleged irregularities. Several people have been arrested during the investigation, including the head of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC), which conducts many of these exams. After weeks of deadlock, protest leaders said on Wednesday that they had agreed to a government proposal for a judicial inquiry instead of an immediate CBI investigation. "If this is not done within two months, we will once again vigorously demand a CBI investigation," Paswan said. The government's concessions, however, have created a new dispute. Its decision to cancel some exams has triggered protests from successful candidates who had already cleared them and taken up government jobs. It remains unclear what will happen to their appointments if the investigations uncover irregularities. Some have approached the Jharkhand High Court, arguing that candidates who qualified on merit should not lose their positions because of alleged irregularities involving others. Government jobs are highly sought after in India for the stability and security they offer. Millions of candidates sit recruitment exams every year, often spending years preparing for them. headline: Supreme Court closes 'The Kerala Story' petitions, says question of law will 'Await Another Movie'
text: The Supreme Court recently concluded proceedings on petitions concerning the contentious 2023 film ‘The Kerala Story’, though it left the broader legal question surrounding challenges to CBFC film certification unresolved. Supreme Court rules certification pleas infructuous According to PTI, a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant disposed of numerous cases on Friday that were either filed during the COVID-19 period or had lost relevance over time. Among these, the bench, which also included Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana—addressed two petitions calling for the cancellation of CBFC certification granted to "The Kerala Story," ruling that the pleas had become infructuous. Supreme Court sees withdrawal of West Bengal ban plea Meanwhile, a third petition, filed by the film's producers Sunshine Pictures Pvt Ltd and Vipul Amritlal Shah challenging the West Bengal government's earlier decision to ban the film, was withdrawn. Supreme Court hears arguments on continued relevance of pleas Back in May 2023, the top court had stayed the state government's ban. In the other two matters, advocate Nizam Pasha, representing petitioners Qurban Ali and B R Aravindakshan, argued that his clients' concerns remained relevant even though the film had since been released. He also highlighted that the Kerala High Court had already disposed of a writ petition on the film, noting at the time that such a plea could not be sustained against the CBFC's decision to certify the movie. He argued that although producers had a statutory route to challenge CBFC certification, individuals aggrieved by a film's content lacked any such statutory recourse and had to seek relief through a writ petition in court instead. The bench, however, pointed out that the film had already been released. Supreme Court says legal question will 'await another movie' Justice Bagchi remarked that the legal question could remain unresolved for now. headline: Purification Is Not Cleaning, It Belongs To A Different Vocabulary
text: Purification is not cleaning. The distinction matters because cleaning concerns hygiene, while purification can carry a disturbing caste and religious meaning. The alleged “shuddhikaran” ceremony at Haldwani must be viewed in that context. Anyone who has visited a venue after a political, religious or social gathering knows the scene: plastic bottles, paper, food waste and other rubbish scattered across the ground. The larger the gathering, the greater the mess. Cleaning staff remove the waste and restore the place. Nobody calls it purification. The same workers perform an equally thankless task after heavy rain, clearing mud and garbage from roads and lanes. Their contribution is rarely noticed. Yet nobody suggests that they are purifying the roads. Purification And Caste Prejudice Purification belongs to a different vocabulary. India has a long history of treating the presence of certain people as polluting. Jagjivan Ram, one of the country’s tallest political leaders and a distinguished minister, once learnt that a place from which he had addressed a gathering was subsequently subjected to a purification ceremony. Former Union minister Vayalar Ravi had a similar experience. His grandchild was taken to a famous temple for a religious function, but the authorities apparently failed to appreciate one fact: Ravi’s wife was Christian. These are not isolated curiosities. They show that the battle against caste prejudice is far from over. Kerala’s Temple Entry Proclamation of 1936 was a historic repudiation of untouchability. Yet its author, poet Ulloor S. Parameswara Iyer, faced ostracism from sections of his own caste. His assertion that he had ceased to be defined by caste and was simply a human being captured the moral force of the reform movement. Questions Over Haldwani Incident The Haldwani incident appears to belong to this troubling history. The facts must be established. But if Mallikarjun Kharge’s presence at a venue was followed by a purification ritual because of his caste, this was not merely an insult to an individual; it was an affront to the Constitution, and it cannot be accepted under any circumstances. The authorities’ response makes the episode more disturbing. Instead of first asking who conducted the purification and why, an FIR has reportedly been registered against the Leader of Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, for protesting against it. Those who allegedly performed the ritual appear to have escaped similar scrutiny. This inversion of accountability is becoming familiar. text: In connection with the alleged irregularities involving the Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission (CGPSC), the Directorate of Enforcement is conducting raids at seven locations on Tuesday. The ED had earlier arrested former CGPSC Chairman Taman Singh Sonwani. The agency has now intensified its investigation into the same case from the money laundering angle. What happened? The ED has stepped up its action in the Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission recruitment scam and paper leak case. While investigating the case from the money laundering perspective, the ED arrested former CGPSC Chairman Taman Singh Sonwani a few months ago. He has been questioned to gather information about alleged financial transactions and other monetary aspects linked to the recruitment scam. The allegations relate to irregularities in CGPSC recruitments conducted between 2020 and 2022. According to the investigating agency, serious allegations have emerged regarding nepotism, financial transactions, and the selection of relatives of government officials and political leaders in recruitments conducted during this period. The investigation is being taken forward on the basis of these allegations. A report by ANI stated that the ED also carried out searches at the residence of former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel's PA, KK Chandrakar, among seven places across the state in the alleged Chhattisgarh Public Service Commission (CGPSC) scam. At the time of his arrest, officials said Sonwani had remained evasive during questioning by the agency. The ED's money laundering case stems from a 2024 FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). The CBI case was based on a complaint by the Chhattisgarh Police following the BJP's return to power in the state after defeating the Congress in the November 2023 Assembly elections. Sonwani was also arrested by the CBI in 2024 in connection with the case. The ED has alleged that Sonwani facilitated the leakage of question papers and manipulated the selection process in exchange for illegal gratification, allegedly benefiting his relatives and candidates who paid bribes. According to the agency, the CGPSC recruitment rules were amended in 2021 to remove the term "nephew" from the definition of family members, allegedly to facilitate the selection of Sonwani's relatives for government posts. headline: Tension prevails in Jadavpur University after SFI, ABVP groups clash; several students hospitalised
text: Kolkata, Aug 20 : Tension broke out at Jadavpur University (JU) campus in South Kolkata on the intervening night of Wednesday and Thursday over clashes between the Students' Federation of India (SFI), the CPI(M)'s students' wing and the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). The tension between the two rival students' unions erupted over the general body meeting of the Faculty of Engineering and Technology Students' Union (FETSU). The SFI has claimed that the ABVP has been trying to take control over the JU since the formation of the new state government in West Bengal, mobilised outsiders within the university campus and resorted to vandalism. The ABVP, on the other hand, has accused the SFI, assisted by activists of the Socialist Unity Centre of India (Communist)- affiliated Democratic Students' Organisation (DSO), of launching an attack on the ABVP office-bearers inside the campus in the guise of a general body meeting. Some of the students injured in the clashes are currently under treatment at the nearby K.P.C. Medical College and Hospital. The local Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) legislator from Jadavpur Assembly Constituency, Sarbori Mukherjee, an actress-turned-politician, arrived at the hospital on Thursday morning to enquire about the injured students admitted there. Both the rival groups have lodged FIRs at the local Jadavpur Police Station over the incident. At the same time, both the rival students' wings have announced massive protest demonstrations on Thursday over the issue within the campus. At the time the report was filed, no one had been arrested in connection with the clashes that broke out in the intervening night of Wednesday and Thursday. According to the ABVP's central working committee member, Subhabrata Adhikari, the attack on their office-bearers was orchestrated not just by SFI activists but also by students affiliated to other Left-wing student groups, including those having links with Left-Wing Extremism (LWE) groups. On the other hand, SFI's general secretary, Srijan Bhattacharya, said the SFI was nowhere to be found in the entire mess. "What I heard is that the ABVP activists aided by local BJP associates resorted to vandalism within the campus. Why is ABVP so scared to face elections and democratically take control of the students' body in JU?" Bhattacharya questioned.

headline: J&K CM’s remark ahead of U.S. envoy meeting draws flak from PDP
text: Ahead of his meeting with the U.S. envoy in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday (August 19, 2026) said it should be the Centre, and not Washington, that “solves our problems". This drew criticism from the Opposition People’s Democratic Party (PDP), which described the remark as “pre-emptive defensiveness”. Ruling out any attempt by the ruling National Conference to raise political issues with the visiting envoy, Sergio Gor, who serves as the U.S. Ambassador to India and Special Envoy to South and Central Asia, Mr. Abdullah said, “Our problems have nothing to do with him. It is not my habit to complain to an ambassador of another country. Washington should not solve our problems. Our central government should solve our problems.” Criticising the comment, PDP leader Iltija Mufti said, “I am yet to see an Indian CM so apologetic about a simple meeting with the U.S. Ambassador that he feels the need to announce beforehand what he will and won’t discuss. A meeting is a meeting. Why the public pre-emptive defensiveness?" Meanwhile, BJP spokesperson Altaf Thakur described the U.S. envoy’s visit as a “very positive thing” and said that the world should see what the “actual situation” in Kashmir now is, compared to how it was earlier. headline: Executioner-in-Chief? The SC's ever-changing dance with death under HL Dattu & other justices
text: Chief Justice of India (CJI) HL Dattu is not far from matching a new record: since he became CJI on 28 September 2014, he has confirmed the death sentences of 10 persons in five cases. This year alone, Dattu presided over apex court benches that confirmed eight death sentences in four cases, including two persons whose appeal he refused in a judgment delivered last month (15 May), and two on the Friday before that (8 May). In a Supreme Court tenure that started in 2008, Dattu has confirmed 13 death sentences in seven cases with nearly six months remaining before he retires, according to a tally of such judgments that is with Legally India. If Dattu continued at the pace he’s set in early 2015, he could be on track to approach the former Supreme Court judge Justice Arijit Pasayat’s record tally of 23 death penalty confirmations in 13 cases between 2001 and 2009. And although Dattu commuted one death sentence to life imprisonment because he found the prosecution’s evidence too circumstantial to warrant the death penalty, in two cases he also dismissed four prisoners’ special leave petitions (SLPs) to appeal their sentences to the Supreme Court outright with only a cursory hearing (in limine, in legal speak). For lawyers, academics and activists opposing the state putting anyone to death even for the most heinous crimes in the rarest cases, things are looking far more bleak now than they did only 12 months ago. Sathasivam’s legacy “I personally feel sullied every time a person is executed in my name,” says advocate Dr Yug Mohit Chaudhry about why he is spending so much time fighting to save the lives of those sentenced to death. “It’s almost certain that the person is being executed because of his poverty. You’re criminalising poverty here because he couldn’t defend himself adequately.” Chaudhry has handled hundreds of murder trials and appeals, and around 25 “end stage cases of death-row prisoners on the verge of execution”, having written more mercy petitions than he can remember, he says. He, along with senior advocates Colin Gonsalves, Ram Jethmalani, Anand Grover and R Basant argued for a raft of death row prisoners in a case that would prove to be a game-changer in death penalty jurisprudence, wedging open a door that no one was sure had even existed until that point. headline: Abhishek Banerjee’s Kolkata office building ordered to vacate floors over fire safety lapses
text: The West Bengal Fire Department on Friday ordered the evacuation of the basement and sixth and seventh floors of a high-rise building in central Kolkata that houses the office of Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee, citing a lack of adequate fire safety measures, according to a report by news agency PTI. The action came a day after Banerjee’s Camac Street office was ransacked, with the TMC blaming men linked to the BJP for the attack. The BJP has denied the allegation. The same building was at the centre of another controversy last week when authorities removed an “illegal” TMC billboard. Private security guards at Banerjee’s office, his supporters and some party leaders had clashed with police and Kolkata Municipal Corporation officials during the removal. According to PTI, the fire department found no fire safety measures in the building’s basement during an inspection. It subsequently issued a show-cause notice to the building owner, giving them 48 hours to respond. “Since we did not get any response and the deadline passed, we sent them a notice to evacuate the basement, sixth and seventh floors of the building. If the basement of any building has no fire safety measures, it could lead to a big disaster in case of a fire,” a fire department official told PTI. The official said the fire safety certificate for the premises had expired on August 10 and had not been renewed. In its notice to the building owner, the department said the basement, sixth and seventh floors would remain prohibited from use until the deficiencies were rectified and a valid fire safety certificate obtained. A joint team of police and fire officials conducted a floor-by-floor inspection of the building on Monday. The inspection found inadequate firefighting arrangements on the seventh floor, no designated fire exit and issues with the fire alarm system, according to the notice. (With PTI inputs)

headline: Karnal: 86 sanitation workers resume duty after month-long stir; strike extended till Sept 13 - The Tribune
text: Karnal: 86 sanitation workers resume duty after month-long stir; strike extended till Sept 13 900 employees still yet to join work, continue agitation for regularisation of jobs Days after the issuance of notices by the Karnal Municipal Corporation (KMC), as many as 86 sanitation workers have joined duty after remaining on strike for over one month. However, 900 employees are still yet to join duty and are continuing to be on strike to press their demands. Sanitation workers have been staging protests across the state since August 6 to press their demands including regularisation of their jobs. Ashok Kumar, Additional Municipal Commissioner, said that the KMC has 986 sanitation employees, including 94 regular and 892 contractual workers. Of these, 10 employees resumed duty on Tuesday, while 76 more joined on Wednesday. He further maintained the KMC, with the assistance of the police is making efforts to lift garbage from various points across the city. Kumar said that on the directions of KMC Commissioner Saloni Sharma, notices had been issued to all the striking employees, directing them to resume duty by September 5. Meanwhile, sanitation employees, under the banner of Nagar Palika Karamchari Sangh, Haryana, have extended the strike until September 13. As part of the ongoing agitation, Jan Nyay Panchayats will be organised in all districts of the state from September 10 to 12. A condolence meeting was also organised at the protest site outside the KMC office on Wednesday to pay tribute to four sanitation workers who allegedly died during the ongoing agitation in different parts of Haryana. Earlier, President of the Nagar Palika Karamchari Sangh Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, Vinesh Manothia reached the protest site to extend support to the striking workers. He warned if Haryana government failed to regularise contractual employees soon, protests and strikes would also be launched in UP. Karnal unit president Raj Kumar demanded that the government fully implement the agreement reached on May 13 and stop issuing notices and warnings to employees. He said regular and contractual sanitation workers remained united and that the strike would be called off only after the notification for regularisation of sanitation workers is issued. Kumar, along with other employees' leaders held the government responsible for the inconvenience being faced by residents due to the strike.

headline: Noel Tata meets PMO, Home Ministry officials as Tata Sons prepares for leadership transition: Report- Moneycontrol.com
text: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata met officials in the Prime Minister’s Office and the Union Home Ministry in New Delhi on Saturday, people familiar with the matter told CNBC-TV18, days after N Chandrasekaran said he would not seek another term as chairman of Tata Sons. The meetings were aimed at briefing the government on the current situation at the Tata group, including the impending leadership transition at its holding company, the people said. The Financial Express first reported the meetings, saying Tata met Home Minister Amit Shah and a senior PMO official. Chandrasekaran said on August 12 that he would not offer himself for reappointment as chairman when his current term ends on February 20, 2027. In his statement, he pointed to the absence of unanimous board support for another term and said clarity on leadership was important given the strategic projects underway across the group. The development has started the formal process of identifying his successor. A day after Chandrasekaran’s announcement, the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust said it had passed a resolution to initiate the constitution of a selection committee “as soon as possible” to recommend the next Tata Sons chairman. Tata Trusts said it would support a “smooth, timely and orderly transition of leadership”. The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust are Tata Sons’ two principal charitable shareholders and together owned more than half of the holding company as of March 31. Tata Trusts collectively controls about 66% of Tata Sons. AGM faces separate quorum hurdle The succession process is unfolding alongside a separate procedural issue around Tata Sons’ annual general meeting scheduled for August 18. CNBC-TV18 reported earlier on Monday that the AGM is likely to be adjourned because the required quorum may not be available. The issue stems from regulatory restrictions on the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, which have prevented it from taking the decision needed for a joint nomination under Tata Sons’ Articles of Association. Article 86 requires at least five members to be personally present for a valid quorum, including an authorised representative jointly nominated by the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust. headline: Not a single pothole on Mumbai-Pune Expressway in 27 years: Nitin Gadkari
text: Not a single pothole on Mumbai-Pune Expressway in 27 years: Nitin Gadkari Nitin Gadkari said that 27 years ago, he built the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and claimed it has not developed any potholes to date. Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari on Monday complained that he is blamed for road problems even when they are built by state governments. Speaking at the Festival of Thinkers lecture series in Pune on Monday, Gadkari said that 27 years ago, he built the Mumbai-Pune Expressway and claimed it has not developed any potholes to date. But, he said, that has never been reported. "I built the Mumbai-Pune Expressway 27 years ago. To this day, not a single pothole has appeared on it; the road remains in excellent condition, yet news about this never gets published," Gadkari told the gathering. The union minister lamented that he gets blamed even when a road built by a state government caves in. "During my tenure, the Forest Department did not grant permission, so I could not construct the 'missing link' road. The state government has now built that missing link road. When issues arose with it, I was targeted on social media, even though the project was executed by the Maharashtra government," Gadkari said. What is the ‘missing link’ road? The Mumbai-Pune Expressway Missing Link opened to traffic on May 1. It is a 13-km bypass that cuts through the Sahyadri mountains, features two twin tunnels and a cable-stayed bridge. The road bypasses the winding Lonavala-Khandala ghat section and is designed to reduce the travel distance by 5.7 km and cut journey time between Mumbai and Pune by 20 to 30 minutes. The road quality was called into question after a landslide triggered by incessant monsoon rains blocked the Pune-to-Mumbai carriageway, forcing authorities to close the route and divert traffic. The problem arose just nine weeks after the ₹6,695-crore project was inaugurated, triggering sharp criticism from the Opposition over the quality of construction. Drawing a comparison with the construction of the Konkan Railway, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis rejected criticism of the 'Missing Link' project and said the government would implement additional safety measures suggested by experts while asserting that the engineering achievement should not be judged by a single incident. headline: NDA-ruled Andhra Pradesh refuses to defend changes to trans rights law in SC; Uttarakhand says law beneficial
text: The NDA-ruled Andhra Pradesh government, in an affidavit in the Supreme Court, has refused to defend the Centre’s controversial 2026 amendments to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act. The court is presently hearing at least a dozen petitions challenging the law. The State, in the affidavit filed in August, told the court that it had no role in enacting the Act, and that the constitutional validity of the law is “primarily a matter for the Union of India”. The Union government had introduced amendments to the law earlier this year, removing provisions that guaranteed transgender people the right to their “self-perceived gender identity” and limiting the definition of a “transgender person” to physiological characteristics. The amendments triggered widespread protests across the country and led members of the government’s National Council for Transgender Persons to resign over the changes, even as Parliament passed the Bill and the government notified it. ‘No discrimination’ With the Union government yet to respond to the challenges to the law in the Supreme Court, the Andhra Pradesh government, ruled by the Telugu Desam Party, a BJP ally, has told the top court that it has “not taken any independent action that is discriminatory towards transgender persons”. Interestingly, while the Bill was being discussed in the Lok Sabha on March 24, Telugu Desam Party MP Byreddy Shabari was among the MPs of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) who had supported it, by raising purported complaints that people were falsely adopting a transgender identity for begging at traffic signals. In its affidavit, the Andhra Pradesh government also provided data on the number of transgender persons certified across the State, showing that of the total 3,750 applications for transgender identity cards, 3,233 had been issued certificates, 403 had been “filtered”, and 114 applications were pending. The State further asserted that it “remains committed to safeguarding the constitutional rights, dignity, equality, and welfare of transgender persons, and undertakes to faithfully comply with any directions or orders” that the court may issue. Uttarakhand in favour On the other hand, the BJP-ruled government in Uttarakhand has defended the 2026 amendments to the law, saying that matters related to rights and healthcare needs of transgender people are "influenced by social norms and existing systems”, in addition to government regulations. headline: PoK would be protesting today to join J&K if Article 370 hadn't been revoked: Omar Abdullah
text: SRINAGAR: Recalling the 1947 National Conference (NC) slogan, “Hamalawar Khabardar, Ham Kashmiri Hain Tayyar (Attackers beware, we Kashmiris are ready),” Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday praised his grandfather and NC founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah for fighting the tribal invasion of 1947, saying Kashmiris fought the invaders even before Indian soldiers landed in Kashmir. Omar also called for strengthening federalism in the country and questioned the establishment of national-level examination systems such as NEET and JEE, saying they had eroded the autonomy of states. He went on to say that had the central government not revoked Article 370 on August 5, 2019, people in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir would have been protesting to join J&K today. “When we talk about the independence of the country, when we talk about August 15 in Jammu and Kashmir, then this occasion will be incomplete without paying tribute to the biggest leader of Jammu and Kashmir, the most respected person, Baba-e-Qaum Janab Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah,” Omar said. “Before the Indian Army reached here, it was the people of Jammu and Kashmir who fought the tribal invaders, who fought the infiltrators sent from across, who fought the soldiers sent from across. The slogan ‘Hamalawar Khabardar, Ham Kashmiri Hain Tayyar’ kept echoing in every city, every village, every street and every house. Those who had weapons used them. Those who did not have weapons showed fake guns and fought the intruders. In thousands, brave people sacrificed their lives,” Omar said. In doing so, the chief minister sought to reiterate the stature of Sheikh Abdullah, whose legacy has come under attack, particularly from the Bharatiya Janata Party, following the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019. In January 2020, five months after the abrogation of Article 370, the Lieutenant Governor’s administration removed Martyrs’ Day, observed on July 13, and the birth anniversary of Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, observed on December 5, from the list of public holidays. headline: FDA suspends 14 licenses of e-commerce platforms during raids across Maharashtra - Bilkul Online
text: Mumbai Intensifying its crackdown on food safety violations, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Friday conducted a statewide inspection drive and suspended 14 licenses, including of quick-commerce and online food delivery establishments, officials said. According to an official statement, a total of 86 establishments were raided, including those selling food through online platforms such as Blinkit, Zepto, and Instamart. Authorities seized 698 kg of dairy products and 1,270 kg of other food items during the searches. Ten First Information Reports (FIRs) were filed over banned pan masala and gutkha, with nine arrests, officials said. Overall, 15 raids were conducted, resulting in seizures worth Rs 46.89 lakh. The Food and Drug Administration carried out major action against milk and dairy products. Total seized dairy stock stood at 698 kg, approximately valued at Rs 34,302. Ten FIRs were registered in cases involving the sale, distribution and transportation of banned food items such as pan masala and gutkha. In these cases, 9 persons were arrested and stock worth a total of Rs 46,76,631 was seized. Authorities said approximately 1,270 kg of other food items (milk and dairy products, bakery items, edible oil, etc.) worth around Rs 1,29,762 were seized. A total of 109 hotels, restaurants, dhabas, etc. were inspected, with 49 establishments issued improvement notices and 4 food establishment licenses suspended. Earlier, the Maharashtra government imposed a complete ban on the manufacture, sale, storage, transportation, distribution, and processing of analogue paneer (artificial or non-dairy cottage cheese) across the state. With this decision, Maharashtra becomes the second state in the country, after Chhattisgarh, to prohibit the product. According to an order issued by Food Safety Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe on July 30, the ban came into immediate effect. It covers the manufacture, processing, packing, storage, transportation, wholesale and retail sale, as well as the offering for sale of analogue or non-dairy cheese throughout the state. The FDA has clarified that any individual or establishment selling analogue paneer while misrepresenting it as genuine dairy cheese will be deemed to have misled consumers and engaged in unfair trade practices under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Authorities have warned that strict legal action will be taken against violators.

headline: Delhi court sends AAP's Satyendar Jain to judicial custody
text: New Delhi, Aug 19 : A Delhi court on Wednesday sent Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader and former Delhi Minister Satyendar Jain to judicial custody in a case pertaining to alleged irregularities in the Delhi Jal Board (DJB). Jain and former Delhi Jal Board (DJB) CEO Udit Prakash Rai, an IAS officer, were among six people arrested by the Delhi government's Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) on Tuesday in connection with an alleged corruption and tender-manipulation case involving the augmentation and upgradation of sewage treatment plants (STPs) of the Delhi Jal Board. The other four accused arrested in the case are Ankit Srivastava, a former contractual consultant with the DJB; Nagendra Yadav, proprietor of M/s AN Enterprises; Raja Kumar Kurra, owner of M/s Euroteck Environment Private Limited; and Pankaj Verma, proprietor of M/s Srijanhar. Special judge Dig Vinay Singh of Rouse Avenue Courts passed the order after the accused were presented in the court. Though Jain's application seeking to declare his arrest as illegal was rejected by the judge, the court will hear the AAP leader's bail plea on August 25. Another accused arrested in the case, Ankit Srivastava, has been sent to two days' custody of the Anti-Corruption Branch. The remaining accused have also been sent to judicial custody. The arrests were made in connection with an FIR registered on May 11, 2024, at the ACB police station on a complaint from the Delhi government's Directorate of Vigilance. The FIR invokes Sections 7, 7A, 9 and 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, as amended in 2018, along with Sections 420, 409, 418 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code. According to the ACB, the case concerns alleged large-scale irregularities, manipulation of tender conditions and criminal conspiracy in the tendering process for DJB's STP projects. During the investigation, the ACB allegedly found that the tendering process contained restrictive technical specifications and conditions favouring a particular technology provider, M/s Euroteck Environment Private Limited.

headline: Satya Niketan building collapse: Delhi CM orders magisterial inquiry, FIR against owner
text: ANI 07 Sep 2026, 01:27 GMT+10 New Delhi [India], September 7 (ANI): The Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the collapse of a building in Satya Niketan and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the Chief Minister's Office said on Saturday. According to Garg, the building that collapsed was originally a ground-plus-one structure but was later converted into a three- or four-floor building. headline: Delhi building collapse: Death toll climbs to 6; search, rescue Ops on
text: New Delhi, Sep 7 : Six people have died, and 11 have been rescued while several others are feared trapped after the deadly multi-storey building collapse in Delhi's Satya Niketan, officials said. According to the rescue officials, during the overnight operations, one more person was rescued but was found dead. The search and rescue operations continued throughout the night. Officials said that several people, mostly students, are still feared to be trapped in the debris, and efforts are underway to rescue them safely. Earlier on Sunday, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered a magisterial inquiry into the collapse of the boys' PG building. Following an on-site inspection of the tragedy, Gupta directed officials to conduct a detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the building collapse and ordered that an FIR be registered against the building owner. The Chief Minister said those found responsible would face strict action under the law. "Those found responsible for this grave incident will be held fully accountable and dealt with under the strictest provisions of law," Gupta said after reviewing the situation at the spot. According to police, the FIR has been registered at the South Campus police station against alleged owner Hariram and others. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel confirmed the registration of the case. The building, which was around 40-50 years old, had a basement and five upper floors and was being used as a paying guest accommodation for students, many of whom were studying at Delhi Universityâ€™s South Campus. Police said the premises had rooms to accommodate around 40 people. The collapse occurred at around 1.30 p.m. while repair work was reportedly underway in the basement. Officials also indicated that heavy rains may have contributed to the incident. Rescue operations involve teams from Delhi Police, the National Disaster Response Force, Delhi Fire Service and the Delhi Disaster Management Authority. Further details are awaited.

headline: SATYA NIKETAN COLLAPSE | Delhi to Mandate Structural Audits for PGs, Schools and Nursing Homes
text: SATYA NIKETAN COLLAPSE | Delhi to Mandate Structural Audits for PGs, Schools and Nursing Homes The Delhi government will introduce mandatory structural audits and periodic safety certification for buildings operating as paying guest accommodation, schools, nursing homes and other public-use facilities, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on Monday. Buildings that fail to secure the required safety clearance will not be allowed to continue such activities. The announcement follows the collapse of a five-storey boys’ PG in Satya Niketan near Delhi University’s South Campus, which killed six people and left several others injured. “The government, in collaboration with the Municipal Corporation, is formulating a policy mandating that any building intended for public use, whether a PG, nursing home, school or any other facility, must undergo periodic structural audits and safety certification,” Gupta said after revisiting the collapse site. Without certification, she said, “no public activity will be permitted there”. The proposed policy could significantly widen Delhi’s building-safety regime by linking permission to operate a public-facing establishment with evidence that the structure remains fit for occupation. Its effectiveness, however, will depend on who conducts the audits, how frequently certification must be renewed and whether the results are independently verified. Unsafe PGs to Be Shut, Evacuated Students Shifted Gupta said the government would not allow students to remain in unsafe PG accommodation. Students evacuated from buildings around the collapse site are being temporarily housed in college hostels. The administration is also contacting the families of those affected and arranging assistance for them, she said. The chief minister promised action against officials whose negligence or failure of oversight contributed to the conditions surrounding the disaster. “No one will be spared,” she said, adding that action would be taken against any government employee found responsible. The Delhi government has already ordered a magisterial inquiry into the collapse, while police have registered an FIR against the building owner. The inquiry is expected to examine the legality of the structure, its conversion into a high-occupancy PG and the nature of the work reportedly being undertaken before it fell. headline: MPSC Drug Inspector exam case: Seventh arrest in Nandurbar
text: The Mumbai Crime Branch arrested Rutuja Patil on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) from her residence in Nandurbar, taking the total number of arrests in the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) Drug Inspector examination paper leak case to seven. The investigation has expanded to examine property purchases made by one of the accused and possible links to other recruitment processes. Police took her for a medical examination and then transported her to Mumbai. The Crime Branch team visited Nandurbar three times over a period of six days for the investigation. Of the seven people arrested so far, three are officers associated with MPSC. The remaining accused are residents of Nandurbar district. Police obtained a document containing mobile phone messages exchanged between Ms. Rutuja Patil and Gaurav Patil. This document provided a line of inquiry for the investigation. Ms. Rutuja Patil had secured a position on the merit list of the examination. Gaurav Patil did not pass the examination. Mr. Gaurav Patil filed a complaint with MPSC regarding the paper leak after his relationship with Ms. Rutuja Patil deteriorated. Investigation records indicate that Ms. Gaurav Patil changed his statement during the process. Police proceeded with the investigation on the basis of the available evidence and the digital communication document. Gopal Marathe, an employee of MPSC, is a resident of Dahindule village in Nandurbar taluka. He is a student of Kautilya Academy. Investigators are examining whether similar examination papers or confidential information had been leaked earlier. They are also looking into whether other recruitment processes faced interference of this nature. Information available with the investigation team states that Gopal Marathe purchased properties in recent months. Investigators are examining whether these property transactions have a financial connection to the paper leak case. They are also checking whether money from the irregularity was used for these property purchases. The investigation team initially questioned Praveen Patil, the director of Kautilya Academy. Two days ago, the team arrived in Nandurbar at midnight with Amrut Patil and Ms. Rutuja Patil for questioning. The Mumbai Crime Branch team continues to conduct the investigation in Nandurbar. The team has not provided official information on the direction of the inquiry, the persons being questioned, or the evidence collected. Nandurbar has emerged as a location of repeated focus due to the case’s connections to the district. Published - September 02, 2026 07:13 pm IST

headline: Bihar Minister Santosh Suman demands renaming Bakhtiyarpur as ‘Nitishpur’
text: Bihar Minister and National President of Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) Santosh Kumar Suman on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) demanded that the name of Bakhtiyarpur be changed to Nitishpur in honour of former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. He has urged Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary to rename the town, which is also the birthplace of Mr. Kumar. Writing a post on his social media account X, Mr. Suman said, “Let the birthplace of Bihar’s great mass leader bear his name—Bakhtiyarpur becomes ‘Nitishpur’.” Son of Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi further said, “Bakhtiyarpur is not merely a geographical identity. headline: Delhi horror: Woman stabbed to death by husband at hotel, accused attempts suicide
text: NEW DELHI: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly stabbed to death by her husband at a hotel in Delhi’s Lahori Gate area, following a family dispute, police said. The man later allegedly consumed poison in an apparent suicide attempt and remains under treatment at a hospital. The couple had been married for around six months. The woman, a native of Bihar, worked at a beauty parlour in Delhi, while her husband, from Rajasthan, ran a tea stall there. The husband had come to Delhi on Wednesday and met his wife at Hotel Prince, where the couple checked in at around 3.30pm, police said. According to investigators, the man allegedly stabbed his wife three times during the night following a family dispute. He then allegedly consumed a poisonous substance. Hotel staff alerted police on Thursday morning after finding the woman lying in a pool of blood inside the room. According to a police statement, Lahori Gate Police Station received information on Thursday morning about a man and a woman found unconscious at Hotel Prince. "A police team immediately reached the spot, where a woman was found lying unconscious with multiple stab injuries. A man was also found unconscious at the same location," police said. Both were taken to a nearby hospital. The woman was declared brought dead, while the man remains under treatment, police said. The woman's body has been sent for post-mortem examination.

headline: Calcutta HC sets aside fire dept order to vacate two floors of building housing Abhishek Banerjee's office
text: The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday set aside the West Bengal Fire Services Department’s order directing the vacating of two floors of a high-rise building on Kolkata's Camac Street that houses TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee's office. The court directed the department to reconsider the reply submitted by the Trinamool Congress on September 3, and inspect the premises again after issuing notice to the petitioner. Justice Krishna Rao set aside the department's September 4 order to vacate the sixth and seventh floors of the building in the upmarket south Kolkata locality, which houses the office of the TMC MP. The court directed that if further shortcomings in fire safety measures on the two floors are found during the inspection, the authorities will inform the TMC to take corrective action. Justice Rao directed that the department will be at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law if the petitioner fails to implement fire safety measures even after issuance of such notice. The high court had on September 11 directed the Fire Services Department not to implement its order to vacate the two floors of the high-rise building until it passed a final order. During the arguments challenging the department's order, the TMC's lawyer stated that they were served with a notice on September 4 to vacate the two floors on the ground that the fire safety certificate had expired. Opposing the petition, the state’s Advocate General Surojit Nath Mitra had argued before the court that several fire safety parametres were flouted on the sixth and seventh floors, and that a number of LPG gas cylinders were stocked on one of these floors. Earlier in August, authorities removed an "illegal" billboard of the TMC from the same building, during which private guards at Banerjee's office, his supporters and some party leaders scuffled with the police and Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) officials. text: Mumbai: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday gave his first reaction to the Bombay High Court's order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register an FIR and probe the death of Disha Salian. Speaking to reporters, Fadnavis said, “Mumbai Police had completed its investigation and submitted its report. However, perhaps the High Court felt that further investigation was required or that there were some technical shortcomings. Therefore, the case was handed over to the CBI.” CM Fadnavis further added that there was not much more he could comment on the matter at this stage. According to reports, a bench headed by Justice Sarang Kotwal passed the order while hearing a petition filed by Disha's father, Satish Salian, seeking an independent investigation into his daughter's death. headline: Indian airline launches direct Mumbai–Hà Nội route
text: | Vietnamese Ambassador to India Trịnh Minh Mạnh (middle) and Vietnamese Consul General in Mumbai Lê Quang Biên (fourth from left) at the flight route inauguration ceremony. — Photo courtesy of the Vietnamese Embassy in India | NEW DELHI — Indian airline Akasa Air on September 4 officially launched a direct route between Mumbai and Hà Nội, marking its first expansion into Việt Nam. The new route operates four flights a week and is the first direct Mumbai–Hà Nội service operated by an Indian airline. Hà Nội has become Akasa Air’s seventh international destination and its second destination in Southeast Asia, after Phuket, Thailand. The launch ceremony at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport in Mumbai was attended by Vietnamese Ambassador to India Trịnh Minh Mạnh and Consul General of Việt Nam in Mumbai Lê Quang Biên, along with Akasa Air Co-founder and Chief Commercial Officer Anand Srinivasan and Co-founder and Senior Vice President for Strategy Bhavin Joshi. Addressing the ceremony, Mạnh said the direct route between Mumbai and Hà Nội would not only provide a convenient transport link between the two major cities but also open up new opportunities for cooperation in tourism, trade, investment and people-to-people exchanges between Việt Nam and India. Mumbai is one of India’s most important financial, commercial and economic centres, while Hà Nội is Việt Nam’s capital and a major political, economic and cultural centre, he said. The direct connection between the two cities is expected to help deepen bilateral economic cooperation while creating more favourable conditions for businesses from both sides to expand their operations and seek investment and business opportunities, the ambassador added. The Embassy of Việt Nam in India said it had coordinated with relevant authorities and partners to support Akasa Air during preparations for the new route. It will continue working with the airline to enhance connectivity and strengthen Việt Nam-India cooperation, the embassy said. The inaugural flight, QP625, departed Mumbai at 5:35 am on September 4 and landed at Nội Bài International Airport in Hà Nội at noon the same day, local time. The return flight, QP626, departed Hà Nội at 1:30 pm. The route is operated by Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft, with a flight time of about five hours. headline: Mithun Chakraborty announces 30 pc subsidy for film productions shooting in Bengal
text: Kolkata, Sep 4 : After the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal named actor and party leader Mithun Chakraborty as its cultural advisor on Friday, the latter announced 30 per cent subsidy for film productions shooting in the state. A day before, during a programme to mark the birth centenary of Bengali legend Uttam Kumar, the actor-turned-politician had said that he had made a "special request" for the subsidy to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, to which the latter had agreed. Speaking to reporters after the BJP government announced his new role, Chakraborty said: "We will try to bring back whatever we have lost. We are giving 30 per cent subsidy so that we can bring everyone, the whole of India, to Bengal. We are asking people to come to Bengal and shoot here." When asked about former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's threat to stage protest outside BJP leaders' houses in Delhi, The actor-turned-politician retorted: "Whatever she (Mamata Banerjee) is saying, does it suit her? The 'atrocities' that she had mentioned, does it suit her?.. We are the ones who have endured all this. I do not insult anyone by speaking too much, but all this does not look good coming from her." Following the alleged attack on Trinamool Congress General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee's party office, the former Chief Minister had accused the BJP of sending goons and spoke about her plans to take the protests in the matter to the national capital. "How long will you 9Mamata Banerjee) continue with your atrocities? If the atrocities are not stopped, I will be personally going to New Delhi and stage protest demonstrations in front of the houses of the BJP leaders there," the former Chief Minister had said in a Facebook Live video. Meanwhile, Chief Minister Adhikari made the announcement of Mithun Chakraborty's new role while attending the foundation stone laying ceremony of "Uttam Kumar Film Centre" at New Town in the northern outskirts of Kolkata, earlier on Friday. The centre will be developed over a cost of Rs 25 crore, which the State Information and Cultural Affairs Department had already sanctioned. Speaking on the occasion, the Chief Minister said that work of finalising the design of the centre will be left to the experts from the Bengali silver-screen world and the state government under no circumstance will interfere in the matter.

headline: Mumbai: Former Mayor Vishakha Raut Disqualified As Corporator For 6 Years Over OBC Certificate Issue
text: Mumbai, September 5, 2026: The Maharashtra Government has barred senior Shiv Sena (UBT) corporator and former Mumbai Mayor Vishakha Raut from contesting or holding the post of corporator for six years, in a major setback for the veteran leader. For the Thackeray camp, however, the move goes beyond a legal blow—it has turned into a prestige battle over retaining its grip on a key Shiv Sena stronghold. The Palghar Caste Certificate Scrutiny Committee cancelled her OBC certificate on August 21, citing the wrong jurisdiction, following which the Urban Development Department issued her disqualification order through a GR dated September 1. The civic house is likely to formally announce the disqualification on Monday. Disqualification Order Issued The GR states that Raut’s disqualification under Section 16 of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act has rendered her seat as a councillor vacant. Exercising its powers under the same provision, the Maharashtra Government has disqualified her from being elected or serving as a councillor for six years, effective from August 20, 2026. Raut’s Narrow Dadar Victory Raut represents the politically prized Dadar–Shivaji Park belt, where she retained Shiv Sena (UBT)’s OBC-reserved Ward 191 in one of the BMC election’s closest fights. She polled 13,236 votes to defeat Priya Sarvankar, daughter of Shiv Sena (Shinde) former MLA Sada Sarvankar, by a razor-thin 197 votes. With only two candidates in the fray, the contest was a straight political face-off, making Raut’s narrow victory particularly significant. Fifth Opposition Corporator Disqualified Raut is the fifth Opposition corporator to lose her seat over a caste certificate issue. However, hers is the first case in which the Urban Development Department has issued a direct disqualification order. Several of them have challenged their disqualification in court. headline: No state should interfere in another's affairs: K'taka CM hits back at TN CM over remarks on deaths in Chamarajanagar reserve forest
text: Bengaluru, Aug 18 : Karnataka Chief Minister, D.K. Shivakumar, on Tuesday hit out at Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. text: 31 years of Jaswant Singh Khalra’s kidnapping: Why it took ‘Satluj’ to carry his story to the masses #WebSpecial: Amid row over "Satluj", Khalra's wife appealed to Akal Takht Jathedar to set up people’s commission to establish true scale of disappearances and fake encounters in Punjab It has been 31 years since human rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra, who exposed fake encounters and secret cremations in Punjab, was kidnapped outside his home in Amritsar’s Kabir Park and disappeared forever. On the morning of September 6, 1995, a Maruti Omni van pulled up outside Khalra’s house as he was washing his car. A team of policemen bundled him into the vehicle in full view of an eyewitness, Rajiv Singh, a Punjabi Tribune journalist who had come to accompany Khalra to the cremation grounds in Patti with a group of journalists from Delhi. Khalra was never seen alive again. He was tortured in custody for weeks and killed in late October 1995. His body was disposed of in the Harike river and was never recovered. Born in 1952 in Khalra village in Tarn Taran district, on the India-Pakistan border, Jaswant was the youngest of four brothers and five sisters. His family had already spent two generations fighting power before he took up his own cause. Khalra village traces its origins to 1714, when Sikh settlers who were part of the peasant militia raised by Banda Singh Bahadur established the settlement. The family’s ancestor, Sardar Surat Singh, led that founding group, and a monument to him still stands in the village. Jaswant’s grandfather, Harnam Singh, left for Shanghai before World War I in search of work and joined Indian revolutionaries linked to the Ghadar movement. The British arrested him in 1915 and put him on trial. He was acquitted, but the government kept him confined to his own village until 1922. It was during this period, in 1917, that his son Kartar Singh, Jaswant’s father, was born. Harnam went back to Shanghai after his release and never returned to India, so Kartar grew up without a father. Despite the family living on a modest teacher’s income, Kartar insisted all his children get an education. It was against this background that Jaswant grew up to become a banker before turning to human rights work. headline: Modi’s restricted media landscape | The Express Tribune
text: In the summer of 2020, Supriya Sharma was working from home when a fellow journalist called and asked her a question she had not been expecting. “Is there an FIR against you?” Yes, there was. The police complaint accused Sharma, executive editor of Scroll, of misrepresenting the words of a woman from a marginalised community and making a false claim about her experience during the Covid lockdown. From the onset, Sharma knew the allegation was false. She had a recording of the interview that showed she had quoted the woman accurately. Still, an FIR meant the possibility of arrest. Her editor, Naresh Fernandes, called and suggested she leave her house in case the police were on their way. When Sharma refused, a lawyer involved in the case called her. “Why make it easy for them? At least let them look for you,” she told her. So, before dawn, Sharma left home. She did not know when she would be able to return. In the meantime, she began thinking about what she would need if she ended up in prison: a toothbrush, sanitary napkins, and books. She would spend the next two months living with the possibility of arrest before her lawyers secured protection from it. The case eventually became, in Sharma’s telling, a relatively minor inconvenience. She did not go to prison. But the fact that she had started packing for one stayed with her. At the Oslo Freedom Forum, organised by the Human Rights Foundation, this year, Sharma used the episode to explain what it means to be an independent journalist in Narendra Modi’s India. The problem, she suggested, is not only that journalists can face arrest or legal action, but that after years of watching colleagues and activists go through it, the possibility begins to enter the ordinary calculations of newsroom life. Sharma had evidence that her reporting was accurate, but that did not prevent a police case from being registered against her. For other journalists, the consequences have been much more serious. headline: Congress leader Chenthi Anil arrested for blocking Kerala CM's convoy
text: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM: Congress leader Chenthi Anil has been arrested for allegedly blocking the convoy of Kerala chief minister VD Satheesan in Thiruvananthapuram, news agency PTI reported. The incident occurred on Friday evening when Satheesan was on his way to attend a programme held to mark the birth anniversary of social reformer Sree Narayana Guru. headline: Karnataka Forms SIT to Reinvestigate 2012 Rape and Murder Case
text: Bengaluru, September 24 (Udaipur Kiran) : The Karnataka government has announced the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to conduct a fresh inquiry into the 2012 rape and murder case of Soujanya, registered at the Belthangady police station. This move comes in response to directives from the Supreme Court. IPS officer N. Shashikumar has been appointed as the head of the SIT, which also includes members CK Sudhir Kumar Reddy, Nikhila James, Lokesh Jagalasar, and Venkatesh Prasanna. According to government orders, the SIT is tasked with completing the investigation within three months and submitting its report to the relevant court. The case dates back to October 2012 when 17-year-old Soujanya, a second-year pre-university student at SDM College in Ujire, went missing while returning home from college in Belthangady taluk of Mangaluru district. Her family filed a missing person report at the Belthangady police station on October 9, 2012. The following day, her body was discovered in bushes near Mannasanka, leading to charges of rape and murder being added to the case. Initially, the Belthangady police investigated the matter, which was later handed over to the Karnataka CID and subsequently to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). The police arrested Santosh Rao as the sole accused in the case and proceeded with the trial against him. However, in June 2023, a special CBI court acquitted Rao, stating that the prosecution failed to provide sufficient evidence to support the charges. The CBI has since challenged this verdict in the Karnataka High Court. On September 21, 2026, the Supreme Court ordered a complete reinvestigation of the case, directing the Karnataka government to establish the SIT while also stating that no officers involved in the previous investigations should be included in the new team. headline: Kanimozhi meets Mamata Banerjee as DMK works on third front
text: CHENNAI: DMK has started working on the formation of a prospective third front by trying to wean away some of the INDIA bloc constituents. DMK deputy general secretary and MP Kanimozhi Rajathi Karunanidhi met Trinamool Congress chief and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee at her Kalighat residence in Kolkata on Thursday. This came after Kanimozhi’s meetings with Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackerey and NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule in Mumbai on Sept 12. DMK broke all ties with Congress since the latter walked out of its alliance to join the TVK-led govt in Tamil Nadu in May. A DMK leader said Kanimozhi has been tasked with reaching out to opposition leaders. “We are exploring the possibility of a third front without Congress,” the leader said. Kanimozhi’s discussions with these leaders have predominantly been on the proposed delimitation, though the broader idea is to bring them on board. Mamata has been particularly unhappy with Congress after the latter rejected her seat-sharing offer for the Oct 6 Nandigram and Rejinagar byelections. A senior Trinamool MP said, “Mamata Banerjee shares an excellent relationship with DMK chief M K Stalin. She also maintains very good ties with non-NDA parties and remains close to INDIA bloc members that are not allied with Congress. Today’s discussion was strictly between her and Kanimozhi. Anything said beyond that would be speculation.” NCP (SP) sources said the party leadership remains non-committal to DMK’s proposal. “DMK floated the idea of a third front, and a preliminary meeting was held. DMK is testing the waters with opposition parties with which it has a good equation, unlike Congress,” a senior NCP leader said. Meanwhile, chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Sept 9 named the TVK-led combine as Secular Social Justice Victory Alliance (SSJVA), which includes erstwhile DMK allies Congress, VCK and IUML. headline: ‘Responsibility not solely with owner, but also MCD, DU... ’: HC orders MCD inquiry in Satya Niketan collapse
text: ‘Responsibility not solely with owner, but also MCD, DU... ’: HC orders MCD inquiry in Satya Niketan collapse The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to conduct an inquiry at the highest executive level into the Satya Niketan building collapse, asking it to determine whether the structure had been constructed with valid permissions and fix responsibility on officials if lapses were found The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to conduct an inquiry at the highest executive level into the Satya Niketan building collapse, asking it to determine whether the structure had been constructed with valid permissions and fix responsibility on officials if lapses were found. A bench of chief justice DK Upadhyaya and justice Tejas Karia said the incident was “unfortunate” and prima facie suggested that responsibility for such mishaps did not lie solely with the owner of the paying guest (PG) accommodation, but also with MCD and university authorities responsible for ensuring compliance with building bye-laws and other regulations. “Had the authorities been alive to the responsibilities and duties casted on them statutorily, such incidents could have been avoided,” the bench said. The court directed MCD to ascertain whether the collapsed building had been constructed pursuant to valid and requisite permissions and, if not, identify the officers or employees responsible for the lapse. Its response must also specify what action had been proposed or taken against officials found responsible. “The reported incident is not only unfortunate but it evokes deep concern about inadequate housing facilities in the form of hostel run by the Delhi University/ Delhi government, safety and security of the students and the not-so-adequate measures deployed by MCD and other authorities to regulate such PG hostels,” the bench held. “Seven of them have died … majority of them may still be lying under the debris. text: Chamarajanagar: Protests were held in Chamarajanagar and Mysuru on Sunday seeking justice for three men who were killed in an alleged exchange of fire with Forest Department personnel on August 15. The protesters blocked the road to Male Mahadeshwara Betta and demanded action against the forest personnel involved in the shooting. headline: Delhi Bus Safety Rules: GPS, Panic Buttons Mandatory After Greater Noida Sexual Assault Case
text: The Delhi government has reiterated strict safety norms for buses operating in the national capital following the alleged sexual assault of a 16-year-old girl on a moving bus between Greater Noida and Delhi. The Transport Department has directed bus operators to ensure that essential safety measures, including functional GPS tracking devices and panic buttons, are in place. The State Transport Authority (STA), in an order issued on August 31, directed all bus operators, including those from other states operating in Delhi, to comply with passenger safety and operational requirements. GPS tracking, panic buttons mandatory Under the directions, buses must have functional Vehicle Location Tracking Devices (VLTDs) and accessible panic buttons. Operators have also been asked to ensure that buses have adequate internal lighting while they are in motion so that activities inside can be visible from outside. The government has also reiterated the ban on curtains and window films that obstruct visibility inside buses. Buses must also be parked only at authorised, secure and adequately lit locations, particularly during night hours or when they are not in operation. No unauthorised stops The order also prohibits buses from stopping at unsafe or unauthorised locations, particularly in the middle of roads or at intersections. Passenger boarding and alighting must take place only at designated bus stops or other authorised locations. Drivers and other bus staff have been directed to maintain proper conduct and carry valid licences and badges wherever applicable. Operators must also verify the credentials of drivers, conductors and other staff before deploying them. Bus crews told to act against harassment The directions also put emphasis on the responsibility of bus staff when it comes to the safety of women passengers. Drivers, conductors and other crew members are to be sensitised about preventing harassment and the consequences of misconduct against women passengers. In cases involving molestation, eve-teasing or other offences against women, crews have been instructed to immediately inform the police and take the bus to the nearest police station, police post or PCR van. Violations could lead to vehicle impounding, permit cancellation The Transport Department has warned that violations of the prescribed safety norms could result in penalties, detention or impounding of buses, and suspension or cancellation of permits. Operators have also been asked to circulate the directions among their drivers and staff. Delhi has around 450 registered private bus operators, according to officials cited by Hindustan Times. headline: CM Rekha Gupta orders magisterial inquiry into Satya Niketan building collapse
text: New Delhi, Sep 6 : Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Sunday ordered a magisterial inquiry into the collapse of a boys' PG building in South Delhi's Satya Niketan that left at least five people dead and 11 others injured. Following an on-site inspection of the tragedy, Gupta directed officials to conduct a detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the building collapse and ordered that an FIR be registered against the building owner. The Chief Minister said those found responsible would face strict action under the law. "Those found responsible for this grave incident will be held fully accountable and dealt with under the strictest provisions of law," Gupta said after reviewing the situation at the spot. The Chief Minister, along with Lieutenant Governor T.S. Sandhu and Mayor Pravesh Wahi, visited the site and monitored the rescue operations. She also visited AIIMS and met victims receiving treatment, enquiring about their condition and the medical care being provided to them. According to police, the FIR has been registered at the South Campus police station against alleged owner Hariram and others. Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel confirmed the registration of the case. The building, which was around 40-50 years old, had a basement and five upper floors and was being used as a paying guest accommodation for students, many of whom were studying at Delhi University's South Campus. Police said the premises had rooms to accommodate around 40 people. The collapse occurred at around 1.30 p.m. while repair work was reportedly underway in the basement. Officials also indicated that heavy rains may have contributed to the incident. Rescue operations involved teams from Delhi Police, the National Disaster Response Force, Delhi Fire Service and the Delhi Disaster Management Authority. Eleven people trapped in the debris were rescued using gas cutters and JCB machines. An AIIMS statement said 10 patients were brought to the JPN Apex Trauma Centre, including four who were declared dead on arrival. One critically injured patient later succumbed to injuries, taking the death toll to five. CM Rekha Gupta said the government would ensure accountability and that anyone found responsible would face the strictest legal action.

headline: Anbumani Ramadoss demands CBI probe into killing of 3 Tamils by K'taka forest personnel - Mangalorean.com
text: Anbumani Ramadoss demands CBI probe into killing of 3 Tamils by K’taka forest personnel Chennai: PMK leader Anbumani Ramadoss has demanded a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the fatal shooting of three Tamil men by Karnataka Forest Department personnel near the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary in Chamarajanagar district. In a statement, Anbumani condemned the incident and alleged that the three men had been killed on the false accusation that they were involved in poaching. He conveyed his condolences to their families. The deceased were identified as Anthonysamy, John Rose Peter and Kumar, residents of Jagannathothi, Mariyamangalam and Lasardothi villages, respectively. Anbumani claimed that forest guards attached to the Kollegal forest division opened fire on them despite their not being involved in any illegal activity. The Karnataka Forest Department reportedly maintained that the men had entered the forest to hunt deer and were killed during an exchange of fire. However, the families of the deceased have rejected this version and accused officials of fabricating an encounter narrative to conceal the killings. According to Anbumani, the victims belonged to Tamil families that migrated to the Mariyamangalam region of Chamarajanagar district after losing their homes and properties during land acquisition for the construction of the Mettur dam nearly a century ago. The families subsequently settled in Karnataka in search of a livelihood. He said there was no evidence to establish that deer hunting had taken place in the Mariyamangalam forest area or that an armed confrontation had occurred between the men and forest officials. He also disputed the Forest Department’s claim that the victims were carrying firearms. The killings have triggered protests among Tamil residents in the area, leading to tension. Local political representatives, including Congress MLA and district in-charge minister Puttaranga Shetty and JD(S) legislator Manjunath, have reportedly questioned why the operation was conducted in the early hours. Human rights activists have also condemned the Forest Department’s action. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has ordered a magisterial inquiry following conflicting accounts of the incident. Anbumani, however, said such an inquiry would not uncover the full truth and insisted that the case be handed over to the CBI. He urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to condemn the Karnataka government and press for compensation of Rs 1 crore each for the families of the three deceased men.

headline: India police clash with protesters a month after Gen Z demonstrations
text: Indian students and unemployed youth have clashed with police as they marched towards the residence of the chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar, ruled by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s party, demanding access to jobs and transparency in recruitment exams. The government forces in Bihar used water cannons and lathis – the Indian version of batons – as a few thousand protesters broke through security barricades in the state capital Patna, videos seen by Al Jazeera showed on Tuesday. The protests began last week with unemployed youth demanding jobs, but they later expanded to include calls for education reform. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary said his office was “listening to every student’s voice”. A delegation of student representatives met Bihar’s top bureaucrat, Pratyaya Amrit, after the protests. headline: Russell Sinha: Breaking From Family Politics, Building His Own BJP Identity
text: KAMALPUR, DHALAI: In a family where politics was closely associated with the Communist movement, Russell Sinha’s decision to join the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) marked a significant break from tradition. Sinha, born on October 6, 1991, in Kamalpur, Dhalai, comes from a family with a long association with Tripura’s political life. Yet, instead of following the political path of his predecessors, he chose to build his career within the BJP, eventually taking up organisational, media and youth-related responsibilities. His political background is rooted in several generations. His great-grandfather, late Gana Singha, was a member of Tripura’s first 30-member Territorial Council, constituted in 1957. His uncle, late Bimal Singha, was a former Health and Family Welfare and Urban Development Minister of Tripura and was assassinated in 1998. His father, late Govinda Das Singha, popularly known as Biman Singha, was Bimal Singha’s elder brother and worked as a school teacher. The family’s political connections continued through his aunt, Bijoy Laxmi Sinha, wife of Bimal Singha, who was a sitting MLA from the Communist Party when Russell entered active BJP politics. On November 22, 2016, Russell formally joined the BJP as a karyakarta. He has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership and the Centre’s decision to implement demonetisation influenced his political choice. The decision represented more than a change of party for Russell. It placed him on a political course different from the one followed by his family for decades. Russell has also spoken about the personal difficulties that accompanied his political transition, including alleged death threats. The assassination of his uncles, he said, left a lasting impact on the family and influenced his views on political violence and political vendetta. From Kamalpur to Agartala Russell’s political career began to take shape under the guidance of then BJYM State President Tinku Roy, along with late Advocate Arun Kanti Bhowmik and Dr Ashok Sinha. In 2017, he moved from Kamalpur to Agartala and began working as a full-time BJP worker. His responsibilities soon expanded to the party’s media activities, and he served as Co-Coordinator of the BJP Media Cell under then Media In-charge Victor Shome. He later became involved in social media and content-related work for then State BJP President Biplab Kumar Deb. Russell remained associated with Deb until November 2018.
