headline: SC turns down ex-Delhi mayor Farhad Suri’s plea seeking FIR against UP cops over raid - The Tribune
text: SC turns down ex-Delhi mayor Farhad Suri’s plea seeking FIR against UP cops over raid A Bench led by CJI Surya Kant asks Suri to approach the Delhi Police for registration of an FIR, instead of directing moving the top court under Article 32 of the Constitution The Supreme Court on Tuesday turned down former Delhi Mayor Farhad Suri’s petition seeking registration of an FIR against Ghaziabad police officials for allegedly conducting an "illegal" raid at his residence in search of journalist Abhishek Upadhyay in connection with a criminal case. Upadhyay, who reported on Ayodhya Ram Temple donation ‘theft’, is an accused in a road rage case registered by the Ghaziabad police. A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant asked Suri to move the Delhi Police for registration of an FIR, instead of invoking Article 32 of the Constitution to directly approach the top court. "The relief regarding direction to register an FIR against police authorities of Uttar Pradesh can very well be addressed if the petitioner approaches a jurisdictional police station under Section 175 (3) of the BNSS (Bharatiya Nyaya Suraksha Sanhita). We have no reason to doubt that competent police (officials) will not strictly act in accordance with the law," said the bench – which also included Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana. Suri had alleged that on the intervening night of August 22 and 23, a large contingent of Ghaziabad police officials entered his Delhi residence without a warrant while searching for Upadhyay. The bench also refused to entertain Suri's counsel Anoop Prakash Awasthi’s request for issuing guidelines to govern inter-state police raids. The Uttar Pradesh government counsel vehemently opposed Suri’s plea, saying the petitioner could not have directly come to the top court under Article 32 for registration of an FIR without first exhausting the statutory remedies under the BNSS. "We were trying to arrest a gentleman (Upadhyay). There was a proper GD entry. Delhi police officers simply rang the bell of this person...to find out if the person was there. When he said no, we simply left. We did not even enter his house," the UP government counsel told the bench.

headline: Bihar govt. restricts CBI power; State nod mandatory to probe against its employees
text: The Bihar government has issued an order regarding actions taken by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) against State government officials. It will now be mandatory for the CBI to obtain prior permission from the State government before initiating any investigation, search, interrogation, arrest, or other action against any public servant posted under the Bihar government. The CBI will not be able to take any such step without prior permission. However, the notification issued by the Home Department on September 3, 2026 clearly stated that the CBI will not require permission from the State government to take action against Central Government employees. The two page Home Department notification issued by the Principal Secretary Pankaj Kumar reads, “In exercise of the powers conferred by section-6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, and in supersession of all previous notifications on this subject, the Governor of Bihar hereby accords consent to the extension of the powers and jurisdiction of the members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment throughout the State of Bihar for the investigation of offences or categories of offences notified under section 3 of the said act, as amended from time to time, and offences under The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 and The Information Technology Act, 2000 as well as cybercrime cases and Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (as amended time to time) allegedly committed by employees of the Government of India, Public Sector Undertakings, and private individuals under direct control of the Government of India.” It further said, “Provided that, in cases where the aforementioned offences involve public servants appointed in connection with the affairs of the Government of Bihar or persons appointed in connection with the affairs of any corporation, company or bank owned and controlled by the Government of Bihar or any institution receiving or having received financial assistance from the Government of Bihar, it shall be mandatory to obtain the prior consent of the Government of Bihar for the investigation of such offences by the members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment.” It added, “Furthermore, upon receipt of a proposal from the members of the Delhi Special Police Establishment, the State Government shall consider and decide on the matter of granting investigation powers on case-to-case basis in such cases.” The Home Department has sent a copy of the notification to the Ministry of Personnel,

headline: ‘Happens in US, Japan too’: Bihar minister's bizarre remark over Jamui, Samastipur incidents sparks row
text: PATNA: While incidents of crime of various kinds have been happening in the state with increasing frequency, food and consumer protection minister Ashok Choudhary on Thursday defended the government, saying criminal incidents are not specific to Bihar but happen even in developed countries like the US and Japan, and the government has not backed away from taking quick action. Over the last five months, the state has been scarred by encounter killings by police, murder of a couple of government officials in their offices, criminal incidents such as murder by anti-social elements, and molestation of girls by groups of hoodlums at Jamui, Darbhanga, Samastipur and Madhepura. These occurred in quick succession, with the Jamui incident first sending shock waves across the country, including Bihar. When asked by a reporter if the government had lost its ‘iqbal (authority, awe, prestige, commanding influence)’, Choudhary shot back, “Where in the world the criminal incidents don’t happen? It occurs even in the developed countries, like the US and Japan, and it is not specific just to Bihar. There is no head of a state who will say that crimes do not take place in his or her country, but the Bihar government administration has responded quickly to handle the situation in all cases. ” He was talking to reporters at the state JD(U) headquarters. “In the state, the government has not lost its ‘iqbal.’ Instead, the police responded quickly in 12 hours and arrested the criminals at Jamui and Samastipur. The government has not made any attempt to cover up any incident. The Samrat Choudhary government has been working on the tradition set by former CM Nitish Kumar, and the rule of law acts with the full force of a bulldozer.” “The Nitish Kumar government did not spare anyone belonging to his own party even. Whosoever be the person involved in the crime, the administration has always responded swiftly and will take action against anyone involved,” Choudhary also said. The minister said this when he was informed about five pistol shots being fired at Anil Yadav, the husband of a woman ward councillor of Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC), at his residence on Wednesday. “He lives in my locality, and what happened is unfortunate. I assure you no one will be spared,” he added.

headline: Maharashtra Drought Relief: Govt To Provide Immediate Aid To Farmers Under First Trigger Norms
text: Mumbai: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Thursday said the state government would issue an order Friday, 25, to provide immediate assistance to farmers affected by drought, under the first trigger of the state's drought relief norms. Fadnavis visited drought-affected areas in Washim and Amravati districts to take stock of the situation. He said the entire Amravati division had been affected by drought, putting crops under severe stress. “We have undertaken this visit to provide relief to farmers and assess the situation on the ground,” Fadnavis said. Drought relief measures announced After touring drought-hit areas in Washim, the Chief Minister held discussions at Amravati airport with Divisional Commissioner Nayana Gunde and the district collectors of Amravati and Washim. He later addressed the media. He said some areas may have been left out of the initial assessment and would be included under the third trigger of the drought relief mechanism. Given the widespread drought conditions, relief measures would be undertaken across the affected areas, he said. The Chief Minister said the government would also take measures to address fodder and water shortages and provide foodgrain assistance wherever required. Direct assistance would be provided to ensure that the education of farmers' children is not disrupted because of the drought, he said. Support for farmers and Rabi crops The government will assess the availability of water for taking up Rabi crops in areas where water resources are still available and provide assistance to farmers for Rabi cultivation. Fadnavis also said the government would focus on water conservation works to generate employment in drought-affected areas. Desilting of dried-up water bodies and repairs to ponds and other water conservation structures requiring maintenance would be taken up, he said. “Since the crop situation is similar across the affected areas, the state government has formulated a relief policy,” Fadnavis said, adding that efforts would be made to ensure that the assistance reaches farmers before Diwali. Also Watch: Loan waivers and procurement On farm loan waivers, the Chief Minister said the state government had implemented a loan waiver and that the waived amount was being credited to farmers' accounts. Banks would be required to provide fresh loans to eligible farmers as per the rules, he said. He also announced that government procurement of agricultural produce at the prescribed support prices would be undertaken and registration for the procurement process would begin shortly. headline: 4,249 Objectionable Books Removed from J&K Libraries, Mirwaiz Questions Government Move
text: Separatist leader and chairman of the All Parties Hurriyat Conference (APHC), Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, has questioned the Jammu and Kashmir Government's decision to remove more than 4,000 objectionable books from libraries across the Union Territory. The Jammu and Kashmir Government informed the Legislative Assembly that the Higher Education Department had removed 4,249 books from libraries of colleges and other higher educational institutions after reviewing more than 21.81 lakh books and other publications. The government said the books were removed after they were found to contain material allegedly glorifying terrorists and anti-national elements, following verification and screening. According to official figures, 3,996 of the books removed were from educational institutions in the Kashmir division, while 253 belonged to institutions in the Jammu division. The figures, however, do not include books formally banned under a separate process. The department said it had so far reviewed a total of 2,181,582 books and other publications, including 1,248,641 in the Kashmir division and 932,941 in the Jammu division. The government said the review process was extensive and time-consuming, given the large volume of material available in college and institutional libraries. The screening of other material considered objectionable is still underway and may take additional time to complete. The government further informed the House that 518 copies of 19 titles formally banned under Government Order SO-203, dated August 5, 2025, had also been removed from circulation. The department said guidelines and defined criteria had been adopted for identifying and reviewing material available in college libraries. According to the government, institutions of higher education have a responsibility not only to promote higher education, research and academic excellence but also to foster an environment that encourages constitutional values, academic freedom, critical thinking, scientific temper and responsible citizenship. The action concerning the formally banned books has also been challenged before the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court. The petitioners have questioned the validity of SO-203 and raised issues concerning constitutional rights associated with the order. The government, meanwhile, has defended the action, citing legal provisions and public interest. The review of library material remains in progress, with the department maintaining that the exercise is being conducted in accordance with the prescribed guidelines and criteria. headline: What’s Behind India’s Tit-For-Tat Move To Remove Barriers Outside Pakistan High Commission?
text: India has dismantled the external security perimeter outside the Pakistan High Commission in New Delhi, removing traffic bollards and barricades that had surrounded the diplomatic compound. The move came three days after Pakistan reportedly removed protective security barricades outside the Indian High Commission in Islamabad, making the action a clear tit-for-tat response amid continuing tensions between the two neighbours. Visuals from the site showed broken railings, gates, metal frames, roofing sheets, bricks and concrete scattered outside the Pakistan compound. Parts of the outer fencing and roofing were also pulled down. The visa section remained visible among the debris, with signs reading “Window 1”, “Pakistani Passport Only” and “Window-5 / Collection of Visa Applications”. Pakistan faces reciprocal action as diplomatic tensions deepen The latest move comes amid a prolonged diplomatic stand-off following the Pahalgam terror attack last year, in which 26 people were killed. India has blamed Pakistan-backed terrorists for the attack and responded with Operation Sindoor, striking terror infrastructure. Military exchanges continued until May 10, when Pakistan sought a ceasefire. The latest India-Pakistan friction also comes after US Ambassador Sergio Gor visited Srinagar on Wednesday and described Jammu and Kashmir as an “important part of India”. Gor’s visit was the first by a US envoy to the region in six years and drew a sharp response from Islamabad. Pakistan objects after US envoy’s Jammu and Kashmir remarks During his visit, Gor met Chief Minister Omar Abdullah and praised efforts by the Central Government and the Jammu and Kashmir administration to improve safety and stability. He also indicated that Washington could review its travel advisory for the region. “This is an important part of India and so I am here visiting for the first time. It is an incredibly beautiful place and I’m thrilled to be here, thrilled to see this place,” Gor told local media. “I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” he said, adding that both governments “have made some incredible steps in keeping this area safer”. Pakistan summons US diplomat after Gor’s statement Gor said Washington would also examine whether its travel warning should be downgraded. “We will be looking at if the travel warning that is recommended by the US is something that should be downgraded because, as I said earlier, this is a beautiful area. headline: Karnataka Legislative Council Passes 2 Bills Amid BJP Din
text: The Council passed the Karnataka Municipalities Amendment Bill, 2026, and the Karnataka Apartment Ownership and Management Bill, 2026, amid the Opposition's protests Bengaluru: Two Bills were cleared in the Karnataka Legislative Council amid a din created by the Opposition BJP and JD(S), which were protesting the induction of B Nagendra into the state Cabinet and demanding his removal over his alleged involvement in the Valmiki Corporation scam. The Council passed the Karnataka Municipalities Amendment Bill, 2026, and the Karnataka Apartment Ownership and Management Bill, 2026, amid the Opposition's protests. Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah moved the Karnataka Municipalities Amendment Bill, 2026, for passage. Chairman Saleem Ahmed put the motion to vote and, amid the din, declared: "I think the 'Yeses' have it. The 'Yeses' have it. The motion is carried and the Bill is passed." Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda then moved the Karnataka Apartment Ownership and Management Bill, 2026, saying the legislation was aimed at providing a legal framework for the management and maintenance of apartments and resolving disputes between residents, builders and resident welfare associations. "Today, more and more people are living in apartments. There are many issues relating to apartment living," Gowda said, citing disputes over maintenance, common areas, residents' associations and redevelopment of old buildings. He said apartment resident welfare associations would have to be registered under the new law and annual audits would be mandatory. Existing associations would also have to register afresh under the new legislation. "Therefore, registration under this law will be compulsory. That will provide a fresh and a clean start," Gowda said. The minister said the Bill was based on extensive consultations with stakeholders and provided for a dispute-resolution mechanism, including an appellate authority. He also said developers who had collected maintenance or development charges would have to hand over accounts of the collections, expenditure and balance to the recognised Resident Welfare Association. Gowda said the legislation followed the rights-based approach of the RERA law. "Before purchase, buyers receive protection under RERA. After purchasing and beginning to live in the apartment, this law gives them rights," he said. The Bill was passed after the Chairman put it to vote amid the Opposition's protests. The Opposition's protest is centred on the re-induction of Nagendra, who was a minister in the previous Siddaramaiah government but resigned in June 2024 following allegations of financial irregularities in the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes

headline: SC reserves order on Tarun Tejpal’s surrender plea; Goa seeks life sentence- Moneycontrol.com
text: The Supreme Court on Monday reserved its order on former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal’s plea seeking exemption from surrender after the Bombay High Court convicted him and sentenced him to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment in the 2013 rape case. The matter was heard by Justice Alok Aradhe, who reserved the order after hearing arguments from the Goa government and Tejpal’s counsel. The Goa government opposed Tejpal’s appeal being entertained without his surrender. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, argued that Tejpal’s special leave petition could not be considered unless he either produced proof of surrender or filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender. Citing Supreme Court Rules and earlier judgments, Mehta said a convict who has not surrendered must seek an exemption along with the appeal. “Existence of the appeal is dependent on either filing a certificate that he has surrendered or, alternatively, he will have to pray to Your Lordships to allow an exemption from surrendering,” Mehta submitted. He also urged the court to consider the gravity of the offence. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, opposed the argument, saying the rule would not apply as the Bombay High Court had given his client four weeks to surrender. Sibal argued that Tejpal was not required to surrender immediately because the High Court’s order granting him time remained in force. The Bombay High Court, in its August 6 verdict, overturned Tejpal’s 2021 acquittal and convicted him in the 2013 rape case. While refusing to stay the conviction, the court granted him four weeks to surrender before jail authorities. Under the timeline set by the High Court, Tejpal has until the first week of September to surrender. Sibal urged the Supreme Court to take up Tejpal’s appeal, filed on August 20, on August 31. “I don’t know why my learned friend (SG Mehta) insists that I must go to jail when I’m protected,” Sibal submitted, arguing that Tejpal should be allowed to seek interim protection. The case relates to allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague twice inside an elevator at a luxury hotel in Goa during a Tehelka event in November 2013. He was arrested later that month and granted bail in July 2014. The trial began in 2017, and the Goa Sessions Court acquitted him in May 2021. headline: Pfizer C&F Depot licence suspension case: K'taka Health Dept warns consumers over suspicious labels, QR codes in fake drug racket case
text: Bengaluru, Sep 21 : Following the Karnataka Health Department suspending the licence of Pfizer C&F Depot along with eight other drug licences in connection with a fake medicine racket unearthed in Bidadi, the department on Monday urged citizens to purchase medicines only from licenced pharmacies against valid tax invoices and report suspicious packaging or non-scanning QR codes on labels to Drug Enforcement authorities. The action follows a raid conducted by the Drug Enforcement Wing of the Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) at a farmhouse at Kurubarakeranahalli in Bidadi, Bengaluru South district, on August 18, 2026. The operation allegedly uncovered an unlicenced pharmaceutical repacking and relabelling racket. Spurious drugs, machinery and printing materials worth an estimated Rs 5.05 crore were seized during the raid. The inventory value of the seized materials was estimated at Rs 4.91 crore. According to the preliminary investigation, low-cost medicines procured from neighbouring states were allegedly repacked into new vials and relabelled to resemble expensive life-saving medicines of multinational companies, including products purportedly carrying the Pfizer brand. The authorities also found QR and scanning codes on the suspected counterfeit labels that reportedly did not function when verified. Officials said the seized products are suspected to contain no active medicinal ingredients, incorrect ingredients or potentially harmful substances, posing a serious risk to public health. A criminal case has been registered under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. The department has invoked provisions relating to spurious drugs, while further investigation is underway to identify and trace the entire supply chain in six states across the country. As part of the investigation into retailers and wholesalers allegedly involved in the distribution and sale of spurious medicines, 16 drug licences have been cancelled and eight licences suspended. The licence of M/s Pfizer C&F Depot at Kempalinganahalli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural district, has also been suspended. The department has blocked the batch numbers and entries of the seized medicines on the Karnataka FDA portal to prevent their further sale or distribution. Samples of the seized products have also been sent to laboratories for testing to determine their chemical composition, sterility and potency. The seized medicines, machinery and printing materials will be produced before the JMFC Court, Bengaluru South, as part of the legal proceedings. headline: J&K Government Dismisses Teacher In Kishtwar Rape And Death Case
text: The Jammu and Kashmir government has taken stringent action by dismissing a school teacher implicated in the tragic rape and death of a 15-year-old girl in Kishtwar, underscoring a firm stance on child safety and accountability. Key Points - The Jammu and Kashmir government dismissed a school teacher over the rape and death of a 15-year-old girl in Kishtwar. - The teacher, Khalid Hussain, was dismissed under Article 311(2)(b) of the Constitution, bypassing a regular departmental inquiry. - The victim died during a pregnancy termination procedure, and the teacher is currently in judicial custody. - Hussain faces charges under BNS sections and the POCSO Act for sexual assault and abetment. - A Special Investigation Team has arrested six individuals, and the case has been transferred to the Crime Branch for thorough investigation. The Jammu and Kashmir government has dismissed a government school teacher from service with immediate effect in connection with the rape and subsequent death of a 15-year-old girl in Kishtwar district, officials said on Monday. The action against the accused teacher, Khalid Hussain, was taken by the government under Article 311(2)(b) of the Constitution, the officials said. The teenager was allegedly raped by her school teacher, currently in judicial custody, over several months. She died on August 20 during a pregnancy termination procedure. Teacher Dismissed Under Constitutional Provisions According to an order issued by the school education department on Monday, Hussain, teacher at Government Middle School Bumalpora, Gurinalla, Zone Inderwal, Kishtwar, has been dismissed from service. The order said the competent authority, after considering the facts and material on record, was satisfied that the case warranted imposition of the major penalty of dismissal. It said Hussain, who was already under suspension and was in judicial custody, was dismissed under Article 311(2)(b) read with Rule 30(viii) of the J&K Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1956. headline: KPSC veterinary officers scam: K’taka HC orders SIT, report in 100 days - Mangalorean.com
text: KPSC veterinary officers scam: K’taka HC orders SIT, report in 100 days Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court on Monday ordered the formation of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by senior IPS officer Alok Kumar, to probe the alleged scam in the recruitment of veterinary officers conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC). The court directed the SIT to complete the investigation and submit its report within 100 days. The court further instructed the SIT to file a progress report every 30 days. It noted that “all connected petitions seeking to quash the cases will be taken up only after the SIT submits its report.” The development has assumed importance as jailed IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar and BJP leader Basavaraj Kannale are being grilled by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy has repeatedly targeted Home Minister Priyank Kharge over the recruitment scam. MLA Basanagouda Patil and activist Manjunath filed the petition, seeking a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). A High Court bench headed by Justice M. Nagaprasanna directed the state government to accord the SIT police station status and issue a notification at the earliest. Alok Kumar will head the SIT, which will comprise senior IPS officers Divya Gopinath, Anoop Shetty, Kushal Choukse and Kshama Mishra. The High Court also directed the ED to extend all necessary cooperation to the SIT. The court instructed the SIT to complete the investigation within 100 days and submit progress reports once every 30 days. It also directed the CID to hand over all case-related records to the SIT. Police currently investigating the case have been instructed to hand over the documents within one week. It also ordered that no obstruction should be caused to the investigation. headline: Lawyers strike work over 50% pre-deposit for challan appeals
text: Lawyers across all seven district courts in Delhi abstained from work on Monday (September 22, 2026) in protest against changes to the traffic challan system, particularly the requirement to deposit 50% of the penalty before a person can approach a court. The day-long protest was called by the Coordination Committee of all district court Bar Associations over amendments to Rule 167 of the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989. Advocates assembled at the district court complexes and raised slogans demanding that the Delhi government withdraw the amendment. Under the revised mechanism, a person issued a challan can either accept it and make the payment or contest it through the prescribed portal before an authority designated by the state government. Such a challenge has to be filed within 45 days. The lawyers have opposed the provision allowing a person to approach a competent court against an order of the designated authority only after making the mandatory pre-deposit. The lawyers have also questioned the role given to the Executive in deciding a challenge before the matter can be taken to court, arguing that determining a dispute over a traffic violation is essentially a judicial function. They said the mandatory pre-deposit could place an additional financial burden on those contesting a challan and potentially discourage them from seeking judicial redress. The advocates also raised concerns about the digital nature of the new mechanism, pointing to difficulties it could create for people unfamiliar with online systems, including commercial and truck drivers. They further contended that the procedure could leave limited opportunity for a person to place the circumstances surrounding an alleged traffic violation before approaching a court. The district court Bar Associations flagged the amendments to Rule 167 in a circular issued on September 20, 2026. Published - September 22, 2026 12:10 am IST

headline: Textbook Errors & MMDR Act: Twin Opposition Attack Paralyses Odisha Assembly
text: he opening day of the Monsoon Session of the Odisha Legislative Assembly collapsed into absolute chaos on Tuesday as the Opposition Biju Janata Dal (BJD) and Congress joined forces to stall proceedings, forcing Speaker Surama Padhy to adjourn the House twice until 4:00 PM. BJD Demands Resignation Over School Textbook Errors Immediately following the obituary references, BJD lawmakers surged into the Well of the House, clutching placards and shouting slogans against School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond. The Opposition demanded the Minister’s immediate resignation over glaring errors spotted in newly distributed school textbooks. Demonstrating their fury, BJD members displayed placards featuring absurd textbook mistakes—including references to “Nimbuda Nimbuda”, a photo of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly printed in place of the Odisha Assembly, and lessons on “Sukhua Podha” (roasted dried fish). Several BJD MLAs climbed onto the reporters’ table right in front of the Speaker’s podium, triggering intense commotion. With normal business rendered impossible within just one minute of the uproar, Speaker Surama Padhy first adjourned the Assembly from 11:36 AM to 1:10 PM, and subsequently from 1:11 PM to 4:00 PM. Senior BJD leadership, including Leader of Opposition Naveen Patnaik and Deputy Leader Prasanna Acharya, remained present in their seats throughout the agitation. March to Lower PMG and Night-Long Dharna Following the adjournment, BJD legislators marched from the Assembly premises to the Lower PMG demonstration site, joining the ongoing day-and-night protest launched by the Biju Yuva Janata Dal (BYJD) and Biju Chhatra Janata Dal (BCJD). Speaking at the protest site, senior BJD leader Dr Arun Kumar Sahoo launched a sharp attack on the state government: “This administration is running on empty promises and playing with the future of Odisha’s children. If a minister in Delhi can resign over policy failures, why won’t Minister Nityananda Gond step down here?” MLAs Sarada Prasad Jena, Dhruba Charan Sahoo, Byomakesh Ray, Manohar Randhari, Barsha Singh Bariha, and Manorama Mohanty reiterated that the protest would continue unabated until the Minister resigns. BYJD President Chinmay Sahoo and BCJD President Ispita Sahoo confirmed that youth and student wings from across the state have assembled at Lower PMG for an indefinite night-and-day sit-in. Congress Raises MMDR Act Issue Simultaneously, the Congress party targeted the government over the amended Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) — MMDR Act. headline: Delhi Police register FIR against unknown persons on pellet gun complaint
text: New Delhi, Aug 21 : Following the sit-in staged by Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Delhi Police on Friday lodged a First Information Report (FIR) against unknown persons on a complaint by a purported pellet-gun victim, Sahil Lochab. Gandhi had been staging the sit-in outside the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police at Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station, protesting the alleged refusal of the police to register an FIR on Lochab's complaint Addressing reporters after the FIR was lodged, Lochab expressed gratitude to the LoP, saying: "I am thankful to Rahul Gandhi ji who sat here for eight hours following which this FIR was registered. His team has been in touch with me for the last one month, and he (Gandhi) himself had been enquiring about my health." Stating that he didn't plan to come in front of the media, he said: "Yesterday when he (Gandhi) had called, I told him that my FIR was not being registered. He immediately asked me to meet him today and assured me that he would get my FIR lodged. I thank him for this." He also thanked the public for praying for his recovery because of which he could again stand on his feet despite "200 pellets being lodged in his body". "This is a victory for justice," he asserted. However, the student said that he is upset that despite the Leader of Opposition and the complainant being present, "it took eight hours for the police to register an FIR". "In fact, the FIR might not have been lodged if the LoP had not helped me. From August 14, I have been making frequent visits (to the police station) to lodge an FIR, but it has been registered now, after seven to eight days," he added. Further, Lochab said that he had faith that the LoP's presence would ultimately lead to the filing of the FIR. His mother also thanked LoP Gandhi for assisting them in getting the FIR registered.

headline: Bihar Job seekers detained following scuffle with police during Lok Bhavan protest
text: Patna: Several job aspirants were detained on Saturday after a scuffle with police during a march to Lok Bhavan in Patna to press for a transparent recruitment process, officials said. A large number of job aspirants participated in the march, which was stopped near R-Golumber where barricades were put up, they said. A scuffle broke out as the protesters tried to breach the barricades, following which the security personnel used “mild force” to disperse them. Many protesters were subsequently detained, they added. City SP (Central) Mamta Kalyani said, “Adequate forces have been deployed to handle any situation.” The protesters are demanding adherence to UGC rules in the appointment of professors, an increase in the maximum age limit, a single-tier examination for BPSC TRE-4 and a level playing field for Hindi-medium candidates, among others. Guest faculty members of universities in Bihar and PhD holders have been protesting for over a fortnight, seeking implementation of UGC Regulation 2018 in the appointment of assistant professors, raising the maximum age limit for applicants to 55 years, regularisation of assistant professor appointments and implementation of a domicile policy. One group of protesters warned that they would gherao the Bihar chief minister’s official residence on August 25 if the government failed to hold a meaningful dialogue with them by August 24. Protesters seeking changes in the BPSC TRE-4 recruitment process also threatened to call a Bihar bandh if their demands were not considered by the government.

headline: Rain lashes Jharkhand, govt issues safety warning for tourists visiting waterfalls
text: Rain lashes Jharkhand, govt issues safety warning for tourists visiting waterfalls Ranchi, Jharkhand received light to moderate rainfall on Thursday under the influence of a deep depression, with the state administration issuing a safety advisory for tourists visiting waterfalls. The India Meteorological Department has issued an 'orange' alert , predicting heavy to very heavy rainfall in isolated places in Ranchi, Khunti, Gumla, Simdega and West Singhbhum districts for 24 hours till 8.30 am on Friday. A 'yellow' alert , predicting heavy rain, has also been issued for 11 districts for the same period, according to an IMD bulletin. "Heavy to very heavy rainfall is expected in a few pockets of southern and central parts of Jharkhand on Thursday. Lightning coupled with gusty winds at speeds of up to 50 kmph is also likely in some districts," Ranchi Meteorological Centre Deputy Director Abhishek Anand said. He said the intensity of rainfall is likely to decrease from Friday evening. Meanwhile, the Ranchi administration has issued a safety warning for tourists visiting the state's famed waterfalls, including Jonha, Hundru, Dasam, Sita and Remix Falls. On Wednesday, two tourists were rescued at Hundru Falls after being swept away by the strong currents while taking a selfie. "Due to continuous torrential rains in Ranchi and surrounding areas, Jonha, Hundru, Dasham, Sita and Remix Falls, and all other waterfalls are in full flow, prompting a safety warning for tourists. The waterfalls are at their peak surge. While this is captivating and mesmerising, it is also extremely dangerous," the administration said in a statement. The district administration and local authorities have appealed to tourists, visitors, and locals to exercise extreme caution while venturing near the areas around Jonha and Hundru waterfalls. "Currently, the areas surrounding the waterfalls are very risky. Swift currents, slippery rocks, and the potential for sudden rises in water levels pose a severe threat to tourists," it added. The administration suggested that visitors not go near the waterfalls, stay in safe places and strictly follow all guidelines issued by the local administration and police. headline: ED raids IAS officer in Karnataka exam money laundering case
text: ED raids IAS officer in Karnataka exam money laundering case The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Sunday raided the premises of IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in Bengaluru and Bareilly in connection with a money laundering investigation linked to alleged irregularities in an exam conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), officials said. Gangwar is a 2016-batch IAS officer and is currently posted as Director-MSME in the Karnataka Department of Industries and Commerce. He earlier served as the Controller of Examinations at the KPSC and was replaced in March this year. Officials said Gangwar’s premises in Bengaluru’s Jayamahal area and UP’s Bareilly were searched under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). It was not immediately known if the officer was found on the premises by the central agency. A controversy erupted on Saturday after Gangwar was reported missing for a few hours. Later, Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge denied the reports and clarified that Gangwar was in his native place in UP following a family emergency involving his father’s health. The probe is linked to a money laundering investigation into a Veterinary Officers recruitment exam ‘scam’. It is alleged by the ED that some middlemen called the candidates, including the complainant, and demanded bribes ranging from Rs 70 lakh to Rs 80 lakh (per candidate) for selection. Additionally, the agency is looking into allegations of paper leak, OMR answer sheet tampering and facilitation in final selection of relatives of KPSC officials, ED officials had said. Last week, the Karnataka Cabinet decided to recommend to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot the suspension of KPSC Chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar.

headline: 'Engaging in vote-bank politics': JD-U MLA Anant Singh hits out at Bihar LoP Tejashwi Yadav
text: Patna, Sep 22 : Janata Dal-United MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Tuesday criticised the Bihar Leader of Opposition (LoP) and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav for his criticism of the state government over the Jamui molestation case, accusing the latter of indulging in "vote-bank politics". Earlier in the day, Tejashwi Yadav demanded the resignation of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, saying that the incident shows "women and girls are not safe anywhere in the state". Speaking to IANS, JD-U MLA Anant Kumar Singh said: "Pay no heed to what he (Tejashwi Yadav) says...these people are merely engaging in vote-bank politics." "Instead, people should themselves take charge that such incidents should not take place in Bihar or in the country...people involved in such crimes will have to face punishment," he added. Anant Singh backed the encounter of an accused in the Jamui molestation case, saying: "The (Bihar) government is doing the right thing regarding this incident. Such people should be killed immediately. The public also needs to remain vigilant about such incidents and report them to the government. What can the police achieve alone? The public must cooperate." "There should be action if such an incident takes place...such people should be encountered," he said. Regarding the upcoming Member of Legislative Council (MLC) polls in Bihar, the JD-U MLA said: "I am supporting Anuj Singh; he is the one who will win." "We appeal to the people of all three districts comprising the Patna Graduate MLC constituency, to bless us so abundantly that, in the future, no one dares to contest an election against me," he emphaised. Anant Singh openly rebelled against his own party's prominent leader and chief spokesperson Neeraj Kumar, who is the incumbent MLC seeking another term from the Patna Graduate constituency. Defying the party line, Anant Singh declared his complete support for Anuj Singh, a candidate backed by Prashant Kishor's Jan Suraaj Party. Last week, Anant Singh openly challenged JD-U MLC Neeraj Kumar, proposing a face-to-face public debate on all contentious issues and even offering what he described as a Rs 20-crore wager to settle their long-running disputes. He called upon Neeraj Kumar to join him near a Hanuman temple in Patna for an open discussion. "Let us sit across from each other and debate face-to-face. We will settle all scores," Singh said. The roots of the rivalry stretch back to the 2015 Bihar Assembly elections.

headline: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches expanded Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme for govt. school students
text: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) launched the expansion of the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme to benefit students studying in Classes VI to VIII in government and government-aided schools across the State. Launching the expansion of the scheme at Chennai Middle School, Gandhi Gramam, at Thiruvanmiyur in Chennai, Mr. Vijay served sweet pongal to students and had breakfast with them. The Chief Minister also inspected the classrooms and interacted with students who were having breakfast. The students were served sweet pongal, pongal, and sambar during breakfast on the day of the launch. The expanded scheme will cover 15.3 lakh students studying in Classes VI to VIII in 15,454 government and government-aided schools across the State. Breakfast will be prepared and served through centralised kitchens in 447 government and government-aided schools in the Greater Chennai Corporation. In 2,150 government and government-aided schools in other municipal corporations, municipalities, and adjoining town panchayat areas, breakfast will be prepared and served through centralised kitchens by the Directorate of Municipal Administration. In 12,857 government and government-aided schools in rural areas and adjoining town panchayat areas, members of self-help groups under the Tamil Nadu Corporation for Development of Women will prepare and serve breakfast at the respective schools. The Chief Minister’s Breakfast Scheme for students in Classes I to V in government and government-aided schools was launched during the previous DMK regime in September 2022. After the TVK-led government assumed office, Mr. Vijay directed that the scheme be expanded to cover students in Classes VI to VIII in government and government-aided schools as well. Subsequently, the scheme was renamed the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme. A total of ₹724 crore has been allocated for this scheme, including additional funds of ₹217.63 crore for the expansion component. Ministers N. Anand, Aadhav Arjuna, Rajmohan, K. Jegadeshwari, and R. Kumar, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, and senior officials of the School Education and Social Welfare and Women Empowerment departments were present during the launch. After launching the scheme, Mr. Vijay also met Praveen Kumar, a person with disabilities, and his mother, Malar, who were waiting outside the school. She submitted a petition seeking financial assistance and a job for her educated daughter. The Chief Minister received the petition and assured her appropriate action would be taken. headline: IIT Bombay student suicide: Welfare reforms, mental health focus sought; security beefed up - top developments
text: MUMBAI: Students at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay have demanded changes to the institute’s student welfare system and greater focus on mental health, following concerns raised in the wake of the Sahil Wakode suicide case. Security was beefed up outside the IIT-Bombay campus on Tuesday. They also said that targeting one professor over the case was "completely wrong". Wakode, 22, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found hanging from the ceiling fan in his hostel room at IIT Bombay’s Powai campus on the evening of September 18. He was allegedly caught using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination earlier that day. The incident triggered protests by students on the campus. The Mumbai Police have booked Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, who has been removed as the dean of Administrative Affairs, under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, following a complaint lodged by Sahil's family. "Even if students differ on the issue, we all agree on one thing: changes need to be brought in student welfare, including the wellness cell, psychiatrist support, and similar areas. Students' voices should be heard when decisions are made," a student told news agency PTI on Monday. "But, I think students disagree on the treatment of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla. The caste angle portrayed in the media is wrong and does not exist," he asserted. The student said Prof Doolla’s removal as Dean (Administrative Affairs) was “completely wrong”, asserting that he was only doing his job. Another student told the media that reports of caste discrimination were incorrect. "There is no discrimination on the basis of caste in the institute. Therefore, the media reports on caste bias in IIT Bombay are completely wrong," he said. Another student said stress might have led Sahil Wakode to take the extreme step. "I feel stress must be the reason; otherwise there is no such other reason that could have led Wakode to take such a step. But stress is there because the courses are difficult. I feel that is a part of engineering, and that is how you learn," he said. However, some students also alleged that Prof Doolla had a track record of suspending students over what they described as trivial reasons and removing them from hostels. text: Bihar Cabinet approves Mata Sita, Ramdhari Singh Dinkar universities PATNA, Sep 23 : The Bihar Cabinet on Wednesday approved the establishment of Mata Sita University in Patna and Rashtra Kavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai. PATNA, Sep 23 : The Bihar Cabinet on Wednesday approved the establishment of Mata Sita University in Patna and Rashtra Kavi Ramdhari Singh Dinkar University in Begusarai. The decisions were taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. Additional Cabinet Secretary Arvind Kumar Choudhary told news persons after the meeting that the Cabinet approved Rs 15 crore each for the establishment of the two universities to meet expenditure on salaries and other establishment-related requirements. The proposed university in Patna was initially referred to as Maa Sita University, but the Cabinet approved an amendment changing the name to Mata Sita University. The cabinet also cleared a slew of proposals involving police modernisation, dairy and fisheries development, power sector liabilities and prison reforms. Among the major decisions, the Cabinet sanctioned Rs 24.50 crore for procurement of 50 drones under the centrally sponsored scheme for assistance to states and union Territories for police modernisation. The drones are intended for crowd-control and management, riverine and anti-Naxal operations, disaster management and other policing requirements, 8nforned Choudhary. An additional Rs 33.685 crore was approved for procurement of equipment and other items for district police, railway police, the Bihar Special Armed Police, the Prohibition Department and the State Narcotics Control Bureau, among other agencies. The Cabinet also approved a one-time remission measure for eligible convicted prisoners to facilitate their release from jails on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi''s birth anniversary on October 2, 2026. It further approved amendments to Rule 743 of the Bihar Prison Manual, 2012, in accordance with the Supreme Court''s orders of July 30 and September 10, 2026, in the case concerning discrimination inside prisons. text: Haunted by ghosts of 1984 anti-Sikh riots, ex-Congress MP Sajjan Kumar dies He should've been hanged: Witness Haunted by the ghosts of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, which clouded much of his political career, former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar died on Thursday while serving two concurrent life sentences at Tihar Jail. Kumar, 80, was declared dead at Safdarjung Hospital after being taken there following complaints of uneasiness. Ironically, he died on the same day the Supreme Court was to hear his parole application. Kumar had sought three weeks’ parole to tend to his ailing wife. A former three-time Lok Sabha MP from Outer Delhi, Kumar remained the only high-profile Congress leader to ever face justice for his role in the riots that led to the killing of more than 2,700 Sikhs in the aftermath of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi’s assassination on October 31, 1984. Kumar was sentenced to life imprisonment in two separate cases. The first involved killings of five members of Jagdish Kaur’s family, who resided in Delhi’s Palam Colony’s Raj Nagar at the time of the crimes on November 1 and 2, 1984. The second was for the murders of Jaswant Singh and his son in the Saraswati Vihar area. Jagdish Kaur, whose relentless quest for justice led to Kumar’s first conviction on December 17, 2018, when the Delhi High Court convicted him in the Raj Nagar murders, said she had always wanted Kumar to be hanged. “Sajjan Kumar should have been hanged to death or lynched in full public view for the crimes he committed. headline: Karnataka rejects Ghats report, seeks 1-year survey window
text: BENGALURU: Karnataka legislature Tuesday unanimously adopted a resolution rejecting the Centre’s seventh draft Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) notification. The resolution followed a discussion, held in both the assembly and council, on the Kasturirangan report on the Western Ghats. Moved by chief minister DK Shivakumar , the resolution seeks a one-year window from the Centre for a ground-level survey to separate forests from farms, plantations and human settlements before the notification is finalised. Shivakumar announced a committee headed by a retired judge, with revenue and forest officials, farmer associations, industrialists and ecology experts on the panel, to address the draft’s shortcomings. The resolution adopted by Karnataka objected to the inclusion of agricultural land, plantations, homes and public utility spaces alongside forested areas under ESA. It also flagged a lack of precise demarcation of land, calling it unscientific to declare an entire village as ESA merely because a fifth of it fell within forest limits. “Forests must be protected and people of the Western Ghats have done so for generations. They should not face hurdles or threats,” the CM said, adding that a delegation would soon travel to Delhi to press the region’s case. Claiming that the draft offered no economic assistance to or alternative livelihood for affected people, the resolution urged the Centre to exclude farmland, plantations, settlements and public-use spaces from ESA. Responding to a question from opposition leader R Ashok on the National Green Tribunal ’s directives, Shivakumar said senior advocates would be appointed to present Karnataka’s stand before the Supreme Court on the Centre’s Kasturirangan report notification. The CM clarified that the state was not disrespecting the Kasturirangan committee’s recommendations, but wanted those scientifically revised in Karnataka’s interest, adding that since drone surveys tend to show the entire topography as green, a survey through the revenue department was needed. When MLAs cutting across party lines flagged unresolved issues, including Bagar Hukum, forest rights, deemed forests, land grants and pending court cases, Shivakumar assured those would be taken up separately. headline: Congress targets PM Modi over CBI inquiry into ‘irregularities’ involving Arunachal CM
text: New Delhi The Congress on Friday (September 18, 2026) questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s silence over the Supreme Court-ordered preliminary CBI inquiry into allegations of irregularities in the award of public works contracts worth about ₹1,270 crore to firms linked to family members of Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu. Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said Mr Khandu should have resigned, or have been asked to resign, after the Supreme Court directed the CBI on April 6 to conduct a preliminary inquiry into the award and execution of public works contracts in the State between 2015 and 2025. “But both the CM and his Supreme Leader the PM decided to brazen it out,” Mr Ramesh said in a post on X. The Supreme Court directed the CBI to register a preliminary inquiry and submit a status report within 16 weeks on whether a full-fledged independent investigation was warranted. It had also directed the Arunachal Pradesh government to cooperate with the agency and ensure that relevant records were preserved. headline: Haryana’s 3 technical universities functioning without regular VCs - The Tribune
text: Haryana’s 3 technical universities functioning without regular VCs GJUST, DCRUST and YMCA universities currently being headed by acting or additional-charge VCs All three technical universities in the state — Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology (GJUST), the JC Bose University of Science and Technology, YMCA, Faridabad (YMCA), and Deenbandhu Chhotu Ram University of Science and Technology (DCRUST), Murthal, in Sonepat district — have been functioning without regular vice-chancellors. The term of GJUST, Hisar, VC Prof Narsi Ram Bishnoi ended on May 2. He was given an extension but later relinquished the charge on August 29. headline: MP: Fresh student protests in Vidisha put school transport, education in focus
text: Bhopal, Aug 25 : School students staged two separate protests in Vidisha on Tuesday over school transport and education issues, adding to a series of demonstrations by schoolchildren across Madhya Pradesh in recent weeks. The fresh protests followed a demonstration in Sironj, also in Vidisha district, where schoolgirls opposed a proposed increase in concessional bus fares. The developments have brought concerns over affordability and accessibility of education, particularly for students from rural and economically weaker families, into focus. In Sironj, private bus operators had proposed increasing the concessional fare for students from Rs 10 to Rs 25. A group of schoolgirls from a government higher secondary school protested against the move, after which the administration intervened and retained the fare at Rs 10. Madhya Pradesh Congress president Jitu Patwari, reacting to the protests, said students were being forced to take to the streets even in Budhni constituency, associated with former chief minister and Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. He said the sudden increase in bus fares was taking a toll on the education of children from poor and middle-class families, and demanded that the government roll back the hike and address studentsâ€™ grievances. Beyond transport costs, students and activists have opposed the proposed merger of smaller government schools with larger Sandipani and CM Rise campuses. Students in Bherunda have also raised concerns about bus fares and access to educational facilities, while protests elsewhere have focused on demands for roads and basic school infrastructure. Members of the School Bachao Sangharsh Samiti argued that shifting neighbourhood schools would force children, particularly from rural areas, to travel longer distances to attend classes. Last week, hundreds of girls demonstrated outside the district collectorâ€™s office against the proposed shifting or merger of several smaller government schools with a larger school in the Daudkhedi area of Ujjain, the home district of Chief Minister Mohan Yadav.

headline: Over 50 ABVP members detained during protest outside KPSC office in Bengaluru
text: Over 40 members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) were detained by Bengaluru police on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) after they staged a protest outside the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) office. The protesters staged a dharna on the busy road outside the KPSC office, raising slogans against the State government. The protest disrupted traffic in the area for some time, following which police personnel rushed to the spot and detained the protesters. The protesters were taken to the High Grounds police station for allegedly violating High Court orders governing protests and public gatherings. At the police station, some ABVP members alleged that the police used excessive force while detaining them and claimed that several students sustained injuries during the police action. They also alleged that police personnel refused to take the injured students to hospital and instead provided first aid at the station. Senior police officials, however, denied the allegations of brutality. They said no excessive force was used while detaining the protesters and maintained that the police followed the prescribed protocol. Published - August 25, 2026 08:06 pm IST

headline: Haryana varsity faculty to protest government move to abolish vacant posts - The Tribune
text: Haryana varsity faculty to protest government move to abolish vacant posts Move to target posts lying vacant for 4 years The faculty members of state universities will stage protest demonstrations against the Haryana Government’s move to abolish the vacant posts at the universities. A decision to this effect was taken at a meeting of the Haryana Federation of University and College Teachers Organisations (HFUCTO) organised recently. “The university teachers and students will stage a series of protest demonstrations at all state universities and submit memorandums to the top authorities through the vice-chancellors,” said Dr Narender Chahar, vice-president, All-India Federation of University and College Teachers Organisations (AIFUCTO), who is also a member of the executive committee of the HFUCTO. The protests will begin from Kurukshetra University next week, following which demonstrations will be held in all the universities one by one. “Students will also be roped in for the protest as the government diktat will jeopardise the job prospects of those who aspire to join as teachers and are qualified for the posts,” said Dr Chahar. The statewide demonstrations have been planned to oppose the Haryana Government’s move to abolish all newly created posts at the state universities which remain vacant for a period of four years. A communique in this regard was recently shot off by the office of the Additional Chief Secretary (ACS), Finance Department, to all administrative secretaries of the state government, the heads of all departments and the vice-chancellors of all state universities. The said communique, issued under the subject of ‘Economy Measures’, maintains that, “All newly created posts in state universities which remain unfilled/vacant for a period of four years from the date of approval by the Finance Department may be considered as deemed abolished.”

headline: ‘Who Let Her In?’ Undertrial Officer Found With Alleged Girlfriend During Hospital Inspection

text: Karnataka IAS officer goes missing after Bengaluru flight; govt clarifies his whereabouts Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, a 2016-batch IAS officer, had reportedly been incommunicado since August 20 and had booked a flight to Delhi. Karnataka IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, who was reported to have gone missing after being last traced to Bengaluru airport, has communicated with the state government and clarified that he had travelled to his hometown due to a family emergency, Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge said on Saturday. Kharge said the officer had sought leave and travelled urgently, but was not reachable on his official phone during the period, leading to confusion and speculation about his whereabouts. “There have been reports that an IAS officer in Karnataka has gone missing,” Kharge said in a post on X. “The officer concerned has since communicated with the Government and clarified that, due to a family emergency, he had sought leave and had to travel urgently to his hometown.” Gangwar, a 2016-batch IAS officer, is currently serving as Director, MSME, in the Department of Industries and Commerce. headline: Delhi: CJP cites 3 pending demands ahead of Sept 5 march - The Tribune
text: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Wednesday reiterated its plan to march in Delhi on September 5, saying three of the four demands that led it to call off the protest on July 25 had not been met so far. The party has planned a march from India Gate to the New Delhi Police Headquarters on September 5. The CJP said the march would be led by families of the deceased NEET aspirants and “victims of the alleged police brutality”. Students, youth organisations and young citizens are also expected to join the mobilisation. The CJP said it had withdrawn its protest a month ago after receiving assurances that all four demands would be addressed. According to the CJP, the pending issues are compensation for the families of NEET aspirants who had died by suicide, withdrawal of FIRs and a commitment that no action would be taken against student protesters, and an apology from the Rapid Action Force (RAF) and the Delhi Police. The party on Wednesday said the decision to resume the protest was taken after a review of commitments made by the government. It has also referred to the Supreme Court proceedings on August 18, in which, according to the organisation, the court sought a list of FIRs registered across the country so that it could consider dealing with them together. The issue of FIRs has remained one of the central points in the CJP’s decision to revive the mobilisation. On Wednesday, the party also pointed to what it called its “Black Monday Record”, an archive documenting the crackdown on protesters. headline: Karnataka Minister Nagendra rejects reports of his resignation: ‘Completely untrue’ | Mint
text: Karnataka Minister Nagendra rejects reports of his resignation: ‘Completely untrue’ Rumours had it that Nagendra told Shivakumar he did not wish to embarrass the party leadership any more, and, hence he wanted to voluntarily resign by Wednesday evening. Rumours had it that Nagendra told Shivakumar he did not wish to embarrass the party leadership any more, and, hence he wanted to voluntarily resign by Wednesday evening. "The reports currently being aired in the media are completely untrue. I have not received any call from the Chief Minister's Office, and there has been no discussion regarding any resignation. I request your cooperation," Nagendra's office said in a statement quoting him," Nagendra was quoted as saying by newas agency PTI rejecting the reports. BJP mounts pressure The Opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Karnataka and its ally JD(S) have been demanding Nagendra's removal from the Cabinet over the alleged ₹89 crore irregularities in the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation. The Opposition disrupted the Monsoon session of the Karnataka Legislature through sloganeering and protests inside and outside the Vidhana Soudha and it was adjourned sine die on August 24, three days before the scheduled end. The Valmiki Corporation case came to light after the corporation's accounts officer Chandrasekharan P died by suicide in May 2024, leaving behind a note alleging unauthorised transfer of funds. Investigations subsequently alleged that large sums were transferred from the corporation's bank accounts to various accounts, triggering a political controversy and demands for Nagendra's resignation. headline: Centre opposes Kiran Bedi's plea to join Delhi PG collapse pleas, HC says her ‘long experience’ could be useful
text: Centre opposes Kiran Bedi's plea to join Delhi PG collapse pleas, HC says her ‘long experience’ could be useful The bench held that Kiran Bedi’s experience as an administrator could be useful when considering the issues arising from the collapse. The Centre on Thursday opposed former IPS officer Kiran Bedi’s plea, which sought impleadment in petitions concerning the Satya Niketan building collapse, and requested time from the Delhi High Court to file its response. Granting the Centre three days to file its reply, the bench of chief justice DK Upadhyaya and justice Tejas Karia held that Bedi’s experience as an administrator could be useful when considering the issues arising from the collapse. In her application, Bedi submitted that through her impleadment, she wished to bring forth critical public domain disclosures that established a “nexus” between local political representatives, administrative apathy, and the rampant operation of illegal PGs owned and run by theadministrators, politicians and their associates. headline: Ex-Delhi Police commissioner Satish Golcha to take over as Home Guards' Director General from October 1
text: Ex-Delhi Police commissioner Satish Golcha to take over as Home Guards' Director General from October 1 The latest order comes ahead of the superannuation of Virender Singh, who has been heading the Directorate of Home Guards. Senior IPS officer Satish Golcha, who served as Delhi Police commissioner until last month, will take over as Director General of Home Guards, Delhi, from October 1, according to an order issued by the Delhi government on Tuesday. Golcha, a 1992-batch AGMUT cadre IPS officer, has been transferred and posted as Officer on Special Duty (OSD) in the Directorate of Home Guards until the superannuation of incumbent DG Virender Singh, a 1991-batch IPS officer, on September 30. He will assume charge as Director General, Home Guards, with effect from October 1, the order issued by the Home Department of the Delhi government said, news agency PTI reported. Delhi Police will retain Golcha on its strength until he takes over as DG Home Guards. Also Read: Who is Satish Golcha, Delhi's new police chief? 30+ years in IPS, held many key posts in capital Golcha took charge as Delhi Police commissioner on August 22, 2025, succeeding Sanjay Arora. He was replaced by 1994-batch IPS officer Anurag Kumar as police commissioner on July 17 this year. Who is Satish Golcha? A 1992-batch AGMUT cadre IPS officer, Golcha has held several senior policing and administrative positions during his career. He served as DGP in Arunachal Pradesh between 2022 and 2023. After being transferred back to Delhi, he was appointed Special Commissioner of Police (Intelligence) and later DG, Prisons. Before his Arunachal Pradesh stint, Golcha served as Special CP (Law and Order, Zone 2) and headed the Delhi Crime Branch. He has also headed several police ranges within Delhi. Additionally, Golcha served as Director General of Tihar Prisons before becoming Delhi Police commissioner. He took charge as Delhi Police commissioner on August 22, 2025, succeeding Sanjay Arora, and was replaced by Anurag Kumar on July 17 this year. Golcha belongs to the AGMUT cadre of the IPS, which stands for Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Mizoram and Union Territories and includes the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi. The latest order comes ahead of the superannuation of Virender Singh, who has been heading the Directorate of Home Guards. The Home Guards organisation assists the civil administration and police in maintaining law and order, traffic management and during emergencies and disasters.

headline: Environmentalists Sound Alarm Over Karnataka's Delay in Ecologically Sensitive Area Protection
text: Environmentalists warn against delaying ESA protection Development pressures raise concerns over protection of the Western Ghats Experts warn the state’s demand for another survey could prolong uncertainty, leaving sensitive Western Ghats areas open to development pressure Karnataka legislature’s recent decision to reject the Centre’s seventh draft Ecologically Sensitive Area (ESA) notification has drawn widespread criticism from ecologists and environmentalists. Experts say the delay in its implementation could have ecological consequences, as areas proposed for protection remain exposed to development pressures. “Either the government has not applied its mind or understood what the notification says, or it is doing so due to vested interests. Under the ESA notification, mining and quarrying are not permitted, while there are no restrictions on horticulture or agricultural activities,” said wildlife conservationist Akhilesh Chipli. Experts said several ongoing projects in the Western Ghats could face restrictions if the state accepts the seventh ESA notification, including the NTPC nuclear thermal plant in Sagar taluk, which would fall within the ESA and consequently have to be dropped if the seventh draft notification is implemented. Similarly, ongoing geological exploration for rare minerals in the area by the Geological Survey of India, along with the Karnataka Department of Mines and Geology, would also have to be dropped. Other projects could also face obstacles. According to Joseph Hoover, former member of the State Board of Wildlife and founder of the United Conservation Movement and Charitable Trust, the public has been misled into believing that their land will be taken away, leading to unrest among locals over theKasturirangan report . “Many with political clout own large tracts of land in the Malnad region. For these owners, the adoption of the seventh draft notification would have spelled doom. While the government’s logic of conducting a physical survey has some valid points, why were these surveys not conducted earlier? This is the seventh draft issued by the Centre, not the first one,” said Hoover. Experts say that, given the ongoing climate crisis, Karnataka should implement the Kasturirangan report sooner rather than later. On July 27, 2026, the Government of India issued the seventh draft ESA notification based on the Kasturirangan report, identifying around 20,668 sq km across 1,449 villages in 10 districts of Karnataka under the ESA. Karnataka rejected the seventh draft in its present form after the state legislature unanimously passed a resolution on September 22 seeking changes and a fresh ground-level assessment.

headline: Mumbai Congress suspends 79 for ‘anti-party activities’; some already in BJP, others threaten legal action
text: MUMBAI: Congress’s suspension of 79 office-bearers, including former corporators, for alleged anti-party activities has triggered fresh controversy, with some of those named having already joined the ruling party, resigned from Congress more than a year ago, or threatened to send legal notices to Mumbai Congress chief Varsha Gaikwad for allegedly defaming them. Most of these politicians left the party due to differences with the party leadership, including Varsha Gaikwad. A Congress insider said the expulsion decision was taken by the party’s administrative body and not by Gaikwad. The insider added that some of those expelled were trying to re-enter the party, and it was therefore decided to bar them from the party for six years, along with others who had left Congress. Gaikwad said, “We have democracy in our party so we don’t mind them sending us their reply in whatever way. It’s the party’s internal affair and we will handle it.” Among those expelled was former corporator Ravi Raja, who had already joined the BJP . Dharmesh Vyas , another name on the list, left the party last year and is now with the BJP. Vyas has threatened legal action against Varsha Gaikwad, saying he had already resigned from Congress and therefore could not be suspended. He alleged that the move was aimed at defaming him. The Congress insider said many of these politicians had left the party by posting their resignations on social media or announcing them publicly, instead of submitting their resignations to the party office. Congress said it followed the required procedure, including issuing show-cause notices before expelling them. Raja, who was denied an MLA party ticket and was later refused a meeting in Delhi by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to raise his concerns against the Mumbai Congress leadership, left the party in 2024 and joined the BJP as its vice-president. Raja said, “I even contested an election on BJP ticket from the Dharavi area. How can she (Gaikwad) be so ignorant? Senior leaders of the party sidelined us, which forced us to leave the Congress long ago. Now it’s nothing but a joke. I will send a notice to her.”

He said suspending a single Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner would not solve the problem. “The names of influential BJP leaders whose money is invested here, resulting in the exploitation of students, must be made public,” he said. Mr. Bharadwaj also said the Central government must build hostels for students in the area. “Until hostels are constructed and allotted to students, the government should pay students’ PG fees. Only then will the government have an incentive to build hostels quickly, otherwise, it will not,” he said. ‘Justice for victims’ Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav staged a sit-in at the site of the collapse, demanding justice for the injured and the families of those killed. Mr. Yadav alleged that corruption in the BJP-led system was responsible for the collapse. He questioned who had permitted repairs to be carried out in the basement of the 50-year-old, five-storey building without safety arrangements after the basement was flooded, and alleged administrative irresponsibility and corruption. “The Congress’s protest against the Rekha Gupta government will continue till strict action is taken against the culprits and justice is done to the injured and the families of the deceased students. headline: BRICS Summit 2026: Delhi, Central govt offices to remain closed on September 11
text: NEW DELHI: Central government offices in Delhi and New Delhi, as well as Delhi government offices, autonomous bodies and public sector undertakings under the Delhi government, will remain closed on September 11, in view of the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit being hosted in the national capital. The Delhi government declared September 11, which falls on a Friday, as a holiday through a notification issued by its general administration department on Thursday. The decision was taken in view of the BRICS Summit and the arrangements connected with it, news agency PTI reported. According to an official memorandum issued by the ministry of personnel, public grievances and pensions, the closure of central government offices was decided considering the scale of the event, the extensive logistical arrangements required and the need to minimise inconvenience to the public. The ministry has directed that the decision be communicated to all concerned, news agency ANI reported. The Delhi government notification said the holiday would apply to all government offices, autonomous bodies and public sector undertakings under the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. September 12 and 13 fall on Saturday and Sunday, respectively. The order for central government offices states: “Recognising the magnitude of this event, the substantial logistical arrangements involved, and to minimise inconvenience to the general public, it has been decided to keep the Central Government offices located in Delhi/New Delhi closed on Friday, the September 11, 2026 (September 12 and 13, 2026 being Saturday and Sunday respectively).” BRICS Summit from Sept 11 to 13 The BRICS Business Forum and the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit are scheduled to be held from September 11 to 13 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, ANI reported. The summit is expected to be attended by leaders from around 30 BRICS member and partner countries, along with heads of international organisations and business representatives from BRICS nations, including India. The move to keep government offices closed comes as authorities step up security and traffic arrangements in the capital ahead of the summit. Delhi Police has intensified security around 10 hotels designated for visiting dignitaries and delegates, while 22 diversion points have been earmarked to facilitate their movement. The summit-related arrangements are also expected to involve traffic restrictions and diversions as authorities prepare for the movement of visiting delegations in the city.
