headline: PIL against school curbs on outsiders dismissed amid CJP campaign
text: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has dismissed a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) challenging restrictions imposed by the Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh education departments on the entry of journalists, YouTubers, social-media personalities and civil-society members in government schools. The dismissal of the PIL plea assumes significance in the wake of a recent assault on Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists in Rajasthan during their inspection of a government school as part of the “school thik karo” campaign. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed the PIL filed by Priya Mishra. “We are not inclined to entertain the writ petition filed under Article 32 of the Constitution of India,” the bench said in its September 1 order. The PIL had also challenged curbs placed on photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live-streaming from government schools. It had specifically challenged an August 16 circular issued by Rajasthan’s director of secondary education, requiring outsiders to obtain prior permission from the principal before entering the premises of a government school. According to the circular, prior written permission for photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and livestreaming is also needed. The plea had also challenged the August 19 order issued by the district basic education officer, Ayodhya, directing that outsiders, YouTubers and persons associated with social media should not enter council schools or take photographs or videos without permission from the competent authority. It had said similar orders have been issued in other districts of Uttar Pradesh as well.

headline: Pune activist Vidyanand Bapat assaulted over opposition to loud DJs at Ganpati processions- Moneycontrol.com
text: Pune activist Vidyanand Bapat was allegedly assaulted on Thursday while speaking to reporters about his campaign against the use of high-decibel DJ systems and loudspeakers during Ganpati processions. A video of the incident shows a man approaching Bapat as he was interacting with the media and allegedly slapping him. The alleged attacker has been identified as Santosh Chavan, according to News18. Pune Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar assured that strict action would be taken against the person accused of assaulting the activist. It may not be possible to achieve this 100% in the beginning, but it can be achieved," he said. The chief minister’s remarks came as the alleged assault triggered condemnation over the manner in which Bapat was confronted for his position on DJ systems during Ganpati celebrations. NCP (SP) leader Rohit Pawar also criticised the attack and said disagreements over the use of DJs during Ganeshotsav should be settled through discussion rather than physical aggression. “Differences of opinion can exist; if their stance doesn’t convince you, oppose it ideologically and articulate your stance with thoughtfulness, just as Bapat does. However, resorting to thuggery in this manner is absolutely unacceptable," Pawar said. Pawar called on the police to initiate appropriate legal proceedings against the alleged attacker and ensure Bapat’s safety. “The police administration must take appropriate legal action under relevant sections against the village thug who attacked Bapat and provide protection to Vidyanand Bapat," Pawar said. The police action followed concerns over Bapat’s security immediately after the alleged assault. headline: Sanitation workers to receive ₹50 as food allowance daily
text: The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order for the payment of a food allowance of ₹50 every day to 24,264 conservancy workers of the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC). The decision follows a survey in which 92% of conservancy workers expressed a preference for the allowance instead of the meals currently supplied to them, according to the GCC. Only for working days The order was issued to provide “food allowance of ₹50 per worker per day, calculated only for the days attended for work, to be added to the salary every month and paid in cash as an alternative to the meals currently provided, to all 24,264 sanitation workers working under the Greater Chennai Corporation’s self-help group sanitation workers and private cleaning agencies — Urbaser Sumeet and Chennai Enviro Solutions Private Limited.” The annual expenditure for the allowance was estimated at ₹44.28 crore and will be met from GCC funds, according to the order issued by the GCC’s Deputy Commissioner (Revenue and Finance), following directions from the GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran. Food quality The Government Order issued on September 21 stated that when implementing the meals scheme through the contractor firm, “various complaints were received from sanitation workers, Project Management Consultants (PMC), and Corporation officials regarding the quality of food provided, failure to distribute food at the specified time, hygiene deficiencies prevailing in kitchens, substandard raw materials, and shortcomings in the quality and maintenance of utensils.” The order further stated that a survey and opinion poll was conducted among sanitation workers of Zones 1 to 15 regarding whether the meals currently provided should continue. “In that, approximately 92% of workers stated that instead of the meals provided to them, a food allowance should be given in cash, and that it would be very useful for them,” the order read. text: ANI 27 Sep 2026, 10:31 GMT+10 Chennai (Tamil Nadu) [India], September 27 (ANI): Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Sunday paid tribute to all those who died in last year's Karur stampede, a tragedy that claimed 41 lives and left an enduring emotional scar on the state. headline: ‘A Wound That Does Not Heal’: Vijay Remembers 41 Karur Stampede Victims a Year On
text: ‘A Wound That Does Not Heal’: Vijay Remembers 41 Karur Stampede Victims a Year On A year after 41 people lost their lives in a stampede at his political rally in Karur, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay described the tragedy as “a wound that does not heal, a pain that does not fade”. In a tribute posted on X on Sunday, Vijay remembered the victims and expressed solidarity with their families, saying the grief remained deeply felt across Karur, Tamil Nadu and his party. The stampede occurred on September 27, 2025, during a rally addressed by the actor and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) chief. Several others were injured. ‘Comfort, Support and Refuge’ Recalling the date, Vijay said the tragedy had left a lasting wound in his life and in the lives of those affected. headline: Academic freedom issues threaten India’s global standing
text: INDIA Academic freedom issues threaten India’s global standing Academic experts say India’s classification as “severely restricted” in the latest global academic freedom report could affect India’s international standing in higher education, potentially making collaboration in some fields more difficult and affecting efforts to build international research partnerships and attract overseas students and faculty. The latest Free to Think 2026 report by Scholars at Risk (SAR) says academic freedom in India was “severely restricted” between July 2025 and June 2026, and placed it in the same category as Hong Kong, Pakistan, Indonesia, Ukraine and the occupied West Bank. The report says the federal government increased its influence over higher education through the higher education regulator the University Grants Commission (UGC), affecting university governance, leadership appointments and academic decisions. It also claims that university authorities limited free discussion by cancelling events, dismissing professors and restricting student protests. The SAR report also points out that the governments now play a bigger role in appointing university leaders, including vice-chancellors. As a result, decisions that were once made by universities themselves are increasingly influenced by outside authorities. Increased ideological influence On India’s classification as “severely restricted” in the latest academic freedom assessment, Nandini Sundar, professor of sociology at the Delhi School of Economics at Delhi University, attributed the deterioration to what she described as increasing ideological influence over universities and government institutions. She alleged that political and ideological considerations had influenced some senior academic and research appointments and the content of teaching and research. She told University World News: “Effects could be seen in areas including university courses, syllabi, school textbooks and recruitment.” “If you have ideologically driven people, they’ve been messing around with the courses, with syllabi, with NCERT (National Council of Educational Research and Training) textbooks, and with recruitment to universities. So, everything follows from that,” she said. The report says ideological clashes involving student groups, especially the right-wing Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, or ABVP (student wing of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh nationalist organisation), and the left-wing All India Students’ Association (AISA) and National Students’ Union of India, or NSUI (the student wing of the main opposition Indian National Congress party), turned many campuses into political flashpoints. headline: ‘Will protest if constructionon Pallikaranai Marshland is not halted’
text: PMK leader Anbumani Ramadoss on Friday opposed the construction of the three-km-long compound wall and a walkway on the Pallikaranai Marshland, as part of ‘Neithal Restoration and Conservation Work’. He urged the Tamil Nadu government to halt the work, remove the structures that have already been built, and restore those areas, failing which the PMK would launch massive protests. He condemned the TVK government for continuing the project initiated by the DMK, and said it could cause flooding in the area. He said that two immediate measures need to be implemented to restore the Pallikaranai Marshland. “The encroachments on the marshland, which has shrunk from 15,000 acres to just 1,750 acres today, should be removed, and its boundaries should be demarcated and notified officially. Instead, the DMK government began an effort that would further destroy the marshland,” Dr. Anbumani said. He further said, “While the Tamil Nadu government should be removing encroachments from the Pallikaranai Marshland, it is itself encroaching upon it by constructing a 3-km-long, 6-foot-high retaining wall and, inside it, a 2-km-long walkway. Both the retaining wall and the walkway have been constructed in a manner that obstructs the natural flow of water. As a result, rainwater generated by rainfall in the area and in other parts of Chennai will not be able to flow into the Pallikaranai marshland, causing waterlogging and flooding.” Published - September 05, 2026 12:52 am IST

headline: Man Arrested In Mumbai For Issuing Death Threats To Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav
text: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The Crime Branch on Friday arrested a man in Mumbai for allegedly sending a death threat to Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on WhatsApp. The threatening message was sent to the Dial-112 helpline WhatsApp number operated from the Radio Headquarters in Bhadbhada. According to reports, the message was received on Wednesday around 11.30 am on the Dial-112 WhatsApp number. The sender allegedly mentioned the Chief Minister by name and threatened to kill him, claiming that he would not survive for long. The message also contained other objectionable remarks against the Chief Minister. The sender later edited the message twice and added further threatening remarks before finally deleting it. However, Dial-112 personnel had taken a screenshot of the message and saved it as evidence. Following the incident, senior officials were informed and the Radio Headquarters submitted a complaint to the Bhopal Police. The complaint was forwarded to the Crime Branch, which registered a case against the sender on Thursday and launched an investigation. Crime Branch officials conducted a technical investigation into the mobile number from which the WhatsApp message was sent. The investigation indicated that the number was being used from Mumbai. A police team reached Mumbai on Friday and arrested the accused. The accused is being brought to Bhopal, where police will question him about the motive behind the threat, the claims made in the message and whether anyone else was involved in sending it. Police have preserved the screenshot of the threatening message along with other technical evidence as part of the investigation.

headline: India-US Trade Deal Becomes Flashpoint as Farmers' Delhi March is Halted
text: India-US Trade Deal Becomes Flashpoint as Farmers' Delhi March is Halted Haryana Police stopped farmers from proceeding to Delhi during the 228-km Kisan Bachao Padyatra. The farmers are protesting the proposed India-US trade deal and demanding a legal guarantee for MSP. Haryana Police stopped farmers from proceeding to Delhi on Sunday as part of the 228-km ‘Kisan Bachao Padyatra’, setting up multiple barricades at the Khanauri inter-state border between Punjab and Haryana. The march, led by the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (Non-Political), was planned from Data Singh Wala village on the Haryana-Punjab border to Jantar Mantar in Delhi. A farmers’ panchayat was scheduled for August 29. Three rounds of talks between farmer representatives and Haryana government officials failed to resolve the issue. SKM (Non-Political) leader Jagjit Singh Dallewal said officials offered a meeting with the Haryana chief minister, but the farmers rejected it. Dallewal says, “Our main issue is the India-US trade deal. CM saab is not capable of addressing this issue. Nothing will come out of a meeting with him. headline: Farmers' group All India Kisan Sabha alleges eviction of 25,000 forest dwellers in Tamil Nadu is illegal
text: The All India Kisan Sabha has alleged that attempts to evict forest dwellers from 5,072.653 hectares in the Meghamalai-Varusanadu area of Tamil Nadu are illegal. AIKS says the area, part of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve in Theni district, is home to about 25,000 people across nine village panchayats. The organisation says many affected residents are Adivasis, Dalits and members of Most Backward Classes who meet the Forest Rights Act’s definition of traditional forest dwellers. AIKS has demanded that the Tamil Nadu government implement the Forest Rights Act in the region and urged the Supreme Court to uphold the law “in its true spirit”. Farmers’ group All India Kisan Sabha has alleged that ongoing attempts to evict traditional forest dwellers from 5,072.653 hectares of land in the Meghamalai-Varusanadu area of Tamil Nadu are illegal. In a statement issued on September 2, 2026, AIKS said the eviction attempts reflected the “colonial and anti-democratic legacy” of forest governance in India. The area, located in Theni district, is part of the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve. The organisation said the affected people included Adivasis, Dalits and members of Most Backward Classes, and alleged that they were being branded as “encroachers” despite long histories of habitation and cultivation in the area. AIKS said it was “of the firm opinion” that the case represented a systemic and deliberate violation of the law by the state. “Branding peasants as ‘encroachers’, the Tamil Nadu forest department is deploying every dirty trick in the book to evict toiling peasants from this terrain,” the statement said. “The fact that the major chunk of the affected peasants belongs to Adivasis, Dalits and Most Backward Classes is a mirror of the brutal forest governance regime implemented by the Indian ruling classes,” it added. headline: Activist arrested over remarks against Maharashtra minister Chandrakant Patil
text: Activist arrested over remarks against Maharashtra minister Chandrakant Patil Influencer and activist Santosh Pandit has been raising civic issues and posting videos on social media Social media influencer and activist Santosh Pandit was arrested from his residence in Pune in the early hours of Thursday for allegedly using derogatory language against Maharashtra minister Chandrakant Patil, police said. Pandit has been raising civic issues and posting videos on social media. The arrest came a day after Pandit confronted another ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Gopichand Padalkar for allegedly not having the mandatory high-security registration plate on his vehicle. The confrontation was recorded and circulated on social media. An audio clip purportedly involving Padalkar’s associates abusing Pandit later surfaced online. In March, a woman filed a complaint accusing Pandit of allegedly abusing her, making objectionable comments about her attire, filming her without her consent, and behaving in a sexually inappropriate and intimidating manner during the coverage of a protest. Sunil Pandey, a BJP leader, lodged a complaint against Pandit over his remarks against Patil on August 30. Pandit released a video showing his detention and alleged that police treat activists unfairly. In the video, Pandit is seen handing over his keys to an associate and his mobile phone to police before being taken into custody. Pandit asked chief minister Devendra Fadnavis to take note of how the police treated an activist. “If the police can knock on my door at 1am and take me away, what should a common man expect? Is this the way the administration wants to treat citizens who raise questions?” Pandit said in the video. Runal Mulla, a police officer, said Pandit was taken into custody over his remarks against Patil as per the First Information Report Pandey lodged. On August 30, police registered a case against two people, including Pandit, on Pandey’s complaint. Police said a video Pandit posted on the social media account “Rajkaran Express” contained derogatory, abusive, and allegedly defamatory remarks about Patil. He was booked under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections 356, 296, and 3(5) related to criminal defamation, public obscenity, and joint criminal liability (common intention).

headline: MCD orders inspection of all PG hostels in Delhi after High Court directive | Mint
text: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has ordered an inspection of all paying guest (PG) hostels under its jurisdiction after the Delhi High Court directed the civic body to complete the exercise within a week. The inspections will examine permissions, building bye-law compliance and the number of students staying in each premises. The direction follows the court’s September 7 order in a public interest litigation titled ‘Aniket Gupta Vs. MCD’. An MCD circular issued by the Additional Commissioner (Engineering) instructed executive engineers (Building) across all zones to conduct inspections in their respective areas and submit signed, comprehensive reports to Building headquarters by September 10. According to the prescribed inspection format, officials have to record the zone, division and address of each PG hostel, along with right of way, number of floors, number of rooms and the sanctioned building plan. The report will also include the number of occupants or students living at each premises. Engineers have been asked to establish whether occupancy or building plan approval has been obtained and whether any regularisation has been secured. They must also check if structural stability certificates and Delhi Fire Service no-objection certificates have been obtained. The inspection will additionally determine whether the activity being carried out at a premises is permissible under the Master Plan of Delhi and whether conversion charges applicable under the plan have been paid. Any violations noticed during the inspection are to be recorded along with remarks. The civic body’s exercise comes amid increased scrutiny of accommodation facilities following the collapse of a building in Satya Niketan, where six people died. The Delhi government has directed inspections of nearby PG accommodations and other buildings, with sealing ordered where violations are found. The MCD circular states that the data collected through the inspections will be incorporated into an affidavit to be filed before the Delhi High Court within 10 days. The exercise has therefore been given a tight reporting schedule, with zonal executive engineers required to submit their findings to headquarters by September 10. The concerned Zonal Additional Commissioners have been directed to personally monitor and supervise the inspections. The circular, issued with the prior approval of the municipal commissioner, asks officials to accord the exercise top priority. The inspection will identify properties with missing permissions or certificates and establish where building bye-laws, Master Plan requirements or other conditions have been breached. headline: Zilla Parishads reorganised in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitharama Raju districts of Andhra
text: The Andhra Pradesh government has issued orders for administrative division and restructuring of Zilla Parishads following the formation of new districts. As per the new directives, the Zilla Parishad offices will now function from their respective new district headquarters in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts. The restructuring process addresses administrative bottlenecks that arose after new districts were carved out in April 2022. At that time, Zilla Parishad elections had concluded under the unified setup, and administrative hurdles initially prevented the division of elected bodies to match the new geographical boundaries. Consequently, elected panels continued functioning on a unified district basis, attended jointly by Collectors and officials from Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts. With the current term of the local body governing councils scheduled to expire on September 24, the government accelerated the division. The existing staff members are being reallocated across the three newly created district administrations, based on population density and the relative count of mandals. According to the allocation framework, Anakapalli district—comprising 24 mandals—will receive 60% of the existing personnel. Alluri Sitharama Raju district, encompassing 11 mandals, has been allocated 30% of the workforce, while Visakhapatnam, which now retains four rural mandals, accounts for the remaining 10%. The district authorities noted that independent institutional spaces are critical for streamlining rural development schemes and ensuring localised governance. “Preparations are being done to set up full-fledged administrative machinery at the respective headquarters before the incumbent board’s tenure officially expires later this month,” a senior official told The Hindu on Tuesday. headline: Investigation Must Come First: DK Shivakumar on KPSC Row
text: He also underlined the need for an investigation into the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) examination recruitment row Bengaluru: Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Sunday said the state government was taking steps to reform the education sector and provide greater opportunities to students, while dismissing the BJP's demand for the resignation of Minister Priyank Kharge. On the BJP's demand for Cabinet Minister Priyank Kharge's resignation and allegations raised by R Ashoka, CM DK Shivakumar told reporters here, "...Let them say whatever they want. He also underlined the need for an investigation into the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) examination recruitment row. "...I am not in a hurry. For the development of this state, there should be discussions about farmers, discussions about students, and discussions about exams. headline: ABVP members clash with police during protest outside MCD headquarters over building collapse
text: The Delhi police on Sunday detained at least 15 members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) after they allegedly broke through the gates of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) headquarters while staging a dharna on Sunday evening. The protesters sought the resignation of the MCD Commissioner in connection with the collapse of a five-storey building housing a boys’ hostel in Satya Niketan, in which four persons were killed. According to a police statement, around 150–200 ABVP members gathered near the Civic Centre to protest against the building collapse. “The protesters entered the Civic Centre through Gate No. 5 and sat outside the main building, raising slogans and protesting against the functioning of the MCD. Subsequently, some protesters attempted to forcibly enter the main Civic Centre building, resulting in jostling with police personnel. Around 15 people were detained and taken to Kamla Market police station, where action under the Delhi Police Act is being initiated. The remaining gathering was dispersed by the police. The situation is presently under control.” Speaking on the incident, ABVP national general secretary Virendra Singh Solanki said, “The Satya Niketan incident is deeply tragic and alarming. There must be an impartial probe into this collapse, strict action against those responsible, and immediate justice for the affected students. Accountability must be fixed for officials who failed to ensure student safety, and the MCD Commissioner should resign immediately.” Stepping up demands The protests come ahead of the Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) election later this month, with organisations stepping up demands for accountability in student accommodations across the Capital. National Students’ Union of India president Vinod Jakhar said, “It is extremely painful to see students suffering like this. Several students were trapped under the debris, and every minute was critical. The police arrived nearly an hour after the incident and the NDRF around two hours later. This raises a very serious question: if emergency agencies take hours to respond when students’ lives are at risk, who will take responsibility?” The Delhi State Committee of the Students’ Federation of India also staged a protest at the Delhi Secretariat, demanding a comprehensive safety audit of PGs and student accommodations and strict action against illegal and unsafe constructions. “The absence of effective regulation and accountability has allowed unsafe buildings and exploitative PG and building mafias to proliferate across student residential areas.” Published - September 07, 2026 01:12 am IST

headline: 28-year-old man killed after Tamil Nadu minister Jagadeeswari’s car hits 2-wheeler in Chennai
text: CHENNAI: A 28-year-old man was killed after a car belonging to Tamil Nadu Social Welfare Minister Jagadeeswari hit his two-wheeler on the Trichy-Chennai National Highway near Kattankulathur around 12.30am on Monday. Police arrested the car driver and registered a case of rash and negligent driving. Iraiyanbu, a resident of Kattankulathur in Chengalpattu district, was returning home on a Honda Dio after attending a temple festival. Police said he was crossing the highway near Kattankulathur junction when the Maruti Ertiga hit his two-wheeler. He was thrown off the vehicle and died at the spot. The car was registered in the minister’s name. Jagadeeswari, who was travelling from Virudhunagar to Chennai in her official vehicle to attend the Assembly session on Monday, was travelling ahead of the Ertiga. Her relatives were travelling in the private car, which was following the minister’s convoy. Personnel in the escort vehicle alerted the traffic police and arranged for the victim’s body to be shifted. The Guduvanchery Traffic Investigation Wing police sent the body to Chengalpattu District Government Hospital for postmortem. Police seized the Ertiga and arrested its driver, Chinna Agni, 28, of Madurai. A case was registered against him under sections relating to rash and negligent driving on a public road and causing death by negligence. Police were questioning him and examining CCTV footage and other evidence to establish how the accident occurred. headline: Delhi Minister accuses Kejriwal of shielding extortionists who assault govt staff
text: New Delhi, Sep 27 : Delhi Cabinet Minister Parvesh Verma has levelled serious charges against former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, alleging that his associates systematically engage in extortion and violence against government employees in the capital. In a strongly worded social media post, the minister claimed that Kejriwal's "goons" forcibly extract money from the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and other government officials, and that when the police arrest the culprits, Kejriwal himself steps in to defend them. Verma questioned Kejriwal directly, "Kejriwal-ji, why are you supporting an extortionist who forcibly extracts money from MCD or government officials?" He also asked him if he will support such "goons" while visiting the area. He accompanied the post with a video that purportedly shows an MCD employee being beaten by one of Kejriwal's associates. The minister described the incident as evidence of a larger pattern of lawlessness that has been allowed to flourish under the Aam Aadmi Party's influence. The allegations paint a disturbing picture of a former chief minister allegedly using his political clout to protect those who terrorise public servants. Government employees, who are meant to serve the public without fear or favour, are being subjected to physical assault and financial extortion by individuals linked to Kejriwal's network. Instead of condemning such criminal behaviour, Kejriwal is accused of intervening to shield the perpetrators once the police take action. This conduct, if true, represents a complete betrayal of the principles of good governance that Kejriwal once claimed to uphold. A leader who rose to power on the slogan of "honesty" and "clean politics" is now being accused of providing cover to extortionists who prey on ordinary government workers. Such actions not only demoralise the administrative machinery but also erode public trust in the system. The repeated pattern of violence followed by political protection raises serious questions about the culture of impunity that appears to have been cultivated. When elected leaders choose to stand by goons rather than by law-abiding employees, it sends a dangerous message that muscle power and political patronage can override the rule of law. Parvesh Verma's charge, backed by the video evidence he shared, demands a clear and accountable response from Kejriwal.

headline: Delhi CM backs Election Commission over SIR amid allegations of Opposition
text: Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Sunday rejected the Opposition’s allegations against the Election Commission, saying the revision of electoral rolls to remove deceased voters, duplicate entries and other invalid names was being dubbed “vote chori”. Addressing a press conference at Jan Seva Sadan, Ms. Gupta said eligible voters remained on the rolls. “Everyone has the right to ask questions in a democracy, but such questions should be based on facts,” she said. Her remarks came amid demands by Opposition parties and organisations for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar following an investigation by The Indian Express. The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions concerning the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The investigation also reported that the two Commissioners had objected to changes linked to Form 6, describing them as “illegal” and “unauthorised”. The revised process sought information on whether an applicant or their parents were on the electoral roll during the last SIR in the early 2000s. Ms. Gupta said there had been no change in Form 6 and that, under the SIR, a separate declaration had been provided along with the form, according to the Election Commission. Delhi Bharatiya Janata Party president and Union Minister Harsh Malhotra asked booth-level agents to coordinate with booth-level officers to ensure every eligible voter is enrolled. He said no name would be deleted without a hearing. More protests planned Meanwhile, the Delhi Congress plans to stage a protest outside Nirvachan Sadan on Monday over the issue. It will be the party’s second protest, after a demonstration on September 25. The Cockroach Janta Party has also warned of a nationwide agitation, including “Jantar Mantar 2.0”, if Mr. Kumar does not step down. headline: 'How was leak overlooked?' Uttarakhand Congress chief demands probe into Pipalkoti tunnel tragedy
text: NEW DELHI: Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee president Ganesh Godiyal on Saturday criticised the Pushkar Singh Dhami government over the Pipalkoti tunnel accident in Chamoli district, questioning how a reported leak at the site was allegedly overlooked despite workers claiming it had persisted for some time. The criticism came as the death toll in the under-construction THDC tunnel accident rose to eight, with two workers still trapped and rescue operations continuing. Godiyal said workers injured in the accident had told him that water leakage had been occurring at the same spot for a considerable period before the tunnel was inundated by a massive surge of water. "When I spoke to the injured, I learned that a leak had been occurring for quite some time at the very spot where the incident took place. How this was overlooked or why there was such apathy towards it is a matter for further investigation. NTPC provided Rs one lakh, but that amount is insufficient. I will discuss what arrangements can be made to ensure the families can sustain themselves properly," Godiyal told ANI. He also questioned the compensation announced for the families of those killed in the accident. "The CM announced compensation of Rs four lakh, though I believe that amount is not sufficient," he said. Congress leader Harikrishna Bhatt echoed the criticism, saying the compensation did not reflect the value of human life and calling for safety audits across all ongoing infrastructure projects in the state. "Regarding the announced compensation of Rs 4 lakh, a human life cannot be valued at merely Rs 4 lakh," Bhatt said. "Safety audits should have been conducted for all such ongoing projects. The entire population of Uttarakhand is bearing the brunt of these disasters which are man-made. headline: LG Sandhu hoists Tricolour at Lok Niwas on 80th Independence Day
text: LG Sandhu hoists Tricolour at Lok Niwas on 80th Independence Day Lieutenant Governor Sardar Taranjit Singh Sandhu hoisted the National Flag at Lok Niwas on the 80th Independence Day, with freedom fighters, their families, RWA representatives, youth icons, students, and city residents in attendance. The police contingent presented the National Salute. Delhi Assembly Speaker Vijender Gupta hoisted the national flag at his official residence on the 80th Independence Day, while Delhi ministers, including Ashish Sood, hoisted the flag in his constituency. Manjinder Singh Sirsa, along with Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra, hoisted the national flag at the state BJP headquarters. The Lieutenant Governor paid tribute to freedom fighters and nation-builders. He referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Independence Day address, highlighting the vision of ‘Shakti Ki Saptdhara ’-seven streams of growth including manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, the green and blue economy, and soft power. Sandhu stated these areas are relevant to Delhi and urged residents to contribute to the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047. The LG outlined the objective of making Delhi a model of excellence, safety, and civic pride. He described his long association with the city and called service to Delhi a responsibility. He said the administration must work to improve convenience, dignity, and well-being for all residents. The LG said Delhi’s governance should follow the Prime Minister’s principle of inclusive development. He stressed the importance of coordination among the Union Government, Delhi Government, municipal bodies, neighbouring states, and citizens to address challenges. Key priorities include cleaning the Yamuna, reducing air pollution, housing, healthcare, safety, traffic management, and heritage restoration. Addressing the city’s youth, the LG said they remain the ultimate drivers. He said the youth are key to Delhi’s future and highlighted the importance of civic responsibility. headline: PoK people would've joined India before 2019: Omar on Independence Day

headline: T.N. parties demand Assembly resolution against Union labour codes
text: Political parties including the Congress, MDMK, VCK, and the Left on Monday urged the state government to adopt a resolution in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly rejecting the Union government’s labour codes and safeguarding the state’s legislations and 39 welfare boards meant for unorganised sector workers. headline: Karnataka CM Shivakumar encourages students to pursue studies abroad and become job creators
text: Bengaluru: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Sunday urged students to study abroad and become job creators, not job seekers. He was speaking after launching the Skill Development Department's 'Study Abroad 2026' programme here. The programme, inaugurated at Palace Grounds, offers students opportunities to pursue higher education at foreign universities, with more than 80 universities participating and over 300 subjects on offer. "Our talented human resources are unmatched by those in any other state in the country. We want our children to learn at the global level. We desire that they should not merely become employees, but become employers," Shivakumar said. He said the government had opened a new avenue for overseas education and stressed that investment in knowledge was the best asset. "Human beings have limitations, but knowledge has no boundaries. Access to global-level education makes people mentally stronger," he said. Shivakumar said 3,145 students had been selected to study at foreign universities following an agreement with the University of Queensland. He said scholarships were being offered by various government departments, while banks were providing education loans of up to Rs 2 crore. "More than 80 universities are participating in this programme, offering opportunities to study more than 300 subjects," he said. The CM highlighted Bengaluru's large pool of skilled professionals, saying the city had 2.6 million IT professionals, compared with 1.6 million in Silicon Valley. Karnataka, he said, produced more than one lakh engineers and 13,940 doctors annually. Referring to leaders including Mahatma Gandhi and B R Ambedkar, Shivakumar said studying abroad had helped them acquire knowledge that they later used to contribute to the country. "Your future is the future of the state, and your strength is the strength of the country. Students are our assets. The entire world is watching us. India is being viewed through Bengaluru and Karnataka," he said. He urged students not to forget their roots, parents and teachers. "You should not forget your roots. If you forget them, you will not achieve success. Therefore, you should not forget your parents and teachers," he said. Shivakumar also said the government had decided to allow teachers to use the prefix 'Tr' before their names as a mark of respect. headline: Couple Detained by Police for Attempting to Breach CM Vijay Convoy
text: Chennai: A couple who attempted to breach Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's convoy near the Secretariat here was detained by the police, an official said on Thursday. The couple, according to the police, were said to be the parents of a custodial death victim. The duo attempted to break through the police security in a frantic bid to stop the chief minister's convoy, apparently to petition him. However, the police overpowered the couple and detained them, the official said. "They suddenly ran into the security perimeter of the chief minister's moving fleet but were immediately chased and detained by the police for questioning," the official said. Preliminary enquiry by the police reveal that the parents and relatives of a young engineering graduate of Manamadurai in Sivaganga district who allegedly died in police custody in March this year have been protesting seeking justice for him. Due to the sudden commotion, Chief Minister Vijay's vehicle briefly slowed down as the police frisked the duo away.

headline: IAS officer suspended after arrest over KPSC recruitment exam row
text: IAS officer suspended after arrest over KPSC recruitment exam row The Karnataka government has suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar after his arrest in a case involving alleged corruption in recruitment conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission The Karnataka government has suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar after his arrest in a case involving alleged corruption in recruitment conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission. Gangwar, a 2016 batch IAS officer serving as Director of MSME, was arrested on August 29 in a case registered at Vidhana Soudha police station. He had earlier served as Controller of Examinations at the KPSC. The suspension follows investigations by the Criminal Investigation Department and the Directorate of Enforcement. In a letter dated August 23, the ED’s Bengaluru Zonal Office told the state government that material seized under Section 17 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act indicated that “instances of corruption were prevalent in the recruitment processes conducted by the Karnataka Public Service Commission, which is solely attributable to the Controller of Examinations of the KPSC (i.e.) Sri Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, IAS”. The criminal case, registered as Crime No. 89/2026 at Vidhana Soudha police station, was filed under Section 318(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Section 10 of the Karnataka Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Corruption and Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2023. After his arrest, Gangwar “was produced before the jurisdictional Magistrate and was remanded to Judicial Custody on 30.08.2026”. He was taken into police custody on August 31 for further investigation. The government said his detention for more than 48 hours amounted to a “gross violation of Rule 3 of All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968”. An order issued by T. Mahanthesh, Under Secretary to Government in the Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms, said: “THEREFORE, in exercise of the powers conferred under Rule 3(2) read with 3(3) of the All India Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969, Sri Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, IAS (KN: 2016), is placed under suspension with immediate effect and until further orders, pending further investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department.” Gangwar will receive a subsistence allowance under Rule 4 of the All India Service (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969, during his suspension. The government has also directed that “the officer shall not leave the headquarters under any circumstances without the written permission of the State Government”.

headline: Supreme Court Dismisses PIL Challenging Rajasthan, UP Curbs On Journalists, YouTubers In Government Schools
text: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has dismissed a PIL challenging restrictions imposed by the Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh education departments on the entry of journalists, YouTubers, social-media personalities and civil-society members in government schools. The dismissal of the public interest litigation (PIL) plea assumes significance in the wake of a recent assault on Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists in Rajasthan during their inspection of a government school as part of the "school thik karo" campaign. A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe dismissed the PIL filed by Priya Mishra. "We are not inclined to entertain the writ petition filed under Article 32 of the Constitution of India," the bench said in its September 1 order. The PIL had also challenged curbs placed on photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and live-streaming from government schools. It had specifically challenged an August 16 circular issued by Rajasthan's director of secondary education, requiring outsiders to obtain prior permission from the principal before entering the premises of a government school. Also Watch: According to the circular, prior written permission for photography, videography, interviews, audio recording and livestreaming is also needed. The plea had also challenged the August 19 order issued by the district basic education officer, Ayodhya, directing that outsiders, YouTubers and persons associated with social media should not enter council schools or take photographs or videos without permission from the competent authority. It had said similar orders have been issued in other districts of Uttar Pradesh as well. headline: 'They wanted to kill me': TMC MLA's car attacked in Kolkata
text: TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh alleges his car was attacked in Kolkata and Hooghly, accusing the BJP of political violence, while the BJP dismisses the claims as a staged drama for publicity. Key Points - TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh reported his car was attacked in Kolkata with hammers, and a gun was aimed at his security personnel. - This incident follows a similar alleged attack on his vehicle in Hooghly district the previous day, where stones and eggs were hurled. - Ghosh has filed a police complaint and accused the BJP of creating a 'jungle raj' in West Bengal, with police allegedly looking the other way. - BJP leaders, including MLA Dipanjan Chakraborty and spokesperson Debajit Sarkar, have dismissed Ghosh's claims as a staged drama for publicity. Trinamool Congress MLA Kunal Ghosh, aligned with the Mamata Banerjee camp, on Sunday alleged that his car was attacked while he was on his way to a programme in his Beliaghata constituency in east Kolkata. Allegations Of Political Violence Ghosh claimed motorcycle-borne attackers smashed his car's windshield with hammers while one of them trained a gun at his security personnel in the Narkeldanga area. Stones and eggs were allegedly hurled at Ghosh's car in Hooghly district on Saturday when he was going to attend a meeting of Banerjee. "Yesterday there was an attack on me at Uttarpara. Today, they wanted to kill me," Ghosh told reporters showing broken glass shards of the windshield to reporters. Ghosh said he has lodged a complaint at a police station here. After the alleged Uttarpara attack, Ghosh had taken the vehicle to West Bengal Police headquarters Bhabani Bhavan in Kolkata but was not allowed to enter. Ghosh later filed a complaint at a police station. The TMC MLA alleged, "Under the BJP reign, a 'jungle raj' is prevailing in West Bengal and even an elected MLA is coming under attack by goons of the ruling party with the police looking the other way." Uttarpara BJP MLA Dipanjan Chakraborty on Saturday alleged that Ghosh was staging drama. BJP spokesperson Debajit Sarkar said, "Ghosh is engineering the attacks on his vehicle by instigating TMC workers to get publicity, and none from our party is involved."

headline: Cracks in 10 buildings: Sanjauli, Bhattakufer residents seek halt to tunnel blasting over safety concerns - The Tribune
text: Cracks in 10 buildings: Sanjauli, Bhattakufer residents seek halt to tunnel blasting over safety concerns Demand Central, state governments order an impartial investigation into the alignment of the proposed 4-lane tunnel between Chalounthi and Bhattakufer Residents of Sanjauli and Bhattakufer on Sunday staged a protest against the ongoing tunnel construction work beneath their localities, alleging that blasting and excavation activities had caused cracks in several buildings. The protesters demanded that both the Central and Himachal Pradesh governments order an impartial investigation into the alignment of the proposed four-lane tunnel between Chalounthi and Bhattakufer. They also sought the immediate suspension of tunnelling and blasting activities in the area. Addressing the gathering, Vinit Sharma, councillor of Shanti Vihar Ward, said residents of Sanjauli, Chalounthi, Shanti Vihar, Bhattakufer and nearby areas were facing a serious threat to life and property due to the twin-tunnel project being executed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) through Gabar Construction Company Pvt Ltd and its associate, Bharat Construction Pvt Ltd. He alleged that continuous blasting and vibrations had led to cracks in more than 10 buildings, triggering panic among homeowners and tenants alike. Sharma further claimed that despite repeated representations to NHAI and the construction companies, no safety audit or survey of the affected area had been carried out. “A large population lives directly above and around the proposed tunnel alignment. Many residents have built their homes using lifetime savings and substantial bank loans. Any ground movement, blasting, settlement or geological failure caused by tunnelling could seriously damage these properties and push affected families into financial hardship,” he said. The protesters also demanded an independent verification of the geological and geotechnical suitability of the tunnel alignment before any further work is allowed. They warned of intensifying their agitation if their demands are not addressed promptly.

headline: 'Shouldn't be viewed from political or religious angle': BJP on Saharanpur mosque demolition
text: New Delhi, Sep 5 : The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday stated that the demolition of a mosque at the Saharanpur Collectorate, should not be viewed from a political perspective and that there was no need to look at any building through the lens of religious identity. Earlier in the day, the Uttar Pradesh administration demolished the mosque located within the Collectorate complex in Saharanpur, after the Muslim sideâ€™s appeal was rejected by the court. Addressing a press conference, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said: "The agencies and whichever departments of the government are involved, are taking action in accordance with the law. So, I do not believe there is any need to view this from a political perspective, nor is there any need to look at any building through the lens of its religious identity." "Whatever type of structure it may be, it should only be viewed from the perspective of whether it is legal or illegal," he added. The BJP MP asked Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi to answer "who is allowing such loots" since his party is in coalition in the state. Referring to Mahatma Gandhi's three wise monkeys, he said: "It appears that all those political parties that were roaring and yelling in Delhi over the examination matter, seems to have become Rahul Gandhi's three monkeys when it came to Jharkhand. They are sitting with their eyes shut as if they do not wish to see anything; with their ears covered as if they do not wish to hear anything; with hands over their mouths as if they do not wish to say anything." headline: MP govt transfers six state admin service officers
text: Bhopal, Sep 5 : The Madhya Pradesh government has issued a fresh order transferring six officers of the State Administrative Service to key positions in district panchayats and related administrative roles, officials said on Saturday. The state government has moved officers currently serving in development authorities, collectorates, election offices and existing panchayat posts to new responsibilities across several districts. Accordingly, Narottam Prasad Bhargava of the 2008 recruitment batch, who was serving as Chief Executive Officer of the Gwalior Development Authority, has been transferred as Chief Executive Officer of the Harda District Panchayat. Akhilesh Kumar Jain, also of the 2008 batch, moves from the dual role of Additional Collector of Guna district and competent authority for GAIL (India) Limited at Vijaypur in Guna district to take charge as Chief Executive Officer of the Dhar District Panchayat. Surbhi Tiwari of the 2008 batch, previously posted as Deputy Chief Electoral Officer of Madhya Pradesh in Bhopal, has been appointed Chief Executive Officer of the Vidisha District Panchayat. In a related move, Omprakash Sanodiya of the 2011 batch, who was holding the post of Chief Executive Officer of Vidisha District Panchayat, has been transferred as Additional Mela Officer for the Simhastha fair in Ujjain. This posting is significant in view of the organisational preparations associated with the large religious congregation that draws millions of devotees. Shailendra Singh of the 2011 batch shifts from Chief Executive Officer of Satna District Panchayat to the corresponding position in Datia District Panchayat. Completing the set of changes, Sapna Tripathi of the 2012 batch, earlier serving as Additional Collector of Rewa district, has been posted as Chief Executive Officer of Satna District Panchayat. The changes are expected to strengthen rural local body administration and support upcoming organisational requirements linked to large-scale religious events. Officials have been directed to assume charge of their new responsibilities without delay. The transfers form part of the ongoing administrative realignment aimed at ensuring effective functioning of district panchayats, which play a central role in implementing rural development schemes, local self-governance and coordination with district administrations.

headline: Madhya Pradesh tribal children deaths: Centre, State caution against attributing it to a single pathogen
text: The Union Health Ministry and Madhya Pradesh government have cautioned against attributing all the recent deaths and hospitalisations in some tribal areas of the State, mainly children, to a single pathogen. A senior health official in the Union Health Ministry told The Hindu that investigations are examining the combined role of measles, malaria, respiratory illness, malnutrition, anaemia, dehydration, and delayed access to treatment. Bearing the brunt Earlier this year, a health crisis in remote tribal settlements of Balaghat district raised concerns over infectious diseases, malnutrition and access to healthcare, with children bearing the brunt of the illness. The first cases emerged in late June in villages in Birsa block, where several children developed fever, rashes and other symptoms. At least six child deaths were reported by the district administration in June and August, with officials saying malaria and measles, or even co-infection, were among the principal illnesses identified. Local representatives, however, have claimed a substantially higher toll. The illness has not been confined exclusively to children. Health teams have been screening the wider population in affected tribal settlements, although children and adolescents have accounted for most of the serious cases and reported deaths. More than 100 children received treatment by mid-August, while about 400 children were subsequently reported to have been hospitalised over six weeks. Enhancing surveillance The Centre and State have since intensified surveillance, with Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) teams and a National Joint Outbreak Response Team joining the investigation. Samples have been collected for laboratory testing, while mobile medical units, vaccination drives, malaria control and nutrition interventions have been expanded. Meanwhile, the senior official added that no new measles case has been reported in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat district in the past seven days, indicating an improvement in the situation. “This is following an intensified public health response in tribal areas,” he said, adding that the response was stepped up after reports of fever, fever with rash and associated deaths emerged from tribal habitations of Birsa block in the second week of July. Giving details of the Centre-State action, he said that a National Joint Outbreak Response Team was deployed to Balaghat on August 12, with the Centre, Madhya Pradesh government and national health institutions coordinating the investigation and containment measures. headline: Maujpur Play School Incident: Delhi Govt Orders Premises Sealed, Police Probe Underway | Outlook India

headline: UP trader's murder: Ajay Rai detained on way to meet victim's family, calls action 'oppression'
text: Lucknow, Sep 12 : Uttar Pradesh Congress President Ajay Rai was detained by Barabanki Police on Saturday while he was on his way to meet the family members of utensils trader Vinod Kumar Sahni, whose death in Gonda has triggered political outrage and protests. Rai was stopped by police near the Shahpur toll plaza after arriving in the area with his convoy. According to the information available, police detained the State Congress President at around 12:34 p.m. on Saturday and subsequently took his convoy to the police station. Rai was reportedly travelling with around six vehicles when the police action took place near the toll plaza, leading to a stir in the area. After detaining Rai, the police also took the vehicles accompanying him to the police station. Rai had arrived near the Shahpur toll plaza on Saturday afternoon as he was proceeding to meet the family members of Vinod Kumar Sahni. Speaking to IANS, Ajay Rai strongly objected to the police action and accused the Uttar Pradesh government of deliberately targeting the Congress. "This is complete oppression and injustice taking place here. And this (Bharatiya Janata Party) government is deliberately getting it done. Understand this, we are going to express our condolences at the house of the deceased trader, and we are being stopped." Uttar Pradesh Minister Sanjay Nishad also staged a sit-in protest at the King George's Medical University mortuary in Lucknow late Thursday evening over the death of party worker Vinod Sahni. "A Minister sits on a dharna. If the Minister has even a little morality, then resign. Resign from the Ministerial post and come and fight with us, fight together. We will uproot the government. If they have stopped us, it means they are arresting us," Rai said. The detention comes amid growing outrage over the death of utensils trader Vinod Kumar Sahni in Gonda district. According to police, Vinod was attacked following a dispute over a social media post. Vinod sustained serious injuries in the attack and was undergoing treatment at Lucknow's KGMU. However, he succumbed to his injuries on Thursday. Following his death, police added murder charges to the case and arrested three accused persons. headline: Major GST Seizure at Nizamuddin Railway Station
text: New Delhi, September 12 (Udaipur Kiran) : The Delhi government’s Goods and Services Tax (GST) department, in collaboration with railway authorities, has seized goods valued at approximately ₹5 crore at the Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station. The confiscated items include around 25 tons of copper scrap and an additional 50 tons of various goods, all of which were being transported without the necessary documentation. According to the GST department, they received information indicating that certain goods were being shipped via rail without required documents such as invoices and e-way bills. Acting on this tip-off, the department launched a special operation with the help of railway officials. The shipment, which originated from Renigunta in Andhra Pradesh, arrived at Nizamuddin Station. During the investigation, authorities recovered about 25 tons of copper scrap, estimated to be worth around ₹3 crore. Alongside this, approximately 25 tons of mixed scrap, textiles, and other items were also found, valued at around ₹2 crore. The total estimated value of all seized goods is approximately ₹5 crore. The GST department noted that the seized goods lacked the necessary invoices and e-way bills. They are currently conducting a thorough verification of the goods and associated documents, while also examining compliance with legal requirements related to the transportation of goods under GST laws. Officials from the department emphasized that this operation marks a significant step toward enhancing monitoring of goods transported via both road and rail networks. Through stringent surveillance of railway routes and improved coordination with railway authorities, they aim to identify unaccounted goods, document irregularities, and potential tax evasion cases. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta stated that her government will not tolerate tax evasion and revenue loss under any circumstances. The government aims not only to enforce actions but also to develop an effective system that ensures businesses operate with full transparency and that all due taxes are paid. The Chief Minister further mentioned that monitoring will be intensified across all modes of transport, including railways, to strengthen GST compliance. Ensuring good governance, transparency, and the protection of government revenue are among the Delhi government’s top priorities, and strict action against those involved in tax evasion will continue. text: BENGALURU — The Karnataka Special Investigation Team (SIT) investigating an alleged counterfeit pharmaceutical racket has conducted searches at 10 locations across six states as authorities widen their probe into a suspected interstate network involved in the sourcing, repackaging and distribution of fake medicines. The raids were carried out Friday jointly by the SIT and the Drugs Control Department at locations in Karnataka, Haryana, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh and Telangana. Between 80 and 100 officials and staff were involved in the searches, which targeted offices, properties and other premises linked to companies allegedly connected to the network. In Bengaluru, investigators searched the premises of a pharmaceutical company near Minerva Circle and Lalbagh. Officials are examining medicines allegedly sourced from different locations and subsequently repackaged or distributed through the suspected network. Investigators are also looking into possible international connections, including allegations that counterfeit labels used on the medicines were sourced from outside India. The Food Safety and Drug Administration and local police seized counterfeit medicines estimated to be worth about Rs 5 crore and discovered an alleged unlicensed repackaging operation at a farmhouse in Kurubara Karenahalli, near the Bidadi toll gate. According to investigators, low-cost, substandard or expired medicines were allegedly collected from different states and transferred into new vials. The case has drawn particular concern because some of the allegedly counterfeit medicines were reportedly intended for use in hospital intensive care units. headline: Man detained from Deoghar in bomb threat case | Ranchi News - The Times of India
text: Deoghar: Gujarat Police on Saturday detained a man in his 20s from his maternal grandparents’ house in Deoghar, in connection with alleged email threats concerning the Brics summit venue in Delhi and the Gujarat secretariat in Gandhinagar . Police identified the suspect as Gulshan Kumar Singh, a native of Bihar’s Jamui. Singh was picked up from Town police station area with the assistance of Deoghar police. He was later taken to Gandhinagar on a transit remand obtained from a local court, officers said. Deoghar SP Praveen Pushkar confirmed Singh’s detention and said he had created the email account allegedly used to send the threatening messages. “He has been taken into custody in connection with the email threat and will be interrogated in the case,” Pushkar said. An FIR was registered at a police station in Gandhinagar on Sept 10 in this connection. Gujarat Police had earlier arrested another person in connection with the case and questioned him. Investigators subsequently obtained leads that prompted a team to travel to Deoghar, sources said. Police are examining technical evidence, including the email account allegedly created by Singh, and scrutinising his WhatsApp and other social media accounts to ascertain his role and identify others who may be linked to the threats. Officials from Gujarat and Deoghar police have refrained from disclosing further details, citing the sensitivity of the investigation. They are also probing whether Singh had any direct role in sending the threatening emails or was connected to a wider network. Police activity increased in Deoghar following the arrival of the Gujarat team. Officers said the exact nature of Singh’s involvement and the possible network behind the threats would become clear only after questioning and analysis of the digital evidence are completed.

headline: Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi's supporters protest ED raids in Bengaluru, Gokak - Mangalorean.com
text: Karnataka Minister Satish Jarkiholi’s supporters protest ED raids in Bengaluru, Gokak Bengaluru: Supporters of Karnataka Public Works Department Minister, Satish Jarkiholi, staged protests in Bengaluru and Gokak on Friday, condemning the Enforcement Directorate (ED) searches at premises linked to the minister. Hundreds of supporters gathered at Freedom Park in Bengaluru in support of sugar baron Jarkiholi and raised slogans seeking justice for their leader. They held posters carrying messages such as “We are with you always” and “We condemn conspiracy against Ahinda leader.” The protesters also raised slogans against the ED and the Centre, alleging that the raids against Jarkiholi were politically motivated. Similar protests were held in Gokak, Jarkiholi’s stronghold, where his supporters formed a human chain at Basava Circle and expressed their opposition to the ED searches. Speaking about the development in Bengaluru today, Minister K.H. Muniyappa accused the ED of being used for political purposes and said the agency should not indulge in politics. “The raids against Satish Jarkiholi are equivalent to the murder of democracy,” Muniyappa said. He alleged that the ED was being used against people who were financially well-off and refused to join the BJP. “If they want to conduct raids in a justifiable manner, let them do so. If there are any issues or clarifications required, they should act according to the law. But conducting raids in an unjustifiable manner across the country is politics. This is criminal and condemnable,” he said. Muniyappa also alleged that the BJP was carrying out political activities through the ED and claimed that the agency had not learnt its lessons despite criticism from the Supreme Court. He said Jarkiholi, who is an industrialist would provide accounts and clarifications regarding the cash recovered during the searches and respond to the allegations against him through legal channels. “Satish Jarkiholi will give accounts for the cash found and provide clarifications to the allegations,” Muniyappa said. He further claimed that the people would teach the BJP a lesson in the 2029 elections. Muniyappa said Jarkiholi would not be intimidated or forced to “bend” because of the ED searches. headline: Mumbai Fire: Blaze Erupts At Income Tax Office In Churchgate, Fire Brigade Launches Rescue Operation To Evacuate Stranded Employees
text: A fire broke out in the basement of Aayakar Bhavan, the Income Tax office on Maharshi Karve Road in Mumbai's Churchgate, on Monday afternoon. The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) launched firefighting and evacuation operations after smoke spread to the upper floors of the building. According to the BMC Disaster Management Cell, the fire was reported at around 2:01 p.m. and was officially declared a Level-I fire at 2:10 p.m. The blaze was confined to the basement of the basement-plus-ground-plus-seven-storey building. While one team of the Mumbai Fire Brigade was engaged in firefighting operations, another team was evacuating employees and others stranded on the upper floors. Fire personnel used ladders through the windows to rescue people from the building. A turntable ladder and an aerial ladder platform were also deployed to assist with the evacuation. Multiple agencies, including the Mumbai Fire Brigade, Mumbai Police, BEST personnel, 108 ambulance services and BMC ward staff, were mobilised at the spot. Several senior fire officials and firefighting personnel, along with multiple fire engines and specialised emergency vehicles, were deployed to bring the blaze under control and assist with the rescue operation. No injuries or casualties have been reported so far, according to fire officials. The exact cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained. Firefighting and rescue operations were continuing, with further details on the cause and extent of the damage awaited.

headline: Shivakumar says Kumaraswamy’s KPSC attack is aimed at BJP, not Congress
text: Bengaluru: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday said JD(S) leader H D Kumaraswamy was targeting the BJP, not the Congress, over the alleged KPSC scam. Speaking to reporters here, he said Kumaraswamy was free to make whatever allegations he wanted. “Kumaraswamy is not fighting against us (Congress). He is fighting the BJP. Let him do his duty. Let him make whatever allegations he wants. He wants to see to it that the BJP is no more there and that he remains at the top. Let him do whatever he wants,” Shivakumar said when asked about Kumaraswamy’s allegations against the government over ‘irregularities’ in the Karnataka Public Service Commission. Asked about Kumaraswamy’s claim that he would release documents that would create a “storm”, Shivakumar said, “Very happy.” The union minister of Heavy Industries and Steel in India on Sunday launched a scathing attack on the Congress government over alleged irregularities in KPSC recruitments and questioned Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi’s silence on the issue. headline: UP Legislators Across Parties Demand GST Exemption On Vidhayak Nidhi, Cite Reduced Development Funds
text: Lucknow: Legislators cutting across party lines in Uttar Pradesh have demanded that the Vidhayak Nidhi, or constituency development fund, be exempted from the 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST), arguing that the levy reduces the money available for development works in their constituencies. The demand was raised during the recent Monsoon Session of the Uttar Pradesh Legislature. BJP MLC Devendra Pratap Singh submitted a notice under Rule 138 seeking a unanimous resolution to exempt Vidhayak Nidhi from GST. The Legislative Council was adjourned before the issue could be taken up for discussion. MLAs seek GST exemption The demand has also found support among legislators of the Samajwadi Party, Bahujan Samaj Party and Congress. BJP MLA Manish Asija of Firozabad said the government publicises that each MLA receives Rs 5 crore annually, while nearly Rs 90 lakh is deducted as GST, leaving about Rs 4.10 crore for development work. SP MLA Kamal Akhtar said the government should either quote the amount after GST or increase the Vidhayak Nidhi to Rs 6 crore. The legislators argue that Vidhayak Nidhi is meant exclusively for public welfare works and does not involve a commercial transaction between an MLA and the government. They therefore see little justification for imposing GST on expenditure incurred on development works. Government cites GST Council decision The Uttar Pradesh government, however, has pointed out that the GST Council has already rejected a proposal to exempt Vidhayak Nidhi from the tax. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya had prepared the government's response to the demand. The issue is not confined to Uttar Pradesh. Legislators in Tamil Nadu, Bihar and Uttarakhand have also raised concerns over the GST burden on constituency development funds. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin announced in April 2025 that the state government would bear the 18% GST on the MLA Local Area Development Fund. Tamil Nadu allocates Rs 3 crore annually to each MLA under the scheme. In Bihar, legislators demanded in February 2026 that the MLA LAD fund be increased from Rs 4 crore to Rs 5-6 crore annually to compensate for the GST deduction. Uttarakhand MLAs have also repeatedly expressed their frustration over the levy. headline: Major Multi-State Crackdown Dismantles ISI-Backed Shahzad Bhatti Terror Network Ahead of I-Day
text: In a major success, security agencies have carried out a multi-state crackdown against the ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti network ahead of Independence Day, busting its terror syndicate operating across different parts of the country. Union Home Minister Amit Shah said the Narendra Modi government had dismantled the ISI-backed terror network ahead of Independence Day and foiled attempts to create disturbances in different parts of the country. "Modi govt destroyed the ISI-backed terror group Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day and thwarted its plans for subversive attacks by arresting more than 200 operatives," Amit Shah posted on his social media handle. "Indian security forces ripped apart the network by launching coordinated operations across different locations in 14 states, upholding a brilliant example of India's zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism," he said. He added, "Substantial recoveries, including IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, live cartridges; and CCTV cameras used for espionage, were made from the ISI-funded group. The network was involved in several terrorist activities." The Shahzad Bhatti Network is a Pakistan-based, ISI-backed terror syndicate allegedly linked to grenade, IED and petrol-bomb attacks as well as targeted killings across India. The network has also allegedly been paying local conduits to conduct reconnaissance of police, defence and religious sites and install CCTV cameras for espionage. To counter disruptions allegedly planned by the network around Independence Day, a coordinated multi-state operation was carried out on August 12 using a real-time intelligence-sharing system in coordination with state police forces. The operation led to 253 detentions across 14 states — Uttar Pradesh (62), Haryana (52), Delhi (51), Punjab (44), Rajasthan (15), Maharashtra (8), Uttarakhand (5), Karnataka, Gujarat and Bihar (3 each), and Telangana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Kerala (2 each). Fresh FIRs were also registered in Delhi and Karnataka. Cumulatively, more than 80 FIRs have been registered, and over 200 arrests have been made against members of the Shahzad Bhatti Network under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Arms Act, Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and Explosive Substances Act. headline: Blocked from Delhi march, Punjab farmers camp at Haryana border
text: Blocked from Delhi march, Punjab farmers camp at Haryana border Punjab farmers remained camped at the Khanauri border point on Monday, August 17, a day after Haryana Police blocked them from proceeding toward Delhi as part of their 228-kilometre "Kisan Bachao Padyatra," officials and farmer leaders said. Police had erected multi-layer barricades at the border on Sunday, August 16, to prevent the march from continuing. Speaking to reporters, Jagjit Singh Dallewal, leader of the Samyukt Kisan Morcha (Non-Political), which is spearheading the foot march, said only a small group of farmers would continue sitting at the border point. "We have put up small tents as protection from the sultry weather. But having a Pucca Morcha here is not our agenda," he said. Dallewal said farmers plan to organise protest marches across the country on August 20, during which they will burn effigies and question the government over whether citizens have the right to peacefully march to the national capital on foot. He rejected the government's characterisation of the protest, saying farmers were sitting along a service road while Haryana authorities had blocked the highway with concrete slabs. "They used to say farmers will not be allowed with tractors and other vehicles, but they won't let us go even on foot now. This time, there are less than 300 farmers who want to march to Delhi in a peaceful manner, but the government still has a problem with us. Don't we even have the basic right to go to our national capital on foot?" he said. Three rounds of talks between Samyukt Kisan Morcha (Non-Political) representatives and Haryana government officials on Sunday failed to yield a resolution, according to the report. Dallewal had turned down an offer to meet Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, insisting instead on an appointment with Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan to discuss the farmers' central concern the proposed India-US trade deal. After police halted the march, Dallewal said the farmers would continue to sit peacefully at the Khanauri border point. The SKM (Non-Political) had called for the "Kisan Bachao Padyatra" from Data Singh Wala village on the Haryana-Punjab border to Delhi's Jantar Mantar, with the march set to culminate in a farmers' panchayat in the capital on August 29. headline: Congress legislators flash banners demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation inside Jammu and Kashmir assembly
text: Congress legislators on Friday (September 26, 2026) flashed banners inside the Jammu and Kashmir assembly that called for resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in the wake of recent reported controversy about differences with the Election Commission of India (ECI). During the Question Hour, several Congress legislators stood up and trooped into the well of the house with banners and disrupted the proceedings. They flashed banners stating that “there was no democracy without fair elections” and demanded the removal of the CEC Kumar.
